title: Stop is clipped out of the expanded composer during every run, with no key, palette or slash alternative
statement:
While a run is active, the expanded composer never paints Stop at any width. I checked live at 80x24, 120x40, 160x45 and 235x52 with the slow proxy. The row always ended 'Queue  Dictate  Redir' and 'Stop' appeared 0 times on screen.

Cause: the row has a fixed budget of 33 cells (BASE_ACTIONS_WIDTH 25 plus Send width 14 minus 6). Send 14, gap 2 and Dictate 11 use 27 of them. That leaves 6 cells for Redirect (10 cells, added by TASK-28227 / commit 42d9b7b737), which is cut to 'Redir', and 0 for Stop (6 cells).

Keyboard access is worse than the finding says:
- Tab does reach Stop, but with no visible focus. The order is Composer, Menu, Dictate, Redir, then an invisible focus, then the header.
- Enter on that invisible Stop does not stop the run. ChatScreen.on_key sends Enter from any composer descendant to the send path before the Button can handle it (log: phase=ui_action status=not_dispatched), and the run finished normally.

No other route stops the run:
- No stop binding exists.
- Esc, Esc and Ctrl+C during a run did not stop it.
- Ctrl+P 'stop' lists only navigation and settings commands.
- There is no /stop command, and /emergency-stop holds only new runs.
- The 'stop' WorkbenchAction exists but is filtered out of the header by TOP_ACTION_IDS.

The only working route is to collapse the composer ('Composer' toggle). The strip then shows 'Expand / Composer hidden - Generating ... Stop'. Clicking that Stop mid-run gave 'Assistant  Stopped' and 'Response stopped by user.' Nothing in the UI points users to this route. The User Guide says Stop appears 'between Send and Mic', which is false.

Minor corrections to the finding:
- At 120 columns I saw 'Redir', not 'Red'.
- The collapsed Stop was already present about 3.5 s into the run.
- 'Queue' is not enabled-looking: it uses the same disabled style as idle Send (#9e9e9e on #0d0d0d). The mismatch is only that the text says 'Send disabled' next to a button labelled 'Queue'.
expected: A visible, fully labelled, focusable Stop whenever this tab has an active run, at every supported width (80/120/160/235), acknowledged within 0.1 s and placed nearest the draft with warning treatment. Redirect shows its full label. There is also a documented keyboard route (e.g. Esc-Esc, or Ctrl+C on an empty composer while running) shown in the footer, a palette command and a /stop slash command. The disabled-reason text matches the Queue state (e.g. 'Type to queue').
why: Stopping a runaway, wrong or expensive agent run, which may be executing tools, is the core recovery action on a live work surface (DESIGN: 'make cancellation available'). The default layout makes it unreachable at every width, and the guide promises a button users cannot see. This is a user-control violation serious enough to generate support contacts.
repro: Launch ready mode at 235x52 (also 160x45, 120x40) and set the proxy to slow (curl …/_mode/<id>/slow). Send any prompt, then read the composer row within 5–10 s while 'Running'. Search the capture for 'Stop'. Then press Ctrl+P and type 'stop'.
recommendation: Make the action-row width run-aware and derive it from the buttons actually displayed: running width = Queue + Stop + Redirect (+ Dictate only if it fits). Put Stop first after the draft, in warning styling, so clipping can never remove it; while running, hide Dictate or swap Send for Stop before Stop is at risk. Shrink the 'Send disabled: …' reason to a tooltip, or drop it when space runs out, and say 'Type to queue' while running. Add a Stop key binding for the viewed tab's run (e.g. Esc-Esc, or Ctrl+C on an empty composer), shown in the footer only while a run is active, plus a 'Console: Stop this tab's run' palette command and a /stop slash command. Update chat-basics.md. Add a layout regression test asserting #console-stop-generation's region lies fully inside the screen at 80, 120, 160 and 235 columns whenever a run is active.
fix_direction:
- Make the row budget run-aware and derive it from the controls actually shown. Better still, place Stop right after the draft or swap it into Send's slot while running, so clipping can never remove it.
- Budget Redirect explicitly, or drop Dictate while running.
- Exclude #console-stop-generation and the other composer Buttons from the Enter capture in _should_capture_console_input, so a focused Stop presses on Enter.
- Add a stop route for the viewed tab's run: a key binding shown in the footer while running, a palette command, and /stop.
- Fix chat-basics.md:325.
- Add a Textual pilot regression test asserting that #console-stop-generation's region is fully inside the screen and not clipped by #console-composer-actions at 80, 120, 160 and 235 columns while run_active. Also test that Enter on the focused Stop cancels the run.

title: Every default Console send to OpenAI or Anthropic fails with HTTP 400 because of invalid built-in tool schemas, and the recovery copy blames the model
statement: Confirmed as stated. On origin/dev 64579cce2c, with a default isolated profile (setup complete, local tools on by default), every Console send fails with HTTP 400. This holds for Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 and OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini, sent directly with no proxy, and a second send in the same session fails the same way. The UI shows 'Assistant Failed / Response failed.' plus a System row: 'Agent run failed: provider returned HTTP 400 (Provider error from <provider>: bad request. Status: 400. Selected model: <model>. The provider rejected this request. Confirm the model is still available, or choose another model from the model picker.)'. The cause is the top-level schema combinators in three built-in tools in tldw_chatbook/Agents/local_tool_provider.py: watchlists_update_collection_sources (anyOf, ~line 4776), watchlists_check_sources (oneOf, ~4815) and todo_update (anyOf+allOf, ~4977). Each of the three is rejected on its own by both providers. The recovery advice is wrong: the same schema is rejected on claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-opus-4-1, gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4.1. The OpenAI path logs the full provider body (tools[34], invalid_function_parameters). The Anthropic path logs only 'Handler for anthropic directly raised; error_type=ChatBadRequestError; status=400', with no provider message.
expected: Default sends succeed. When a provider rejects a request, the message names the real cause (a tool definition, not the model), and the log records the provider body.
why: On a default profile the core loop is broken for the two most common cloud providers. The recovery advice points to the wrong fix, since changing models cannot help.
repro: launch.sh <name> 160 45 ready with DIRECT=1 (bypasses the proxy); send any message.
recommendation: Flatten the three schemas: move the either/or constraint into handler validation and the tool description. Add a provider-schema conformance test over every LocalToolSpec's parameters. Classify provider 400s that name a tool or parameter as 'tool definition rejected', with the tool name. The general copy mechanism is covered in G4-06.
fix_direction: 1. Flatten the three schemas. Remove the top-level anyOf/oneOf/allOf and keep type=object with properties, required and additionalProperties. Enforce 'at least one of add/remove', 'exactly one of source_ids/collection_id' and 'deleted excludes content/activeForm' in the handlers, which already need to validate, and state the rule in each tool's description. 2. Add a conformance test that iterates every LocalToolSpec (and ideally every disclosed ToolSchema, including MCP-bridged ones, or sanitise at projection time in schemas_to_openai_tools and the Anthropic converter). It should assert that the top level is type=object with no anyOf/oneOf/allOf/enum/const/not. 3. Classify provider 400s whose body names a tool or parameter (OpenAI code invalid_function_parameters or param tools[N]; Anthropic message 'tools.N...input_schema') as 'tool definition rejected: <tool name>', and suppress the 'choose another model' advice for that class. 4. In the Anthropic error path, log a redacted provider error message the way the OpenAI handler already does.

title: After swapping a character into a chat, sends silently get no reply and later sends are refused with no reason; the draft disappears into an 'Unsent turn needs attention' strip
statement:
On origin/dev @ 64579cce2c, any Console chat that has a system prompt cannot get a reply. The trigger is not specific to the character swap. It fires the same way whether the prompt comes from Status > System Prompt (set before the first send or mid-chat), from 'Swap in this chat' with a character, or from 'Start new chat' with a character. It reproduced 5 out of 5 times; it is not a one-off. The swap only triggers it because the swap installs the character's system prompt; the status row flips to 'System Prompt: set'.

What the user sees:
- The first send is saved as a user row in the transcript. It gets no reply, no SYSTEM row and no toast.
- The header still says 'Ready'. Inspect says 'Run: Ready', 'Live work: No active work' and 'Ready to send'.
- The only sign is a lowercase 'blocked' border label at the bottom-right of the transcript. It has no reason and no action, and it disappears when you switch tabs. In one run the stuck user row itself did not show until the next send.
- Every later send in that tab is refused. Each refused draft is parked in an amber 'Queue 0/10 · Unsent turn needs attention' strip with a clipped 'Rest' (Restore) button and a 'Discard' button, and no cause is given.

Nothing gets the tab working again: not Restore then resend, not Discard then send, and not clearing the system prompt then sending. A new tab with no system prompt sends normally.

The draft is not lost. It is parked in the strip, and Restore puts it back in the composer. The controller does compute recovery copy, 'Trace provenance could not be saved. Retry, Send without capture, or Cancel.', but it is never shown.
expected: When a turn is blocked or refused, the transcript shows next to the stuck message what blocked it and the specific next step (for example 'Character change needs … — Retry / Start new chat'). The recovery strip names the cause instead of 'Queue 0/10', and 'Restore' is not truncated.
why: The user cannot continue the conversation and has no way to find out why without the logs. PRODUCT.md explicitly forbids 'interfaces that require reading logs to understand status'. The draft also disappears from the composer.
repro: ready mode: send one message ▸ Status ▸ 'System Prompt' ▸ set text ▸ Apply ▸ Status ▸ 'Assistant: General' ▸ choose a character ▸ 'Swap in this chat' ▸ send 'Who are you?'. No reply arrives. Send again and the draft moves into 'Unsent turn needs attention'.
recommendation: Make every terminal non-success outcome (blocked, refused, RuntimeError) add a SYSTEM row to the transcript, as the _block path already does (console_chat_controller.py:23565-23578), stating the cause and offering Retry / New chat. Rename the strip to 'Unsent message — <reason>' and size the Restore/Discard buttons to their labels (see also G4-28). Investigate why a character swap leaves the session unable to send.
fix_direction:
1. Root cause: land the TASK-32951 fix, or its equivalent, so that unsaved and effective system prompts, including character system prompts, count as rendered system context in _build_durable_trace_request. Captured sends with a system prompt must succeed. Add a regression test that sends with a system prompt set before the first turn and mid-chat, and after both a character swap and a new character chat.
2. Every terminal non-success path (BLOCKED from _handle_durable_trace_provenance_failure and the other BLOCKED returns, plus refused submits) must append a SYSTEM row next to the stuck turn, the way _block does. The row carries the visible_copy and actionable buttons wired to the existing paused-preparation recovery (Retry / Send without capture / Cancel).
3. The header run chip and Inspect 'Run:' must reflect a BLOCKED run state instead of 'Ready'.
4. For turn-recovery, the queue strip should show the refusal's visible_copy, as the dispatch-recovery branch already does, instead of the fixed 'Unsent turn needs attention'. It should drop 'Queue 0/10' when the queue is empty and size Restore/Discard to their labels.
5. Check that the strip's Discard, or a new explicit action, can clear the paused preparation so the tab can send again.

title: Compaction fails silently after a billed summarizer call, and every later send in that chat is billed again and stays blocked
statement:
I reproduced this live, and every user-visible claim holds. The finding misses the cause, though: in a live session, compaction never succeeds.

Setup: app-created chat, automatic compaction, custom 6,000-token budget, default stop_and_ask.
- 7th send: the header says 'Running' and the status bar says 'Run: Validating provider.' Nothing mentions summarizing. It ends at 'Response accepted; waiting for dispatch.' with Retry/Discard, and 'Send blocked - resolve response recovery first'.
- Retry makes a second billed summarizer call and ends with 'Response failed.' plus 'Conversation compaction did not complete; the provider request was not sent.'
- A fresh send makes a third billed call and is blocked again.
- Settings > Compact now makes a fourth billed call and shows the same copy.

All four attempt rows are status=failed (7,156 in / 111-115 out). No memory is written, the log has only started/finished, and the table has no reason column.

Why it fails: live-created messages keep parent_message_id=None in memory, because _hydrate_durable_turn_owner_messages sets only persisted_message_id. The commit's durable_lineage is built from those snapshots, so _validate_branch_memory_commit_ownership raises 'durable_lineage must be one ordered parent chain'. compact() swallows that as memory_commit_failed without logging, and the controller shows the fixed generic copy.

The summaries were valid (non-empty, no wrapper tags, far below the 1,024 cap). After an app restart, when messages reload from the DB with parents, Compact now on the same chat SUCCEEDED.
expected: Compaction should either succeed or fail with a named reason (e.g. 'the kept recent turns alone exceed the 55% target') and a next step: omit older context, raise the budget, turn compaction off, or start a new chat. Billed attempts should be disclosed as spent, and a failed compaction should not re-run automatically, at a cost, on every later send.
why: Every long-running conversation reaches the threshold eventually, and small-context/local models reach it quickly. At that point the chat becomes unusable, money is spent on every attempt, and nothing tells the user why or what to do. A user would contact support.
repro: EXTRA_TOML with [console] compaction_mode='automatic', conversation_budget_mode='custom', conversation_budget_tokens=6000; launch ready; send 7 prompts asking for ~600-word replies; then click Retry response, then send another message; query console_auxiliary_attempts.
recommendation: Carry the CompactionTransactionResult.reason through to the UI and persist it on the auxiliary-attempt row. Render a turn-level card: 'Couldn't compact this chat: the 3 most recent turns alone exceed the target (3,300 tokens). Spent: 6,947 in / 319 out (~$0.01).' with actions [Send without older turns] [Raise budget…] [Turn compaction off for this chat] [New chat from summary]. After one failure, do not auto-retry compaction on later sends until the conversation or policy changes. Show 'Summarizing older turns… (1 extra model call)' in the turn status while the auxiliary call runs. Replace 'the provider request was not sent' with 'your message was not sent'.
fix_direction:
Fix the root cause first:
- Set the in-memory parent_message_id when hydrating committed turn owners, for example the user row to the prior persisted leaf and the assistant row to the user's persisted id.
- Or build the commit lineage fences from persisted DB rows rather than the in-memory message fields.
- Add an integration test that runs a real store, a durable send and automatic compaction, with no fakes.

Then address the UX points the finding raises:
- Log and persist transaction.reason on the attempt row.
- Map each reason to specific copy and a next step: omit older context, raise the budget, turn compaction off, or start a new chat.
- Disclose the spent tokens and cost.
- Suppress automatic re-attempts after a failure until the conversation or policy changes.
- Show 'Summarizing older turns (1 extra model call)' while the auxiliary call runs.
- Replace 'the provider request was not sent' with 'your message was not sent'. In the Compact now context no message was involved, so it should say compaction failed and nothing changed.

title: Extends G4-03: any chat whose history holds a non-model assistant turn (a character greeting from 'Start new chat', or a /generate-image result) silently blocks the next send, and the prepared recovery copy is never rendered
statement:
On dev @ 64579cce2c, a Console send is refused before the provider is contacted, and no reason or recovery is shown, whenever the request carries a system prompt or the chat's only assistant history is a /generate-image result. Every log shows the same pattern: 'durable_commit status=succeeded' followed about 4 ms later by 'controller_submit status=blocked', with no error line in between. The proxy log shows no provider request.

The finding's diagnosis of trigger (1) is wrong. The character greeting is not the cause:
- Deleting the greeting before sending still blocks.
- Swapping a character into a plain chat that has already worked, where no greeting is inserted, blocks.
- A plain 'Assistant: General' chat with only a session system prompt ('Be brief.') blocks. This reproduced in two separate profiles.

So every character chat (built-in Default Assistant and Samira both show 'System Prompt: set') and every manually set system prompt blocks. Trigger (2) is correctly attributed. A chat created by /generate-image blocks on its next send; after deleting the image in such a chat, the send completes.

The controller catches everything around _build_durable_trace_request and pauses with TRACE_PROVENANCE. trace_call_recovery_state() filters that pause out, even though controller.trace_call_recovery_preparation() and send_without_capture() both accept it. As a result, the 'Retry / Send without capture / Cancel' copy is never rendered for these cases.

The block is not fully silent. The left-rail Chats list shows '⛔ Blocked' and a 'blocked' edge badge appears. But no cause and no actions are given, the header still says 'Ready', the Inspect rail says 'Run: Ready', and the strip's 'Agent blocked' is shown from launch before any send, so it signals nothing. The composer clears, but the user turn stays in the transcript. A follow-up send becomes 'Queue 0/10 · Unsent turn needs attention [Rest][Discard]', where 'Rest' is a truncated 'Restore' label, and Restore brings that draft back.

The image variant is narrower than stated. An image generated after a normal model exchange fails at a different stage: trace_dispatch_commit, error_category=surface_prefix_mismatch ValueError, which is logged. That path DOES render a 'Trace capture blocked' callout, and its 'Send without capture' works, though the next send blocks again.
expected: A normal chat with a character, or a chat that includes a generated image, sends like any other. If a pre-send stage does fail, an inline recovery callout names the cause and offers the actions the copy promises. The header or status strip reflect the blocked state, and the draft is kept.
why: The user cannot talk to their own imported character at all, and one image generation breaks the rest of the chat. Both fail silently, so the user cannot tell what happened or how to recover. A user would contact support.
repro: Profile 'ready'. Status strip 'Assistant: General' → Choose character → pick an imported card → 'Start new chat' → type a message → Enter. Separately: /generate-image <prompt> (with any working backend) → then send a normal prompt in the same chat.
recommendation: Fix the underlying failure in _build_durable_trace_request for greeting and generation messages: treat non-model assistant rows as context-only turns. Log the exception type with the attempt_id. Add TRACE_PROVENANCE to the recovery projection so the inline callout renders, with working Retry, Send without capture and Cancel actions. Set the header and strip state to 'Blocked — trace provenance' so every region agrees.
fix_direction:
1. Add TRACE_PROVENANCE to trace_call_recovery_state() so the existing Retry / Send without capture / Cancel callout renders; the controller already supports all three for this pause. Add a copy variant that says the provider was not contacted.
2. Log a content-free error_category and exception_type at the except in console_chat_controller.py:12232, keyed by attempt_id, as the trace_dispatch_commit path already does.
3. Fix the root causes by trigger, not by 'non-model assistant rows':
   - (a) System-role rows, whether from a character or a session system prompt, must admit or align provenance in _build_durable_trace_request / build_console_request. Characters are only one source of this, so a greeting-only fix would leave every character chat broken.
   - (b) Image-generation assistant rows (list content with image parts) need provenance admission, and the dispatch-surface prefix check must accept them.
4. Make the header and the Inspect 'Run' preview reflect BLOCKED with its reason.
5. Add a regression test for each trigger: session system prompt, character new chat, character swap-in, image-only chat, and image after an exchange.
6. Separately, the queue shelf's 'Restore' label is truncated to 'Rest'.

title: 'Copy as ▸ Save .md…' on a conversation row crashes the app; the target modal also lacks Esc and backdrop cancel
statement:
The core claim holds. Conversation row 💬 > Copy as > Save .md... ends the app every time: 2 of 2 live runs on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. The cause is self.push_screen(ConsoleSaveMarkdownModal(...), callback=_write) at chat_screen.py:7149. ChatScreen is a Screen, and Screen has no push_screen in Textual 8.2.8. The worker raises "AttributeError: 'ChatScreen' object has no attribute 'push_screen'", the log records event=unhandled_exception at raise_line=7149 and then "App Unmounting", and no file is written.

What the user sees after the crash varies:
- Run 1: the process stayed alive, full-screen traceback on display, and ignored app input (typed keys echoed as raw text) for over 2 minutes, until Ctrl+C.
- Run 2: the process exited within about 1 s and the tmux session died.

On relaunch the open tabs and the unsent draft are gone, and a fresh "Chat 1" tab appears. Saved conversation history survives.

Three details in the finding are wrong:
(a) The loss does not happen "because the Close-session/Leave/Quit impact dialogs never run". The Quit dialog only counts live agent runs, delegated agents and queued prompts. A clean Ctrl+Q with an unsent draft and two open tabs shows no dialog and also loses both on relaunch. The loss is real because the user never chose to exit. Only live runs and queued prompts lose a warning they would otherwise get, and that part is inferred from code, not reproduced.
(b) "on_mount skips super(), so the opener-focus capture is lost" is false. Textual dispatches on_mount to every class in the MRO, so SafeModalDismissMixin.on_mount still runs.
(c) The missing Escape binding and missing SAFE_MODAL_CONTENT are real in code. ConsoleSaveMarkdownModal is the only one of 51 ModalScreens in Widgets/Console that lacks them. But no user can see this today, because the crash happens before the modal ever opens.
expected: Save .md… opens a path prompt that closes with Esc like every other Console modal. No menu action can terminate the app.
why: A visible, advertised feature destroys in-progress work with one click.
repro: ready mode; send one message; click the conversation's 💬 in the rail Chats group ▸ Copy as ▸ Save .md… → the app exits.
recommendation: Call self.app.push_screen(...). Give ConsoleSaveMarkdownModal BINDINGS=[('escape','request_safe_cancel','Cancel')], call super().on_mount(), and set SAFE_MODAL_CONTENT. Add a parametrised test that dispatches every ConversationMenuItem/WorkspaceMenuItem action id against a live ChatScreen, and a test that every Console ModalScreen binds escape.
fix_direction: At chat_screen.py:7149, change self.push_screen to self.app.push_screen, or use the screen's existing push-screen delegate. Replace the monkeypatched test with one that runs the real _save_console_conversation_markdown under a pilot and asserts the modal mounts and the file is written. Add a parametrised test that dispatches every ConversationMenuItem and WorkspaceMenuItem action id against a live ChatScreen with no stubs. Then fix the modal under TASK-32864 / ADR-031: add BINDINGS=[('escape','request_safe_cancel','Cancel')] and SAFE_MODAL_CONTENT='#console-save-markdown-box', and route Cancel/Save through dismiss_safe_once so opener focus is restored. Adding super().on_mount() is harmless but not needed. Separately, and outside this finding: a clean quit also drops unsent drafts and open tabs with no warning, which may deserve its own look.

title: 'Choose folder' for project instructions freezes the whole app: Esc, Enter, clicks and Ctrl+Q are all ignored
statement:
In a named workspace with one bound git folder, the Inspect pin 'Choose folder · Project' opens the Conversation Inspector (Project Instructions, 'State: Choose folder'). Pressing its 'Choose folder' button makes ConsoleConversationInspector._recover_project_instructions, an @on message handler that is not a worker, await session.py:5420 app.push_screen_wait(ProjectInstructionSetupModal(...)). Textual appends the modal to the screen stack first and then raises NoActiveWorker. The TASK-32533 keep-alive swallows the error and shows the 'Something went wrong in _select_project_instruction_binding' toast. Textual then ends the Inspector's message loop and detaches the Inspector and its children, but the Inspector stays on the screen stack.

The picker modal is still alive at this point: hovering its buttons highlights them. The background is sometimes blank (run 1) and sometimes the dimmed Console (run 2). The first Esc, Cancel, 'd' or folder-row click is handled and closes the modal, but the result goes to a future nobody awaits. The chosen folder is never applied: the pin still reads 'Choose folder · Project' after a restart. The screen is also never repainted, so a stale picker image stays on screen.

The top screen is now the dead, detached Inspector. Every later key, click and resize is forwarded to it and dropped. Ctrl+Q cannot reach the App either: Screen._binding_chain is built from the detached focused button's ancestors, which no longer include the App. The process stays alive and nearly idle (1-6% CPU), and Ctrl+C does nothing. The only way out is to kill the process (SIGTERM); the terminal does not need to be killed. Reproduced 3 out of 3 times.

The data-loss argument is overstated. An unsent draft in this scenario is also gone after a normal Ctrl+Q and relaunch, and Temporary chats are ephemeral by design.
expected: Choosing a project folder opens a working picker, applies the choice and returns to the Inspector. If something goes wrong, the dialog can still be dismissed, and Ctrl+Q always quits.
why: This is the only in-Console control for giving file tools a bound folder (the Inspect pin points straight at it). It hard-locks the app and loses all unsent drafts, the parked queue and Temporary chats, which is worse than a crash because nothing is saved and nothing exits.
repro: Isolated profile. Create a named workspace with a folder bound. Open Inspect and click 'Choose folder · Project' (or open the Conversation Inspector). Click 'Choose folder'. Then try Esc, Enter or Ctrl+Q.
recommendation: Run the binding selection inside a worker (run_worker), or use push_screen with a callback instead of push_screen_wait. The keep-alive handler must never leave a freshly pushed modal on top of a broken pump: pop it, or dismiss the Inspector. Add a test that Ctrl+Q works while a modal is up after a handler error. Add a live test that drives the Inspector 'Choose folder' button.
fix_direction:
1) Root cause: do not await push_screen_wait from a message handler. Either run the recovery flow in a worker (decorate _recover_project_instructions with @work, or call run_worker(..., exclusive=True, exit_on_error=False) from the handler), or switch _select_project_instruction_binding to push_screen(modal, callback=...) resolving an asyncio.Future. The same file already uses the callback pattern in _project_project_instruction_binding (session.py ~5430-5470).
2) Keep-alive (app_lifecycle.py ~877-930): never keep the app alive when the pump that died is a Screen, or the screen that owns the focused widget. That leaves a detached screen on the stack that swallows all input. Either fall through to Textual's loud exit, or remove the dead screen from the stack (and any screens pushed on top of it) and reset focus to a live screen before notifying. Popping only the pushed modal is NOT enough, and making Ctrl+Q priority=True is NOT enough: the minimal repro shows the binding chain comes from a detached widget.
3) Guards: add a W003 rule to scripts/check_textual_worker_contract.py that flags push_screen_wait / push_screen(wait_for_dismiss=True) reachable from a non-@work coroutine. Add a Pilot test with _keep_screen_alive_on_handler_error=True that raises in a ModalScreen handler and asserts the app can still quit, and add a Pilot/live test that drives the Inspector 'Choose folder' button through selecting a folder and asserts the binding is applied. Extend TASK-32569's ACs to cover the dead-screen-on-stack case.

title: First-run wizard: arrowing onto most Cloud providers blanks the Provider step, kills keyboard control, and re-entering the step quits the app
statement:
Confirmed, with small refinements. On Quick setup ▸ Provider, the list shows a header plus 4 Popular rows. The 4th Down leaves llama.cpp for the first Cloud row, ByteDance Seed (BytePlus). The step body goes blank, a red toast says "Something went wrong in _ownership_for — the screen was kept open…", and the log records ValueError at provider_setup_persistence.py:193. A mouse click on another affected row (MiniMax) fails the same way, so this is not arrow-specific. Picking any listed provider whose key is outside _CANONICAL_PROVIDER_KEYS triggers it. That is 13 of the 24 Cloud rows (BytePlus, Cerebras, DeepInfra, Fireworks, MiniMax, Nebius, Novita, NVIDIA NIM, SambaNova, StepFun, Tencent TokenHub, Together, Xiaomi MiMo) plus "Custom Hosted", which the wizard lists under Local rather than Other. A canonical Cloud row (Google Gemini) works normally as a control.

After the failure, none of Up, Ctrl+B, Esc, Tab ×3 or Ctrl+N changes the screen (byte-identical captures). Only the mouse works. Clicking ← Back works, but clicking Next → from Welcome re-enters the step, raises NoMatches in _credential_draft (FirstRunSetupWizard.py:2225), and the app exits ("App Unmounting"). Clicking Next → straight from the blanked step also exits the app, through NoMatches in commit (line 3263). In a session resumed from "Continue setup?", ← Back is disabled, so Next (which crashes) and Exit setup are the only controls. The one clean escape is clicking Exit setup: its confirm modal takes the keyboard and exits to Console. Relaunching offers "Continue setup? Resume", so the profile is not bricked and the draft keeps no bad provider.
expected: Every provider the wizard lists can be highlighted and chosen, or it is not listed. A step failure never takes away keyboard control or kills the app, and the user can always go Back or Exit.
why: This is a new user's first task. Browsing providers with the arrow keys is the natural move: one keystroke blanks setup and the second attempt closes the app.
repro: launch.sh j12 235 52 fresh → Enter (Quick setup) → Down ×4 → blank step + toast; Esc (ignored); click ← Back then Next → → app exits.
recommendation: Use one source of truth: derive the wizard list from the providers provider_setup_persistence can own, or add the missing keys to _CANONICAL_PROVIDER_KEYS/_ALIASES. Add a test that highlights and selects every catalog entry. Guard the highlight handler so an unsupported provider shows an inline 'not available in setup yet — configure in Settings' row instead of raising. Make _credential_draft tolerate a missing input. After any kept-alive handler error in the wizard, restore focus to the nav buttons so Esc and Ctrl+B still work.
fix_direction: Use one source of truth. Filter the wizard's provider list to keys that provider_setup_persistence can own (or the same set Settings offers, see TASK-33002.13 AC#1), or add the missing 14 keys to _CANONICAL_PROVIDER_KEYS and _ALIASES along with their endpoint and credential ownership. Add a parametrized test that highlights and selects every catalog entry the wizard lists. Guard select_provider so an unsupported key shows an inline 'not available in setup yet — configure in Settings' row instead of raising. Make _credential_draft and commit tolerate a missing #setup-provider-api-key (return a skip or no-key draft). After any caught handler error in the wizard, restore focus to the nav bar (reuse TASK-1267's focus strategy) so Esc and Ctrl+B still work. Also re-check why ← Back is disabled on a resumed Provider step.

title: Emergency stop leaves no persistent indicator: the header says 'Ready', the refusal says 'Clear it to resume' without saying how, and it is the only 'stop' command
statement: Reproduced live at 120x40 on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. Running /emergency-stop shows a warning toast for about 5 s: 'Emergency stop ACTIVE - new runs and scheduled dispatches are held. Run /emergency-stop clear to resume.' Once the toast fades, the Console looks exactly as it did before the stop. A diff of the before and after captures differs only in transcript rows. The header still reads 'Ready' and the status strip is unchanged. That strip shows 'Agent blocked', but that chip is the Library-access permission (TASK-25732) and was already there before the stop. The Agent rail section reads 'Agent: idle'. With a draft typed, Send reads 'Send | $' and is enabled. The stop survives a restart: emergency_stop.json stays active=true. After relaunch there is still no indicator anywhere, and the empty transcript even says 'Ready - type a message to begin.' Each send, before and after the restart, is refused with the toast 'Emergency stop is active: new runs and scheduled dispatches are held. Clear it to resume.' That copy does not name the clear command. The draft is kept. /emergency-stop clear lifts the stop and the next send streams normally. Scheduled dispatches are held in silence: SchedulerLoop._dispatch_due logs at debug level only, and no UI anywhere reads the stop state. Held tasks are not lost, though: they stay queued and fire once the stop is cleared. Two small corrections to the finding. First, the slash menu matches by prefix only, so typing '/stop' suggests nothing. /emergency-stop turns up for a 'stop' search only in the unknown-command list shown after pressing Enter on '/stop', where it is the only stop-like command. Second, the clear syntax can be found elsewhere: the slash-menu row ends '(clear to resume)', and '/help emergency-stop' shows '/emergency-stop [clear | <reason>]'. That partly offsets the vague refusal copy.
expected: While active, a persistent header state and strip chip ('Emergency stop — new runs held [Clear]') are shown. Send's disabled reason names the hold, the refusal copy includes the exact clear action, and a per-tab '/stop' ranks above '/emergency-stop'.
why: A global, cross-restart block behind a 'Ready' header is a classic mode error and the hidden-recovery-state anti-pattern PRODUCT.md forbids. Scheduled work can silently not run.
repro: At 120x40: /emergency-stop + Enter; wait 6-8 s and check header and strip; type a message + Enter; then /emergency-stop clear.
recommendation: Read emergency_stop_state in the header and status-strip presenters and render a persistent 'Hold: emergency stop · Clear' chip plus a header hold state. Feed the hold into the composer's Send disabled-reason. Put the literal clear command, or a Clear button, into EmergencyStopState.visible_copy. Add '/stop' for the per-tab run and rank it above '/emergency-stop'.
fix_direction: Change EmergencyStopState.visible_copy to name the exact action, e.g. 'Run /emergency-stop clear to resume.' This closes the TASK-26004 AC#5 gap. Have the Console header and status-strip presenters read emergency_stop_state: render a persistent warning chip ('Emergency stop - new runs held · Clear') whose action runs the clear, and replace the header's 'Ready' with a hold state. Put the hold into the composer's Send disabled-reason so the block is visible before Enter. Surface the hold on the Schedules screen too, and at boot when the persisted flag is active. The /stop ranking belongs with G3-03, which covers the per-tab Stop visibility. Optionally make slash suggestions match substrings so '/stop' finds both commands.

title: Enter does not send when the draft holds a collapsed paste, inserted file or prompt token: it arms 'Expand?' and then dumps the content into the draft
statement: Confirmed live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c (235x52, ready mode). When the draft contains any collapsed token (a paste over 50 chars, an inline text-file token, or a /prompt insert, all of which go through insert_pasted_text/insert_file_segment), Enter does not send. Each Enter moves the first remaining token one step, collapsed -> 'Expand?' -> expanded, and the draft only sends once no collapsed token is left. That makes 2N+1 Enters for N tokens: 3 for one paste and 5 for two file tokens. The file name is replaced by an orange 'Expand?', and the expanded contents are spliced into the draft. Esc does not reset a pending 'Expand?'. One thing is worse than the finding says. Enter on the keyboard-focused Send button is hijacked the same way: it armed 'Expand?' and sent nothing, and Space on the focused Send button went into the draft instead of pressing the button. So a keyboard-only user can't send the staged token collapsed. The only way is to expand every token first, and only a mouse click on Send sends in one step. When the message does finally go out it carries the full content, so nothing is lost.
expected: Enter always sends the draft as it stands, with collapsed tokens sent in full (which is what the user staged). Expanding a token is a separate, explicit action on the token: click, or a dedicated key such as Space/Ctrl+E/Alt+E while the caret is on the token. The chip names that affordance ('Pasted 30 lines · 2,811 chars · Expand (click)'). Esc clears a pending 'Expand?', and the file name stays visible while confirming ('Expand photosynthesis.md?').
why: Pasting logs or code, or bringing notes in and asking a question, then pressing Enter is the most common power-user and grounding flow. Here the core send gesture silently fails twice and rearranges the draft, so users conclude the app ignores Enter.
repro: Ready 235x52. Bracketed-paste more than about 500 chars (or two .md file paths, or use Menu ▸ Attach file on a .txt), type a question, and press Enter. Observe 'Expand?'. Press Esc: nothing changes. Press Enter again: the content expands into the draft.
recommendation: Remove the token-unfurl hook from the Enter/send path. Enter sends, and collapsed tokens go with their full content. Advance a token only by click, or by a distinct key while the caret is adjacent to or inside it. Esc clears a pending 'Expand?'. Keep the file name in the confirm label. Add a regression test: paste over 50 chars, press Enter, assert dispatch.
fix_direction: Remove activate_focused_paste_token() from the Enter/send path in chat_screen.py:22789-22793, so Enter always sends the canonical draft (tokens included in full). Narrow _should_capture_console_input, or special-case Enter, so a focused Send/Menu/Dictate button handles its own Enter/Space. Advance a token only on click, or with a dedicated key (e.g. Space/Ctrl+E) while the caret is adjacent to the token. Make Escape call composer.reset_pending_unfurl() before focus_console_composer_home's other work. Render the confirm state with the label kept (e.g. 'Expand photosynthesis.md?' / 'Expand 30-line paste?'), and put the affordance in the chip ('Expand (click)'). In the same change: update Tests/UI/test_console_send_draft_snapshot.py:383-388 (it pins the 3-Enter flow); add a regression test (paste >50 chars, press Enter, assert one dispatch with the full text, with the token still collapsed in the sent payload); add one for Enter on the focused Send button; update Docs/User_Guide/console/chat-basics.md 'Large pastes' (it is also stale on the 'Unfurl?' / 'Pasted Text: N Characters' copy).

title: Enter on the focused composer 'Menu' button sends the draft to the provider; Space types into the draft; the menu never opens by keyboard
statement: Confirmed live on origin/dev 64579cce2c at 160x45 in ready mode. From the composer, Tab Tab lands on 'Menu', which shows the focus cue (bold, underline, bg #155486). Pressing Enter there sends the draft: the User turn 'hello menu test' appears, the Assistant row shows 'Connecting tools…', the log records console_send_stage phase=provider_entry status=entered, and a real reply comes back. With a blank draft, the same Enter logs phase=ui_action status=not_dispatched, no menu opens, and focus leaves Menu. Space on the focused Menu inserts a space into the draft: the placeholder disappears and the caret moves. The Composer actions menu opens only by mouse click, and when it does, focus lands on its first item. The defect is wider than Menu. Enter on the focused 'Dictate' button also goes down the send path (not_dispatched with an empty draft) and never starts dictation. Every composer-bar button except Composer ▾, Expand and the collapsed-mode Stop is affected. Two details need correcting. (1) Textual's Button binds only Enter, not Space, so "Space should activate" follows web/ARIA convention rather than a Textual default. The real Space defect is that the keystroke edits a draft that does not have focus. (2) Some menu entries have other keyboard routes: the palette's 'Console: Insert prompt…', 'Save draft to shelf…' and 'Paste image from clipboard', plus /prompt and /generate-image. Attach file, Save as Chatbook, Generate Caption, Impersonate, Buddy… and 'Improve current draft…' have no palette or binding route I could find, so they are mouse-only. A related cue problem: while Menu has the focus ring, the draft keeps painting its caret, so two focus indicators show at once.
expected: Enter and Space on a focused button activate that button. Enter on 'Menu' opens the composer menu with focus on its first item. Keys reach the draft only when the draft itself has focus.
why: A keyboard-only user who tabs to Menu and presses Enter fires a paid provider request with a half-written prompt, and the menu's features stay out of reach.
repro: Ready mode, 235x52 or 160x45. Type text in the composer, press Tab Tab (Menu focused), press Enter: the draft is sent. Press Tab Tab again, then Space: a space is inserted.
recommendation: In _should_capture_console_input, return False whenever the focused widget is a Button or Switch (anything other than the draft surface), so Button.press runs on Enter, and add Space activation for these buttons. Add a keyboard test for every composer-bar button (Composer ▾, Menu, Dictate, Send, Queue, Redirect). Add a 'Console: Open composer menu' palette command.
fix_direction: In _should_capture_console_input, stop capturing when focus sits on a control inside the composer rather than on the draft surface. Replace the three-id allowlist with `focused is None or focused is composer`, or return False whenever `isinstance(focused, (Button, Switch))`. That lets Button's Enter binding press Menu, Dictate and the other composer buttons. Keep global chords (paging, undo/redo) routed as intended. Stop painting the draft caret while a sibling control holds focus, so only one focus cue shows. Space activation for composer buttons is optional (it is a web convention, not a Textual default); at minimum Space must not edit a draft that lacks focus. Add a 'Console: Open composer menu' palette command, plus palette entries for the Menu-only actions (Attach file, Impersonate, Save as Chatbook, Improve draft). Add a Pilot test for each composer-bar button: focus it, press Enter, and assert that its own action runs and no console_send_stage fires. Extend the TASK-15704 test rather than adding another id to the allowlist.

title: A stale 'Unsent turn needs attention' shelf stays after the turn was sent, and its clipped 'Rest' (Restore) re-queues the already-answered prompt
statement: Confirmed live on origin/dev 64579cce2c. With Capture On (the default), every send in a Temporary tab pauses on 'Save chat to capture this send'. At that moment the runtime records a turn recovery, so the queue shelf reads 'Queue 0/10 · Unsent turn needs attention' with a clipped 'Rest' and 'Discard' even while the pause callout is still on screen. After 'Send without capture' the turn is dispatched once and answered ('OK 7'), but nothing settles the recovery. The shelf keeps reading 'Unsent turn needs attention' until the user presses Rest or Discard; it was still there more than 30 s after the reply. Clicking 'Rest' (Restore) puts the already-answered prompt back into the composer. It does not auto-send: a duplicate send needs one more Enter, which the stale shelf invites. The clipped label comes from the 8-cell button width. Two sub-claims are real but not specific to this bug, so they should be split out. (a) The shelf after a blocked send in an archived tab is a legitimate recovery, not a defect. (b) A parked recovery is held only in memory. Ctrl+Q quits with no confirmation and the parked draft is gone after relaunch, but a plain unsent composer draft is not persisted across restart either.
expected: The recovery entry clears once its turn has been dispatched or answered, button labels are never clipped, and a parked turn that will be lost at restart says so.
why: The status is misleading and invites a duplicate paid send. A clipped 'Rest' is unreadable as a command.
repro: In a Temporary tab send a message, choose 'Send without capture', and wait for the reply. The bottom shelf still shows Rest/Discard. Click Rest.
recommendation: Settle the turn recovery (discard_turn_recovery) as soon as the recovery callout's 'Send without capture' or 'Save & Send' succeeds. Size the shelf buttons to their labels ('Restore', 'Discard'). Warn when a parked turn will be lost at restart.
fix_direction: Tie the runtime turn recovery to the paused preparation. Either skip recording a recovery for a PAUSED (non-terminal) preparation refusal, because the callout already owns that turn, or call discard_turn_recovery for the matching turn_id once send_without_capture or save_and_send reaches durable acceptance (and on 'Cancel send' if that restores the draft). As a guard, restore_turn_recovery should refuse an entry whose turn was since accepted. Size #console-prompt-queue-manage and #console-prompt-queue-pause to their labels (width: auto, or at least 9 for 'Restore'). Handle loss at quit or restart separately, as general draft behaviour: either persist drafts and recoveries, or include parked recoveries in the quit and close lifecycle impact so the user is warned.

title: A multi-prompt queue halts after successful turns under a false 'Turn failed', and its Retry replies 'No matching stopped or failed turn is available'
statement:
With two or more prompts queued behind a turn in one Console tab, the queue stops after the first queued prompt is accepted, and it says "Turn failed" although no turn failed.

Live repro (v504a, 160x45, Anthropic haiku through the proxy):
- ALPHA was sent, then BRAVO, CHARLIE and DELTA were queued. The shelf read 'Queue 3/10 · Draining · Next: BRAVO'.
- ALPHA completed and BRAVO was dispatched. Within about 3 s of BRAVO's durable commit, while BRAVO was still 'Generating…', the shelf switched to 'Queue 2/10 · Turn failed · Next: "Answer with the word CHARLIE."' with [Mana] [Retry]. The tab changed from Q3 to Q2, and the rail showed 'Prompt queue paus…'.
- BRAVO completed normally (log: controller_submit status=completed, no errors). More than 40 s later CHARLIE and DELTA had still not been dispatched. The tab read 'Q2' with no pause marker, and the header read 'Ready'.
- The FIRST Retry press showed the top-right toast 'No matching stopped or failed turn is available.' The finding says the first press did nothing; that part did not reproduce.
- Manage showed 'Queue 2/10 · paused · failed', a 0-based list, 13 buttons and no button labelled Resume. 'Paused' is disabled for this pause.

The only working recovery is 'Skip & resume'. Despite its label, it skips nothing: it resumes the queue and dispatches the head entry. Each press advances exactly one entry, then the queue pauses as 'failed' again as soon as that entry is accepted while others wait. After CHARLIE completed, the rail row showed a failure glyph although every turn succeeded.

The cause is not the one the finding cites. It is not the _SUCCESS/BLOCKED check at coordinator:636-643, because BRAVO's terminal status was COMPLETED. It is ConsolePromptQueueRegistry.settle_durable_acceptance (console_prompt_queue.py:1110-1113), which sets PAUSED/FAILED whenever an entry is still waiting. That call runs on every ordinary queued acceptance.
expected: The queue keeps draining after successful turns. If it pauses, it names the real reason and the turn involved, and the offered action (Resume or Retry) works.
why: The user believes their follow-up prompts are lined up. Instead they silently never run, under a failure label that is false, and the recovery button refuses. The user is left with no explanation and must re-send by hand.
repro: In one tab (slow proxy) press Enter on four prompts in quick succession (the first sends, the rest queue). Wait for the first two answers, then read the queue shelf, press Retry and open Manage.
recommendation: Pause with FAILED only when a turn's message actually failed, and store that message id on the pause so Retry always has a target. If the pause reason cannot be tied to a message, present 'Paused — Resume' instead. Add a plain Resume primary action, number the list from 1, group the 13 buttons (item actions / queue actions / recovery), and show the paused state on the tab (for example 'Q2 ⏸').
fix_direction:
In ConsolePromptQueueCoordinator.acknowledge_durable_acceptance, when a live chain owns this exact claim (chain is not None and chain.current_entry_id == entry_id), settle it without pausing: either through settle_claim or through a settle_durable_acceptance flag that skips the PAUSED/FAILED transition. Keep the FAILED pause only for the detached case the round1 tests pin (chain is None). Add a joined controller test that drives three queued entries through the real durable postcommit path and asserts that all of them run and the queue never pauses. As defence in depth:
- A claim_next refusal after a COMPLETED turn should not report a FAILED chain terminal.
- The shelf's Retry should fall back to a plain Resume when no failed message exists. Alternatively, store the failed message id on the pause.
- Rename 'Skip & resume' to 'Resume' (it skips nothing).
- Number the list from 1 and group the modal's buttons.
- Guard the modal's worker completion (_recover, _toggle_pause and the others) with an is_mounted check before calling _show_feedback/_apply_snapshot (see the crash in notes).

title: A refused raw-CLI command is 'restored' by appending, doubling it to '! git status --short! git status --short', and the composer offers 'Run' while raw CLI is unarmed
statement:
With raw_cli_permitted=true and nothing armed, typing '! git status --short' switches the composer to 'RAW CLI · HOST ACCESS' with an enabled primary 'Run' button. The SGR styling is identical to the armed state, so the composer never shows 'unarmed'.

Pressing ENTER refuses the command with 'Raw CLI is Unlocked but not armed for this launch. Arm it in Settings > Privacy & Security. The exact draft was restored.' That is false. The captured draft is prepended to the live draft, which is still in the composer, so the draft doubles. Each further Enter doubles it again: 1 copy, then 2, then 4. Clicking 'Run' with the mouse restores the draft verbatim, so the defect is on the Enter path only.

Raw CLI can be armed only in Settings > Privacy & Security, behind a disclosure modal. Terminal has an in-place 'Arm Terminal' button in Console. That asymmetry is real, but separate arms are deliberate (ADR-099, and the Settings card says 'Each feature still arms separately').

The claimed hazard, 'one arm-and-Enter away from running concatenated text', did NOT reproduce. After arming and pressing Enter on the doubled draft, the app refused with 'Raw CLI could not persist this command locally. The exact draft was restored.' and doubled the draft again, from 2 copies to 4. A separate defect masks the hazard for now.

Sibling symptom with the same root cause: a successful Enter-run leaves the command in the composer.
expected: A refused command is restored verbatim in place of the draft. When unarmed, the composer says 'Raw CLI not armed — Arm…' with an in-place arm action like the Terminal's, and doesn't offer 'Run'.
why: A corrupted command with host-user authority is one arm-and-Enter away from running concatenated text. Two arm locations for one unlock also break the mental model. This is the same append class as G1-37, but for host shell commands.
repro: With raw_cli_permitted=true and nothing armed, type '! git status --short' in the composer and press Enter.
recommendation: Replace the draft rather than append on restore, and add an idempotence test. Show the unarmed state in the composer, with an in-place arm that shares the Terminal disclosure, or make one arm cover both. Keep the button label 'Run' only when armed.

title: Prompt queue reports 'Turn failed' and pauses after a turn that succeeded, stranding the next queued prompt
statement:
Confirmed live on a clean isolated profile, and it is deterministic. In any persisted (non-Temporary) Console chat with two or more queued prompts, the queue drains at most one of them. When the first queued turn is durably accepted, the queue is paused with reason FAILED, and this happens while that turn is still generating. The shelf reads "Queue 1/10 · Turn failed · Next: <prompt>" with Mana/Retry, and the modal reads "Queue 1/10 · paused · failed". The next prompt is kept in the queue (not lost), but it never sends.

The cause is not the turn's outcome and not a capture or retrieval error. `ConsolePromptQueueRegistry.settle_durable_acceptance` sets mode=PAUSED, pause_reason=FAILED and reservation=RELEASED whenever `state.waiting` is non-empty (tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_prompt_queue.py:1110-1113). The live postcommit `queue_acknowledgement` effect calls it for every queued turn (console_chat_controller.py:12439-12456 → console_prompt_queue_coordinator.py:529-576 `acknowledge_durable_acceptance`). After the turn completes, `_drain_waiting`'s `claim_next` is refused because the mode is no longer DRAINING. `_pause_after_exception` then re-pauses the queue as FAILED.

Recovery makes it worse. The shelf's primary "Retry" button and the modal's "Retry failed" both dead-end with "No matching stopped or failed turn is available.", because no turn actually failed. Only "Skip & resume", whose label suggests it discards something, sends the next prompt.

The modal claims are all confirmed: 13 buttons in 3 rows. 7 are disabled with no reason given (Save, Up, Down, Paused, Review, Use current, Retry stopped). "Paused" is a disabled button used as a status (label and disabled flag at console_prompt_queue_modal.py:252-264). Rows are numbered from 0 (`f"{entry.position}. …"` at :311, positions come from enumerate at console_prompt_queue.py:480). The row text is centred, with "Waiting" at the far edge.
expected: The queue keeps draining after successful turns. A real failure names the turn and its cause. The modal shows only the actions that apply, gives disabled ones a reason, and numbers items from 1.
why: Queued work silently stops on a false failure. The user must notice, open the modal and guess which of 13 controls resumes it.
repro: curl …/_mode/<name>/slow → send prompt → immediately queue 2 more → wait for both replies → read the queue shelf → Manage.
recommendation: Derive the queue's turn outcome from the controller's terminal status for that turn, not from an auxiliary signal such as capture or retrieval errors. Show 1-based positions. Collapse the modal to its context-relevant actions (Resume/Pause, Edit, Reorder, Remove) and give each disabled control a text reason. Show the queue state as text, not as a disabled button.
fix_direction:
Scope the pause-on-settle in settle_durable_acceptance to the detached case: pause FAILED only when no live chain owns the session. On the live path (coordinator has a chain for the session and chain.current_entry_id == entry_id), settle the claim and keep mode DRAINING and the reservation HELD. Equivalently, acknowledge_durable_acceptance could call a non-pausing settle when a live chain matches. Add a regression test that runs a real durable path with a live chain and ≥2 queued entries and asserts that all of them drain.

Separately, only show 'Retry' when a failed assistant message actually exists; otherwise offer Resume. Fix the modal: number rows from 1 (entry.position + 1); left-align the preview; show queue state as text rather than a disabled 'Paused' button; hide or explain inapplicable actions (Save outside edit mode, Retry stopped when nothing stopped, Review/Use current when the context is unchanged); and rename 'Skip & resume' so it does not suggest discarding the next prompt.

The finding's recommendation to stop deriving the outcome from 'capture or retrieval errors' points at the wrong cause. The coordinator already reads the controller's terminal status, which is COMPLETED here.

title: Staged-evidence strip goes stale after send and leaks into new tabs and workspaces, contradicting the Sources chip and the Inspect card
statement:
Confirmed as filed, with three additions and one correction to the root cause.

What reproduced live (two independent runs, Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5, 235x52):
- A manual Library search stages 1 source. The strip reads 'Staged for next send · 1 source · Un-stage', the chip reads 'Sources: 1' and Inspect reads 'Sources: 1 staged'.
- The next send consumes it: the reply cites [S1], the chip drops to 'Sources: 0', Inspect's 'What happens if I send now?' card says 'Sources: None staged', and the Inspect Run card says 'sources sent with the last message · 1 source'.
- The strip keeps saying 'Staged for next send · 1 source · Un-stage', still after 20 s and after further sourceless sends.
- Clicking Un-stage removes nothing, because nothing is staged. It only resyncs the strip, which then shows 'Evidence sent with this message · 1 source'.
- That notice is never cleared. It stays after a sourceless turn ('Say hi in 3 words.' -> 'Hi there, friend.'), in a brand-new Ctrl+T tab showing 'No messages yet.', after that tab's own sourceless turn, and in a newly entered workspace chat.

Additions:
1. Inspect contradicts itself, not just the strip. Next to 'Sources: None staged' it keeps showing a stale 'Sources — next send 1 · Ready · Seed note...' card, or after Un-stage a 'Live work sources ... Status: staged' card with the old query and result_id. The Run card's 'sources sent with the last message · 1 source' also persists after sourceless sends and in empty new chats.
2. The leak into a workspace chat does not need Un-stage. The stale 'Staged for next send · 1 source' form also carried into 'Workspace 1 › Workspace 1 Chat'.
3. The stale 'Staged for next send' promise is false going forward: the next send carries no source (chip 0; the model answered 'No.' when asked whether any source was attached).

Correction to the root cause: the heading strings at console_display_state.py:1214 and 1223 are correct. The bug is how the runtime owns and wires this state:
- Staged evidence and its sent-notice are one value for the whole app on ConsoleRuntime, not one per session.
- The runtime's release path refreshes no view.
- Custodied sends never clear the notice.
- The prior-art explanation (TASK-2372 moving it into screen-level serialized state) is out of date: the state moved into ConsoleRuntime in commit b7dd8e53f2.
expected: Staged evidence belongs to one draft in one session. After send it becomes a per-message 'Sources (n)' affordance on that turn and disappears from the composer area. New tabs and workspaces start clean.
why: For a researcher, 'which sources did this answer use' is the key trust question. The strip claims sources went with messages that had none, and it persists into unrelated contexts.
repro: Search Library ▸ query ▸ Enter. Wait for 'Staged for next send'. Send a message and compare the strip with 'Sources: 0' and the Inspect card. Click Un-stage. Press Ctrl+T for a new tab: the strip is still there.
recommendation:
1. Scope the pending launch and the sent-evidence notice to (session_id, message_id).
2. Clear the composer strip on send, then render the evidence on that assistant turn as a 'Sources (1)' button that opens the citation/sources modal.
3. Reset the strip and Inspect 'Live work sources' on session, tab and workspace switch.
fix_direction:
1. Key the staged launch and sent_source_count by session_id in ConsoleRuntime, and project only the active session's value. At minimum, clear the sent-notice and resync the strip and live-work card on session, tab and workspace switch.
2. After a successful release, notify the view: add a runtime hook that calls the screen's _sync_console_pending_launch_surfaces, the same as _release_consumed_console_launch does.
3. Clear sent_source_count when a new turn is admitted, inside accept_turn or _run_custodied_turn, so a sourceless turn cannot inherit the previous receipt. Alternatively, make the receipt carry the turn_id it belongs to and render it only for that turn.
4. Move the post-send claim off the composer strip onto the assistant turn as a 'Sources (N)' affordance. For persisted conversations, derive it from the stored message.
5. Make Un-stage on a stale strip resync and hide itself instead of converting into a permanent notice.
6. Add a regression test for each path: send with staged evidence; assert the strip is hidden or shows the sent-notice for that turn only; send again with nothing staged; assert the strip is hidden; open a new tab or workspace chat; assert the strip and Inspect are clean.

title: Automatic Library retrieval runs on every send, but its outcome is invisible even when it finds nothing or fails
statement:
Core claim confirmed live: with Library set to Automatic, a send whose automatic Library search returns 0 matches shows nothing on the turn. The chip still reads 'Library · Auto on', 'Sources: 0' does not change, and the Library access modal has no empty-Library hint.

This is a regression. The controller persists a bounded library_preparation sidecar ({"outcome":"zero_matches"}) on the USER message, and the rows are in the DB. No UI code ever projects that sidecar, so the promised '0 matches · sent without Library evidence' disclosure (TASK-19900.3 AC#6/#7, spec section 6.4) is missing. It is missing live and after a restart. Nothing on screen tells a zero-match turn apart from any other turn: the UI never reads preparation outcomes, so a successful retrieval is not disclosed on the turn either.

Three details in the finding are wrong:
1. capture_provider_failure is not an automatic-retrieval failure. It is logged by _capture_rag_context, the capture of manually staged evidence, which runs after a zero-match automatic search (and with Auto off, see G2-37). It is also not invisible: the Trace view (Y) shows 'Retrieval started -> Retrieval failed' for every such turn, a false failure. The actual 0-match result appears nowhere.
2. 'The Library was empty' was not established in J4. The keyword leg of the manual search found 1 result; only the vector store had 0 documents.
3. The J4 reply was grounded in note text pasted into the conversation. More accurately, nothing distinguishes a zero-match turn.

A real retrieval failure is not silent, and it is worse than the finding describes. The first Automatic send after every app launch hits the 5 s library_preparation_timeout while the RAG service cold-initialises (about 4-5 s even with the embedding model cached). The turn pauses and shows only 'Queue 0/10 · Unsent turn needs attention · Restore / Discard'. Inspect says 'Run: Ready', and no reason is shown. There is no Retry, no 'Send once without Library' and no Cancel for a RETRIEVAL pause: nothing in the UI calls bypass_library_preparation. Every later send in that conversation is refused at controller_submit. This holds after Discard and after switching the policy to Never. The refusal copy is 'Another send is still preparing for this conversation.', and it is not displayed anywhere. This deserves its own, higher-severity finding.
expected: Every turn with auto retrieval on carries a compact line on the turn, such as 'Library: searched · 0 matches' or 'Library: search failed — Retry'. The chip warns when the Library is empty ('Auto on · Library empty').
why: A student relying on 'answers grounded in my sources' cannot tell a grounded answer from an ungrounded one. A silent capture failure is the kind of hidden status that PRODUCT.md rules out.
repro: Status ▸ 'Library · Auto off' ▸ Automatic ▸ Save. Send a question. Compare the transcript with the log lines 'Performing hybrid search… found 0 results' and 'RAG capture unavailable'.
recommendation: Render a per-turn retrieval receipt on the assistant turn (searched / n matches / failed + Retry), driven by the same state that decides whether sources were attached. Add an empty-Library hint to the Library-access modal and the chip. The same capture_provider_failure also produces a false Trace failure with auto-retrieval off (see G2-37); fix the shared cause once.

title: Extends G1-14: with real Library hits, answers carry [S1] markers but no 'Cited sources' row ever appears, so citations cannot be traced to a source
statement:
Confirmed live on dev 64579cce2c: answers that cite [Sn] never get a 'Cited sources (n)' row, and every rag_citation_* table stays at 0. This holds for manually staged Library evidence (Search Library, Enter, send) and for Automatic retrieval. The row never appeared, even after selecting the reply and waiting 20 s, so the Sources modal cannot be reached. The mechanism is not TASK-22302: that fix landed in 3daa56bf4f (Aug 26, an ancestor of HEAD), and only its task file still says To Do. In a default install:
(a) The staged path cannot persist, because canonical citation writes ship disabled. config.py:5366-5367 sets [rag_citations] canonical_writes_enabled = false and the getter is fail-closed, so create_local_trace_builder returns None, no finalizer is built, and no trace is written. No UI exposes this switch, yet the User Guide (context-and-rag.md:877-882) promises a 'Sources (N)' button whenever a reply is grounded.
(b) The Automatic/prepared-bundle path never creates a CitationTraceBuilder, whatever the flag says (console_chat_controller.py:10793-10799 and 10918-10922). It still sends the explicit '[Citation instructions] ... Cite each evidence-supported claim ... for example [S1]' block from answer_citations.py:182-190.
S-labels are numbered per reply and never shown to the user. In the staged turn S1=zephyr-irrigation, S2=quillmere-battery, S3=copper-lantern. In the Auto turn S1=quillmere-battery, S2=zephyr-irrigation. Both answers cite correctly within their own turn, but the same [S1] means different documents across turns and nothing shows the user a key. Staged chips, the Inspector 'Sources - next send' rows and the bottom strip carry no S-ordinals.
Corrections to the finding's evidence: on the manual staged path the model gets only evidence labelled 'Evidence: [S1] MEDIA - title ...', with no citation instructions. The answer_citations.py citation applies to the Auto path. The modal's bare 'Sources unavailable' (console_citation_sources_modal.py:356-363) is confirmed from code only; it cannot be reached live.
expected: Any answer that uses [Sn] labels has a clickable Sources affordance. It lists S1…Sn with the document title, the snippet and 'Open in Library'. Staged chips show their S-label before send.
why: Grounded answers with unverifiable citations undermine the core source-authority promise, and they look more trustworthy than they are.
repro: Library ▸ Import three files → Console ▸ Search Library → query → Enter (stages evidence) → ask a question that says 'cite sources' → select the reply.
recommendation: Persist a citation trace for staged-evidence and auto-retrieval sends, the same way the RAG-answer path does. Alternatively, do not ask the model for [Sn] labels when no trace will be kept. Label the staged chips 'S1 zephyr-irrigation (media)'. In the Sources modal, replace 'Sources unavailable' with the reason and a next step.
fix_direction:
1) Decide the contract. Either enable canonical citation writes by default, provisioning the fingerprint key on first use per TASK-553.17, or, when writes are off or no builder exists, render an in-session, non-persisted 'Sources (n)' affordance from the in-memory evidence bundle (S-ordinal, title, snippet, Open in Library).
2) Give the Automatic/prepared-bundle branch a CitationTraceBuilder, as the staged branch has, so it can persist.
3) When no trace or affordance will exist, do not send '[Citation instructions]' asking for [Sn], or annotate the markers as unverifiable.
4) Show the S-ordinal a source will receive on staged chips and Inspector source rows, and state that labels are per reply.
5) In the Sources modal, replace the bare 'Sources unavailable' with the cause (writes disabled / trace missing / hydration failed) and a next step.
6) Housekeeping: mark TASK-22302 Done or annotate it; file new tasks for the default-off gap, the Auto-path builder, chip S-labels, conditional citation prompting and the modal error. Align the User Guide wording ('Sources (N)' vs 'Cited sources (N)') and document the opt-in.

title: Provider 429/500/504 failures are replaced by a false 'Trace capture blocked — The provider was not contacted' callout; the real cause never appears
statement: Confirmed live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c (Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5, default capture on, 160x45). When the provider returns a transient error (reproduced with 504 and 429; the prior L3 log shows the same for 500), the send ends in the warning callout 'Trace capture blocked / Problem: Trace capture could not be saved. / Impact: The provider was not contacted.' The provider was in fact contacted: the review proxy logged exactly one POST per send, answered 504 or 429. The mechanism is the agent's in-place transient retry (TASK-25901). Its second call is reserved as a TOOL_LOOP continuation. console_trace_runtime.py:497 then refuses it with trace_tool_chain_unavailable, because the previous call never reached RESPONSE_STARTED or COMPLETE. The resulting TraceCallPersistenceError pauses the preparation as TRACE_CALL. 'Not contacted' is literally true only for the blocked retry, never for the send the user made. On the primary surfaces the real cause does not appear: the transcript shows a blank Assistant row, the status strip says 'Agent blocked', no toast appears in 1 s captures from t2 to t17, and the Inspector says 'Run: Ready', 'Provider: ready' and 'Ready to send'. It shows up only in the trace view: press Y, then j/i to open event details. There the user finds 'Model request failed; retry 1 of 2 in 0.78s (ChatProviderError)', a bare 'Model request failed', and 'unexpected provider error (Provider call trace persistence failed.)'. That last event mislabels the trace failure as a provider error. The HTTP status and the words rate-limit or timeout appear nowhere in the UI. By contrast, a non-retried 401 surfaces as 'Response failed' plus 'Agent run failed: provider returned HTTP 401'. A consequence the finding misses: with capture on (the default), the TASK-25901 retry never reaches the provider, so even a one-off blip that a retry would have fixed becomes this misleading callout.
expected: The primary provider failure outranks any secondary bookkeeping failure, e.g. 'Anthropic rate-limited this request (HTTP 429). Nothing was generated. Wait and retry, or switch model.' Any trace-capture problem appears as a separate note. The Impact line states only facts the error object carries, and never says 'not contacted' after provider_entry was reached.
why: A user who hits a rate limit or an outage is told that local trace storage is broken and nothing was sent. They then try capture actions that cannot help and that lead into G4-05. They cannot tell whether to wait, change provider or fix their disk without reading logs.
repro: launch.sh l3 160 45 ready; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/_mode/<name>/504 (or 429, 500); send a message ('Name one colour.'); wait 15 s.
recommendation: (1) When a provider error has already been recorded for the attempt, surface it as the terminal failure: a failed row plus a recovery callout naming the status and category. Skip the follow-on trace reservation, or demote its failure to a secondary note. (2) Add a provider_contacted field (yes/no/unknown) to TraceCallPersistenceError, set at the raise site, and render the Impact line from it. (3) Add a regression test that drives 429/500/504 through the agent path and asserts the visible copy names the HTTP status.
fix_direction: (1) Precedence: when the attempt already has a recorded provider error (status or category), make that the terminal failure. Show a failed Assistant row plus a recovery callout naming the provider, status and meaning, e.g. 'Anthropic rate-limited this request (HTTP 429). Nothing was generated. Wait and retry, or switch model.' Any trace problem becomes a secondary note. (2) Root-cause the retry/trace incompatibility. An in-place transient retry should reserve as a retry of the same logical call (or be exempt from the TOOL_LOOP chain invariant), not as a tool-loop continuation that requires a response-bearing predecessor. Otherwise TASK-25901's retry never runs whenever capture is on. (3) Add a provider_contacted field (yes/no/unknown) to TraceCallPersistenceError, or pass the first attempt's outcome to the callout, and derive the Impact line from it. (4) Make the Inspector run summary reflect a blocked or failed run instead of 'Run: Ready'. Stop labelling the trace-persistence failure as 'unexpected provider error' in the trace view. (5) Add a regression test that drives 429, 500 and 504 through the agent path with capture on. It should assert that the visible copy names the HTTP status and never claims 'not contacted' after provider_entry.
