title: Trace-blocked recovery dead-ends: 'Cancel send' refuses, and Retry capture / Send without capture open a false 'delivery status is unknown on the source device' duplicate-request warning
statement:
I reproduced this live on dev @ 64579cce2c, once in a clean relaunch and once in an earlier v128a session. The first provider call gets HTTP 429 or 500. The agent then retries, and the retry's trace reservation fails before dispatch (ValueError trace_tool_chain_unavailable, reservation_status "unknown"). That produces the 'Trace capture blocked' card, which says 'Impact: The provider was not contacted.' This is false: the provider did answer, with the 429 or 500.

- **Cancel send never cancels.** After both 429 and 500, the card's status line changes to 'Trace reservation status is unavailable.' and the card stays, even after repeated clicks.
- **Send without capture and Retry capture do nothing useful.** With the proxy back on normal, neither makes a provider call: no POST in proxy.log and no send-stage lines in the app log. Each click shows 'Working…' for about 1 s. The card is then replaced by a panel above the composer: 'Response delivery status is unknown on the source device. / Retry anyway may send a duplicate request because delivery status is unknown. [Retry anyway] [Discard]'.
- **The status indicators disagree.** The composer says 'Send blocked — resolve response recovery first', the rail says 'Blocked' and the Inspect handle says 'blocked'. The header chip still says 'Ready', although it is designed to show 'blocked' too (console_workbench_state.py computes running/blocked/ready).
- **Delivery status is actually known.** The only POST was the rejected 429 or 500, and the retry call never left the app. The session is local. The 'source device' sentence comes from the local-checkpoint path (console_chat_models.py:695), with the same text as console_dispatch_repository.py:715 and assistant_generation_state.py:25.
- **Retry anyway works but gives no acknowledgement.** The button row stayed byte-identical, ANSI included, for 4.2 s. The POST went out about 1.5 s after the click, and the panel vanished when the reply arrived at about 4.6 s. The earlier session measured about 5 s.

Two refinements to the finding:
- 'Dead-end' overstates it slightly. Retry anyway does get a reply, and Discard settles the turn. Cancel is the only real dead end; the other paths are misleading and frightening rather than broken.
- The recommended rule, 'skip the panel if provider_entry was never entered', would not catch this case. provider_entry WAS entered for the first call, which got the 429/500. The rule needs to use the definitive HTTP error outcome of the failed call, together with the fact that the retry call never crossed dispatch.
expected: Cancel always works: it discards the pending turn and restores the draft even when the reservation state is unknown. 'Send without capture' dispatches and 'Retry capture' re-runs capture or shows the capture error again. Duplicate-delivery warnings appear only when a request may actually have reached the provider, in plain language without 'source device'. Local copy states the known outcome, e.g. 'The provider rejected this request (HTTP 429); nothing was generated. Retry or discard.'
why: The one escape hatch fails, and the other actions produce a scarier panel warning about duplicate charges that contradicts the previous claim ('provider was not contacted'). Users are pushed toward Discard and lose the turn. Three successive panels make three different claims about the same send.
repro: Reach the Trace capture blocked card (G4-04 or G4-10). Click 'Cancel send', then 'Send without capture' or 'Retry capture', then 'Retry anyway' with the proxy back on normal.
recommendation: Derive the delivery state from the send-stage ledger: if provider_entry was never entered, skip the unknown-delivery panel and re-run capture. Make cancel unconditional from the user's side by marking an unknown reservation abandoned locally and settling it later. Split the dispatch-recovery copy into local and remote variants. Show 'We can't tell whether the provider received this request. Retrying might send it twice.' only when that is true. Add an immediate 'Retrying…' busy state, as TraceCallRecoveryCallout already does with 'Working…'.
fix_direction:
- **Record the failed call's outcome.** When the call that crossed provider_entry got a definitive HTTP rejection (4xx/429/5xx), store that as 'provider rejected'. When the retry's boundary construction failed pre-dispatch, store that as 'not dispatched'. Use these instead of reservation_status 'unknown'.
- **Show honest copy.** The trace card should state the actual outcome ('The provider rejected this request (HTTP 429); nothing was generated.'). Suppress the unknown-delivery panel when both facts are known.
- **Make Cancel always work for the user.** Mark an unknown reservation abandoned locally, settle it later, and restore the draft.
- **Make Retry capture re-run capture**, or re-show the capture error, instead of routing to dispatch recovery.
- **Split the dispatch-recovery copy into local and remote variants.** Use 'source device' only for remote/import handoffs.
- **Give Retry anyway an immediate busy state** ('Retrying…', buttons disabled), matching TraceCallRecoveryCallout's 'Working…'.
- **Derive the header status chip from run state**, so it shows 'blocked' whenever the rail and composer do.

title: Root cause of the misattributed errors: fixed sentences keyed on a coarse enum or on substring matches assert facts the underlying state does not carry
statement:
The root cause is real. Console recovery copy comes from a coarse category, a status code, or a substring match on free text, and the fact that would tell the cases apart (provider body, phase, whether the provider was reached, which subsystem blocked) is dropped or kept only in the log. Reproduced live on origin/dev 64579cce2c:
(h) Doubled wrapper copy: "Agent run failed: provider returned HTTP 401 (Provider error from anthropic: authentication failed. Status: 401.)".
(b) The image hint is appended to that 401 auth failure ("This conversation includes an image attachment; if the model can't accept images, remove that message…") even though the same model had just read the image correctly ("Red.").
(c) After a provider HTTP 500, the "Trace capture blocked" panel says "Impact: The provider was not contacted." The proxy log shows the POST at 17:23:57, and the app log shows provider_entry followed by "Handler for anthropic directly raised; status=500".
(g) A false "setup" badge shows on the closed Inspect rail handle during every ordinary running send, and the pinned line reads "Run: Blocked". Mechanism: while a run is active, readiness returns blocker active_run, so provider_ready is False, the Provider row gets status "blocked", and the "provider" and "blocked" substrings then produce the "setup" badge.
(f) New instance: staging an image with the default claude-haiku-4-5 (a model is selected) shows "Send blocked — choose a model to continue". The underlying reason is "claude-haiku-4-5 can't accept images…"; it rides the setup slot and matches the "model" substring.
(a) is confirmed in code: any 400 gets the "Confirm the model is still available" sentence. The lead's P0 capture shows it on a tool-schema 400.
(d) and (e) are confirmed in code only. The local checkpoint uses "on the source device", and active_run maps to "Provider setup needed: current run is active".
Correction to (f): an unmatched non-empty reason falls back to "Send blocked — finish provider setup to continue". Only an empty reason gets "wait for the active run to finish". So the queue-full and pre-acceptance tooltips (prompt_queue.py:132/136) would read as provider setup.
expected: Recovery copy is rendered from a structured, privacy-safe evidence record. Each sentence depends on a field actually being known, and 'unknown' is stated plainly.
why: Fixing instances one at a time will not hold: each new failure mode reuses the nearest template and asserts something false.
repro: See G4-01, G4-04, G4-05, G4-08; plus uxrev/evidence/L3/15-provider-401.txt.
recommendation: Introduce one ConsoleFailureEvidence value with these fields: phase (prepare/dispatch/response/settle), provider_contacted (yes/no/unknown), http_status, category, a sanitized provider_message (credential-redacted, 240 chars; already implemented in _provider_error_body_detail), origin (local/remote) and blocker_code. Carry it from the gateway, trace runtime and readiness to the UI, and render every callout, failure row, disabled reason and rail badge from it. Remove all substring matching on display copy. Add hints only when they apply: the image hint only for a 400/415 whose body mentions image/vision, and the model hint only for 404/model_not_found.
fix_direction:
Adopt the finding's recommendation: one structured, privacy-safe failure/blocker evidence value with phase, provider_contacted (yes/no/unknown), http_status, category, a sanitized provider_message (reuse provider_failures._provider_error_body_detail), origin (local/remote) and blocker_code, carried from the gateway, trace runtime, readiness, queue and attachment gates to the UI. Render the system row, run state, disabled reason, readiness summary and rail badge from that record's fields, never by substring-matching display copy. Specific consequences:
- Stop treating active_run as a provider-readiness blocker for the Provider row and badge.
- Give attachment, queue and wake blockers their own codes instead of the setup slot.
- Show the image hint only when the status is 400/413/415/422 and the body mentions image or vision content.
- Show the model hint only for 404/model_not_found.
- Emit a single wrapper so copy is not doubled.
- Derive the trace-panel impact line from provider_contacted.
Reconcile with TASK-19642.8.7, which wants failure rows to keep the image hint, and with TASK-2543/32369/33005.2. Separately, file the claude-haiku-4-5 vision capability gap (model_capabilities.py:44-48).

title: Attaching an image with the default claude-haiku-4-5 shows 'Send blocked — choose a model to continue', and the › link opens first-run setup
statement:
In ready mode with Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 selected, staging an image (leaf.png) makes the composer strip read 'leaf.png - 116 B  Send blocked - choose a model to continue >', even though the status bar says 'Model: claude-haiku-4-5'. The app log says 'No capability information found for anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5, using defaults'.

Cause: the vision table covers claude-3*, *opus-4* and *sonnet-4*, plus a direct entry for claude-sonnet-5. This is true both of the code defaults (model_capabilities.py:44-48) and of the shipped config template (config.py:5494-5503). The table misses claude-haiku-4-5, and also claude-opus-5 and claude-fable-5 from the same shipped Anthropic model list (config.py:4288).

Haiku 4.5 does accept images. A live probe through the review proxy returned 'Green' for the 32x32 green PNG (msg_011CfYgJEQuJ1LvoojH8XhRt, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001).

How the wrong copy and link appear: vision_block_reason's accurate copy travels in the setup_blocked_reason slot. build_console_disabled_reason matches the substring 'model' and rewrites it to 'Send blocked - choose a model to continue'. The console-composer-setup-blocked class then turns the whole strip into an app.run_setup_wizard link. Clicking it opens the full-screen 'Set up tldw chatbook' wizard at Step 1 (Welcome).

Corrections to the finding's details:
(1) The accurate copy is reachable. Hovering the Send button shows it as a tooltip ('Console send blocked: claude-haiku-4-5 can't accept images. Remove the attachment, switch to a vision model, or mark this model as vision-capable under [model_capabilities.models] in config.toml.'). Pressing Enter with a draft adds a transcript System row with the same text. Only the strip itself has no tooltip.
(2) The wizard is a wrong-destination detour, not a dead end. Esc shows 'Skip setup? Skip setup and stop showing it at launch?' with Keep going focused. Enter or a second Esc only dismisses that dialog (the wizard never closed, so nothing 'reopened'). Tab then Enter on Skip setup returns to Console with the draft and attachment intact and config.toml unchanged.
(3) claude-haiku-4-5 is the review harness's configured model, not the product default. The shipped Console default is OpenAI gpt-5.6-terra and the shipped Anthropic default is claude-sonnet-5, and both classify as vision-capable. Even so, Haiku 4.5, Opus 5 and Fable 5 are all listed models that cannot send images.
expected: Haiku 4.5 accepts images. If a model genuinely cannot, the message says '<model> can't read images — remove the image or switch to a vision model' with Remove and Switch model actions, and never sends the user to first-run setup.
why: The default configured model blocks image grounding. The message blames the wrong thing, and its recovery link drops a user who has already set up into onboarding, a dead end that looks broken.
repro: ready mode: Composer ▸ Menu ▸ Attach file ▸ pick a .png under HOME; read the strip; click the › line.
recommendation: (1) Add Haiku 4.x and the 5-series to the vision table, or derive vision support from the provider catalog. (2) Give attachment blocks their own slot and render attachment_core's precise copy, with 'Remove image' and 'Switch model' actions next to the chip. (3) Point the › link at the specific fix (the model picker), never at the first-run wizard.
fix_direction:
1. Fix the capability data.
   - Add Haiku 4.x and the 5-series (opus-5, fable-5) to the Anthropic vision patterns, in both DEFAULT_MODEL_PATTERNS and the config template. A family rule would be better, e.g. reuse _ANTHROPIC_FAMILY_RE: every tier-first-named Claude family with major >= 4 accepts images.
   - Pin it with a test that iterates the shipped Anthropic model list.
   - Existing user config.toml files carry a copy of the old patterns block, which replaces the defaults wholesale. Either merge the defaults under user entries or migrate the block.
2. Give attachment blocks their own slot or flag in sync_action_state.
   - Stop them riding setup_blocked_reason, so neither the 'model' substring classifier nor the setup-wizard link applies.
   - Render compact strip copy from vision_block_reason (e.g. '<model> can't read images'), with Remove-image and Switch-model affordances next to the attachment chip.
3. Keep the run_setup_wizard link strictly for genuine readiness blockers.
   - Point a model-related fix at the Console model picker, not the first-run wizard.
   - Test build_console_disabled_reason with the verbatim vision_block_reason string, per the TASK-2154.12 lesson.

title: After 'Edit & resend', every later send in that chat stops at a 'Trace capture blocked' card that never names the cause
statement: Confirmed as written, and the scope is narrower than the repro wording suggests. The trigger is Edit & resend specifically. An in-place edit with Save followed by a send captured normally, and a control chat with 5 plain sends never showed the card. After Edit & resend on the last user message, every later send in that chat fails trace reservation (error_category=unsupported_surface_change, ValueError) before the provider is contacted. It stops at the generic 'Trace capture blocked' card, which has no cause copy and no per-chat 'don't ask again' option. Of the card's three actions, only 'Send without capture' works, and it has to be chosen again on every send. 'Retry capture' opens a 'Response delivery status is unknown ... Retry anyway may send a duplicate request' panel, even though the provider was never contacted. 'Cancel send' does not dismiss the card and just shows 'Trace reservation status is unavailable.' The card's 'Impact: The provider was not contacted.' is accurate on this path.
expected: Branching with Edit & resend leaves trace capture working. If capture genuinely fails, the card names the cause and offers a 'don't ask again for this chat' option.
why: An ordinary editing action silently turns the chat into one that needs an extra click on every send, with no explanation.
repro: ready 120x40 fresh; send 2–3 messages; select a user message (click a role label, k), e, edit, Edit & resend; then send any new message.
recommendation: Fix trace reservation for branched lineages (unsupported_surface_change). Until then, map that error category to specific copy ('Trace capture doesn't support edited branches yet — sending without a trace') and remember the choice per conversation. Add a test that edits and resends, then sends, and expects no decision card.
fix_direction: Root fix: route Edit & resend through the same trace-call reservation as a normal send, so the edit appends a replacement record and advances the surface as the user guide promises. That needs an ADR-097 amendment, like the TASK-32048 and TASK-32075 precedents. Stopgap: map unsupported_surface_change to cause-specific copy ('Trace capture can't follow this edited branch yet'), offer 'Send without capture for this chat', and remember that choice per conversation. Also fix the two recovery buttons that don't work: Cancel send must be able to cancel a send whose reservation failed before dispatch, and Retry capture must not escalate to a 'delivery status unknown / duplicate request' panel when the provider was never contacted. Add a regression test that sends, does Edit & resend, sends again, and expects no decision card and a succeeded trace_reservation.

title: Ctrl+Q quits without warning, losing the Temporary chat, per-tab drafts and the parked unsent turn
statement:
Confirmed on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. I had a Temporary chat with a reply ('OK temporary', status chip 'Temporary - not saved'), a saved chat with the unsent composer draft 'draft alpha unsent do not lose', and an 'Unsent turn needs attention' shelf in the Temporary tab. Pressing Ctrl+Q showed no dialog and the Textual UI was gone within 0.5 s. The log shows 'Application quit initiated' and then the screen unmounting in the same second. After relaunching with REUSE=1, open tabs were not restored, the Temporary chat was gone from the rail and the DB, and the reopened saved chat had its messages but an empty composer. The DB holds only the saved conversation's two messages.

The same session shows the asymmetry. Clicking the close button on the Temporary tab raised 'Close Console session?' with 'Temporary or unsaved messages: 2'. Clicking it on the drafted tab raised the same dialog with 'Unsent draft: yes'. Both offer Stay.

Two precision fixes to the finding:
1. The parked unsent turn (ConsoleRuntime._turn_recoveries, memory only) is counted by neither the quit guard nor the tab-close impact (ConsoleSessionCloseImpact has no recovery field). 'Use the same loss model as tab close' would therefore still miss parked turns, so the shared loss model must add them explicitly. In my repro the parked turn duplicated a message I then sent with 'Send without capture', so nothing unique was lost there. In J3 it held a genuinely unsent, refused send ('Can I send here').
2. Pending attachments are also left out of the quit guard (code-confirmed, not driven live).
expected: Quit uses the same loss model as tab close: it lists Temporary chats, unsent drafts and parked unsent turns and offers 'Stay'. Alternatively, drafts are persisted and offered for restore on the next launch.
why: User work is lost silently. The Temporary chip says 'not saved', not 'lost on quit without warning'.
repro: Open a Temporary tab and send; type a draft in another tab without sending; press Ctrl+Q (exits immediately); relaunch with REUSE=1 and open the drafted chat: the composer is empty and the Temporary chat is gone.
recommendation: Extract one ConsoleLossImpact (temporary/unsaved messages, drafts, attachments, parked unsent turns, live runs, delegates, queued prompts) used by both tab close and quit, and show it once at quit, summed per tab. Better still, persist per-conversation drafts and parked turns so only Temporary content is actually at risk.
fix_direction:
Extract one fleet-wide loss projection that sums, per open session, everything below. Use it both for per-tab close (filtered to one session) and for quit and fleet leave (summed), so the two dialogs cannot drift apart again.
- unsaved transcript messages (persisted_message_id is None, which covers Temporary chats)
- non-empty drafts, including the live composer text of the visible session
- pending attachments
- parked turn recoveries (runtime.recoveries_for_session)
- the existing live, queued and delegated counts

Name the Temporary chats and drafted tabs in the quit dialog, and offer Stay. Separately, and better for H5, persist per-conversation drafts and parked turns for saved conversations so that only Temporary content is truly at risk. Also add turn recoveries to the tab-close impact, which misses them today. Keep the revision-pinned re-check loop in _confirm_console_runtime_quit.

title: Extends G4-11: the quit confirmation lists live runs but shows zeros for the unsent work it is about to discard
statement:
Confirmed, and the problem is worse than reported. The Ctrl+Q guard (ConsoleLifecycleImpact) counts only four things: live runs, delegated agents, sessions with queued prompts and queued prompts. It never counts composer drafts, pending attachments, Temporary-chat messages or parked 'Unsent turn needs attention' recoveries, and all of these are thrown away on quit.

(a) When a run is live, the dialog is titled 'Quitting Chatbook will cancel or discard:' and reads 'Live agent runs: 1 / Delegated agents: 0 / Sessions with queued prompts: 0 / Unsent queued prompts: 0'. At that moment another tab held an unsent draft and a Temporary chat held a parked unsent turn. After Quit and a relaunch, both were gone.

(b) Worse: when no run is live and nothing is queued, Ctrl+Q shows no dialog at all. The app exits within about a second and silently discards drafts, Temporary chats and parked turns.

This is also inconsistent with the Console's own tab-close guard. Closing one tab lists 'Unsent draft: yes', 'Temporary or unsaved messages: N' and 'Pending attachments: N'. Quitting closes every tab and asks nothing about any of these.

One correction to the finding: 'no tabs were restored' is not data loss for saved conversations. They stay reachable in the Chats rail after relaunch. Open tabs not being restored is by design (ADR-033:184). The real losses are drafts, Temporary chats and parked unsent turns.
expected: The inventory should count everything that will be lost (drafts, parked unsent turns, Temporary chats, open tabs) or offer to keep them, and the zeros should not suggest nothing is at risk.
why: The dialog is the last chance to save work, and its zeros actively reassure the user as the work is discarded.
repro: Open many tabs, leave a draft and a parked unsent turn, have one run live, press Ctrl+Q, read the dialog, quit, relaunch with REUSE=1.
recommendation: Always show the quit guard when any draft, parked turn or Temporary chat exists, and count them ('Unsent drafts: 1 (1.2 MB) · Parked turns: 1 · Open tabs: 26 — will not be restored'). Offer [Keep tabs for next launch] alongside Stay/Quit, and persist drafts per tab.
fix_direction:
Extend the quit (and fleet) impact with the per-session fields the tab-close guard already computes, summed across all live sessions:
- sessions with an unsent draft
- pending attachments
- Temporary chats with unsaved messages
- parked turn recoveries (`recoveries_for_session`)

Make `has_loss_risk` true when any of them is non-zero, so Ctrl+Q with only a draft or a Temporary chat still asks.

In the dialog:
- Render only the non-zero rows, so the list never reads as all-clear.
- Rename the parked row to match the UI copy ('Unsent turns needing attention: 1').
- Add an 'Open tabs are not reopened on next launch; saved chats stay in Library' note.

Keep drafts content-free in the aggregate (counts only, per TASK-14806 AC#7). Persisting drafts or restoring tabs contradicts ADR-033/098 and needs its own ADR; it is not needed to fix the misleading inventory. Add a regression test that quits with a draft only and asserts a dialog appears.

title: Extends G4-06: an internal turn-commit failure shows as 'Send blocked — finish provider setup to continue ›', with the header stuck on 'Running'
statement: A send in a conversation without a console_conversation_library_policy row (a seeding artifact of this test; see seed_output.txt) failed internally. The log shows 'Durable turn commit failed; turn refused (exception_type=RuntimeError)', phase=durable_commit status=failed. The UI showed the user message with no assistant row, header 'Running', composer 'Send blocked — finish provider setup to continue ›' with 'Preparing...', and the shelf 'Unsent turn needs attention'. None of it changed for more than 3 minutes. The quit dialog counted the chat as 'Live agent runs: 1'. The provider was correctly configured throughout.
expected: An internal persistence failure should say so ('Couldn't save this turn — nothing was sent'), offer retry or copy-draft, and clear the Running state.
why: Users are sent to fix a provider setup that isn't broken, and the chat looks stuck running forever. Any legacy or imported conversation missing sidecar rows would hit the same path.
repro: Insert a conversation via raw SQL without a Library-policy row; open it; send.
recommendation: Map durable_commit failures to a distinct display state ('Turn not saved — nothing was sent. [Retry] [Copy draft]'), end the Running state, and backfill missing sidecar rows on open (or repair them lazily) rather than refusing the turn.

title: Trace export fails on an ordinary two-turn chat under every profile with a raw validation error
statement: Trace export fails for any conversation that contains at least one turn answered from staged Library sources (Search Library, then a send with 'N staged'). It does not fail on an ordinary chat. When it fails, every profile fails: Safe summary, Redacted diagnostic, and Full trace after its confirmation. The dialog shows the raw internal validation error. Redacted and Safe show 'Export failed: Invalid Trace events[0]: dangling parent_event_id 'event-000002''. Full trace leaks the internal id: '...dangling parent_event_id 'console-trace:<uuid>:retrieval:retrieval_completed''. No file is written, the dialog offers no recovery or retry guidance, and one such turn makes the whole conversation unexportable. An ordinary two-turn chat with no Library sources exports successfully under both Redacted diagnostic and Safe summary.
expected: Export writes a bundle for any conversation the Trace view can display. If validation fails, the message says what is wrong in plain words ('Some trace events reference steps that were not recorded') and offers to export anyway without the orphaned links, or to copy diagnostics.
why: Trace export is the documented way to share a diagnostic, and it fails exactly when a user needs it. The error text cannot be acted on.
repro: In a chat with two normal turns: focus the transcript → y → w → Export (keep the default profile, or choose Safe summary).
recommendation: Make build_trace_export tolerate or repair dangling parents by re-parenting orphans to the turn root. Map known validation errors to human copy with a recovery action. Log the full error with the conversation id.
fix_direction: Fix the producer first. On the staged-evidence paths (evidence_bundle and frozen capture), either record the retrieval event that context_attached points to, for example an 'evidence staged/frozen' retrieval_completed under the same console-trace:{echoed_user.id}:retrieval prefix, or set parent_event_id/source_event_id to an event that was actually recorded (the user message) or None. Then harden the exporter. Instead of failing the whole bundle on an orphaned reference, clear or re-parent it to the turn root and record a missing_metadata/redaction_provenance entry (reason 'reference_not_recorded'), so already-stored conversations become exportable again. In TraceExportDialog, map TrajectoryExportError to plain copy ('Some trace steps point to steps that were not recorded') with a recovery action, and log the full error with the conversation id. Add a regression test that runs a staged-evidence send through build_trace_export for all three profiles.

title: Header 'Speak replies' / 'Hands-free' switches have no On/Off word, a 1.42:1 off state and a focus state that hides the value; one Enter on Hands-free starts the microphone pipeline with no consent or cancel
statement:
Header row 4 reads 'Speak replies ▌  Hands-free ▌  Ready'. Both controls are 5-cell Textual Switches squeezed to h-1/w-5/border-none/p-0 (console_speech_controls.py:130-141), and neither has a state word; the .txt row is byte-identical Off vs On. The Off track is #000f18 on the #242f38 header (1.42:1) and the Off knob is #1e1e1e (1.22:1), so Off shows as a near-invisible dark blob. On is a clearly visible green #4ebf71 knob, so unfocused On vs Off can only be told apart by colour and knob position. When a switch is focused it shows only '┌───┐' (#0178d4 on #1c4666, 2.19:1), which replaces the knob. A diff of the focused-Off and focused-On captures shows zero changed cells, so a keyboard user cannot see the value while the control has focus.

Speak replies is behind a consent dialog (provider, destination, charges). Hands-free has no confirm step. Enter on the focused switch immediately starts dictation, audio-recording init and the Parakeet model load, and turns the switch green (On). The app then shows toasts ('Preparing the speech model for the first time… Nothing is being recorded yet — the microphone opens once the model is ready', plus a warm-up failure toast) and the chip reads '◐ Preparing speech model…'. Hands-free reply speech uses the same app TTS handler that Speak replies warns about (OpenAI, charges may apply), so it gets around that cost consent.

Esc does end the Hands-free loop and the switch returns to Off. It does not cancel the in-flight model preparation: the chip still read 'Preparing speech model…' 80 s after Esc and 3 min after Enter. The result is a contradictory display: switch Off, capture still pending. By code (not observed live), teardown's close-capture is a no-op unless recording, so when the model finishes loading the capture would move to recording, with the microphone open, after the user has exited. The only way to cancel is to click the composer's 'Dictate' button (verified: 'Dictation cancelled.'). That button keeps its idle label 'Dictate' during preparation, and 'press to cancel' exists only in its tooltip.

The Ctrl+Shift+H accelerator appears only in the tooltip: it is not in the footer or anywhere in F1 help. The 'paused after a failure' state is NOT tooltip-only. A visible 'Retry speech / Resume auto-speak' row appears in the control bar, along with a warning toast. However, the header switch stays green On while paused. DESIGN.md:266's 'always paired with a text-state word' rule sits in the Settings dense-form convention (task-1586). Applying it to the Console header extends the convention rather than breaking an explicit rule for that header.
expected: The controls read 'Speak replies: Off' / 'On' / 'Paused' and 'Hands-free: Off' / 'On' / 'Starting…', with the word carrying the state and any switch track at 3:1 or better. The focus indicator is an outline of at least 3:1 around label and switch that never hides the value and has no clipped chrome. Starting Hands-free (a microphone/voice loop) uses the same consent pattern as Speak replies, shows 'Starting… (Esc to cancel)' on the control, and Esc actually cancels model preparation. The accelerator and the paused-after-failure state are visible text, not tooltip-only.
why: Speak replies sends output to a cloud provider and costs money, and Hands-free is a listening mode. Users cannot tell at a glance whether either is on: not in low-colour terminals, not when tabbing, and not at all while focused. A single keypress on an unlabelled control started a privacy-relevant microphone pipeline and a model download with no visible way back out.
repro: At 235x52 (or any ready launch), read header row 4 (sgr row 4, cols 206/223). Tab four times from the composer to reach Speak replies (it shows '┌───┐'), then Space, Enable, and move focus away. Tab again to Hands-free, press Enter, and watch the chip; press Esc.
recommendation:

title: Every healthy active run is reported as 'Run: Blocked', 'Provider: blocked - Provider setup needed: current run is active' and a 'setup' edge badge
statement:
Confirmed live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. I reproduced it on 6 of 6 healthy sends at 235x52, with the proxy in both normal and slow mode. At those moments the header read 'Running', the status strip 'Run: Agent running.' or 'Run: Validating provider.', and the transcript 'Connecting tools... 2s', 'Thinking... 5s' or 'Generating...'.

At the same moment the Inspect rail said:
- Pinned summary: 'Run: Blocked'.
- Run section: 'Provider: blocked - Provider setup needed: current run is active', in red.
- Conversation settings: 'Not ready - current run is active', next to a 'Run active' label.
- Collapsed Inspect edge: badge 'setup'.

Every run succeeded, and all four surfaces then reverted to 'Run: Ready', 'Provider: ready', 'Ready to send' and no badge.

The merged G4-08 part is also real, and worse than stated. While the send button reads 'Preparing...' and the status reads 'Run: Validating provider.', the composer shows 'Send blocked - finish provider setup to continue >'. I saw it on 3 of 5 slow-mode sends, 1.5-3 s after Enter, and it disappears quickly. The strip is a link to app.run_setup_wizard. Clicking it mid-run opened the full first-run wizard ('Set up tldw chatbook', Step 1 of 6) over the Console, while the healthy run finished behind it.

Corrections to the finding's details:
(a) The 'Provider setup needed' text on the Inspector Provider row comes from chat_screen.py:14424-14433, which uses build_console_readiness_presentation(...).detail as provider_recovery. The settings-summary widget's own line says 'Not ready - current run is active' with a 'Run active' label. That is misleading, but it does not say 'setup'.
(b) G4-08 is not caused by a 'validating' string. The prompt queue's pre-acceptance 'Preparing...' tooltip ('Wait for this turn to be accepted before queueing a message.', prompt_queue.py:129-132) is passed in the setup_blocked_reason slot (chat_screen.py:22368-22376). build_console_disabled_reason then falls through to the generic 'finish provider setup' copy (console_display_state.py:278-302). Because the reason is non-empty, the composer also gets the console-composer-setup-blocked class, which makes the strip a link to the setup wizard (console_composer_bar.py:1943-1946, 2251-2258). By the same code path, the 'Queue full' tooltip would also read as 'finish provider setup' (from code, not seen live).
(c) While an approval is pending, the pinned line reads 'Waiting for approval', because that check runs before Blocked. The Provider row and the edge badge are still wrong then.
expected: An active run reads 'Run: Running — next message will queue' (or 'Waiting for approval') everywhere. The provider row reads 'Provider: ready (busy with current run)' or is unchanged. The edge badge reads 'running' or nothing. 'Blocked' and 'Provider setup needed' appear only for genuine configuration blockers, and always with a recovery action.
why: The panel that answers 'What happens if I send now?' gives the wrong answer on every turn. 'Blocked … setup needed' during a successful run sends users to Settings mid-run to fix a problem that does not exist. It also teaches them to ignore the word when a real key or endpoint problem occurs.
repro: Ready mode at 235x52 with Inspect open (Alt+I), or with the proxy set to slow. Send any tool prompt, press Alt+I within 10 s, and read the top summary, the Run section and the collapsed edge badge while it runs.
recommendation:
1. Treat 'active_run' as a run-state fact, not a provider-readiness blocker: remove it from the provider operability computation, or give it its own template ('Busy — current run').
2. In the authority rollup, let run_active and pending approval win over provider/source 'blocked', or exclude 'active_run' from 'blocked'.
3. Derive the rail edge badge from the structured run status, not from row text.
4. Reserve 'Blocked' for states that carry a recovery action.
fix_direction:
1. Remove the dependency of provider readiness on active_run in the Inspector path. At chat_screen.py:14415-14433, treat recovery_action=='wait_for_active_run' as provider_ready=True, mirroring the TASK-32345 guard. Better, do not compute active_run as a provider blocker at all for display consumers. Keep it only for gating settings mutations, where the settings modal already renders it correctly (console_settings_modal.py:3413).
2. In project_console_send_authority, let run_active (and pending approval) win over a provider 'blocked' whose cause is active_run. Alternatively, keep 'Blocked' only for rows that carry a real recovery action.
3. Derive the rail edge badge from the structured run status and readiness blocker, not by matching 'provider' plus 'blocked' in row text. While a run is active, show 'running' or nothing.
4. Stop passing the prompt-queue tooltip through setup_blocked_reason. Give the composer a separate queue_blocked_reason (or a flag), so 'Preparing...' and 'Queue full' render their own copy ('Wait - turn starting', 'Queue full - manage to make room'). They must never get the console-composer-setup-blocked class or the run_setup_wizard link.
5. Add a regression test that renders a mid-run Inspector state and asserts all of the following: the pinned Run line is 'Running', the Provider row is not blocked, the edge badge is not 'setup', and the composer reason never contains 'provider setup' while the queue is in Preparing. Cover every consumer, not one function; this is the lesson from TASK-32345.

title: Conversation Inspector 'Exchange history' and 'Usage & cost' can never load captures, so 'Export selected call…' and the exchange-export dialog are unreachable
statement:
Confirmed live on Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 and on OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini. The Conversation Inspector cannot load any captured call. Selecting a turn on 'Exchange history' or 'Usage & cost' shows 'Capture unavailable / Could not load captures. Select this turn again to retry.' Retrying fails every time, so 'Export selected call...' never enables.

The cause is a deterministic code bug, not missing data. ConsoleTraceNativeReader._reconstruct_call calls json.dumps(dict(call.usage)), but stored usage is frozen into nested MappingProxyType objects and dict() is shallow. Both providers' real usage has nested objects (Anthropic cache_creation; OpenAI prompt_tokens_details and completion_tokens_details). json.dumps therefore raises 'TypeError: Object of type mappingproxy is not JSON serializable'. The error is not caught along the way and is swallowed without logging by the Inspector's broad except.

The secondary details also hold:
- When the section list gains focus it scrolls down one row, so Turn 1 is off-screen even while it is selected.
- On 'Usage & cost' the basis label wraps onto a second line, which leaves Turn 1's 'Estimated' orphaned above Turn 2.
- The llama.cpp caveat is a hard-coded string shown for every provider.
expected: The captured call loads and becomes exportable. If loading fails, the reason is shown, for example 'Capture was stored in Safe mode', 'Purged' or 'Decode error', and the failure is logged.
why: The 'what was actually sent' surface is the recovery tool for provider problems, and here it dead-ends behind a false 'retry' promise.
repro: Send one normal prompt → /context → 'Exchange history' → click 'Turn · 2 · assistant' (repeat), or 'Usage & cost' → click the turn.
recommendation: Log and classify loader failures. Show a specific reason, and drop the retry promise when a retry cannot help. Keep all turn rows visible, with the basis label on the same line as its turn. Show provider-specific capture notes only for the relevant provider.
fix_direction: In the native reader, serialise the frozen usage with a deep thaw, or store and decode usage as normalized ProviderUsage JSON, so that it also passes _usage_validation_error. Add a native-reader test that uses real nested Anthropic and OpenAI usage and asserts that a call row loads. Log reader failures with the exception type in the Inspector (and at the projection boundary), classify them, and drop the 'select again to retry' promise for deterministic failures. Keep the highlighted OptionList row scrolled into view when the list gains focus, and keep each basis label on its turn's line. Show the llama.cpp note only for llama.cpp.

title: Typing with focus outside the composer loses the text and fires single-letter commands; 'y' opens Trace, and closing a dialog doesn't return focus to the composer
statement:
Printable keys typed while focus is on a non-text Console control are dropped with no feedback. The bare screen-level 'y' binding opens the full-screen Trace from any such control, and the rest of the user's words then run as Trace single-key commands. All three paths reproduce at human typing speed (150 ms per key) on dev 64579cce2c:
(1) Mouse-click the Library access status chip, press Esc, and type 'yes'. Trace opens. 'e' and 's' then fire Trace actions (toasts 'All records are already loaded.' and 'No matching Trace event.'). After closing Trace the draft is empty and focus is back on the chip.
(2) Alt+I, then type 'Say hi.' + Enter. The 'y' opens Trace, and the draft is empty after Esc.
(3) Mouse-click the header Help, press Esc, and type a 30-character sentence. None of it reaches the composer, which still shows its placeholder and 'Send disabled: type a message'.

Corrections to the original:
(a) Duplicate Library access dialogs stack only under burst input (keys arriving before the modal is pushed). At human typing speed one Space opens exactly one dialog.
(b) 'No obvious signal' is overstated. The focused chip or Help button gets a tint plus bold and underline, and after Alt+I the footer says 'Esc composer'. The real weakness is that the composer itself barely changes.
(c) Returning focus to the invoking control is the default and the recorded design (TASK-16211). F1 followed by Esc does return to the composer. Only mouse-opened dialogs leave focus off the composer.
(d) A second Esc does return focus to the composer, so F1's 'Escape: return to the composer' is accurate.
expected: When a Console dialog closes with Esc or Cancel, focus returns to the composer (or to the invoking control with an obvious ring). Single-letter global actions don't fire while the user is plainly typing; they are scoped to the transcript or need a modifier. A printable key pressed in a non-text pane focuses the composer and inserts the character. Chip re-activation is debounced.
why: 'Just start typing' is the Console's core affordance, and terminal users type without looking. Here a sentence silently becomes navigation and the user's words are swallowed.
repro: launch.sh j17 80 24 ready → click the 'Library · Auto off · Agent blocked' chip → Esc → type a sentence containing 'y' and spaces. Or: ready 235x52 → Alt+I → type 'Say hi.' + Enter. Or: click header 'Help' → Esc → type text.
recommendation: Return focus to the composer when a Console dialog, including Help, is dismissed. Move Trace to a modified key (Alt+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Y) or scope 'y' to the transcript. Add a type-to-compose fallback so unhandled printable keys in the rails and status strip focus the composer and insert the character. Make the composer's unfocused state visibly different (hint 'Esc to type'). Debounce chip activation so one Space can't stack duplicate dialogs. Add a regression test: open Help, Esc, type, assert the draft is non-empty.
fix_direction: Add a type-to-compose fallback in ChatScreen.on_key. When a printable, non-bound key comes from a non-text control in the Console workbench (status strip, rail buttons, header actions), focus the composer and insert the character. Move Trace off the bare 'y': use a modifier chord, or scope it to the transcript or inspector with a check_action gate that is false when the focused widget is a Button or chip in the status strip or header. Consider sending focus to the composer when a mouse-opened status-strip or header modal is dismissed with Esc or Cancel. At minimum, make the unfocused composer visibly different (e.g. an 'Esc to type' hint). Add an in-flight guard to library_policy.open_access, or ignore activation while a ConsoleLibraryAccessModal is already on the stack. Regression tests: (1) click header Help, Esc, type text, assert the draft is non-empty; (2) focus the Library chip, press 'y', assert no Trace screen is pushed.

title: Esc never returns to the composer from the transcript, although F1 and the rail footers say it does; typed prose then runs transcript commands
statement:
Confirmed live at 160x45 on origin/dev 64579cce2c. Once the transcript has focus (via F6 or a click on a message), Esc never gets back to the composer. The first Esc clears the message selection. Every later Esc does nothing visible, because ConsoleTranscript.on_key always calls event.stop() in its escape branch, so the screen's escape fallback to focus_console_composer_home is never reached. The composer stayed unfocused and the transcript title stayed focus-styled after 1, 2 and 3 Escs. F1 still says 'Escape: return to the composer'. The left rail footer shows 'Esc composer - F6 panes' and Esc works there. The transcript footer shows neither that hint nor any mode indicator.

Printable keys typed in this state never reach the composer:
- Unbound letters are dropped: 'hi' vanished.
- 'y' opens the full-screen Trace.
- 'n' toasts 'No review notes on this message.'
- A j or k in the prose re-selects a message, and the letters after it fire bare-letter actions on that message. 'Make a joke about cats.' stacked two Edit Message modals, overwrote the clipboard (Copy), and armed text-selection mode (s).
- 'look around' fired Regenerate, a paid request that creates a new branch (Assistant 2/2).

Nuance: c/e/f/r/o/v/s act only while a message is selected, so after the first Esc they fire only once a j, k or Enter in the typed text re-selects one. In ordinary prose that is common. 'y' and 'n' fire with or without a selection.
expected: When there is nothing left to clear, Esc from any pane, the transcript included, returns to the composer as the help says. Unbound printable keys type into the composer (focus plus insert) or are visibly rejected. An explicit 'Transcript keys active — Esc to type' indicator is shown.
why: The transcript is the pane keyboard users visit most. Without a way back, users lose typed text and can trigger Edit, Fork or Regenerate by accident; Regenerate spends tokens and changes the active branch. The Help text teaches a key that does not work in exactly this state.
repro: F6 to the transcript (or click a message), j, then Esc ×2–3; type 'xyz' or a sentence and press Enter.
recommendation: In ConsoleTranscript's escape branch, stop the event only when something was cleared (selection, menu, text-selection mode); otherwise let it bubble to focus_console_composer_home. Route unbound printable keys to the composer (focus plus insert). Show 'Transcript · j/k c e f r · Esc to type' (or the rails' 'Esc composer' hint) in the footer whenever the transcript has focus.
fix_direction:
In ConsoleTranscript.on_key's escape branch, call event.stop() only when there was something to clear (a selection, the selection menu, an active or finished selection manager, or a More menu). Otherwise let the Key bubble so the screen's focus_console_composer_home runs. Keep TASK-18156's layering for the earlier stages: text-selection mode, then message selection, then composer.

Show the rails' 'Esc composer - F6 panes' hint in the footer (or a 'Transcript keys - Esc to type' indicator) whenever the transcript has focus.

Consider routing unbound printable keys (and printables typed while no message is selected) to the composer: focus it and insert the character. The alternative is to reject them visibly.

Also consider gating r (paid Regenerate) and f (Fork) so they need an explicitly confirmed selection, not one created by a j or k inside prose. Or require the action row to be open first.

Pin all of this with a Pilot test: F6 to the transcript, then j, Esc, Esc, and assert that the composer has focus. Then type 'look around' and assert no action button was pressed and the draft contains the text.

title: After creating a Terminal session, keystrokes still go to the chat composer under the 'HOST TERMINAL' banner, so a shell command becomes a draft for the model
statement: I reproduced this live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. Arm the Terminal and click New then Create: the session starts ("➜ home") under "HOST TERMINAL - FULL USER ACCESS / Terminal content is user-only and is not sent to a model.", but keyboard focus comes back to the chat composer. Typed text ("echo hi", then "ls ~/.ssh") lands in the composer. Pressing Enter really sends it to the LLM: the proxy logged a POST to api.anthropic.com. The Terminal center hides the transcript, so the user sees nothing happen there. The turn finishes "while hidden", and a new chat titled "echo hi" appears with User "echo hi" and Assistant "hi". The footer shows "Enter send / queue | Y trace" the whole time, even while the terminal viewport has input. Three points go further than the finding. (1) The Arm confirmation has the same problem: after Confirm, focus goes to the composer, not to New. (2) When a session already exists, a new one is not even selected. After creating Terminal 2, Terminal 1 stays selected, so "Focus", or a click in the viewport, sends keys to the old session. (3) One small correction: the user does not have to use the Focus button. A click inside the terminal viewport also gives it input. But nothing on screen says either step is needed.
expected: A newly created session takes focus, as _focus_open_console_terminal already does on a center swap. The composer is hidden or disabled while the Terminal owns the center, or at least clearly says 'sends to chat'.
why: This is a classic mode error. A shell command, possibly with paths or secrets, leaks to a remote model, and the agent may act on it. It happens at exactly the moment the user believes they are typing into their shell.
repro: Open Terminal, arm it, click New, then Create. Type 'echo hi' without clicking.
recommendation: After admitted create, call _focus_open_console_terminal. While the Terminal center is shown, collapse the composer or relabel it 'Message chat (Terminal open)', and swap the footer to Terminal hints (Ctrl+] release, Return to transcript).
fix_direction: Make the Terminal center a real focus owner. In _restore_console_workbench_focus (or on_screen_resume), if self._console_terminal_open, call _focus_open_console_terminal() and do not fall back to the composer. This fixes focus after closing both the Arm confirm and the New-session modal. Doing only "call focus after create" would race the resume handler's call_after_refresh. After an admitted create, select the new session (runtime.focus_session(created.session_id, view=...)) and focus its viewport. While the Terminal owns the center, register a Terminal footer variant (Ctrl+] release, Return to transcript). Also relabel the composer placeholder ("Message chat — Terminal open") or collapse it, so typing there is clearly a chat action. Add a pilot test: arm, then create, then assert app.focused is the TerminalViewport and that composer text is unchanged after key presses.

title: 'Filter visible titles' drops keystrokes, lowercases input and loses focus because the input is re-mounted on every sync
statement:
The rail's 'Filter visible titles' input does not keep what the user types. About 200 ms after each pause in typing, the debounced search rebuilds the whole tray with refresh(recompose=True), and that includes a new ConsoleBrowserSearchInput. The new input is seeded with browser.query, which build_console_conversation_browser_state has already stripped and lowercased (conversation_browser_state.py:519, 566), so 'OK' reads back as 'ok'.

Three things can then happen to the next keystrokes:
(a) Focus comes back, but Textual's Input select_on_focus=True selects the whole query, so the next key replaces it. Typing 'OK', waiting 1 s, then ' 9' left the field showing '9' with '0 matches'.
(b) Focus does not come back. It lands on the Conversations section toggle and the keys are dropped: after 'zebra', ' 9' left the field at 'zebra', and 'A' then 'B' 300 ms apart gave 'a'.
(c) A key reaches a screen-level single-letter binding. Typing 'Say' at about 250 ms per key opened the full-screen Trace view, twice, because 'y' is bound to open_trajectory_view.

The search is already debounced (200 ms). The damage comes from the re-mount after the debounce, not from a missing debounce.

The count mismatch is real but has a different cause. It is not the row cap, which never drops below 12 rows. The persisted DB search counts matches in message content, and that count becomes result_total_count. The display state then re-filters rows by title, workspace and status only (_row_matches), so a match found only in message content is counted but can never be shown. Live, filtering 'zebra', a word that appears only in one chat's messages, read '1 match. Showing 0 of 1' with no rows. A 'Show all' control would not fix this; the count and the rows have to use the same matching rule.
expected: The input keeps exactly what was typed and keeps focus, and filtering is debounced. Counts match the rows shown, or a 'Show all' control is offered.
why: Users lose characters and see a query they didn't type. A filter that fights typing gets abandoned, which pushes users to Ctrl+K or Library.
repro: Click 'Filter visible titles', type 'OK', wait 1 s, then type ' 9'.
recommendation: Stop recomposing the search input: keep one Input instance and update only the result list, keyed by rows. Show the raw query and normalise only for matching. When results are capped, show 'Show all N'.
fix_direction: Keep one Input instance across syncs. Take the search row out of the recomposed subtree, or update only the result list and status, keyed by rows, while leaving the Input mounted. Never write a normalised query back into the Input: show the raw text and normalise only for matching. If a programmatic refocus is ever needed, keep the cursor where it was and do not select all (set select_on_focus=False on this input, or restore the cursor position). Add a regression test that types across the debounce boundary (for example 'OK', wait 300 ms, ' 9') and asserts the value is 'OK 9', that focus is on the input, and that the Trace screen is not pushed. For the count, make the total and the rows use the same rule. Either count title matches only, which matches the 'Filter visible titles' placeholder, or show content-matched rows with a 'matched in messages' hint. Do not add 'Show all N': the hidden row is filtered out, not capped.

title: Extends G4-58: in any light theme the hard-coded black Console modals become black boxes whose explanation text is 1.27:1
statement:
Confirmed live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. With general.default_theme = "textual-light", the Console modals that hard-code `border: tall gray; background: black` render as black boxes in an otherwise light UI. Body copy with no explicit colour inherits the theme foreground and becomes nearly invisible. Measured values:
- Library search description ("Manual search for this send only…"): #1f1f1f on #000000, 1.27:1. This modal inherits the black frame from ConsoleRagSettingsModal's DEFAULT_CSS (console_library_search_modal.py:47 subclasses it).
- Edit Message consequence line ("Save keeps the edit in place; Edit & resend creates a new response branch…"): #1f1f1f on #000000, 1.27:1. Its text area is dark navy (#001423).
- Composer Menu focused row "Browse Prompt Library…": #dde0e2 on #001322. The other rows are light-grey slabs (#d8d8d8).
- Rewind's highlighted row is also dark navy inside a black box.
- In solarized_light the same description reads 4.71:1 (#657b83 on #000000), but the modal is still a black box in a cream UI.
- In textual-dark the same line is 15.91:1, so the defect only appears in light themes.

Two small corrections:
1. Dark-navy highlights are not unique to these modals. The light UI's own primary button ("Apply to this chat") and footer are navy too. The real problem is the black frame, not navy selection as such.
2. By grep I count 17 Widgets/Console files with `background: black`, plus the inherited Library search modal. I could not check G4-58's own "18 files" list.

By code reading only (not reproduced live), AutoSpeakConsentModal is a black frame with no colour rules at all. So in a light theme its whole consent text ("Speak new replies automatically?", Provider, Destination, "Provider charges may apply.") would render at the same ~1.27:1.
expected: Modals take their surfaces from theme tokens ($ds-surface-panel, a round $ds-grid-line border), like ConsoleAppearancePickerModal already does, and their explanation copy stays at 4.5:1 or better in every theme.
why: The copy that goes dark is the consequence explanation: what Save versus Edit & resend will do, and what a Library search stages. In a light theme the user must choose between irreversible-looking actions with that explanation invisible. The black boxes also make the app look broken, or dark-only, to light-theme users.
repro: Switch to textual-light. Click the header 'Search Library' button, and in a separate step select a user message and press e. Read the description line. Run sgr.py runs on that row.
recommendation: Replace every `border: tall gray; background: black` (and `color: gray` / `color: red`) in Widgets/Console with one shared modal-frame class that uses theme tokens. Add a lint or test that fails on literal colour keywords or hex values in Console widget CSS, except for documented light/dark token pairs.
fix_direction: Add one shared Console modal-frame class, or a small base-CSS mixin, built on theme tokens: `background: $ds-surface-panel; border: round $ds-grid-line` (or `tall $accent`, as ConsoleAppearancePickerModal does). Migrate the 17 literal-black files to it, and remember that subclasses such as ConsoleLibrarySearchModal inherit the fix. Replace `color: gray/red` with `$text-muted`/`$error`. Give explanation/consequence copy an explicit token colour (e.g. $text) so it cannot inherit a clash. Add a ratchet test, in the spirit of ADR-150, that fails on colour keywords or hex literals in Widgets/Console CSS strings. Add a light-theme snapshot or contrast check for at least Edit Message, Library search, Rewind, the composer Menu and AutoSpeakConsent.

title: After Enter, the draft vanishes and nothing acknowledges the send for about 1–10 s ('No messages yet.', header 'Ready')
statement:
Reproduced on origin/dev 64579cce2c (160x45, ready mode, Anthropic haiku via the review proxy, 100–150 ms tmux polling). After Enter, nothing on screen changes for 0.44–0.66 s. The composer then clears to its placeholder with 'Send disabled: type a message' while the Send button still reads 'Send'. For the next ~1.1–1.9 s every status surface stays idle: header 'Ready', no tab '●', no 'Run: Agent running.' chip, the left-rail chat row unchanged, and the transcript either still says 'No messages yet.' (first send, or new tab via Ctrl+T) or shows only the previous turn (warm send). The user row first appears 1.8–2.8 s after Enter, in the same paint as the tab marker and the Run chip.

Measured runs:
- First send of the session: clear at 0.66 s, header 'Running' and rail ⟳ at 1.75 s, user row at 2.50 s.
- Warm second send: clear at 0.65 s; row, 'Running', ● and chip together at 2.51 s.
- New tab: clear at 0.44 s, 'Running' at 1.55 s, row at 2.76 s.
- Second new tab: 'No messages yet.' still on screen at 1.0 s and at 1.9 s (with 'Running'); row at 3.2 s.

The store has the echo long before it is painted: durable_commit succeeded at 760–773 ms. The gap is rendering, not admission.

The 6.5–10 s tail from J5 was not reproduced here. The J5 profile log does show a 2.9 s synchronous admission (ui_submit entered 236 ms, accepted 3111 ms), so longer gaps on cold first sends are plausible.

Consequence verified: retyping the same prompt and pressing Enter 0.9 s into the gap made a queued duplicate ('Q1'). It auto-dispatched as a second turn: two identical user rows, two assistant replies, two provider calls.
expected: Within 100 ms of Enter, the user's message renders in the transcript optimistically (marked pending/'Sending…'), and the header, tab marker, Run chip and Send control flip to Sending/Running synchronously. The composer never says 'type a message' while a send is in flight, and 'No messages yet.' disappears the moment a send is accepted. If admission or commit fails, the row rolls back with an inline error.
why: A cleared draft plus 'No messages yet.'/'Send disabled: type a message' reads as a lost message. Impatient users retype or press Enter again, which creates duplicate sends that then queue, and trust that input is accepted erodes.
repro: Launch ready mode (80x24 or 235x52) or press Ctrl+T for a new tab. Type a short prompt (e.g. 'Reply with exactly: second') and press Enter. Capture the pane every 100–250 ms for 3–10 s and compare header, transcript and composer; correlate with console_send_stage log phases.
recommendation: Render the user turn optimistically, plus a 'Sending…' assistant placeholder, synchronously on Enter or at the ui_submit accepted event, before run admission, validation, trace reservation and capture. Flip the header to 'Sending…' and start the tab marker and Run chip in the key handler. Suppress the empty-draft reason while _console_pending_send is set. Key the empty state off 'no messages and no pending send'. Roll the row back with an inline error if admission or commit fails.
fix_direction: Restore the acceptance-time echo removed in b7dd8e53f2, and make it earlier and cheaper than before. Paint the pending user row (marked 'Sending…') and flip the header, tab marker and Send/Queue control directly from the key handler, or from the runtime accept_turn return. Do not go through the whole-screen _sync_native_console_chat_ui tick, and do it before the synchronous admission work in _admit_console_turn_to_runtime (or move that work off the paint path). While a turn is in custody or pending, suppress 'Send disabled: type a message' and key the empty-state card off 'no messages AND no pending send'. If admission or commit fails, roll the row back with an inline error (TASK-485's transient-echo rollback already exists). Replace or augment test_console_send_echoes_user_message_before_transcript_poll with a test that holds admission/validation (not just the stream) and asserts the row and the Sending state are visible before gateway.started, plus one asserting a quick re-entry during the gap does not silently queue a duplicate. Raw admission latency (ui_submit 0.3–2.9 s, 10 s personal-context bootstrap) stays with the PERF series.

title: At 80x24 the approval card clips its buttons: 'Approve on' is visible, the row's Deny is gone, and only 'De' of 'Deny all' shows
statement:
When the Inspect rail is open and the terminal is roughly 105 columns or narrower, the chat column is too narrow for the single-row approval card's fixed controls. The row needs 55 cells: a 27-cell Select plus two 14-cell buttons. The batch bar needs about 48. Both clip on the right, and Deny is the control that disappears.
- 80x24 with Inspect open: the card is 44 columns and the finding's text reproduces exactly: "Approve on", no per-row Deny, and "Approve all · Submit · De".
- 90x30: only "Approve" shows on the row, and "Deny all" is gone entirely.
- 100x30: the per-row Deny is a 2-cell red sliver with no label.
- 110x30 and wider: everything fits.

The finding's repro is missing a precondition. At the default 80x24 the Console is transcript-only. The card is then 78 columns and "Approve once / Deny" and "Approve all / Submit / Deny all" are all fully visible. The rail only shows after an explicit Inspect toggle (Alt+I), which then persists across widths (right_open_explicit) as ADR-043 intends.

The clipped fast Deny still takes keyboard focus. Tab from "Approve once" moves focus to an invisible control, with no visible change anywhere on screen, and Enter there denies the call. Deny is still reachable as the fifth option of the decision Select plus the visible Submit, and the timeout auto-denies. So the one-click safe controls vanish, but a visible deny path remains.

This is not a regression of TASK-32287: its AC#2 still holds in the default 80x24 layout, and its test runs with Inspect closed. It is an uncovered, width-dependent case.
expected: At the smallest supported size, every decision is fully visible and Deny is never the one clipped: stack the buttons, or collapse Inspect while a decision is pending.
why: The safe choice disappears and the risky one stays in view. That invites approval by default on the terminal size the product commits to supporting. G4-15 covers transcript crushing, not decision controls.
repro: Resize to 80x24 and ask for any Ask-gated tool call, for example the MCP stamp_text.
recommendation: Below about 60 content columns, lay the card out vertically with Deny before Approve, or show only the fast Approve/Deny pair. Auto-collapse the Inspect rail while a decision card is pending at narrow widths. Add a snapshot test at 80x24.
fix_direction:
Make the card respond to its own width, not the terminal size:
- When the card's content width is under about 60 cells, stack the controls: Select on its own line, then a Deny + Approve once pair with Deny first or equally prominent.
- Order or wrap the batch bar so Deny all never clips; `layout: grid` or a vertical fallback both work.
- Optionally, auto-collapse or temporarily yield the Inspect rail while an approval is pending in the compact/narrow bands, without writing the preference.
- Add mounted tests with Inspect explicitly open at 80x24, 90x30 and 100x30. For each Deny control, assert that get_widget_at on its centre returns it and that its region lies inside the card's content region. The existing 80x24 test only pins Submit, with Inspect closed.

title: The focused Terminal hides the first column of output, and at 80x24 it is a 44×6 viewport with buttons cut to 'Ren Focu Clos Jum'
statement: Unfocused, the prompt renders '➜  proj-alpha git:(main) ✗'. After 'Focus', a 1-cell accent border appears and column 0 of the PTY is hidden: 'git status --short' shows 'M README.md' and '? untracked.txt' (really ' M' and '??'), and the prompt loses '➜'. At 80x24 the Inspect rail stays open, so the viewport is about 44×6, the tab label reads 'Ter', and the action row reads 'Ren    Focu    Clos    Jum     Return to'.
expected: Focus changes the border colour without shifting content, the PTY is sized to the visible cells, and at 80x24 the Terminal gets the full center with rails collapsed and readable actions (for example icons plus key hints).
why: A terminal that silently drops a column misreports git status and command output, and the narrow layout is unusable for real shell work.
repro: Create a Terminal session, click Focus, run 'git status --short' in a dirty repo, then resize to 80x24.
recommendation: Reserve the focus border in both states (use outline, or keep a constant border and change its colour) and recompute PTY columns from the content region. When the Terminal owns the center, auto-collapse both rails below 100 columns and use short labels that don't clip.

title: False 'A Console turn completed while hidden' toast and '!' nav badge fire on turns completed in the visible Console tab
statement:
Confirmed, with three clarifications. In the visible, active Console tab, every completed turn after the first in a session shows the toast "A Console turn completed while hidden. Return to Console to review." (information severity, about 5 s). The nav tab also shows "⌃2 Console !" at the same moment. I reproduced this on turns 2, 3 and 4 in a fresh 120x40 ready profile, never leaving Console.

1. The '!' badge is a brief flash (about 0.75 to 1.3 s), not a lasting state. It clears once the view renders and acknowledges the receipt. No marks were left in conversation_local_marks afterwards.
2. The first send in a session escaped. The likely reason is timing: it awaits an extra config write (`_record_successful_first_send`, console_runtime.py:2468), which delays the task's done-callback until after the view has already acknowledged the receipt.
3. Scrolling, theme switches or palette pushes are not needed (G4-32's hypothesis). Plain back-to-back sends reproduce it.

The toast fired while the transcript still showed "Assistant Streaming…" and the status bar still read "Run: Agent running.". So the notice is raised before the terminal result is even rendered, which is the opposite of 'hidden'.
expected: No hidden-turn toast or '!' badge when the turn's conversation is visible in the active Console tab. The notice is reserved for genuinely backgrounded tabs or destinations.
why: A status message that is wrong on every turn teaches users to ignore toasts, including the 'failed while hidden' variant on the same channel. It also adds visual noise at the moment of reading.
repro: Ready mode, fresh 120x40 profile. Send two or three messages without leaving Console and watch the top-right toasts and the nav tab.
recommendation:
1. When the terminal message renders in the attached visible view, acknowledge the receipt synchronously, before `recompute_console_attention` runs.
2. Alternatively, suppress the notice when the Console screen is current and the receipt's conversation is the attached, active tab.
3. Add a test: two visible sends produce zero notify() calls and no '!' badge.
fix_direction:
Gate the notice and the badge on real hiddenness. Two options:

1. In `recompute_console_attention` / `_notify_terminal_receipt`, skip the notice, and exclude the mark from the '!' projection, when a view is attached, the Console screen is current, and the mark's conversation is the attached view's active session conversation. Let the view's render-ack clear the mark as it does now. TASK-31385 already uses this visibility-gating pattern for blocking rounds.
2. Or, when a view is attached, have turn completion hand off to the view first (refresh plus acknowledge), then recompute. A short grace-and-recheck before notifying would also work.

Add a regression test: two or more turns completed with the view attached, visible and active produce zero notify() calls and never publish needs_attention=True. Keep a negative control where a detached or hidden completion still notifies exactly once. Track this as a defect or AC on TASK-22514 (AC #7) or a child task.

title: Tab close (✕ and middle-click) silently does nothing, and repeat presses are dropped
statement:
Closing a Console session tab fails on dev @ 64579cce2c, and the user is never told. Every close attempt ends with the tab still open. The cause is not a hung worker and not the dedupe guard. The close worker raises an exception at once: `AttributeError("'ConsoleSessionController' object has no attribute '_console_runtime'")` at `tldw_chatbook/UI/Console_Modules/session.py:2796`. That line calls `self._console_runtime().close_session(...)`, but the controller only has `self._console_runtime_accessor`. The worker runs with `exit_on_error=False`, so Textual swallows the error and nothing reaches the UI or loguru.

What I observed live:
- **Saved idle tab or blank never-sent tab:** clicking ✕ does nothing. There is no dialog, no toast and no close. The ✕ keeps focus and shows underlined.
- **Repeat presses:** they are not dropped. The `finally` block clears `_closing_session_requests`, so each press starts a new worker and fails the same way (6 identical worker errors captured).
- **Tab with an unsent draft:** the itemised "Close Console session?" dialog does appear. Clicking Close dismisses it, and the tab and draft both stay. That is misleading.
- **Middle-click:** it is not a no-op. Textual walks the handler MRO and `ConsoleSessionTabButton._on_click` does not call `prevent_default`, so a middle-click both activates (switches to) the tab and fires the same broken close.
- **Archive:** "Archive this chat" is not a workaround. It shows a "Conversation archived" receipt, and the receipt says the open tab stays.
- **Keyboard:** there is no dedicated shortcut (such as Ctrl+W) and no palette command for closing a tab. The ✕ itself can be reached with Tab/Enter, but it runs the same broken path.
- **Overflow at 100 columns:** the ✕ and the New tab / Temporary buttons do scroll out of view, but ◂ ▸ overflow hints are shown and the strip scrolls. That is a separate, lesser (P2) issue.

This is a regression from b7dd8e53f2 (2026-09-08).
expected: Closing a saved, idle tab closes it immediately. A tab with something at risk shows the itemised 'Close Console session?' dialog. If closing cannot proceed, the user is told why.
why: The power-user persona opens many tabs. Without close, the strip overflows. The silent failure also teaches users that the control is broken. The reviewer called this a release blocker for tab management.
repro: Ready mode at 235x52. Send 'Say OK 1', press Ctrl+T, then click the ✕ of either tab. Relaunch with REUSE=1, open a saved chat from the rail and click its ✕. Wait 8 s: nothing changes. Middle-click a tab: nothing.
recommendation:
1. Find out why the close worker never finishes.
2. Make every exit path from the close flow end in one of three visible outcomes: the tab closes, the confirmation dialog opens, or a toast gives the reason.
3. Add a watchdog that clears _closing_session_requests and notifies the user if the flow has not settled within about 2 s.
4. Add a keyboard/palette close.
5. Add a test that clicks ✕ on an idle saved tab and asserts the tab count drops.
fix_direction:
1. At session.py:2796, call `self._console_runtime_accessor().close_session(...)`, or `self._screen._console_runtime()` as at :5439. Then run Tests/UI/test_console_button_routing.py close-tab tests; they already encode the expected outcome and should go green. Add a pilot test that clicks the real ✕ (not `.press()` on a harness) on an idle saved tab and asserts the tab count drops.
2. Make close-flow failures visible. In start_close_console_session_tab's `_run`, catch Exception, log it with context, and call app_instance.notify("Couldn't close this tab: …", severity="error"). A blanket `exit_on_error=False` with no handler is what hid this for three weeks.
3. In ConsoleSessionTabButton._on_click, call event.prevent_default() on the middle-click branch so Button._on_click does not also activate the tab.
4. Optionally add a Ctrl+W / palette "Close tab" action that routes through start_close_console_session_tab.

No watchdog is needed: the flow does not hang. The 100-col overflow belongs in a separate P2 finding if it is kept at all.

title: Renaming an open, non-active chat from the rail menu toasts 'Renamed' but the tab, rail row, Ctrl+K and transcript header keep the old name
statement:
Renaming a conversation that is open in any Console tab, whether active or not, through the rail row menu (💬 → Rename…) shows the toast "Renamed to X.", writes X to the DB and bumps the version. The tab strip, the transcript header "Conversation | <old>", the rail Chats row, the Conversations section and Ctrl+K's CURRENT/OTHER OPEN rows all keep the old title. Switching to the tab and sending another turn does not change that. Only a restart (or reopening the chat) shows X. The same menu rename on a chat that is not open does update its rail row.

Two corrections to the finding:
1. It is not limited to non-active tabs. Renaming the active tab this way is just as stale.
2. Searching Ctrl+K for the new name still reaches the chat. It shows up as a History "SAVED CHAT X" row, and Enter switches to the existing open tab (no duplicate tab is opened), but that tab still carries the old name.

The DB title is never reverted: the only code that writes a title to the DB is the tab-rename path (ConsoleChatStore.rename_session), so nothing loses data. The UI stays inconsistent until restart.
expected: One rename updates every surface at once: tab label, rail row, Ctrl+K row, transcript header and Library.
why: One conversation shows two names in two places. A researcher searching Ctrl+K for the new name won't find the open tab, and after a restart a title appears that the Console never showed.
repro: Open two tabs with sent messages. On the non-active tab's rail row choose 💬 → Rename… and save 'Delta check'. The toast says Renamed, the tab still shows the old title, and sqlite shows the new title.
recommendation: Route every rename (tab click, Ctrl+K F2, rail menu, Library) through one rename service. It should update the DB, set the title on every open native session bound to that conversation_id, and publish one refresh. Show the 'Renamed to…' toast only after every surface has the new title.
fix_direction: Send every rename through one service (rail/tree row menu, tab click, Ctrl+K F2, palette, Library). In the rail-menu path, find each ConsoleChatSession whose persisted_conversation_id matches, set its title (for example via store.rename_session, or a store method that applies the in-memory title after the DB write succeeds), then call _invalidate_console_persisted_rows_cache() and run _sync_native_console_chat_ui() as the tab path does. Toast only after that. Add a regression test that opens two sessions, renames one through the rail action (active and non-active), and asserts the tab label, header, rail row and switcher rows all show the new title.
