title: A Temporary chat's first send is blocked by a capture interstitial whose main action turns it into a saved chat
statement:
Confirmed live at origin/dev 64579cce2c. The finding understates the problem.

In a Temporary tab, every send, not only the first, stops before the provider. It shows an orange callout above the tab strip: 'Save chat to capture this send / Owner: This Console send / Problem: Temporary chats cannot store durable captures. / Impact: The provider was not contacted. Choose how to continue.'

The buttons:
- 'Save & Send' comes first and is full-width orange.
- 'Send without capture' is also full-width orange, so the two carry equal weight.
- 'Cancel send' is neutral.

Focus stays in the composer, and no button is focused.

'Send without capture' is one-shot: the next message in the same Temporary chat raises the same callout again. 'Save & Send' ends the chat's temporary status: the tab marker changes from ◌ to ● and the status bar drops 'Temporary — not saved'.

Two more surfaces fire at the same time:
- The queue shelf shows 'Queue 0/10 · Unsent turn needs attention' with Rest/Discard buttons. It stays, stale, even after the one-shot send has replied.
- The rail shows ⛔ 'Blocked', and the transcript edge shows 'blocked'.

ADR-097 and TASK-23113.5 intend the pause and the Save & Send action. The UX critique targets things the ADR does not decide: the Capture-On default for Temporary, the order of the buttons, the error framing and the duplicate surfaces.

Separate defect found while verifying: 'Save & Send' saves the chat but never sends (2 of 2 tries). The log shows 'Durable turn commit failed; turn refused (exception_type=RuntimeError)' and the proxy got no POST. The UI then sits for more than 60 s on:
- 'Run: Validating provider.' in the status bar and 'Preparing...' in the composer.
- A wrong composer hint: 'Send blocked — finish provider setup to continue ›'.
- 'Running' in the header, and the tab still counted as 'other agents running'.

A normal saved chat in the same session sent fine (control).
expected: Choosing Temporary implies capture off for that chat, or session-only in-memory capture, and sends just work. If a choice really is needed, it is made once per Temporary chat, before the first send. The default keeps the chat temporary, and the copy does not frame an explicit user choice as a Problem.
why: The normal Temporary path is framed as an error. The default action silently undoes the user's explicit privacy choice, and three recovery surfaces fire for one non-error.
repro: Click 'Temporary' in the tab strip, type 'Say OK 4' and press Enter.
recommendation:
1. Make Temporary chats capture-off by default, or capture in memory only and drop it on close.
2. If a choice remains, show one inline notice in the composer area when the Temporary tab opens ('Temporary chats don't keep traces — Send normally / Save this chat instead'), with the temporary-preserving option focused.
3. Drop the Owner/Problem/Impact framing, the duplicate queue shelf and the rail '⛔ Blocked' for this case.
fix_direction:
Stay within ADR-097, which already allows explicit Capture Off. Add the following as a new UX task.

1. When a Temporary tab is created, set conversation-scoped Capture Off for it, so sends in that chat just work. Show a quiet 'Temporary · traces off' chip in the status bar. Offer 'Save chat (enables capture)' as an optional action rather than a gate.

2. If a choice is kept, make it apply to the whole chat, not one message. Put the temporary-preserving option first and focus it, and label it 'Keep temporary (no trace)'. Use neutral info styling, not the Problem/Impact error card. Suppress the queue-shelf 'needs attention' and the rail ⛔ Blocked for this pause kind. Also clear the stale queue shelf after a one-shot send succeeds.

3. File separately and at higher priority: the Save & Send durable_commit RuntimeError after promote_ephemeral_session. Add a regression test that drives Save & Send end-to-end through the real store (not fakes) to a provider call. Also make any refusal from _continue_prepared_submission end the 'Validating provider' / 'Preparing...' state and show honest copy instead of 'finish provider setup'.

title: A prompt typed right after clicking another tab during a live run is sent to the previous tab's chat
statement:
The user-visible defect is real. I reproduced it 3 of 3 times in the live app (v501a, 235x52, proxy slow), and it is worse than the finding says.

- With a run live in tab B, I clicked tab A, then typed a prompt and pressed Enter 1.5 to 2.2 s later. Each time the prompt was queued into B (B's tab showed Q1) and later answered in B's transcript. A received nothing.
- In trial 3, B still held a leftover draft ('Reply with the single word ECHO.'). At the moment of Enter the screen already showed A: A's tab was highlighted and A's transcript was on screen. The composer read 'Reply with the single word ECHO.Count from 1 to 20 in Swedish words.' That merged 68-character text was queued into B and answered there as one turn. The user was looking at A and the prompt went to B.
- The click is acknowledged much later than 0.9 s. During a run, B stayed highlighted with its transcript for more than 2.6 s, and the view flipped about 4.4 s after the click. Idle, it took about 2 to 3 s. Until then the clicked tab shows only its dim focus style.
- Idle case: text typed 0.4 s after a tab click was lost from both composers. Its letters also fired screen bindings: the 'y' in the text opened the full-screen Trace view.

The finding's mechanism is wrong. The cause is not the `await begin_manual_read_visit` at session.py:2711:
- Key events bubble into ChatScreen's message queue, so they wait behind the awaited `on_button_pressed` tab handler anyway.
- The real cause is in `_activate_native_console_session`, which relies on `_sync_native_console_chat_ui()` to rebind the composer. When a console-sync pass is already running, that call returns immediately and only sets `_console_sync_requested` (chat_screen.py:18703-18708). This is routine during live runs.
- The pass already in flight ran `_sync_console_session_draft()` at its start, before the switch. So the composer and `_console_visible_draft_session_id` stay on the old session.
- That same pass then paints the new session's tabs and transcript (`_sync_console_native_session_tabs` and `_sync_native_console_transcript`), because they read the updated `store.active_session_id`.
- Enter pins the send to the stale `_console_visible_draft_session_id` (chat_screen.py:22799 and 19098-19104). `prompt_queue.dispatch` then queues it into the old session's live run.

Minor correction: the second draft was not 'restored asynchronously' by prompt_queue.py:918-924. The draft is never removed from the composer. In my run the second Enter was swallowed by the `_console_pending_send` duplicate-Enter guard, and the text simply stayed in B's composer.
expected: A tab click is acknowledged within 0.1 s. From then on, keystrokes and Enter belong to the tab that is visibly active, or are buffered for it. A prompt is never submitted into a chat the user is not looking at.
why: The user's prompt runs in the wrong conversation, with that chat's context, tools and approval authority. It spends tokens, pollutes one chat, and loses the turn from the other, and nothing on screen reveals it. I needed the app log to reconstruct where the prompts went. This breaks the core promise that 'each tab runs its own agent'.
repro: Profile ready, 235x52, proxy slow. Tab A: send a long prompt. Click tab B, wait about 2 s, type a prompt and press Enter. Then check tab labels (Q1 / ●) and both transcripts. Also: in A, press Enter on a second prompt within about 1 s of the first (it is refused), click B, type and press Enter.
recommendation: Make activation two-phase. Synchronously set the active session, tab highlight and composer binding BEFORE any await: move begin_manual_read_visit after switch_session, or off the critical path. While a switch is in flight, show the composer read-only as 'Opening <title>…' and buffer keystrokes into the target session's draft. In the submit path, assert that the composer's bound session id equals the visibly active tab, and refuse with an explicit message otherwise. Restore refused drafts only into their owning session's draft store, never into whatever composer is displayed.
fix_direction:
In `_activate_native_console_session`, bind the composer synchronously right after `controller.switch_session(session_id)`. Call `_sync_console_session_draft()`, or a dedicated rebind that saves the old draft to its owner and loads the new one, directly and before any await, so it never depends on the coalescable sync pass. Update the tab-strip active state in the same step, so the click is acknowledged in the same frame. Also:

- In the send path (the Enter handler and `_send_console_message_from_visible_action_observed`), refuse visibly and keep the draft when `_console_visible_draft_session_id != store.active_session_id`. Never queue into a session that is not the active tab.
- Keep typed keys going to the composer during a switch. Make session-tab buttons non-focusable on mouse click, or restore composer focus synchronously, so letters cannot fire single-key bindings.
- Moving `begin_manual_read_visit` after `switch_session` alone will NOT fix this.
- Add a regression test that holds a console-sync pass in flight (`_console_sync_in_progress=True`), activates another session, and asserts that the visible-draft session id, the tab highlight and the send target all equal the new session.
- Coordinate with TASK-26834 (switch latency) and TASK-32826.

title: Extends G2-04: closing a background tab that waits for approval shows a dialog that doesn't name the tab or the approval, then does nothing after 'Close'
expected: 'Close "Call the todo_create…"? 1 tool call waiting for your approval will be denied and its run cancelled.' Only non-zero items are listed. After Close, the tab closes, or a visible message says why it could not.
why: Users can't tell which tab they are closing. After confirming a destructive action they get no result and no explanation, and the background run keeps holding an approval they meant to abandon.
repro: Tab A: prompt that calls todo_create (slow proxy). Switch to B and wait for ◆ on A. Click A's ✕, read the dialog, click Close, wait 5 s.
recommendation: Put the tab title in the dialog title. Enumerate pending approvals, questions and skill confirms explicitly as consequences, and hide zero rows. After Close, either complete it or show a specific message ('Couldn't close: the run changed state — review again') that re-opens the dialog. Never return silently from a confirmed destructive action.
fix_direction:
1. Fix the regression: in session.py:2796 call the injected accessor, `self._console_runtime_accessor().close_session(...)` (or add a `_console_runtime` property that returns it), and add a test that runs the real ✕ press through the worker and asserts the tab is gone. The existing Tests/UI/test_console_character_avatar.py close tests call `_close_console_session_tab` directly and should already fail with AttributeError on dev; I read this from the code and did not run them, because the worktree is read-only.
2. Never fail silently: wrap the close flow so any exception is logged with context and shown as a specific toast, e.g. "Couldn't close 'X': …". Avoid bare `exit_on_error=False` for user-initiated destructive actions, or add a Worker ERROR handler.
3. Then fix the dialog copy: put the tab title in the dialog title, list only the non-zero consequences, and name the pending approvals, questions and skill confirmations explicitly ("1 tool call waiting for approval will be denied and its run cancelled"). Keep Stay as the default focus.

title: 'Return to transcript' from Terminal shows an empty chat: the tab strip is blank, the transcript says 'No messages yet.', and typing goes nowhere
statement:
The finding holds. Open the Terminal from the Context rail, even the unarmed view, then click 'Return to transcript'. The Console center comes back with the header still naming the active conversation ('Conversation | Reply with just the word AL...'). The tab strip, however, shows only 'New tab': the other tabs and the 'Temporary' button are gone. The transcript says 'No messages yet.' even though the chat has messages. This held 3 out of 3 times at 160x45 with no resize, and the screen stayed unchanged for at least 15 s without input.

Focus lands on the transcript title/surface, not the composer, so typed letters do not reach the composer. Most letters do nothing visible, but screen bindings still fire: typing 'y' opened the Trace view.

No data is lost. The tabs still exist (Ctrl+K lists 'Active (2)'), and a send made from this state goes to the right conversation and redraws the whole transcript. Recovery does not need Ctrl+K → Enter, contrary to the finding's "only" wording. Any later sync restores the tabs and transcript: sending a message, or opening and dismissing any modal or screen (Ctrl+K then Esc, or the Trace view then Esc). A user has no way to know this. The existing tests only check that the transcript widget exists and has focus after returning. They never compare tab labels or message count.
expected: Returning restores the same tabs, transcript and scroll position, and puts focus in the composer.
why: The user sees their conversation apparently wiped and their tabs gone right after using a host terminal, which invites panic, duplicate work or a 'Clear'. Focus is also lost.
repro: In a chat with messages, click 'Terminal' in the Context rail, then 'Return to transcript'.
recommendation: Keep the transcript center mounted and toggle it with display, or re-run the native session UI sync (tabs and transcript) after the swap. Focus the composer on return. Add a test comparing tab labels and message count before and after a Terminal round trip.
fix_direction: After mounting the transcript center in _swap_console_center, run the same native session UI sync that screen resume runs: tab strip sync_sessions plus a transcript refresh for the active session, and restore the captured reading state. A simpler alternative is to keep the transcript region mounted and toggle display between it and the Terminal workspace, so nothing is recomposed. On return, focus the composer, or at least have the transcript forward printable keys to it. Extend test_unarmed_terminal_replaces_only_center_and_return_restores_transcript to seed 2 tabs and N messages, then assert that the tab labels and the transcript message count match before and after the round trip.

title: Delete removes the selected message and every later turn, gives no visible first-press confirmation, and has no undo
statement: Confirmed live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c, with small corrections. I selected the 2nd of 5 turns ('Name one colour.') and chose More… › Delete. The first click changed no text at all (the capture is byte-identical to the selected state); the only visual change is focus returning to More…. The 'Press Delete again to remove this message.' copy appears only as a 'Delete confirmation' row in the Inspector's Selected Message section. The Inspector is collapsed by default, and even after opening it at 160x45 the row sits below the fold (about 20 wheel ticks down). Reopening More… still shows a plain 'Delete' item, with no pending state and no count. The second click removed the selected message, its reply and all three later turns, 8 messages in total, leaving only turn 1. The toast said 'Deleted message from transcript.' in the singular, and no Undo was offered. A second, spurious warning toast also appeared: 'Message deleted; recovered-media reference cleanup is pending.' This was a text-only chat with no media. In the DB all 8 rows are tombstoned (deleted=1, content kept). No message-undelete path exists in the DB, store or UI, so there is no in-app recovery. Every piece of in-app copy says 'this message' in the singular: the tooltip, the pending row and the receipt. The subtree scope is stated only in the User Guide (chat-basics.md:453, 480-484), and that guide also implies the 'Press Delete again' copy is visible. The image-rejection hint does direct users to Delete, which would remove every turn after an earlier image message. One correction to the prior-art triage: this is not a regression of in-transcript feedback. Commit 7829680c7a put the confirmation copy in the Inspector rows from the start (git show 7829680c7a), so the gap is long-standing.
expected: Before deleting, show the scope inline next to the message ('Delete this and 9 later messages? [Delete 10] [Cancel]'), offer 'Delete only this message' where the tree allows it, and follow with an Undo toast or receipt (the rows are tombstoned, so restore is feasible), matching the Archive receipt pattern.
why: One mistaken Delete silently destroys the rest of a conversation, which can be hours of agent work. The copy implies a single message was removed, and the UI offers no way back.
repro: In a conversation with several turns, click an early user message, open More…, choose Delete, then Delete again.
recommendation: Render the pending-delete state in the transcript row itself, not only in the Inspector. Include the subtree count in both the confirmation and the receipt. Add an Undo that restores the tombstones. Consider making Delete hide the branch (as rewind does) rather than tombstone it. Rewrite the image hint to name a non-destructive path ('Edit & resend without the image' or 'switch to a vision model'). The More-menu Delete should also sit in its own separated group (see G1-40).
fix_direction: 1. Render the pending-delete state on the selected transcript row itself, for example an inline strip: 'Delete this and N later messages? [Delete N] [Cancel]'. Take N from store.subtree_message_ids. Also reflect the pending state in the More… item label. 2. Make the receipt state the count ('Deleted 8 messages') and offer Undo that clears the tombstones for exactly subtree_ids and restores the prior active leaf. This needs a new persistence undelete for message subtrees, since none exists today. As an alternative, make Delete hide or branch like rewind does. 3. Rewrite _IMAGE_REJECTION_RECOVERY_HINT to point to a non-destructive path (Edit & resend without the image, or switch to a vision model). 4. Fix the spurious 'recovered-media reference cleanup is pending' warning when no recovered-media references exist. 5. Update chat-basics.md so it states where the confirmation appears. Add a test that asserts the confirmation text is visible in the transcript and not only in _last_console_action.

title: Fork fails on ordinary conversations: any System row (e.g. /help output) blocks it for the rest of the chat, and the error blames the selected message
statement:
Fork does not work on ordinary saved Console chats. Two independent defects cause this, and both reproduce live on origin/dev 64579cce2c.

(a) Fresh saved pair. In a saved chat whose turns were sent in the current app session, no message can be forked.
- The assistant row shows 'f Fork' in the guide with no warning, and the Fork button has normal styling. Pressing f or clicking Fork only shows the toast 'Saved Console fork parent is unavailable.'
- The user row shows 'f Fork' followed by 'Fork unavailable - Saved active leaf lineage is unavailable.'
- Cause: _hydrate_durable_turn_owner_messages (console_chat_store.py:6856-6899) sets persisted_message_id on the committed USER and ASSISTANT nodes but never sets their in-memory parent_message_id, which stays None. _fork_lineage_entry (7311-7318) then fails every assistant boundary, and _fork_database_active_leaf (7286-7293) fails every user boundary.
- The DB rows have the correct parent ids.
- Eligibility never checks the boundary's own parent, so the assistant row advertises Fork as available.
- Temporary chats are unaffected.
- Undiscoverable workaround: restart the app and reopen the chat. Fork then opens its dialog.

(b) Command output. /help, the unknown-command hint, /doctor and similar commands (63 call sites of _append_native_console_system_message) add SYSTEM nodes to the in-memory session tree. These nodes are persist=False, so they are not written to the DB.
- Every later user or assistant message then shows 'f Fork ... Fork unavailable - Only user and assistant messages can be forked.' (on an Assistant row), and pressing f repeats it. The Fork button is dimmed (#9e9e9e on #0d0d0d), but 'f Fork' stays in the guide.
- Messages before the SYSTEM row can still be forked.
- The block lasts until the conversation is reloaded from the DB, not for the life of the chat. After a restart the /help rows are gone and Fork works.
- ADR-092:44-50 and the fork spec :149-150 and :391 say these rows should be excluded, not treated as blockers.
expected: Fork works on a plain user/assistant exchange. Help, diagnostics and command feedback are ephemeral notices that never change what the user can do to the conversation. If a fork really is blocked, the reason names the actual obstacle and the nearest valid boundary ('Message 3 (a /help notice) can't be copied; fork from before it'). 'f Fork' is never shown as available when eligibility would fail.
why: Fork/branching is a headline Console feature. The command a learner is most likely to run (/help), or one mistyped /command, silently disables it with no visible link between cause and effect. The error text contradicts what the user sees, so users conclude the feature is broken.
repro: Ready mode 160x45: /help, Enter, Enter. Send 'Reply with exactly: hello there friend', click the reply, read the guide or press f. Control: Ctrl+T, send, click the reply (no error). Separately: in a new tab send 'Reply with exactly: alpha', select the reply, press f.
recommendation: Render /help, /doctor, skills listings, unknown-command hints and generation errors as display-only notices outside the canonical message tree (as the transcript already does for summary and memory banners), or exclude non-conversational SYSTEM notices from the fork prefix check. Investigate the parent-lineage mismatch for freshly persisted pairs ('Saved Console fork parent is unavailable.'). Reword every fork refusal to name the blocking row and a next step, and gate the 'f Fork' guide entry on real eligibility. Add regression tests for '/help, then fork' and for a fresh-pair fork.
fix_direction:
1. In _hydrate_durable_turn_owner_messages, after binding the persisted ids, set user.parent_message_id = acceptance/commit parent (or _nearest_persisted_ancestor_id) and assistant.parent_message_id = commit.user_message_id. This mirrors publish_first_persisted_conversation (19186-19197) and the recovery path (16146-16147). Add a regression test: natural durable send, then fork_eligibility and the fork confirmation on both the assistant and the user boundary, with no reload.
2. Make the fork prefix walk skip non-conversational SYSTEM, TOOL and display-only nodes, as ADR-092 and the spec require. Alternatively, stop putting command feedback into the canonical tree and render it as ephemeral notices, like the summary/memory banners. Add a regression test: /help, then send, then fork.
3. When a refusal is unavoidable, name the blocking row and give the nearest valid boundary. Keep the guide's 'f Fork' in step with real eligibility, including the lineage-entry parent check, so Fork is never advertised as available when it would fail.

title: Replies are not streamed: 'Generating…' for the whole run, then the full text appears at once
statement: With default settings, Console replies from cloud providers (Anthropic, OpenAI and the other cloud templates) are not streamed. The row shows 'Assistant Generating…' for the whole provider call, then the full text appears in one frame. The cause is a configuration default, not AgentService code. The shipped config template sets streaming = false under [api_settings.anthropic], [api_settings.openai] and the other cloud provider sections, and [chat_defaults] has no streaming key. So the Console session settings resolve Streaming to Off, and Settings > Advanced generation shows 'Streaming Off'. The streaming=False literal at agent_service.py:3155 has no effect: _StreamingModelAdapter (console_agent_bridge.py:3074) ignores it and streams every primary turn live, through the fence-gate, to store.append_stream_chunk whenever the session's Streaming setting is On. With Streaming switched On for the conversation, text arrived progressively in the running app, with a 'Streaming…' header label and partial text visible mid-run. This is not a regression from cd7cc231aab: that commit only wrapped the call in try/finally, and the literal dates to 53d077de6d (2026-07-13). The real user-facing problem has three parts. Out of the box, cloud replies arrive whole with no progress beyond 'Generating…' and 'Running'. The Streaming state is invisible outside the settings modal and the Inspector (TASK-338). The User Guide (chat-basics.md:322-328 and 462-467) promises streaming, a '[streaming]' suffix and a partial reply kept on Stop, and none of these hold at default settings. The suffix copy is also stale: the UI now shows a 'Streaming…' header label.
expected: Tokens render progressively, with the fence-gate holding back only tool-call spans. A '[streaming]' marker shows, and Stop keeps the partial text.
why: Long answers look frozen, sometimes for tens of seconds. Users cannot start reading early, judge whether to stop, or tell a slow run from a stalled one.
repro: Ready 235x52, proxy mode drip. Ask for a 60-line list and poll the transcript.
recommendation: Stream the primary model call through the existing agent_stream fence-gate and push deltas to the transcript row. At minimum, show live progress (bytes or tokens received, elapsed time). If non-streaming is intentional, update the guide.
fix_direction: Do not rewire AgentService: the adapter already streams through the agent_stream fence-gate. Treat it as a product default decision instead. (1) Decide whether Console should stream by default for cloud providers, for example by adding streaming = true to the shipped [chat_defaults], which outranks the per-provider template. First land or confirm TASK-2122, because default-off is what currently keeps usage and cost capture accurate for 8 providers; Anthropic streaming usage is already captured. Also fix the Mistral template inconsistency noted there. (2) Whatever the default, make the non-streamed path honest: add an elapsed counter to 'Generating…' (as 'Connecting tools… · Ns' already has), and show Streaming on/off on the rail or status bar (TASK-338). (3) Update chat-basics.md:322-328 and 462-467 to say that live streaming depends on the Streaming setting (and state its default for cloud and local providers), that Stop keeps a partial reply only when streaming, and that the in-flight marker is the 'Streaming…' header label, not a '[streaming]' suffix.

title: Dictate and Hands-free stick on '◐ Preparing speech model…' after the model load fails; the Dictate label hides that pressing it cancels
statement:
On macOS, when the parakeet-mlx model is not cached (a fresh machine), Dictate and Hands-free show '◐ Preparing speech model…' indefinitely. The model is not downloading. It is deadlocked.

Mechanism:
- Inside the Textual app, the first Hugging Face fetch raises 'ValueError: bad value(s) in fds_to_keep'. tqdm tries to create a multiprocessing lock, and Textual's stderr capture reports fileno() as -1.
- parakeet-mlx swallows that error and falls back to a local path. That fallback produces the misleading "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'mlx-community/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2/config.json'".
- tqdm's class-level thread lock stays held by the dead warm-up thread.
- The warm-up failure is treated as degraded (WARMUP_DEGRADED_REASON_TEMPLATE), so start_dictation goes ahead and loads the streaming model. That load blocks forever at tqdm/std.py:96. The .incomplete blob stays at 0 bytes.

What the user sees:
- About 2 s after the click, two toasts appear together. One says 'Preparing the speech model for the first time… can take several minutes'. The other is a warning: "Could not pre-load the 'parakeet-mlx' speech model; the first part of this capture may be slow. Failed to load model: [Errno 2] … Check the transcription provider and model in Settings…". Both disappear within about 5–8 s. The warning says the capture is still going ahead, which is false.
- After that the chip reads 'Preparing speech model…' with no progress, no size and no further error. It was still up at 90 s in this run, and 52 minutes later in an earlier session.
- A second press in the same process shows no failure toast at all. The warm-up itself now deadlocks, and only the 'can take several minutes' toast appears.
- While preparing, the button reads 'Dictate', the same as idle. The designed 'Dictate…' ellipsis is not rendered. Only the tooltip says 'Preparing the speech model — press to cancel.' Pressing it gives 'Dictation cancelled.' and clears the chip.

Hands-free:
- It starts the same model fetch without asking and raises both toasts at once.
- Esc does turn the Switch OFF. But the capture it started stays in 'starting', because _console_hands_free_close_capture only stops a 'recording' capture. Teardown then re-syncs 'starting', so the chip keeps reading 'Preparing speech model…' (47 s later here, 52 min in the earlier session).
- The Dictate tooltip still says 'press to cancel'. Only a Dictate press ends the capture.
expected: A failed warm-up shows one plain error with a next step ('Retry / Choose provider in Settings ▸ Speech & TTS'). A long download shows size and progress with a labelled Cancel. The button reads 'Cancel' while preparing, and the status clears when the mode exits.
why: The user cannot tell whether dictation is working, downloading or broken, and the visible 'Dictate' button does the opposite of its label.
repro: ready (no speech model cached): click Dictate, wait 30 s, click again; toggle Hands-free, press Esc.
recommendation: On warm-up failure, leave the starting state and show a recovery callout. Label the starting button 'Cancel' (or 'Preparing… ✕'). Add a download size and progress line, and one-time consent for model downloads matching Speak replies' consent. Clear the voice chip when Hands-free exits. Strip errno values and paths from toasts and keep them in Logs.
fix_direction:
1. Make the model fetch work inside the TUI. Options: set HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 (or disable huggingface_hub progress bars) before any in-app download; pre-create tqdm's lock (tqdm.set_lock with a threading RLock) at startup, before Textual captures stderr; or run the download with the Console's own progress reporting.
2. Classify a load failure (model could not be fetched or loaded) as fatal, not degraded. When the warm-up fails because the model is missing, _fail() with a single plain message and a next step (Retry / choose provider in Settings ▸ Speech & TTS). Do not show 'capture may be slow'.
3. Bound the preparing phase. Add a watchdog, or a progress check that watches the HF .incomplete file size, so a stuck load turns into an error instead of an endless chip. Show the download size and progress when a download is really running.
4. On Hands-free exit (_console_hands_free_close_capture), cancel a 'starting' capture too (_request_console_dictation_cancel), so the chip clears when the mode ends.
5. Make the preparing state's button label say it cancels (for example 'Cancel' or 'Preparing ✕'), and make sure the label fits within the width-11 button.
6. Keep errno values and paths out of toasts and in Logs. Optionally ask for one-time consent before a large first-run model download.

title: After Stop, tool rows, Inspect, status strip and left rail still claim a pending approval and a running agent while Alt+A says none is pending
expected: Stop is one state transition: within 0.1-1 s every surface shows Stopped and pending-approval affordances are withdrawn.
why: After stopping, the operator sees 'action required' for an approval that no longer exists and cannot tell whether the stop worked or whether tools may still run.
repro: ready 235x52: send a todo prompt; at the approval card click 'Composer ▾' ▸ Stop; capture immediately and at +15 s; press Alt+A.
recommendation: On Stop, synchronously clear app.pending_console_approval / console_pending_approval_count and set every Queued/Awaiting tool row to Stopped in the same UI turn, before the async cancel completes. Drive the Inspect summary, status chip and left-rail Agent line from one run-state source. Add a regression test that no 'Awaiting approval'/'pending' text remains one frame after Stop.
fix_direction:
Make Stop converge by construction, not by timing.

1. When an interrupt round tears down, and when the agent bridge publishes a terminal live snapshot, request a coalesced Console resync (_request_console_control_bar_sync / _request_console_agent_fleet_sync plus the inspector/status sync) through call_from_thread.
2. Keep the transcript poll alive (or schedule one trailing sync) until the session's bridge worker has actually returned, instead of stopping on controller run_state alone.
3. Make the approval wait wake on the round's cancel_event instead of a 1 s poll, so the card and its live Approve/Submit/Deny buttons are withdrawn within one frame of Stop.
4. Derive the Inspect 'Run'/'Approvals' lines, the status chip and the left-rail Agent line from the same live source that Alt+A reads (_console_pending_approval_count() and the bridge snapshot) at paint time.

Do not blindly relabel tool rows 'Stopped' in the UI before the round is actually cancelled. The worker's _on_outcome can still commit a decision that landed in that window.

Regression test: stop while an approval round is pending, with the worker's cancel detection deliberately delayed past the transcript poll's stop. After the worker returns, assert that no 'Awaiting approval', 'pending · action required', 'Waiting for approval' or 'Agent: running' text remains, without any further user input.

title: Trace records a user Stop as 'Approval denied', a stopped reply as 'Complete', and policy auto-allows as 'Approval granted'
statement:
In the Console run trace (Y), approval and stop events carry no decider, so the trace misstates who decided.

(1) Auto-allowed call. For a built-in with permission 'allow' (get_current_datetime), no card appears and the status bar reads 'Approvals: 0 pending' throughout. The trace still records 'Approval requested for get_current_datetime · Pending' and then 'Approval granted · Approved', with 'actor agent <run-uuid>'. That detail pane has the same fields as a real human 'Approve all → Submit' grant of todo_create (#73). In this run the request and the grant fell in the same second; the finding's '3 s later' is incidental.

(2) Stop during approval. I pressed Stop while three todo_create calls were awaiting approval. The trace then shows:
- the assistant message as 'Complete' with an empty summary;
- three 'Approval denied for todo_create · Denied' rows (actor agent, no reason);
- 'Agent run cancelled'.

Two other surfaces get this right:
- The transcript shows 'Assistant Stopped', each call 'Stopped', and a System line 'Response stopped by user.'
- The app's own MCP ▸ Audit ▸ Executions log lists the same three calls as 'Denied (no decision)'.

So the trace contradicts both.

Three details in the finding go too far:
- The trace does say the run was 'Cancelled' (rows 33 and 52). It never says who stopped it, so 'no row states why the run ended' overstates the gap.
- The detail rows say 'actor agent', not 'you'. The trace is ambiguous about who decided; it does not claim the user denied.
- The quoted promise ('each approval remains explicit and auditable') is in Docs/User_Guide/console/agent-runs-and-tools.md:5, not a Watchlists guide.
expected: Each decision names who made it ('Allowed by policy (no prompt)', 'Approved by you (Once)', 'Denied by you', 'Withdrawn — run stopped by you'). A stopped reply reads 'Stopped', and a terminal 'Run ended: stopped by you at 12:16:02' row closes the turn.
why: The Watchlists guide promises approvals stay 'explicit and auditable'. Reading this trace after an incident, an operator would conclude they denied calls they never denied and approved calls they never saw.
repro: Run the datetime prompt, y, Enter on 'Approval granted'; send a todo prompt, stop while awaiting approval, y, scroll to Turn 3.
recommendation: Add decided_by (policy | user | stop | timeout | kill_switch) to approval steps and render it in the Summary. Emit no Pending request step for calls that never prompt. Label a stopped assistant turn 'Stopped', and append a terminal 'why it ended' row in user language.
fix_direction:
1. Carry the decider through to the trace step: add decided_by (policy | user | stop | timeout | kill_switch | guard) to the STEP_APPROVAL_* payload. Reuse the existing ApprovalDecisions.unresolved_keys and the builtin_gate state instead of inventing new plumbing. Render it in the row summary using the vocabulary the MCP Audit mode already uses ('Denied (no decision)', 'Denied by you', 'Allowed by policy').
2. Do not emit a 'Pending' Approval-requested step for calls the hook resolves without prompting. Either have the hook report which calls it will prompt for, or emit the request step only for calls that end up on a card. Record auto-allowed calls as one 'Allowed by policy (no prompt)' step.
3. Persist a 'stopped' status on the assistant message when the run is cancelled, so trajectory.py stops falling back to 'complete'.
4. Give the 'Agent run cancelled' row a user-language reason, e.g. 'Stopped by you'.
5. Add a regression test that drives an 'allow' built-in and a Stop-while-awaiting-approval through run_agent_loop, then asserts the decider on the emitted trace steps.

title: A failed sub-agent is reported as 'done'; its cause is buried in the left rail, misattributed to the provider, and out of order
statement:
When a spawned sub-agent fails, the Console never states its status or cause consistently, and the cause is hard to reach. It happens every time on this commit: the child fails in about 0.7s before any provider dispatch, with a local "Provider call trace persistence failed."

The same failed child gets five different status words:
(1) The transcript spawn marker reads "Sub-agent · done". This is the spawn step: expanded, it reads "spawned sub-agent: ...". The word "done" comes from classify_activity_status, which returns "done" for any step that is not a tool result.
(2) The wait_agents and check_agents chips read "Succeeded" with a green tint, although their text says "[id] sub-agent — error".
(3) The Inspect Agents header reads "✗ 0 working, 1 done". The ✗ is neutral grey, and the count puts every terminal status, failed included, under "done". Past four rows the glyphs are dropped entirely.
(4) The Inspect row itself does say failure, in red ("✗ ~<1s · ..." / "Agent run failed · Budget unavailable"). The secondary line shows the budget label, not the cause.
(5) The drill-in header reads "Sub-agent · error (Back)".

The cause is only reachable by clicking the row. That click empties and hides the whole Inspect Agents section and puts the detail in the LEFT rail's Agent section. That section is collapsed by default, so in a fresh session the click shows no visible result: the Agents section just vanishes.

Once found, the detail is raw event keys in storage-index order rather than time order: context_attached, context_injected, model_request_started, model_error, then "error: unexpected provider error (Provider call trace persistence failed.)", and only then agent_run_reserved, agent_run_created, agent_run_started, agent_run_failed. The persisted created_at and owner_seq values put reserved, created and started first. A local failure (the provider was never contacted) is worded as a provider error.

The parent then answered 391 itself.
expected: A failed child reads 'failed' everywhere and is never counted as done. Its row carries a one-line cause in user terms and a next action, and details are listed in chronological order.
why: The fleet view is how users know which delegated work actually happened. 'done' plus a hidden, misattributed cause sends them off to debug the provider.
repro: ready 235x52 with Inspect open: 'Use spawn_subagent to start one sub-agent that computes 17*23 with the calculator, then tell me its result.'; read the transcript, then the Inspect Agents section; click the row and read the left rail.
recommendation: Count terminal statuses separately ('1 failed'). Use the same status word on the transcript and Inspect rows. Put the cause, not the budget, in the secondary line. Classify local persistence failures as local. Render the drill-in in the Inspect rail next to the clicked row, in chronological order and human wording.
fix_direction: Count terminal statuses separately in the fleet header (for example "1 failed", with glyph colour matching the row). Give the transcript spawn marker a spawn-specific word ("spawned"), or update it to the child's final outcome. Style a wait_agents or check_agents result whose child errored as a warning. Put a one-line human cause and a next action in the fleet row's secondary line, and keep the budget label for successful runs. Classify TraceCallPersistenceError, and any other pre-dispatch local error, as a local failure ("could not record the provider call locally; the provider was not contacted") rather than "unexpected provider error". Render the drill-in in place in the Inspect rail next to the clicked row; failing that, auto-expand and scroll the left Agent section and leave a pointer in Inspect. List events by created_at or owner_seq with human labels. Separately, investigate why every sub-agent model call fails pre-dispatch with a trace-persistence error on 64579cce2c, since that makes this path the default experience.

title: The Trace table truncates mid-word, runs columns together, duplicates and misorders events, and ignores the available width
statement: At 235 and 120 columns the Event column truncates without an ellipsis ('Retrieval star', 'Approval reque', 'Agent run crea', 'Model first to'). Summary runs into State with no gap ('model request starteStarted', 'get_current_datetimeProposed'). Column widths are identical at both sizes, leaving over half of 235 columns empty. One tool call yields 28 records, including duplicates ('Model response complete' plus 'model Observed'; 'Tool call'/'Tool result' re-listed as rows 26-27 after 'Agent run completed', out of time order). Retrieval rows start before the user message. The header reads 'LIVE · PAUSED'. Detail panes lead with raw UUIDs and event ids. A 'Building trace…' toast overlays rows after the trace has rendered, and the detail pane covers the table so the selected row is hidden.
expected: Flexible columns that fill the width, with ellipsis and a gutter. Deduplicated, time-ordered rows, and a default 'story' view (user message → model → tool proposed → decision → result → answer → end reason) with raw events behind a toggle.
why: The data needed to answer 'what did the agent do, in order, and why did it stop' is present, but the presentation makes that slow and error-prone.
repro: After two tool runs, select a message, press y, read Turn 1; resize to 120x40 and press y again.
recommendation: Make Event and Summary 1fr columns with ellipsis, keep numeric columns fixed, and add a gutter. Collapse Observed/duplicate projection rows into their primary event behind a 'Raw events' filter. Sort by timestamp. Replace 'LIVE · PAUSED' with 'Paused — f to follow'. Dismiss the build toast once rows render. Lead detail panes with the human summary and the decider, with ids last.

title: Approval-card consequence copy is generic and sometimes wrong, 'Always' points to the wrong place, and one call gets five buttons
statement: todo_create (a session-only task) is labelled with source 'Local workspace, web, and Watchlists' and 'Effects: may modify local data'. watchlists_create_collection is a durable DB write marked DEFINITIVE_AFTER_START (cannot be abandoned once started), yet it gets the identical 'Effects: may modify local data', with nothing about durability, reversibility or cancellability. Choosing 'Always' says 'Change it under MCP ▸ Permissions' for a local, non-MCP tool. A single pending call shows 'Once ▼' plus 'Approve once', 'Deny', 'Approve all', 'Submit' and 'Deny all': five buttons and three names for approving, and 'Submit' doesn't say what it submits. After Deny the transcript shows model-directed text: 'tool call denied by the user: … Do not retry this call, do not rephrase it, and do not pursue the same outcome by another route.… (+33 chars)'.
expected: The effects line says what changes and whether it persists or can be undone. Scope copy names the real settings place. A single call shows Approve / Deny / scope only; bulk controls appear for 2+ calls as 'Apply N decisions'. The transcript shows 'Denied by you'.
why: This card is the main safety moment. Uniform effect copy removes the information needed to decide, and redundant buttons slow every decision.
repro: Trigger todo_create (3 calls) and watchlists_create_collection (1 call); compare the cards; pick 'Always'; Deny the Watchlists call.
recommendation: Add per-tool human effect strings (persistence, reversibility, cancellability) and per-provider source labels ('Session tasks', 'Watchlists'). Point 'Always' at the real settings surface for the tool family. Show bulk controls only for >1 pending call, with Submit renamed 'Apply N decisions'. Render denials as 'Denied by you', with the model instruction behind the expand.

title: Focus is lost, with no visible indicator, after approving a tool call
statement: Alt+A → Tab → Enter on 'Approve once' worked, and Alt+A correctly focused the scope select. When the card then unmounted, nothing showed focus: the composer edge stayed dim '│', and the only focus-styled element was the always-on active tab. Typing 'z' went into the composer because keystrokes route there when focus is None, but that routing is invisible.
expected: After the decision, focus moves explicitly and visibly to the composer or the resolved tool row, with a brief transcript confirmation.
why: The approval loop is the core agentic interaction, and afterwards a keyboard user can't tell where they are or what Enter will do.
repro: Trigger todo_update; Alt+A, Tab, Enter; look for a focus indicator.
recommendation: When an approval card resolves, call _focus_console_workbench_target('console-native-composer') or focus the resolved tool row, and show an inline 'Approved · todo_create' confirmation.

title: Alt+A says 'No approval is pending' while another tab is waiting for approval; every approval indicator in the viewed tab reads zero
statement:
When tab A is parked on an approval (todo_create), pressing Alt+A in tab B shows a warning toast saying 'No approval is pending.' Clicking B's 'Approvals: 0 pending' status chip shows the same toast. The same happens whether B was opened before A's card appeared or after the user had viewed A's card and switched back. B's session-scoped readouts all read zero or idle: the status chip says 'Approvals: 0 pending', the header pill says 'Ready', and Inspect says 'Run: Ready', 'Approvals: None pending', 'Live work: No active work' and 'approvals 0'. None of them separates 'here' from 'elsewhere'. Clicking the ◆ tab does activate A and focus its card, so the ◆ tab and Alt+A give opposite answers. This contradicts the User Guide, which says Alt+A 'jumps to the pending approval from anywhere in Console'.

Correction to the title: not every indicator in B reads zero. At 235 columns the left rail shows the fleet line '0 other agents running, 1 waiting for approval.' and A's row with ✋ 'Approval required'. The nav button reads 'Console !' at every width, and Ctrl+K opens the switcher with a 'WAITING FOR YOU · APPROVAL' section on top. At 120x40 the rail collapses, the Approvals chip is cut off, and the footer shrinks to 'Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q', so the Alt+A hint is gone. That leaves the ◆ tab marker and the non-specific 'Console !' badge as the only passive signals. The ◆ is not the only one, as the finding claimed. The warning toast is the only false statement. The other readouts are scoped to the chat but do not say so.
expected: The global approval key reaches ANY pending decision, in whichever tab it lives, or at least says where it is ('1 approval waiting in <title> — Alt+A to open'). Counts in the viewed tab distinguish 'here' from 'elsewhere'.
why: The keyboard-first operator is told nothing is waiting while an agent is blocked on them. The footer advertises Alt+A as the approval route, and at 120 columns the Approvals chip and Alt+A hint are already gone, so the tiny ◆ is the only true signal.
repro: Tab A: 'Call the todo_create tool once with content alpha task' (slow proxy). Switch to B, wait for ◆ on A, then press Alt+A and read the strip, header and Inspect.
recommendation: When the active tab has no decision card, route Alt+A (and Inspect 'Review approval' and the Approvals chip) through the same branch the ◆ tab click uses: activate the oldest NEEDS_APPROVAL session and focus its card, with a toast naming the chat, cycling if there are several. Make the Approvals chip and Inspect line report 'N here · M in other tabs', and keep the header pill from saying plain 'Ready' while any tab waits for the human.
fix_direction: In _route_console_pending_approval_focus, when no displayed card is found, ask the controller for a live session whose run_marker_for is NEEDS_APPROVAL (the oldest, cycling on repeat presses). Activate it through _session._activate_native_console_session, as the ◆ tab branch does, then focus its card with a toast naming the chat. If there truly is none anywhere, keep the current warning. Point ConsoleApprovalsChip's private _focus_pending_approval_card at the same seam so the entry points cannot drift. Make the chip and Inspect wording scope-explicit using fleet_summary_counts(), for example 'Approvals: 0 here · 1 in other tabs' or 'None in this chat · 1 waiting in <title>'. Optionally keep the header pill from reading plain 'Ready' while other tabs wait. Add a test that parks an approval in a non-active session and asserts that Alt+A activates it rather than notifying.

title: Every approved file-tool call failed with 'Private scratch space is unavailable', even calls aimed at the bound project folder, and nothing was logged
statement:
The copy and logging defects are real; the headline is not. In the review harness, every approved fs_* call fails because of how the harness environment is installed. It is not a product regression.

What is real, reproduced live on origin/dev 64579cce2c:
- In a workspace with proj-alpha bound, two approved fs_list calls (path "." and root_alias folder-4979b364c454) each ended "Blocked · 1.0s" with "ERROR: Private scratch space is unavailable; the tool was not run."
- Neither call touched scratch. In a Console primary run the only fs_* authorities are bound folders, and a local bound-folder authority has authority_scope=None, so no scratch lease was involved.
- The string comes from _workspace_execution_error_reason. It maps every WorkspaceToolExecutor code except root_pin_failed, invalid_request and tool_failure to AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE, and that reason renders the one scratch-blaming string.
- Nothing is logged. The worker's stderr is discarded unread, and the executor error code is thrown away.
- The model then gave false advice: "check your workspace connection or try again in a moment."

What is wrong in the finding:
- The 5-of-5 failure and "the coding-agent core is unusable" come from the review environment. The shared .venv's editable install maps tldw_chatbook to the deleted worktree .worktrees/task-2512-mcp-unified. The executor starts its worker as `python -I -m tldw_chatbook.Tools.workspace_tool_worker`, and -I ignores the cwd, so the worker fails with ModuleNotFoundError and that failure becomes worker_crashed.
- The app itself imports fine only because launch.sh runs it from the worktree directory. In a normal `pip install -e .` install, the worker imports.
- So this is not evidence of a TASK-21161 regression.
- The recommendation to "log the lease failure" targets the wrong layer. The lease is not what fails.
expected: An approved call runs. If the authority really is unavailable, the error names the actual root (the bound folder or scratch), the reason, and the fix (for example 'proj-alpha isn't selected for this chat — Choose folder'), and the failure is logged.
why: The coding-agent core (read, edit, write files) was unusable in every session tried, and the message sends the user after the wrong resource. Part of the root cause may be specific to this environment, but the generic copy and the silent fail-closed are real regardless.
repro: W1 with proj-alpha bound read-write and Change Review on. Ask 'Write a new file notes.txt containing hi in your private scratch space', or 'list the files in the project folder', and click 'Approve once'.
recommendation: Log the lease failure (type and alias) at warning level. Split AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE into scratch versus bound-folder copy that names the folder and a next step. Show a user-facing row summary instead of the model string. Verify fs_* end to end in the isolated review harness, where it failed 5 out of 5 times.
fix_direction:
1. Log each non-success WorkspaceToolExecutionError at warning level. Include the code, the tool name, the root alias or binding id, and a bounded, redacted head of the worker's stderr. Do the same in the two bare-except lease branches, logging the exception type.
2. Replace the single AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE copy with per-cause copy for the model and the user:
   - The worker could not start or crashed (spawn_failed, worker_crashed, protocol_failure).
   - The operation timed out (worker_timed_out).
   - Sandbox containment is unavailable (containment_unavailable).
   - Scratch was revoked (ConsoleScratchSpaceUnavailable).
   Name the actual root ("proj-alpha" or the alias) and never say "scratch" for a bound-folder authority.
3. Narrow the `except Exception` around `with authority_scope(): return _invoke_allowed()`. It currently turns any error inside _invoke_allowed into "scratch unavailable".
4. Add a startup or first-use self-check that the isolated worker module can be imported with `-I`. On failure, show one clear diagnosis ("File tools unavailable: the tool worker could not start. Reinstall with pip install -e .") instead of a message on every call.
5. Separately, fix the harness venv (reinstall editable from a live tree) before any further live fs_* review.

title: Extends G3-06: an approval that auto-denied on timeout is traced as 'Approval granted · Approved', and the row says 'Blocked · 0.3s' with a model-directed ERROR line
statement: With approval_timeout_seconds=30, an fs_list card counted down to zero. The transcript row became '▸ fs_list · Blocked · 0.3s' plus 'ERROR: user did not approve within the time limit; do not retry'. 'Blocked' is the same label used for authority failures, and 0.3s ignores the 30 s wait. The Trace for the same call lists 'Approval requested… Pending' (15:04:30), then 'Approval granted for… Approved' (15:05:01), then 'fs_list blocked'. After the timeout, focus dropped to the transcript, so the next typed message fired single-letter commands and opened two stacked Edit Message modals, and later collapsed the composer (G3-15 and G4-12 recurring on the timeout path).
expected: The row reads something like 'Auto-denied — no decision within 30 s' with the true elapsed time and a one-click 'Ask again'. Trace records the approval as timed out or denied. Focus returns to the composer.
why: A user who stepped away comes back to an error that reads like a fault and a Trace that says they approved it. The audit trail is wrong in the direction that matters most.
repro: Set [mcp] approval_timeout_seconds=30, trigger any Ask-gated tool, wait 30 s, then open Trace ('y' in the transcript).
recommendation: Record the invoke-path decision (timed-out, denied, approved) as the Trace decision step. Add a distinct 'Timed out' row state and copy, with duration measured from the request. After a card resolves by any path, focus the composer.
