title: Extends G3-14: Alt+A lands on the scope dropdown, the countdown runs during a 3+ key approval, and the green 'Approve once' button ignores an 'Always' selection
statement: Alt+A focuses the per-row Select ('Once ▼'). Enter opens a dropdown (Once / This session / Always / Deny) over the card's buttons. Approving by keyboard then needs Enter, Tab and Enter while the countdown keeps running: it reached 'Auto-denies in 0:05' during the attempt and auto-denied. Separately, choosing 'Always · these args' in the Select leaves the adjacent green button labelled 'Approve once'. Its tooltip says it 'skips Select + Submit', so clicking the most prominent button discards the scope the user just chose. 'Submit' in the batch row is what applies it.
expected: One decision model per card. The primary button's label follows the chosen scope ('Approve · Always (these args)'), and Alt+A focuses a decision with visible key hints. The countdown pauses while the card has focus, or can be extended.
why: The user picks 'Always' and gets 'Once', or the reverse by mistake. Keyboard-first users lose approvals to the clock.
repro: With an MCP approval pending: press Alt+A, then Enter. Separately, choose 'Always · these args' and read the green button.
recommendation: For single-call cards, drop Submit and the fast pair in favour of one primary that reflects the Select, or remove the Select and offer explicit buttons (Once / This session / Always / Deny) with key hints. Pause the auto-deny timer while the card has focus, and offer '+2 min'.
evidence: evidence/GAP4/77a-before-alta.ansi vs 77b-after-alta.ansi (sgr diff: focus ring on the Select)
evidence/GAP4/101-mcp-always-selected.txt ('Always · these args' next to 'Approve once')

title: MCP tool definition changes aren't surfaced: calls kept auto-running until a hidden per-server refresh, then re-asked with no '(definition changed)' reason
statement: stamp_text was allowed with 'Always · these args'. The server's schema and description then changed (it added a 'loud' parameter). Two further identical calls ran without a card. The Hub's overview 'r refresh' did not re-list tools, and MCP ▸ Tools still showed the old description. Only the per-server 'Refresh tools' button did, after which the grant was silently invalidated and the card re-asked plainly as 'uxstamp · stamp_text' with no '(definition changed)' badge or reason line. The card code has that badge and copy ready.
expected: Tool definitions are refreshed per run, or on any refresh. When a remembered decision is invalidated by a definition change, the card shows 'uxstamp · stamp_text (definition changed)' and 'Definition changed since you last allowed it; review the arguments.'
why: The protection exists in code but never reaches the user. An 'Always' grant silently keeps covering a changed tool, and when it finally lapses the re-prompt looks arbitrary.
repro: Add a stdio MCP server, allow its tool 'Always · these args', change the server's inputSchema, and call it again. Then use Servers ▸ server ▸ Refresh tools and call it again.
recommendation: Set config_changed for any invalidated grant, exact-args included. Make the overview 'Refresh' re-list tools, or rename one of the two refresh actions so they differ. Re-list catalogs at run start, or compare definition hashes on each call.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/Agents/mcp_tool_provider.py:252-257 (reason comes only from tool-level config_changed, not exact-args grants)

title: File-tool approvals don't say which folder a path is in, and a write looks the same as a read
statement: The cards show raw arguments only: '{"path":"."}', '{"path":"notes.txt","content":"hi"}', and '{"path":"proj-alpha/calc.py","root_alias":"folder-aedcecbb8f68"}'. The alias is an opaque hash. No card says private scratch versus the proj-alpha binding, or whether that binding is read-only or read-write. The fs_write card ('Effects: may modify local data') has the same frame, green primary, 'Once' preselect and weight as the fs_read card ('may read private local data'). No '(high risk)' badge appears at the default Ask setting. MCP rows carry no Effects line and no description at all.
expected: A resolved target ('proj-alpha (read-write) › calc.py' or 'Private scratch › notes.txt'), a content preview or diff for writes and edits, visually stronger treatment for mutating calls, and the server's description with 'external tool — effects unknown' for MCP rows.
why: Informed consent needs the object of the action. 'Approve fs_write notes.txt' without a root is a guess, and the user can't tell a read from an overwrite at a glance.
repro: In a workspace with a bound folder, ask the agent to read, then write, a file, and compare the cards. Then call an MCP tool.
recommendation: Resolve the path against the frozen authority (alias to binding label and access mode) on the card. Render writes and edits with a bounded preview or diff, using a distinct warning frame and no preselected Approve. Show the tool description (capped) for MCP.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Chat_Widgets/chat_approval_card.py:317-335 (header: server · tool plus reason badges only)

title: 'Send project instructions?' interrupts every new chat even when there is nothing to send (0 bytes), shows a raw session UUID, and the turn meanwhile says 'Generating…'
statement: The first send in each new chat (the resumed W1 chat and a fresh tab) paused about 25 s ('Connecting tools… · 11s', then 'Generating…') before the modal 'Send project instructions?' appeared. It showed 'Session: 26789c27-faef-4c2a-b514-a346f5ac9848', 'Root source: No root file found · scope . · 0 bytes', and asked to Proceed, Cancel or Disable. The transcript said 'Generating…' while the run was actually waiting on this decision.
expected: No prompt when there are 0 bytes to send, or a one-line non-modal note. When a prompt is needed, it names the chat and folder rather than a UUID, and the turn status reads 'Waiting for your decision'.
why: A consent dialog with no content trains people to click through consent dialogs, and the wrong status adds to G1-24.
repro: In W1 (folder bound, no AGENTS.md), open a new tab and send a message that uses tools.
recommendation: Skip the notice when byte_count is 0 and there are no warnings. Replace 'Session: <uuid>' with the chat title and binding label. Project the turn phase as awaiting the user while this modal is open.

title: ask_user questions show as 'Approval required' ✋ in the Workspaces tree and tab marker, the card has no way to decline, and each surface names the state differently
statement: While the ask_user card ('The agent has 1 question for you:', Red / Blue / Other…, Submit) was open, the tree row read 'Approval requi…✋'. The status strip said 'Run: Waiting for your answer.', and the pin said 'Run: Blocked · Approvals: None pending'. The card has only 'Submit': there is no Skip, Decline or 'Let the agent decide', and Enter is bound with priority to submit. Its rounded amber frame differs from the approval card's heavy frame.
expected: A distinct 'Question for you' attention fact and glyph on the tab, tree and pin, and a visible 'Skip question' that continues the run without an answer.
why: The user looks for an approval that doesn't exist and can't refuse a question they don't want to answer.
repro: Ask the agent to use ask_user, then look at the tree row, status strip and pin.
recommendation: Add a 'question' attention kind with its own label and glyph. Add a 'Skip' button that returns unanswered:true. Unify the card frame with the approval card (see GAP4-16).

title: Extends G3-28: the six inline agent-decision cards use four header grammars, four approve verbs, four remember-scope names and two frame styles
statement: Headers: approval 'Approval required'; ask_user 'The agent has 1 question for you:'; skill install 'An agent wants to install a skill:'; skill script 'An agent wants to run a script from a skill:'; chat create 'An agent wants to {verb}: {title}'; worktree 'Merge agent work into this repository?'. Approve verbs: 'Approve once', 'Run once' (raw shell), 'Allow', 'Allow once'. Remember scopes: 'This session', 'Always · these args', 'Allow for this session', 'Always allow this skill'. Frames: heavy amber █ (approval) versus rounded amber (question). Only the approval card has a countdown. Undo vocabulary drifts the same way: the turn card's 'Undo All' confirms as 'Undo all N files…' and reports 'Reverted N file(s).', while worktree cards say 'Discard'.
expected: One DecisionCard grammar: 'Agent wants to <verb> <object>', then consequence, then target, then [Allow once] [Allow for session] [Always…] [Deny], with the same frame, key hints and timeout behaviour.
why: These are the highest-stakes moments in the Console, and every variant makes the user re-read and re-learn the controls.
repro: Compare the approval card with the ask_user card live, and the skill, worktree and chat-create cards in code.
recommendation: Extract one decision-card component and copy table (header template, verb set, scope names, frame, key hints, timeout slot), and migrate all six cards. Pick one word pair for undo and revert.

title: 'Send | $' / 'Queue | $' and '~+$' are cryptic, hover-only price hints, shown even for slash commands that never call the LLM
statement: With any draft on a paid provider, the Send button reads 'Send | $' and Queue reads 'Queue | $' (console_composer_bar.py:2185-2197; variant at 379-387). The '$' only means a price tooltip exists on hover (send_price.py:126-147), which keyboard users cannot open. The strip's 'On next send ~+$' is also clipped at 235 cols (G1-05). The same suffix and 'On next send ~+$…' appear for '/', '/help', '/foo bar' and '/generate-image a red cube', although command dispatch never sends to the provider (chat_screen.py:19175-19231). The suffix also costs width in the 80-col composer (G1-34).
expected: The button label stays stable ('Send'). The actual estimate appears inline or in the composer reason once computed (debounced), e.g. 'Send · ≈$0.002'; otherwise nothing is shown. Price hints are suppressed when the draft parses as a local command, and the detail is keyboard-reachable through the cost chip or Inspector.
why: A bare '$' carries no information, reads like a separate control or currency toggle, suggests an unknown charge, falsely implies local commands cost money, and is mouse-only.
repro: Type any draft, or just '/', and read the Send button and the cost chip.
recommendation: Gate price availability on parse.kind == NOT_COMMAND. Drop the '| $' suffix from the button. Render a compact debounced next-send amount as text in the reason slot or cost chip ('Next ~$0.001'), and let the cost chip or Inspector carry the detail, reachable by keyboard.

title: At 80 columns the composer's own controls leave 23 columns for text, so a draft grows to 7 rows and leaves 6 rows of transcript
statement: At 80x24, 'Composer ▾  Menu' takes about 19 cols and 'Send | $  Dictate' about 27, leaving a 23-column draft area (fixed action budget at console_composer_bar.py:353-369). A 250-character draft wrapped to 7 rows, above DESIGN's 4-row growth, and the transcript viewport dropped to 6 rows. At 100 cols the disabled reason truncates to the meaningless 'Send disa…'. The placeholder is clipped ('Ask, command, or paste').
expected: Below about 100 columns, the composer chrome collapses to short forms, or the labels move to a second row, so the draft keeps at least about 60% of the width. Growth is capped at 4 rows with internal scroll. The disabled reason is dropped instead of truncated.
why: On small panes users need to see the reply they are answering while they write, and the composer's own labels are displacing both.
repro: Launch at 80x24 and type about 250 chars into the composer.
recommendation: Add a narrow composer layout below about 100 cols: '▾' for 'Composer ▾', '≡' for 'Menu', Send without the '| $' suffix (price in the tooltip or strip; see G1-20), and Dictate moved into the menu. Enforce a maximum of 4 rows. Hide the disabled reason when fewer than about 24 cells are free.

title: The composer 'Menu' is an ungrouped, mixed-scope list of 7–11 tall centred buttons with jargon labels
statement:
'Menu' opens 'Composer actions' with Browse Prompt Library…, Attach file, Save as Chatbook (disabled: 'No Chatbook artifact is available to save yet'), Generate Image, Generate Caption (disabled: 'Attach an image first'), Impersonate and Buddy…. In other states the code adds Improve current draft…, Save draft to shelf…, Undo Prompt change and Save this chat (console_composer_menu_modal.py:100-192,196-230).
- Each item is a height-3 centred Button, spaced two lines apart, so the menu spans about 30 rows.
- There is no grouping, and no shortcuts or mnemonics.
- There are three 'save' notions (Chatbook, shelf draft, this chat). Save as Chatbook is conversation-scoped, while message More ▸ Save as… offers Chatbook enabled for a single message.
- 'Impersonate' and 'Buddy…' are roleplay jargon with no hint of their meaning.
- Generate Image is enabled although no image backend is reachable.
expected: A compact list with height-1 left-aligned rows in short headed groups, each at most about 4 items (Draft: Improve, Prompts, Save draft · Add/Generate: Attach, image, caption, video · Roleplay: Impersonate, Buddy · Conversation: Save chat / Chatbook). Labels are plain language, shortcuts or slash equivalents sit at the right edge, and readiness words appear where relevant ('Generate Image — SwarmUI unreachable').
why: The menu is the discoverability surface for actions with no visible button. Its size and missing structure make scanning slow, hide the three distinct save models, and disagree with the other Save-as surface.
repro: Click 'Menu' in the composer row.
recommendation: Use an OptionList with section headers and height-1 rows, showing each shortcut or slash equivalent (e.g. '/generate-image') on the right. Move Save as Chatbook to conversation actions and unify the save labels ('Save chat locally', 'Save as Chatbook', 'Park draft'). Rename or describe 'Impersonate' ('Draft my reply (roleplay)') and 'Buddy…' ('Buddy avatar…'). Gate Generate Image/Video on backend readiness.

title: The slash popup shows 8 commands in registration order (hiding /help, /model, /new), omits argument hints, marks the selection only by underline, and drifts from /help and the palette
statement:
A bare '/' opens a popup capped at MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS = 8 (console_command_popup.py:23, :93). It lists /prompt, /system, /skills, /fewer-permission-prompts, /prefill, /generate-image, /generate-video and /stream-video, in dict order, which is display order (console_command_suggestions.py:34-58). The other 14 are out of view with no count or scroll cue: steer, redirect, emergency-stop, rewind, research, help, doctor, model, sessions, workspace, new, temp, settings, context, endpoint. (J8 counted 23 commands in total; L2 counted 22.)

Other problems:
- Rows show only '/name  description'. The registry holds argument hints such as '[:backend] <prompt>', '[pin|clear] [text]' and '[clear | <reason>]', and /help prints them, but the popup never does (console_command_suggestions.py:33-57,158-168; console_command_grammar.py:32-120).
- The highlighted row differs from the others only by underline (same fg #e1e1e1, same bg #1e1e1e; console_command_popup.py:31-34).
- /emergency-stop sits in the same flat list as /prompt.
- Wording drifts: the palette says 'Edit system prompt (/system)' (console_command_provider.py:108-112), while /help says '/system [name] — Apply a saved system prompt'.
- An unknown command dumps all 23 names with no did-you-mean.
expected: Commands are frequency- or category-ordered and grouped (Chat: new, model, settings, context, help · Run: steer, redirect, stop · Create: image, video · Diagnostics). Rows read '/name args — description'. A reverse-video cursor row marks the selection. A final row says '+14 more — type to filter or ↓'. One description table serves the popup, /help and the palette. Unknown commands get close-match suggestions.
why: The slash popup is the main recognition surface for keyboard users and the persona's fastest exploration path. Showing niche commands first while hiding /help and /model, and dropping argument hints, turns every argument-taking command into trial and error.
repro: Focus the composer and type '/'. Then '/help' + Enter, then '/foo bar' + Enter.
recommendation: Add a display rank or group and an argument_hint to CommandSuggestion, rendering the hint dimmed after the name. Use reverse-video selection. Show a '+N more' final row, and consider showing recently used commands first. Keep one description table for the popup, /help and the palette. Add Levenshtein suggestions to the unknown-command hint.

title: Command text stays in the composer after /help and similar commands (next command is appended and fails); editing keys and collapsed-typing behave unpredictably
statement:
Draft handling after a command is inconsistent:
- After /help, /doctor, the other list commands and /generate-image run, the draft keeps the command text. Code comment: 'Captured drafts remain in the composer until runtime custody' (chat_screen.py:19226-19231, KIND_COMMAND path never clears; /help at 19415-19442).
- /fewer-permission-prompts (20219-20227), /emergency-stop and '/emergency-stop clear' do clear the draft.
- After /help the caret is also gone. Typing '/help prefill' produced '/help /help prefill' and the system message '/help prefill is not a known command'. build_command_detail does not tolerate a repeated leading /help (console_help.py:62-86).
- A successful detail lookup likewise leaves '/help prefill' in the draft, so a second Enter re-runs it.

Editing keys:
- Ctrl+U clears the draft (readline), but Ctrl+A then Ctrl+K opened the session switcher (chat_screen.py:1942) instead of killing to end of line.

Collapsed composer:
- With the composer collapsed ('Expand ▴ Composer hidden'), typing 'hello' was silently dropped.
expected: A command whose effect is complete (help, doctor, a skills list, an unknown-command hint) clears its own text, with undo, and keeps the caret in the composer. Only commands that hand the draft to a runtime keep it, and a failed command keeps its text for correction. Composer editing is either full readline (switcher moved off Ctrl+K while the composer is focused) or explicitly documented as not readline. Printable input while collapsed re-expands the composer.
why: The learning loop (/help, then /help <cmd>) fails on the second step with a misleading 'not a known command' error, which teaches users that /help <command> doesn't work. Opening a modal mid-edit and silently discarding keystrokes are mode errors against terminal muscle memory.
repro: Run /help (Enter, Enter) and look at the composer. Type /help prefill and press Enter. Type text, then Ctrl+A, Ctrl+K. Collapse the composer and type.
recommendation: Add a per-command 'consumes draft' flag to the registry, and for terminal commands clear in one place with record_history=True and refocus the composer. Make build_command_detail strip a leading 'help ' token. Implement Ctrl+K kill-line while the composer is focused, or move the switcher off Ctrl+K there, and document the composer key map in F1. Auto-expand the composer on printable input.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macbook-dev-Documents-GitHub-tldw-chatbook/c28a6a75-4221-4434-989d-fbf24a73c96b/scratchpad/uxrev/evidence/L4/08-slash-help-detail.txt lines 38 and 43 ('/help /help prefill▌' draft; 'is not a known command')
tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_help.py:62-86 (build_command_detail does not tolerate a repeated leading /help)

title: Multiple staged attachments collapse to '📎 2 files' with no names, and a distant single ✕ clears them all without undo
statement: Pasting two image paths showed '📎 2 files'. Hover shows no tooltip and clicking does nothing; names surface only in transient '<name> attached' toasts (chat_screen.py:22389-22401). The remove control '✕' sits at the far right after Dictate, about 50 columns from the chip. Its tooltip says 'Remove the pending attachment' (singular), but clicking it removed both files and toasted 'Attachment cleared'. There is no per-file removal and no undo.
expected: Each staged file is visible by name (chips or an expandable list) with its own adjacent remove control. A bulk 'Clear all' is labelled as such, and removal offers undo.
why: Users cannot verify what they are about to send, which is the core pre-send question, and can lose all attachments with one click.
repro: Bracketed-paste two image paths into the composer. Hover or click '📎 2 files', then click ✕.
recommendation: Make the attachment indicator a focusable control that opens a staged-items list (name, size, type, Remove for each, Clear all). Place remove controls beside their items, and toast 'Removed leaf.png — Undo'.

title: Prompt variables: {{topic}} silently becomes a literal {topic}; the inserted prompt is collapsed, mislabelled 'Draft improved', and gets no variables dialog
statement:
A Library prompt saved with the template 'Summarize {{topic}} in {{count}} bullet points for a student.' was inserted via /prompt. Three things went wrong:
- No variables dialog appeared (prompts.py:1850-1866 shows no dialog when the plan has no variables).
- The text went in as a collapsed 'Pasted text | 57 characters | Expand' token, hiding the placeholders.
- A recovery row said 'Draft improved · Undo · Review changes'. 'Draft improved' is reused for any undoable replace (console_composer_bar.py:6552-6557).

Expanding showed 'Summarize {topic} in {count} …'. The double braces were silently turned into single braces, because the variable syntax is single-brace and '{{' is an escape (prompt_variables.py:377-384). Character cards and roleplay macros in the same app use {{user}}/{{char}} (Character_Chat_Lib.py).

The prompt picker shows only a centred name, with no template or variable preview, and the Library prompt editor shows no syntax hint. '/prompt' + Enter first only completes the command, and a second Enter is needed to run it.
expected: The editor states the variable syntax, or accepts both forms. The picker previews the template and its variables. A variables dialog appears for detected placeholders. Inserted text is shown expanded, and the recovery row reads 'Prompt inserted · Undo'.
why: Reusable study prompts are a core researcher/student loop, and the conflicting brace conventions produce silently wrong messages.
repro: Library ▸ New prompt ▸ template with {{x}} ▸ Save prompt. In Console type '/prompt', press Enter twice, and pick it.
recommendation: Treat {{name}} as a variable too, or warn in the editor when {{word}} is detected ('did you mean {word}?'). Add syntax help beside the template field and a template preview in the picker. Insert prompts uncollapsed, and give prompt insertion its own recovery copy.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/UI/Console_Modules/prompts.py:1850-1866 (no dialog when the plan has no variables)
tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_composer_bar.py:6552-6557 ('Draft improved' reused for any undoable replace)

title: Pressing Enter in the first seconds after a send is refused; the draft is cleared, then silently restored about 4 s later, possibly after the user has moved to another tab
statement: In tab A I sent R1, then pressed Enter on R2 0.8 s later. The composer emptied, and 0.4 s later there was no toast. I clicked tab B. About 4 s after that Enter, the toast 'Preparing the current turn. Queueing becomes available once it is accepted.' appeared over tab B without naming a tab. R2's text reappeared later in A's composer. In the GAP1-01(a) incident, the same late restore merged into the next prompt the user typed.
expected: Enter during preparation is accepted into the queue (to start once the turn is accepted), or the draft stays in place with an inline 'Preparing — will queue when accepted' state.
why: Queueing a quick follow-up is the natural multi-prompt workflow. The refusal is invisible at the moment it happens, and the delayed restore is a direct ingredient of the cross-tab leak.
repro: Tab A, slow proxy: send a prompt, type a second one and press Enter within about 1 s, click another tab at once, and capture over the next 5 s. Then return to A.
recommendation: Allow queue admission during preparation: store the entry and release it on acceptance. If refusal must stay, keep the draft in the composer (never clear it first), show the reason inline on that tab's composer, and include the tab title in any toast.

title: A paste over the 100,000-character draft limit is accepted without warning, then Send fails with 'remove unsafe markup or shorten your message'
statement:
The core defect is real and reproduces live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. There is no paste-time check against the 100,000-character draft cap. A bracketed paste of 1,193,491 characters (10,000 lines) collapses to 'Pasted text | 1193491 characters | Expand' with no line count, no thousands separator and no warning or toast, and 'Send | $' stays enabled.

The only pre-send hint is grey status text reading 'Context 100%+ - Current $0.00 - On next send unavailable', which never says why. It uses the same grey as 'Sources: 0' and is truncated to 'Context 10' at 200 columns. A paste just over the cap (100,500 chars) shows 'Context 14%', so nothing suggests the draft is too big.

Clicking Send adds the System row 'Message blocked: remove unsafe markup or shorten your message.', which gives neither the limit nor the size. A short draft containing 'onclick=' gets the identical message, so the two causes really are merged into one string. The draft moves to 'Queue 0/10 - Unsent turn needs attention [Rest] [Discard]'. Restore puts it back as raw literal text in an 8-row composer with the collapse lost, and Send is enabled again for the same unsendable draft.

Three corrections to the finding:
(a) The keystroke lag comes from the size of the draft, not from Restore losing the collapse. Echo was 0.16-0.48 s while the paste was still collapsed and 0.22-0.51 s after Restore, against 0.03-0.11 s in an empty tab.
(b) The claim that 'a mis-click could cost a large request' is wrong. The 100k cap is enforced on the client for every provider, and the review proxy logged zero requests for these sends.
(c) The error does name the right remedy ('shorten your message'). It just does so ambiguously and without numbers.

Nothing is lost or billed.
expected: Validate at paste time and explain in numbers: size, limit, and alternatives such as attaching it as a file or trimming. At send time, the error should name the actual cause. Restore should bring back the draft in the same collapsed form.
why: Pasting logs and documents is a core terminal workflow. The error sends users hunting for 'unsafe markup' that doesn't exist, and a mis-click could cost a large request on a provider with a higher limit.
repro: tmux load-buffer a 1.2 MB file; paste-buffer -p into the composer; click Send; click Rest(ore); type.
recommendation: On paste, if the draft would exceed CONSOLE_DRAFT_MAX_LENGTH or the context window, show an inline notice on the chip: 'Paste is 1,193,491 chars / 10,000 lines — limit 100,000 chars. [Attach as file] [Keep first 100,000] [Remove]'. Disable Send with that reason. Split validate_console_draft into separate 'too long (N of 100,000)' and 'contains disallowed markup (…)' messages. Keep the collapse metadata through the unsent-turn shelf. Format the chip as 'Pasted text · 10,000 lines · 1.19 MB'.
fix_direction:
1. Split validate_console_draft so each failure has its own message: 'Message is too long: 1,193,491 of 100,000 characters' and 'Message contains blocked markup (onclick=)'. Have validate_text_input return a reason instead of a bool.
2. Tie Send enablement and the Send hint to the same validation result the price and spend projection already computes, for example 'Send disabled: 1,193,491 / 100,000 chars'. Do not rely on grey 'On next send unavailable' text.
3. Warn at paste time, on the collapsed token or in a toast, when the draft goes over the cap. Offer attach-as-file (see TASK-376) or trim.
4. Format the token with thousands separators and a line count.
5. Keep collapse/segment metadata through turn recovery, or re-collapse on restore above UNDO_RECOLLAPSE_CHAR_THRESHOLD, which the undo path already does.
6. Separately, profile why each keystroke costs about 0.2-0.5 s with a 1.2 MB draft even while it is collapsed. Validation, price projection and context estimation over the full text on every edit are the likely suspects; this is a perf issue for the in-flight efficiency PRs, not a collapse issue.
7. Document the 100k draft limit in the Console User Guide.

title: Undoing a paste-chip deletion swallows the user's typed text into the chip
statement: I typed 'Summarize this: ' and pasted a 20,000-character line, giving 'Summarize this: Pasted text | 20000 characters | Expand'. One Backspace deleted the entire 20,000-character paste with no notice. Ctrl+Z restored it as 'Pasted text | 20016 characters | Expand': the 16 typed characters were now hidden inside the collapsed chip and no longer visible as typed text.
expected: Deleting a chip should say what was removed and how to undo it. Undo should restore the exact segmentation: typed text stays text, and the paste becomes a 20,000-character chip again.
why: The user's own instruction becomes invisible, and it will be sent inside a block labelled as pasted content.
repro: Type a prefix, paste >50 chars (collapse threshold), Backspace, Ctrl+Z.
recommendation: Record chip boundaries in the undo stack so undo restores the prior spans. On atomic chip deletion, show a transient 'Removed pasted text (20,000 chars) · Ctrl+Z restores' in the composer hint slot.

title: A custom system prompt is silently replaced when a character is swapped in, while the chip still says 'System Prompt: set'
statement:
Confirmed live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c, in both an unsaved chat and a saved one. Steps: set a custom session system prompt ('You are a terse biology tutor. Always end answers with the word BANANA.') with Status ▸ System Prompt ▸ Apply. The chip changes from 'System Prompt: off' to 'System Prompt: set', and Conversation Inspector ▸ Context ▸ Next send preview shows the custom text as the system message. Then Assistant chip ▸ Samira ▸ 'Swap in this chat'.

What happens:
- The custom prompt is replaced with the full character card. Nothing is merged in.
- The placement dialog only says '<name>: swap into this chat, or start a new one?'. The toast only says 'This chat now uses Samira "Sammy" Vadem.'
- The chip still reads 'System Prompt: set'.
- The Inspector preview then shows one system message (the Samira card) and then the user turn. 'BANANA' and 'terse biology' appear nowhere, including when scrolled to the end.
- Reopening the System Prompt editor shows the card text. That is the only place the replacement can be discovered.
- In a saved chat the overwrite is written to the DB (conversations.system_prompt went from the BANANA text to the Samira card, version 1 to 4), and there is no undo.
- After an app restart the chip strip reads 'Assistant: General' and 'System Prompt: set', and the rail says 'Character · No chats'. Yet the prepared request still carries Samira's card. So after a reload nothing on screen names where the system prompt came from.

Minor correction to the finding's side note: the workspace flow creates a persona named '<workspace> Agent' with a seeded system prompt (Workspaces/agent_provisioning.py:82), not a character. I did not check live whether it replaces a custom prompt.
expected: The chip and the Inspect card state which system prompt is actually in effect ('System: character card (Samira)' vs 'System: custom'). The swap dialog warns that it replaces or merges the custom system prompt and offers a choice.
why: The user believes their instructions are in force when they are not, so the 'what will the model see' judgement fails without any sign.
repro: Status ▸ System Prompt ▸ type text ▸ Apply. Assistant chip ▸ character ▸ Swap in this chat. Click the Context chip ▸ Context tab ▸ 'Preview · System'.
recommendation: Derive the System chip label from the prepared request (source: custom / character / workspace agent / none). Make the swap dialog explicit: 'Keep my system prompt and add the character' / 'Replace with the character's'.
fix_direction: Give the session system prompt a provenance field (custom / character:<id> / persona / workspace-agent / none). Build the chip label and an Inspect row from it, e.g. 'System: Samira (character)' vs 'System: custom', and fix the TX-06 grammar in the same change. When a swap would replace a non-empty prompt that did not come from a character, make the placement step say so and offer 'Replace with <name>'s prompt' vs 'Keep my prompt and add <name>'. Keep the replaced text so the user can undo it from the toast. Persist the character binding together with the projected system prompt so a reload does not show 'Assistant: General' over a character card.

title: A query typed into the Inspect rail's Library search is dropped: Enter does nothing, and 'Search Library' opens the modal with an empty field
statement:
The Inspect rail's 'Ask Library sources before sending' input is ignored by the search it sits above. Pressing Enter in it does nothing: there is no Input.Submitted handler, the screen text is identical before and after, and nothing is logged. The rail's 'Search Library' button, like the header action, always opens the modal, and the modal is prefilled only from the composer draft. With an empty composer the modal query field is blank, even though the rail text stays visible behind the modal. With a composer draft the modal shows the draft instead of the rail text. If the user then runs the search, the rail text is overwritten with the modal query.

The text is not lost outright. It survives Cancel and stays in the rail. What happens is that it is ignored, and it is overwritten once any modal search runs. The workaround, retyping the query in the modal, is immediate and obvious. The User Guide (Docs/User_Guide/console/context-and-rag.md:789-797) still says that typing in the rail and pressing Search Library runs the search, so this is a stale, contradictory affordance rather than the intended design.
expected: One query field. Either the rail input runs the search on Enter, or the modal opens pre-filled with the rail text.
why: User input is lost with no message, which violates DESIGN's 'preserve user input'. This is on the primary grounding path (staging Library evidence), and users may conclude that search 'didn't take'.
repro: At 235x52 press Alt+I. Click the 'Ask Library sources…' input, type text and press Enter, then click 'Search Library' in the rail.
recommendation:
Short term: in open_library_search, use the composer draft only when it is non-blank, and otherwise fall back to library_rag_query. Also handle Input.Submitted on #console-library-rag-query-input by opening the modal pre-filled.

Longer term: remove either the rail input or the modal step. Given the modal's explicit 'this send only' scope copy, keep the modal and replace the rail input and button with a single 'Search Library… (/)' action.
fix_direction: Collapse to one query path. The preferred option, consistent with ADR-079 and TASK-19900.4's 'exact composer draft' rule, is to remove the rail Input and keep a single 'Search Library…' action, optionally with a read-only 'Last search: <query>' line. The minimal alternative is for open_library_search to fall back to the stored rail query when the composer draft is blank (`if not (prefill or '').strip()`), and to add an Input.Submitted handler on #console-library-rag-query-input that opens the modal prefilled with that text. If the rail input stays, update the spec/AC so it is explicit about which source wins. Either way, correct Docs/User_Guide/console/context-and-rag.md:789-797, which currently says the rail input runs the search.

title: 'Attach file' inserts text files as inline text; the sent turn shows raw wrapper boilerplate, and the chat is auto-titled '--- Contents of photosynthe...'
statement:
Menu ▸ 'Attach file' on mitochondria.txt produced the toast 'mitochondria.txt inserted as text (not attached)' and an inline token '📄 mitochondria.txt · 147 B'. Images get a '📎 leaf.png · 1 KB' chip on the right instead.

After send, the user turn shows raw '--- Contents of photosynthesis.md --- … --- End of photosynthesis.md --- --- Contents of glossary.md ---', with the lines run together.

The auto-title became '--- Contents of photosynthe...'. It appears in the tab, the header, the Library Conversations list, Inspect 'Where:' and even the staged source title.
expected: Staged text files and images share one attachment model: a named chip before send, and after send a collapsible 'photosynthesis.md (141 B)' block in the user turn. Auto-titles come from the user's own words, never from the wrapper.
why: The label 'Attach' promises one thing and does another. The transcript becomes noisy, and conversation titles become useless for finding work later, which also turns this into a Library search problem.
repro: Composer ▸ Menu ▸ Attach file ▸ a .md or .txt file. Add a question and click Send. Look at the tab title and the user turn.
recommendation: Either rename the menu item to match its behaviour ('Insert file as text', next to 'Attach image') or unify both under one attachment-chip model. Render inline-file segments in sent user turns as collapsed file blocks, and strip the '--- Contents of … ---' wrappers before titling.

title: Workspace Files: centred file list, preview shows literal \n escapes, two close actions, and no way to add a file to the next send
statement:
After binding a folder, Workspaces ▸ Show Files listed the file names centred in the list. Selecting glossary.md previewed '# Glossary\n\n- ATP: adenosine triphosphate\n- NADPH: …', with literal escape sequences.

The actions are 'Back to Console · Details · Previous · Next · Refresh', plus a separate 'Clear · Cancel' at the top right, so there are two close actions. There is no 'Add to next send' or 'Attach'.

The header 'Inspector only · Console remains Bio research' is cryptic. Nothing on the Console surface shows that bound folders are available to the model (read-only tool access) or that they are not sent automatically.
expected: A left-aligned tree; a rendered or plain preview with real line breaks; an 'Add to next send' action; one close action; and a line stating '1 folder bound · read-only · available to tools, not sent automatically'.
why: Workspaces are meant to be global context, yet binding a folder has no visible effect on what the model sees and offers no direct grounding path.
repro: Workspaces ▸ New ▸ add a folder ▸ Create ▸ Show Files ▸ select a .md file.
recommendation:
1. Left-align the list and decode newlines in the preview.
2. Add 'Add to next send', reusing the attachment-chip model (G2-25).
3. Merge the Cancel and Back actions.
4. Add a 'Workspace: Bio research · 1 folder (read-only, tools)' row to the pre-send summary (G2-18).

title: The Conversation Inspector (cost chip, /context) opens with a jargon header, an empty section list and a cost that contradicts the chip
statement:
Activating the cost chip on an empty chat opened 'Conversation Inspector · Chat 1' with 'Capture On · Fidelity Safe · Creds filtered · PII Off · Viewer Safe · No active run is frozen', then 'Total -- 0 tokens -- Cost unavailable (unpriced rows) (0 rows)'.

The chip itself reads 'Current $0.00'. A blank left list sits beside 'Select a section'.

Later, the cost tooltip showed 'Context: ~52 / 191,904' next to 'Tokens: 41.4k', with no explanation of the difference (billed tokens including tool schemas vs context).
expected: An empty state ('No calls yet — costs appear after your first send'), consistent cost wording between chip and modal, and labelled token types ('Billed so far: 41.4k tokens across 3 calls').
why: A user who clicks '$0.00' to learn about spend meets compliance jargon and contradictions.
repro: Fresh chat ▸ click the cost chip. After a few sends, hover the cost chip.
recommendation: Move the capture/fidelity flags behind a 'Capture settings' line. Add explicit empty states per tab. Align the cost vocabulary with the chip and label the scope of billed tokens.

title: Trace shows 'Retrieval failed' on every normal send with Library auto-retrieval off, backed by an ERROR log line on every send
statement:
For a successful turn (the 'build failed' reply), the Trace view (opened with Y) lists '2 Retrieval started', then '3 Retrieval failed — Failed', plus a '!' on the Model lane. The status strip says 'Library · Auto off'.

The app log records '[ERROR] Console RAG capture unavailable; reason=capture_provider_failure' on every send in the session. G2-09 found the same error with auto-retrieval on. The reviewer rated confidence as medium.
expected: With auto-retrieval off, no retrieval events are recorded, or they are recorded as 'Skipped (auto-retrieval off)'. Real failures remain distinguishable.
why: The recovery callouts send users to Trace for diagnosis. A permanent false 'failed' row teaches them to ignore failures there.
repro: Send any message with default settings, press Y and read rows 2-3.
recommendation: Emit a 'skipped' outcome when the policy is Never, and investigate the capture_provider_failure raised on every send (shared with G2-09).

title: Power features depend on recall: Rewind only as typed /rewind, Trace only on 'y', side chat only after selecting text, and no visible control for the Conversation Inspector
statement:
Entry points found for each power feature:
- Rewind: only by typing /rewind, plus a hint inside the context controls (console_context_controls.py:282). It is not in the palette, F1, the message More… menu or the action row.
- Trace: only the 'y' key.
- Side chat ('More Details' / 'Ask in Side Chat'): only in the floating menu that appears after a mouse drag or in the transcript's 's' select-text mode (chat_screen.py:22968-23010). 's' is absent from F1 and the action guide.
- Conversation Inspector: Ctrl+Shift+P, /context or the palette, with no button in the Console chrome.

The composer Menu has Browse Prompt Library…, Attach file, Save as Chatbook, Generate Image, Generate Caption, Impersonate and Buddy…, but no rewind or trace. The action row has Copy 🔊 Edit Fork ♻ ---> More…. The palette provider has no rewind, trace or side chat (console_command_provider.py:30-127).

By comparison, these are well covered: prompts (Menu, /prompt, palette), workspaces (rail, Alt+W, palette, /workspace), queue (contextual shelf), focus mode (footer, palette), fork/regenerate/edit (action row with its guide), and voice (header switches, Dictate).
expected: Every power feature has at least one visible, recognisable entry in the Console chrome, with palette and slash commands acting as accelerators on top of it.
why: Rewind and Trace are the recovery and inspection tools PRODUCT.md promises ('recover from blocked states', 'inspect authority'). Users who don't already know the command never find them.
repro: Look for Rewind or Trace in the Menu (20-composer-menu-open.txt), the action row (13-selected-assistant.txt), the palette provider and F1.
recommendation:
1. Add 'Rewind to here…' to a user message's More… menu and to the palette.
2. Add 'Trace' to the Inspector Run group and the palette.
3. Add 'Ask in side chat' to the message More… menu (quoting the whole message), and add 's select text' to the action guide.
4. Add a 'Context' button in the Inspector 'What happens if I send now?' card that opens the Conversation Inspector (see G2-18).

title: Context % and the Inspector's 'Prepared input' under-count the real request because they leave out tool schemas and system scaffolding
statement:
Every occupancy readout the user sees leaves out a fixed overhead of about 13.4k tokens (Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5, default agent runtime). That overhead is the agent's local tool schemas plus scaffolding, which the provider receives on every request. The readouts are the Context % chip, Settings > Context and memory ("Next request"), the Inspector's "Prepared input" and the model popover's "Last request by category".

Measured live on a fresh chat:
- A one-line send was reported by the provider as 13,773 input tokens (cache_read 13,443 + cache_write 327 + 3). After it, the chip said "Context 0%" instead of about 7%. Settings said "Next request 16 tokens · Request overhead unknown tokens". The Inspector said "Prepared input: ~168 tokens". The popover said "Last request by category: Conversation: 12".
- An ~80k-character send: the chip read "Context 6%" and Settings read 11,611 → 11,615. The provider reported 26,064 tokens, which is 13.6% of 191,904.
- The GAP2 near-full data checks out: 78% shown vs 166,557 reported (86.8%). Its cached prefix was the same 13,443 tokens.

So the displayed headroom is about 7–9 points too large, not 8–14. The finding's "27,656 on first send" was a tool-use turn: two model calls with their usage summed, about 13.8k each. It is not a single request's occupancy.

Root causes:
- (a) `build_console_context_estimate` counts only the system prompt, messages, staged text and draft.
- (b) The preflight accounting and the TASK-26019 breakdown fetch tools via `getattr(self._agent_bridge, "preview_tool_schemas", None)`. That method exists nowhere; the bridge has `native_tool_schemas()`. So `tool_schema_tokens` is always 0.
- (c) The Inspector preview lists only the two builtin schemas (calculator, datetime). It says the live run "may add skills/MCP tools", yet the real additions are about 38 built-in local tools.

Formatting is inconsistent in the same Inspector header: "Prepared input: ~168" next to "Input budget: 191904". The Usage & cost tab's "Total -- 13789 tokens" has no separators, while Settings shows "191,904". The Usage "Total" is not purely cumulative billed: it adds estimated user-row input on top of reported assistant input that already contains it. Observed: Total 51,454 / ~$0.0301 vs chip "Current $0.01".
expected: Occupancy should include every token the provider will receive, or reconcile with the last provider-reported input, and label estimate vs reported. Numbers should use one format everywhere.
why: The displayed headroom is 8–14 points of the window larger than reality, so users overflow or hit compaction while the chip still shows room.
repro: Send one short message in a fresh chat and compare chip % with messages.usage_json; in a large chat compare Inspector 'Prepared input' with the reply's usage_json.
recommendation: Add tool-schema and system-scaffolding tokens to the prepared-request accounting that the chip, Inspector and Settings share. After each send, show 'last request: 166,557 reported' next to the estimate and correct the % with the reported/estimated ratio. Replace 'Request overhead: unknown' with the measured value. Use one formatter (thousands separators, '~' only for estimates) everywhere, and label cumulative billed totals 'billed so far', away from occupancy numbers.
fix_direction:
1. Fix the tool fetch in both preflight call sites so the prepared accounting counts the real wire tool list: call the bridge's method that returns the schemas the agent actually sends, i.e. the local provider tools, not only the registry builtins. Add a test that fails if the bridge method is missing, so a getattr-to-None can't silently return zero again.
2. Feed that accounting's non-conversation part (system + tools + mandatory) into build_console_context_control_state as request_overhead_tokens. Add it to request_tokens for the chip, Settings and Inspector, so all three use one number.
3. After each send, reconcile with the last reported input from usage_json (uncached_input + cache_read + cache_write) for the last model call of the turn, not the sum across a tool loop. Show it as 'last request: N reported' next to the '~estimate' and replace 'Request overhead: unknown' with the measured value.
4. Make the Inspector tool preview list the same schemas the run sends, or at least name the local tool set in the note.
5. Use format_context_tokens for 'Input budget' and the Usage totals. Stop adding estimated user-row input to the Usage Total when the paired assistant row already reports it, and label the total 'billed so far'.

title: Making a bound git folder usable takes four hidden steps on three surfaces, and Environment's how-to text is cut off at every width
statement: (1) Bind the folder in New Workspace; it binds read-only, and the folder field has no label. (2) Settings ▸ Workspaces ▸ 'Allow write'. (3) Settings ▸ Workspaces ▸ 'Enable change review', without which Environment stays empty. (4) Choose the project folder in the Conversation Inspector, which freezes the app (GAP4-01). On top of that comes a per-session 'Send project instructions?' consent. Meanwhile Environment reads 'Changes aren't tracked for this workspa…' and 'Bind a folder and enable Change Review …', truncated at 160 and at 235 columns, so the location 'in Settings ▸ Workspaces' is never visible. It also says 'Bind a folder' when a folder is already bound. The pin 'Choose folder · Project' doesn't say what it is for.
expected: One 'Use this folder for agents' flow, reachable from the Environment empty state or the workspace row, that sets access, tracking and project-folder selection together. The empty-state text wraps and names the missing step accurately.
why: Workspaces are meant to be global context for coding work (PRODUCT principle 7). As shipped, a solo builder who binds a repo sees nothing happen and has to discover three other surfaces.
repro: Create a workspace with a git folder and look at Inspect ▸ Environment at 160 and 235 columns.
recommendation: Wrap the Environment empty-state rows, or give them two lines. Offer an inline 'Set up…' action that opens a combined sheet (access mode, change tracking, 'use as project folder'). Default Change Review consent into the bind step, with the retention disclosure shown there.

title: Change Review warns 'agents can write in <the app's startup folder>', which the User Guide says never happens
statement: Environment ▸ 'Review & commit… · 2 files' opens Change Review with '⚠ agents can write in /Users/…/.worktrees/console-ux-review-0929 — it is not tracked here, so changes made there will not appear in this review'. That path is the app's startup directory, here the source checkout. The User Guide says Console 'does not fall back to the app's startup working directory' and uses private scratch plus admitted folders. The code comment says the banner 'mirrors the controller's own resolution, CWD fallback included'.
expected: The authority banner reflects the chat's actual roots (scratch and bound folders) and never names a directory the agent can't reach. If the startup folder really is writable, the docs are wrong and this is a security-relevant disclosure that belongs in the Console itself.
why: Either false alarm or real surprise, it undermines the trust story about what agents can touch.
repro: Open Change Review from Environment with [console] workspace_root unset.
recommendation: Derive the banner from the session's frozen authority (the same source as the Inspect 'Where' fact), drop the os.getcwd() fallback, and add a test pinning the banner to the documented model.

title: The Inspector's next-send preview contradicts itself: staged sources shown as empty, the slash command previewed as a user message, input under-counted about 55×
statement: With 3 sources in the 'Staged for next send' strip, 'Preview · Staged sources' reads 'No messages yet. Write a prompt to prepare the next send.' That is the messages empty-state, reused. 'Preview · Messages (3)' lists 'user /context' as the next message, but the draft was the command that opened the Inspector and is never sent. 'Prepared input: ~258 tokens', while the Usage tab shows the same turn used 14,208 input tokens: tool schemas are excluded from the estimate. Initial focus lands on 'Choose folder' (Project Instructions), so Enter would start an unrelated folder picker. At 80x24 the always-shown Project Instructions block leaves 3 rows for the preview.
expected: The preview matches what will actually be sent, including staged sources, tool payload size and the exclusion of commands. Each section has its own empty state. Initial focus goes to the tab strip or Close.
why: This is the surface meant to answer 'what happens if I send now'. Wrong answers here mislead cost and grounding decisions.
repro: Stage Library results → type /context → Enter → Context tab → 'Preview · Staged sources'; compare with 'Usage & cost'.
recommendation: Build the preview from the same function the send uses: exclude slash commands, include staged evidence and tool definitions in the token estimate, and label the tool share. Give each Preview section its own empty copy. Collapse Project Instructions to one line in the preview context.

title: 'Context' means four or five different things, and the rail called Context doesn't hold the context
statement:
The core is real, but there is one collision, not four or five. The left rail's brand 'Context' (plus the header button 'Context rail', Alt+C and F1's 'open or close the Context rail') is the only use of 'Context' that does not mean the LLM context. Every other use is the same concept family: the Conversation Inspector's first tab 'Context' is the next-send preview (it lists 'Preview - Staged sources'), the chip 'Context 0%' is how full the model window is, and Settings 'Context and memory' is the conversation budget and compaction. These agree with each other.

The rail is not 'only navigation'. It holds Terminal, Workspaces, Conversations, Character, Model (temperature, max tokens, 'System: none'), Agent and Details, so it is session setup plus navigation. It does have no sources or next-send view.

The collision is a regression. TASK-32326 (Done) kept the rail brand only because it renamed the Ctrl+Shift+P viewer to 'Current Context'. TASK-32828 (In Progress) changed that tab back to plain 'Context' (console_conversation_inspector.py:503). The glossary TASK-32326 added to Docs/User_Guide/console.md still says 'Current Context' / 'Next Send' (lines 22, 151, 677), so that fix's own documentation is now wrong.

The header button 'Context rail' only reveals the rail. With the rail already open (the default at 120x40 and at 235x52), a click changes no text on screen, only the button's tint and which widget has focus. The log shows the handler ran and saved only left_open_explicit=True. Alt+C toggles instead. So TASK-32325's AC#1 does not hold.

The tooltip 'Open the Console context rail; stage sources from Library' points to a rail with no staging. Worse, at 120x40 with the Inspect rail open, the button collapses the Inspect rail and hides the 'Sources - next send' tray, the one place staged sources are shown.

Two claims are wrong. 'Staged Context' (console_display_state.py:939/961) is a heading field that nothing renders. 'Show staged sources' is a show=False binding description that never appears in the footer. The names users actually see for staged sources are: 'Sources - next send' (tray), 'Sources: None staged' (readiness card), 'Sources: 0' (chip), 'Staged for next send - N sources' (strip) and 'Preview - Staged sources' (Inspector tab). These are close variants, not a four-way split. 'Not saved: context settings' appears only when a save fails.
expected: One name per concept. The left rail is named for its job ('Chats', 'Browse', 'Navigator'). 'Context' is reserved for 'what the model will see on the next send', which lives in exactly one place. A control that claims to stage sources leads to where sources are staged.
why: Grounding answers in selected sources is PRODUCT.md's core loop. A user asking 'what will be sent?' opens the Context rail and finds a chat list. A user who clicks 'Context rail' while it is open sees nothing happen, which is the dead-button symptom TASK-32325 tried to fix by relabelling.
repro: At 160x45 or 120x40 click the header 'Context rail' (or Alt+C) and diff. Press Alt+I to find 'Sources — next send' in Inspect. Press Ctrl+Shift+P for the Inspector 'Context' tab.
recommendation: Reserve 'Context' (or 'Next send') for the payload: the Inspector tab, the staged-sources tray (one name everywhere, e.g. 'Next-send sources') and /context. Rename the chip to 'Window 0%' or 'Tokens 0%'. Rename the left rail after what it holds and update the handle, header button, Alt+C label, F1, footer, toasts and docs together. Remove the header 'Context rail' button (the handle and Alt+C cover it) or make it a true toggle whose label reflects state. Fix the tooltip. The glossary is covered in G4-17.
fix_direction:
1. Choose one of two options and record an owner ruling, because keeping the rail brand was an owner-accepted TASK-32326 decision:
   - (a) Restore a distinct Inspector tab name (for example 'Next send' or 'Current context').
   - (b) Rename the left rail after what it holds (for example 'Session' or 'Chats'), and update the handle, header button, Alt+C footer label, F1 and docs together.
2. Make the header 'Context rail' button a true toggle, as Alt+C is, with a label that reflects its state, or remove it.
3. Keep that button from collapsing the Inspect rail's sources tray, or change the tooltip so it no longer promises staging; pointing it at Search Library / Alt+I would work.
4. Update the Docs/User_Guide/console.md glossary and shortcut table (lines 22, 151, 677) to match the real tab names.
5. Optionally, delete the dead 'Staged Context' heading field.
6. Keep the chip 'Context 0%' and the Settings 'Context and memory' tab. They use 'Context' in the same LLM-context sense as the payload and are standard terms.
