title: Core nouns drift everywhere: one object is called tab, chat, conversation, session and 'agent'; the right rail is Inspect/Inspector/Conversation Inspector
statement: The same object goes by many names. Entry points: 'New tab' (header, strip, Ctrl+T), 'New conversation' (rail), 'Console: New chat tab' and 'Quick Actions: New Chat Conversation' (palette), 'Temporary' / 'New temporary chat', 'New chat' (workspace menu). One screen shows 'Conversation | Chat 1', 'Conversations' section with a 'Chats' group, 'Archive this chat', 'Archived chats' and 'Search all chats…'. Switching: footer 'Ctrl+K switch session', switcher 'Switch or resume [Active]' with placeholder 'Search sessions, workspaces…', tabs Active/History/Character chats, rows labelled 'Console tab', every plain chat row labelled 'OPEN AGENT' (section 'OTHER OPEN'; fallback at console_session_switcher_modal.py:1224-1229), palette 'Switch session… Fuzzy-find and activate a conversation', and '/sessions — Switch to another conversation (Ctrl+K)', '/new — Open a new Console chat tab'. Rename: 'Rename Chat Tab / Chat tab name', even for a chat not open as a tab. Close: 'Close Console session?' … 'Closing removes this open tab' … 'Close this session?'. Other variants: the rename toast 'Renamed this tab, but saving the conversation title failed…'; Settings 'Make default for new chats | Use for this conversation'; system prompt 'Applies to this session' vs popover 'Applies to this conversation'; F1 'F2: rename a session' and 'Ctrl+T: new tab (new agent)'; Library 'Archive conversation'; the Save-md alias 'Enter:switch'. The Default workspace appears as 'Default', 'Chats' and 'Default (everyday chats)'. The right rail is '◂ Inspect' / '▸ Inspect' / 'Inspect rail' (F1) / 'Inspector rail' and 'right Inspect rail' (palette) / 'Inspector' (docs). 'Conversation Inspector' is a modal whose entry points say 'View chat context' / 'View context' / '/context'. Trace has its own 'Inspector' pane (i) and there is a 'Run inspector'. F2 means Lab globally but rename in the switcher. Glyphs 🔊 ♻ ---> 💬 are mixed with words. The Terminology section in the docs (console.md:132-155) exists largely to explain these collisions. The overloads of Context, Agent/Assistant and Blocked are covered in G4-16, G4-18 and G4-19.
expected: A controlled vocabulary: one noun for the persistent record ('chat' or 'conversation', not both), 'tab' for its open view, 'workspace' for the container, 'agent run' only for execution. Verbs to match: New chat, Close tab, Rename chat, Archive chat, Switch chat. Ctrl+K rows say OPEN / SAVED plus run state (RUNNING, NEEDS YOU), with AGENT only when a run exists. One name for the right rail and one for the Ctrl+Shift+P modal (e.g. 'Send details' / 'Context viewer').
why: Users can't predict whether closing a 'session' deletes the 'conversation', whether 'Search all chats' covers 'sessions', or whether 'OPEN AGENT' means something is running. The close dialog has to explain the model in prose because the labels don't, and every help surface gets longer.
repro: Compare the header, strip, rail, palette ('new', 'switch'), Ctrl+K rows, the rename dialog opened from a rail row, the close dialog, and the / command descriptions.
recommendation: Write a short Console glossary in DESIGN.md (conversation/chat, tab, workspace, agent run, Assistant/Character/Persona, Inspector, Context) and rename to it in one pass. Drop 'session' from UI copy: Ctrl+K becomes 'switch chat', the dialog becomes 'Close tab?', and /sessions stays only as an alias. Align the Ctrl+Shift+P entry points with the modal title. Enforce the glossary with a copy-lint test over Console strings.

title: The active identity (Assistant / Character / Persona / Agent) is named and reported differently on the chip, rail and Inspect
statement: The strip chip reads 'Assistant: General' and opens a modal titled 'Choose character' with a 'Default Assistant' row. After a swap the chip key changes to 'Character:'. The left rail reads 'Character · No chats' / 'No current character · Local · No open chat' while a chat with Samira was open (from another tab), and later while 'Character: Bio research Agent' was active. The Inspect card said 'Assistant: General' while the strip said 'Character: Samira'. The New Workspace modal adds 'Default Persona', 'Create a workspace Agent' and 'Persona memory', and creating a workspace silently created a 'Bio research Agent' character. The rail's Conversations section said 'No active conversation.' while a workspace chat was active.
expected: One noun for 'who answers' (e.g. Assistant, with character as a type), one per-session source of truth feeding the chip, rail and Inspect, and the active chat always shown as active.
why: Users can't tell who will answer or under which instructions, which is part of 'what context goes to the model'.
repro: Assistant chip ▸ pick a character ▸ Swap; compare the chip, the left rail Character section and the Inspect card; then Workspaces ▸ New ▸ Create.
recommendation: Include Assistant/Character/Persona/Agent/Workspace in the DESIGN.md glossary (G4-17) and derive every identity label from one per-session selector. Make the rail's 'current conversation' row reflect workspace-owned chats. Don't create a character as a silent side effect of creating a workspace, or state that it will happen.

title: The setup task has seven names and two destinations; 'continue setup' leads to different places
statement: Wizard: 'Connect a provider'. Console card step: 'Connect a provider (API key or local server)'; card button: 'Set up provider'. Console footer: 'Enter continue setup', which opens F4 Settings ▸ Providers & Models, not the wizard (chat_screen.py:1232-1235). Home: 'Set up Console model'. Wizard exit dialog: 'continue setup any time from Settings ▸ Diagnostics'. Skip dialog: 'rerun setup from Settings ▸ Diagnostics'. Summary: 'Re-run setup any time: Settings ▸ Diagnostics ▸ Run setup wizard'. Voice step: 'Run Setup Wizard'. Toast: 'Review setup and try again'.
expected: One noun ('Set up a provider') and one verb set. 'Continue setup' always resumes the wizard, or the label doesn't say 'setup' when it opens Settings. The wizard is reachable from the Console card as well as from Settings ▸ Troubleshooting.
why: A first-timer told to 'continue setup' lands in a dense expert Settings page and can't find the wizard they left, which is filed under 'Diagnostics'.
repro: Compare evidence 10, 11, 13, 27, 53, 55.
recommendation: Define the vocabulary once (e.g. 'Set up a provider' / 'Resume setup'). Add a 'Resume setup wizard' secondary action on the Console card. Make the footer hint name the real destination ('Enter open provider settings').

title: Palette 'New Chat Conversation' creates nothing but says 'Opened Console for a new conversation'
statement: 'Quick Actions: New Chat Conversation' (help text 'Start a new chat conversation') only navigates to Console (app_command_providers.py:507-511, 571-575: new_chat only calls _navigate_via_screen). The toast says 'Opened Console for a new conversation', yet the active tab is still 'Say OK 5' with its transcript, and the next message goes into it. The palette also lists 'Console: New chat tab', which does open a tab.
expected: One 'New chat' command that always creates a new tab or conversation.
why: The confirmation is false, and it can put a new topic into an existing conversation.
repro: On Console with a chat open: Ctrl+P → 'New Chat Conversation' → Enter.
recommendation: Remove the Quick Action, or alias it to the Console new-tab action under one name, 'New chat (Ctrl+T)'. Never show a toast claiming something was created unless it was.

title: /skills is described as 'List or run a skill', but /skills <name> never runs, and the real $name syntax is taught nowhere in the UI
statement: The slash popup and /help show '/skills [name] [args] — List or run a skill' (console_command_suggestions.py:37). Running /skills <name> only prints 'Run skills by typing $name — /skills only lists them.' (skill.py:119-130). The '[args]' hint implies execution. The $name form is not in F1, the popup or the placeholder. agent-runs-and-tools.md:2429-2431 documents it correctly ('/skills <name> … (never runs)'), so the in-app help contradicts the docs.
expected: The description reads 'List installed skills (run one with $name)' with no [args], and F1's Commands group teaches $name.
why: The popup is the main in-context teacher for commands, and here it sets up a failed first attempt.
repro: Type / and read the /skills row; run /skills anything.
recommendation: Fix the description and argument hint. Add '$name — run a skill' as a pseudo-entry in the popup's skills section and in F1.

title: Extends G1-40: 'Summarize up to' names two different operations, and the Note version saved a non-summary
statement: More… → 'Summarize up to' saved a Note in about 3 s, with no preview and no link; the toast had expired by the time I looked. The Note, titled 'Summary: Using my Library sources: how many litres does e…', contains no summary. Its body is the model apologising: 'I don't have access to your Library sources … I was generating plausible-sounding information rather than drawing from actual sources', because the summary call lacks the staged evidence. It is headed by raw provenance lines 'Conversation: 7d762268-…' and 'Up to message: 7dc78cb3-…'. /rewind → 'Summarize up to here' is a different operation: it replaces conversation memory, shows a cost line ('Uses the active model once') and runs a preview modal.
expected: Distinct labels: 'Save summary as Note' and 'Compact memory up to here'. The Note action previews or validates its output before saving, links to the saved Note, and uses human provenance (chat title, date).
why: The same words lead to either a durable Note or a change to model memory. The Note path can save misleading content without being noticed.
repro: Select a reply in a Library-grounded chat → More… → Summarize up to → open Library ▸ Notes. Compare with /rewind → select a prompt.
recommendation: Rename the two actions to separate them. Pass the same grounding context the turns had (staged evidence) into the note summarizer, or state that sources are omitted. After saving, show 'Saved Note "…" · Open'.

title: Unification: capture and trace-privacy controls are split across four surfaces with four vocabularies
statement: The Inspector header reads 'Capture On · Fidelity Safe · Creds filtered · PII Off · Viewer Safe · No active run is frozen', with a 'View: Safe' button and a 'Capture settings…' button. That button opens a dialog titled 'Trace Privacy' ('Future trace: Capture On · PII masking Off … Safe/Full is chosen in the trace viewer.'). The Trace screen says 'Future exchange capture: Safe · c Change…'. The export dialogs offer 'Safe summary / Redacted diagnostic / Full trace'. 'Safe' therefore means a capture fidelity, a viewer projection and an export profile, each set in a different place.
expected: One 'Trace & privacy' panel owning capture on/off, fidelity, PII masking and the default export profile. The same terms everywhere ('Capture detail: Safe / Full'). The Inspector header summarises in plain words ('Recording requests (safe detail) · PII not masked').
why: Users cannot form a model of what is recorded, what they are viewing and what will be shared, which is central to a local-first, privacy-conscious product.
repro: /context → read the header → Capture settings… → Esc → y (Trace) → read the header → w (export).
recommendation: Define a glossary entry for Capture, Detail (Safe/Full), Viewer projection and Export profile. Route every 'change' link to the same panel. Rewrite the Inspector header as two plain-language chips.

title: Provider errors (401/429/504) share one technical template with no next step; readiness stays 'Ready' after a 401, and 429 is retried 3× in 2 s despite Retry-After: 20
statement:
Reproduced live on origin/dev 64579cce2c (Anthropic claude-haiku-4-5 through the review proxy, with 401, 429 and 504 injected). The core of the finding holds.

The failure copy: every provider failure renders the same way. The assistant row reads 'Assistant Failed / Response failed.' and a separate System row reads 'Agent run failed: provider returned HTTP <n> (Provider error from anthropic: <category>. Status: <n>.).' The categories are 'authentication failed', 'rate limit exceeded' and 'provider unavailable'. A toast repeats the text. There is no next step, no wait time and no link to the key field.

Readiness after a 401: the header goes back to 'Ready'. The Inspect rail shows 'Provider: ready' and the run recipe in green (#4ebf71). The 'Run: Failed — Agent run failed: provider …' line is truncated. The header Settings modal ('Conversation settings') has only Provider, Endpoint and Model, with no API-key field. After two 401s it still says 'Ready to send — credential not verified. A send attempt is permitted… Credential · Present — not verified'.

Retry: it re-sends the same credentials, gets the same 401 and adds a second System row. The failed turn's More… menu (Save as…, Helpful, Not helpful, Delete, Summarize up to, Save transcript) has no key or settings action.

Retry-After: 429 and 504 are retried 3 times about 1 s apart (proxy log 17:27:33/34/35 and 17:29:21/22/23), even though the proxy sent retry-after: 20. The agent trace shows the computed backoff, not the header: 'retry 1 of 2 in 0.67s (ChatProviderError)' and 'retry 2 of 2 in 1.61s'. The cause is that console_provider_gateway rewraps every adapter exception into a generic ChatProviderError(status), which drops the ChatRateLimitError type and retry_after. The Anthropic adapter also never sets retry_after.

Corrections to details:
(a) Copy does not copy 'Response failed.'. It copies the empty message content. The OSC52 capture received nothing, while a control copy of the user message received 24 bytes. The toast still says 'Copied message to clipboard.', which is a false success.
(b) G1-30 is wrong that Retry exists only as the '♻' glyph. Settled failed turns show a labelled 'Retry' button. '♻' appears only while a run is in flight.
(c) 'The UI never showed it was retrying' is true for the turn, header and status bar. The retry was invisible live: the header stayed 'Ready' through all three attempts of a 'Retry anyway' run. The attempts are recorded afterwards in the Y trace view as three 'Model request failed' rows, with the retry count and delay truncated out of view.
(d) With default trace capture on, the first 429/504 retry is blocked by the known 'Trace capture blocked' defect. The storm of three POSTs in 2 s happens once the user chooses 'Send without capture' and then 'Retry anyway', or has capture off.
(e) hosted_chat.py:1382 is not the Anthropic path. The broader point stands: the Console copy is category-only and discards the adapter detail.
expected: Copy specific to the cause, with a next action, in one failed-turn block. 401: 'OpenAI rejected the API key (401). Update the key in Settings ▸ Providers & Models' with a button that opens that field and keeps the draft; header and Inspect show 'Not ready · key rejected' until the key changes. 429: 'Rate limited by Anthropic — retry available in 20 s [Retry]', with a countdown that honours Retry-After. 5xx: 'Anthropic is unavailable (504). Your prompt is kept — [Retry] or [Switch model]'. Retries in progress are shown ('retrying 2/3…').
why: A bad or expired key is the most common first-contact failure. The UI says Ready while every send fails, and users cannot tell whether to wait, fix a key or switch models, which generates support contact.
repro: PROVIDER=openai launch.sh j15 235 52 badkey → send 'Say hello in three words' → wait 17 s → click the failed turn → Alt+I → header Settings. Or use proxy modes 504/429/401, send, and choose Send without capture if the capture card appears.
recommendation: Build one recovery-callout component (owner / problem / impact / next action, per DESIGN.md 'Recovery Callout') attached to the failed assistant turn, filled from an error-category → copy/action table (auth, rate_limit with retry_after, unavailable, timeout, bad_request). Map ChatAuthenticationError to an 'Update API key' action that deep-links to the key field, with 'Switch model' as the secondary action. Write the 401 into the shared readiness/test-evidence owner so the header and Inspect show 'Key rejected'. Honour Retry-After in the retry policy and show attempts in the turn status. Merge the Failed row and the System row into one block. Hide Fork and Copy when a failed turn has no content.
fix_direction:
1. Preserve error semantics across the gateway. Re-raise the typed ChatAuthenticationError / ChatRateLimitError subclasses, or carry `category` and `retry_after` on the wrapping ChatProviderError. Parse Retry-After in chat_with_anthropic's 429 branch and keep it in the Chat_Functions sensitive re-raise. Add a regression test that drives a 429 with Retry-After through ConsoleProviderGateway → run_agent_loop and asserts that retry_delay_seconds honours it (TASK-25901 AC#2 currently holds only below the gateway).
2. Record a send-time 401/403 in the shared readiness owner (the TASK-33005/33005.4 target), so header, Inspect and Conversation settings show 'Not ready · key rejected' until the key changes.
3. Replace the Failed row plus System row with one recovery callout on the failed turn (DESIGN.md 'Recovery Callout': owner, problem, impact, next action), driven by an error-category table. Auth: 'Anthropic rejected the API key (401)' with an [Update API key] button that deep-links to the F4 ▸ Providers & Models key field and keeps the draft. Rate limit: a countdown from retry_after plus [Retry]. 5xx/timeout: 'prompt kept' with [Retry] and [Switch model]. Use the provider display name and drop the duplicated status and 'Agent run' wording.
4. Show retry attempts live in the turn status ('Retrying 2/3 in 18 s…'), and keep the header 'Running' during 'Retry anyway' runs.
5. On failed turns with empty content, hide or disable Copy and Fork (or make Copy copy the error text). Gate Retry after an auth failure behind the key fix or a confirmation.
6. Stop truncating the Inspect 'Run: Failed' line without offering a next action (TASK-24602 AC#2).
prior_art: KNOWN_PARTIAL — TASK-33005; TASK-33005.4; TASK-33005.2; TASK-24602; TASK-25901; TASK-32805.4; TASK-2543; TASK-2154.16; TASK-335; qa/model-config-ux-review-2026-09-26/report.md item 5
verdicts: live: PARTIAL · code: PARTIAL · skeptic: PARTIAL
evidence: uxrev/evidence/J1/50-badkey-inspect.png ('Provider: ready' in green after the 401)
uxrev/proxy.log (12:51:52-54 three j2:429 POSTs; 12:44:09-12 three j2:504 POSTs)
Extends qa/model-config-ux-review-2026-09-26 item 5 (failed TEST never reaches the header) to real SEND failures

title: Internal jargon, Python symbols and raw exception text are used as user copy, with no path or next step
statement: Examples: (1) crash toast 'Something went wrong in _ownership_for — the screen was kept open. That panel may stop responding or disappear until you reopen it; details are in the log file.' (app_lifecycle.py:912-924, where 'where' is the site's function name). It appeared inside the setup wizard, where 'reopen it' is impossible, no log path is given, and Esc/Ctrl+B were dead. (2) 'Fork unavailable — Saved active leaf lineage is unavailable.' in the action guide of every selected user message in ordinary saved chats: a store ValueError string surfaced verbatim (console_chat_store.py:7280-7293). (3) 'Trace reservation status is unavailable.' (console_chat_controller.py:8731). (4) 'vLLM session handoff could not be re-queued yet. Console retained cleanup ownership and will retry before adoption.' (chat_screen.py:8196-8200, severity=error). (5) 'Response delivery status is unknown on the source device.' (G4-05). Pattern: about 25 notify(str(exc)) or f'… failed: {exc}' sites in Console code, e.g. message.py:2246, 2434, 2508 ('Save as Note/Media/Prompt failed: {exc}', not markup-escaped, while message.py:2102/2314 do escape); chat_screen.py:7166, 7173, 14704, 14771, 20847-20908; session.py:2084, 2206; workspace.py:4890. Good contrasting copy exists: 'Attachment limit reached (5 per message). Remove one to attach another.'
expected: Every user-visible failure uses owned copy: what happened, what is kept, what to do. Include the owning screen's user-facing name and the log location or F3 Logs route where relevant, e.g. 'Setup hit an internal error on the Provider step. Press Back to retry, or Exit setup. Details: <log path> (F3 Logs).' Raw detail goes behind 'Details' or into the log.
why: When things fail, the user needs a way forward. Jargon breaks the 'without reading logs' promise, and unescaped exception text can break Rich markup rendering.
repro: Select a user message in any saved chat and read the guide line. For the crash toast, reproduce J1-01 (wizard provider step crash).
recommendation: Map the crash site to the owning screen or widget's user-facing name and name the concrete recovery (Back / Exit / reopen tab) plus the log location. Add a lint or ratchet test that fails on notify(str(exc)) and on f-strings interpolating exceptions in UI/Console_Modules, Widgets/Console and chat_screen. Map store ValueErrors to UI-owned reason codes (the _BLOCKER_COPY pattern). For fork, say 'Fork is available from assistant replies' or explain what to do.

title: Image and video generation errors expose errno values and config keys with no next step, and backend readiness isn't shown before submitting
statement: Generate Image (Menu → 'Paste command') posted the System message 'Image generation failed: SwarmUI request failed: [Errno 61] Connection refused'. The modal had offered 'Backend: Default (config)' with no readiness shown. /generate-video posted "Video backend 'stable_diffusion_cpp' is not enabled. Check [video_generation].enabled_backends.", a TOML key, although Settings has a video-generation page. The two errors use different grammars.
expected: 'Image generation needs a running backend. SwarmUI at localhost:7801 isn't reachable — Start it, or choose another backend in Settings ▸ Image generation.' The picker marks unavailable backends before submit.
why: The user tries generation once and hits jargon dead ends. There is no error prevention: the default backend isn't validated.
repro: Menu ▸ Generate Image ▸ type 'a red cube' ▸ Paste command ▸ Enter; then /generate-video a red cube spinning.
recommendation: Route both through one generation-error formatter (problem · impact · next action, plus a deep link to the matching Settings page). Show backend readiness in the Generate modal's Backend select. Rename 'Paste command' to 'Generate', or explain that it only drafts the command.

title: The same send lifecycle can raise four or five different error and recovery surfaces, far from the failed turn
statement: One send can show: (1) a bordered 'Trace capture blocked' callout at the top of the transcript column, far from the failed turn at the bottom, pushing the transcript down about 10 rows at 120x40; (2) a borderless recovery panel docked above the composer ('Response delivery status is unknown…'); (3) an in-transcript 'Assistant Failed' turn plus a separate 'System' row; (4) a toast repeating the provider error; (5) a composer reason strip ('Send blocked — resolve response recovery first'). Each uses different layout, colours and button styles.
expected: One recovery grammar attached to the affected turn (DESIGN.md: 'Tool, approval, recovery, stopped, and failed turns follow the same flow'), with a single echo in the composer reason and header state and no duplicate toast.
why: Users must learn several visual languages for 'something went wrong'. Errors appear away from their source, and duplicates add noise.
repro: Run the 504 / 429 / Retry-capture paths and compare the surfaces.
recommendation: Build a single ConsoleTurnRecovery block rendered inside the affected assistant turn (owner / problem / impact / actions). The composer reason and header only point to it ('Needs decision ↑'). Drop the error toast when the turn is visible. Feed it from the evidence record in G4-06.

title: Recovery-card buttons: two identical orange primaries, no spacing between buttons, focus not visible
statement: 'Retry capture' and 'Send without capture' are painted the same #fea62b orange as full-width stacked rows with no gap, with 'Cancel send' dark directly beneath, so they read as one orange block. Tabbing produced no visible change on these buttons (the sgr diff was empty) before focus moved on to the status strip, so keyboard users can't see which action Enter will take.
expected: One recommended action styled as primary and the others as secondary, laid out horizontally with gaps. The focused button gets an outline or inverse per DESIGN.md (outline: heavy $accent). Initial focus lands on the card, and the key is named ('Enter: Send without capture').
why: The choice decides whether a request is sent. Ambiguous emphasis and invisible focus invite the wrong choice.
repro: Reach the Trace capture card; Tab through it; diff captures.
recommendation: Use a shared decision-card component with a primary/secondary/tertiary button scale and a visible focus outline. Auto-focus the card when it appears and include it in the F6 pane cycle.

title: The composer accepts a new send while the previous one is paused; the draft vanishes into 'Queue 0/10 · Unsent turn needs attention [Rest][Discard]'
statement: With the trace callout open, the composer still reads 'Send disabled: type a message', and Send becomes enabled once text is typed. On Enter the draft is cleared, controller_submit is refused (log line 212), and the queue shelf shows 'Queue 0/10 · Unsent turn needs attention': a zero count next to an item needing attention, with no reason. The restore button is truncated to 'Rest' (prompt_queue.py:189-195, 350-357). After Retry capture, the dispatch panel's 'Discard' and the queue row's 'Discard' sit seven rows apart and act on different objects. Restore did put the draft back in the composer. The same shelf presentation appears in G4-03.
expected: While a send is paused, the composer says so ('Send paused — resolve the recovery above first'). Enter is blocked, or it queues visibly with 'will send after recovery'. Recovery buttons name their object ('Discard interrupted reply' vs 'Discard unsent message'), and labels are never truncated.
why: The user believes they sent a message, but it is silently parked, and the next click on the wrong 'Discard' can throw away their text.
repro: Reach the trace-blocked state (G4-04), type 'Name a lake.', press Enter, then click Retry capture.
recommendation: Feed the preparation-paused state into build_console_disabled_reason as a first-class blocker. Show 'Unsent: "Name a lake." — held until recovery finishes' in the queue row, with a count that reflects it. Label the buttons 'Restore to composer' / 'Discard message' and size them to their labels.

title: An archived chat's open tab looks normal and accepts typing; sending fails with a toast, and restoring means going to Library
statement: After 'Archive this chat', the tab label and transcript don't change. The rail's current-chat line reads 'No active conversation.' although the chat is on screen. The composer accepts text and shows 'Send | $'. On Enter a toast says 'This conversation is archived. Open Archived chats and choose Restore & resume.' (conversation_archive_actions.py:310), and the text goes to the 'Unsent turn needs attention' shelf. Recovery means going to Library, where Restore opens a confirmation.
expected: An inline 'Archived — read-only · Restore' banner on the tab and composer, the tab marked as archived, and restore in place from Console.
why: Users type a whole message before learning it can't be sent, then have to leave Console to fix it.
repro: On a saved idle chat click 'Archive this chat' → Done; type in the composer and press Enter.
recommendation: When the active conversation is archived, disable Send and use the reason as the disabled label ('Archived — Restore to send'). Put a Restore button in the transcript header or tab. Mark archived tabs with a text badge.

title: Attach errors for disallowed or unsupported files are vague or silent
statement: The attach file picker lets the user browse to any folder, but choosing a file outside HOME produced a top-right toast, 'File path is outside allowed directories', with no hint of which directory is allowed or how to change it (attachment_core.py:289-292). Pasting the path of an unsupported file (weird.bin) silently became a collapsed 'Pasted text | 163 characters | Expand' token, with no message that nothing was attached: a non-attachable path falls through to insert_pasted_text (chat_screen.py:23315-23331; console_paste_attach.py:151-170). Drag-and-drop could not be tested in tmux; bracketed paste was used as a stand-in.
expected: The picker constrains navigation to allowed roots or marks disallowed locations. The error sits next to the composer and says e.g. 'Only files under ~/ can be attached (change in Settings ▸ …)'. An unsupported pasted path produces 'weird.bin: unsupported type — pasted as text instead'.
why: Users believe a file was attached when it wasn't, or hit a dead-end error they can't act on.
repro: Menu ▸ Attach file ▸ Ctrl+L ▸ path outside HOME ▸ Open; then bracketed-paste a path to a .bin file.
recommendation: Name the allowed root in the error and offer a settings link. When a pasted string is an existing file path that can't be attached, say why in a notice. Start the picker at HOME and grey out disallowed roots.

title: Most errors are 5-second toasts with no history, and terminal outcomes rely on toasts that expire
statement: Console code has about 436 notify() calls, 89 with severity='error' and 256 with 'warning', across chat_screen.py and UI/Console_Modules/*. They use Textual's 5 s default (app.py:3671 notes that timeout=None is not persistent). There is no notification history or log view in Console. The run chip deliberately hides at terminal states because 'terminal outcomes already have their ambient signals — task-2154.16's failure toast' (console_status_chips.py:263-268). In the emergency-stop and 401 captures, the only explanation had disappeared within about 6 s.
expected: Errors that change what the user can do next persist in place, as a callout or chip. A short 'Recent notices' list (in the Inspector or behind the status strip) lets users re-read dismissed toasts.
why: Users who look away during a long agent run miss the only explanation and then see a 'Ready' header.
repro: Trigger any toast-only failure and wait 6 s.
recommendation: Add a per-session notice ring buffer (the last 20 notices, with severity and time) shown in the Inspector. Keep error notices whose state persists (emergency stop, failed run, paused send) as chips until resolved.

title: The narrow-width Context collapse toast points to a 'Context handle' that is hidden at that width, and the footer doesn't update after resize
statement: Shrinking below 84 columns (e.g. from 120x40 to 80x24) shows 'Context rail collapsed — the terminal is too narrow for it. Reopen it from the Context handle (or widen the terminal).' (chat_screen.py:22588-22607). In single-pane mode both rail handles are hidden (chat_screen.py:13880-13889), so no Context handle exists on screen. The working routes are the header 'Context rail' button and Alt+C (TASK-32320), and the toast names neither. Its twin toast for the Inspector says 'Reopen it with Alt+I'. After the resize the footer still read 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus | F6 next pane | F1 · Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q', with no Alt+C or Alt+I. The single-pane footer variant (chat_screen.py:5176-5181) appeared only after focus changed. Reproduced in a fresh session (j72).
expected: Both toasts name a route that exists at that width ('Reopen with Alt+C or the Context rail button'), and the footer re-registers when the width band changes.
why: The recovery instruction sends the user looking for a control that isn't there, at the size where space and orientation are scarcest.
repro: ready 120x40 (Context open by default) → resize to 80x24 → read the toast and footer.
recommendation: Generate both collapse toasts from one template, choosing the copy by width band: in single-pane mode 'Reopen it with Alt+C (or the Context rail button)', naming the handle only when it is displayed. Call _register_console_footer_shortcuts from _adapt_console_workspace_to_width when the band changes. Add Alt+C to the single-pane footer set.

title: Unification: every artifact output path picks a different destination model (Downloads, CWD, clipboard, Notes DB), and trace export defaults into the source tree
statement: Image 'Save' writes immediately to ~/Downloads/console_image_<ts>.png and shows the path in a 5 s toast. Trace export defaults to Path.cwd()/trace-export.json in a path field (initial focus there, Browse… Cancel Export). Exchange export defaults to Clipboard, with a hidden path at Path.cwd()/exchange-export.json and initial focus on Export. 'Summarize up to' and 'Capture as note' write to the Notes DB with no link. Evidence that the CWD default matters: an untracked 2.3 MB 'trace-export.json' (redacted_diagnostic, 299 events, 22:19Z; not from this reviewer's session) now sits at the root of the reviewed worktree ('git status: ?? trace-export.json').
expected: One Console output contract: a configurable exports folder under the user's data or Downloads directory, the same dialog grammar (destination, Browse, Cancel, primary action on the right), and a persistent receipt with 'Open folder' and 'Copy path'.
why: Users cannot predict where outputs land. Privacy-sensitive diagnostic bundles are written into project directories, where they can be committed.
repro: Save an image, export a trace and export an exchange call, then compare destinations and receipts.
recommendation: Introduce a single export-destination helper and receipt component. Default files to ~/Downloads/tldw or the configured exports dir, never CWD. Make the dialogs share field order, initial focus (on the choice, not the commit button) and the post-save receipt.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_exchange_export_dialog.py:136-156 (clipboard default, CWD path, focus on Export)

title: Unification: the two inline recovery callouts use unrelated structures, button layouts and copy
statement: The live 'Trace capture blocked' callout uses Owner/Problem/Impact lines, 'Choose one action.' and three centred, vertically stacked buttons (Retry capture / Send without capture / Cancel send). It is inserted above the tab strip, which it pushes down. The provider-continuation callout ('Interrupted tool run') uses a title, an impact line and a horizontal row: Resume, Take over and Reload, all variant='warning' (identical orange), plus Discard. Its copy exposes implementation detail: 'Resume is unavailable until continuation replay support is enabled for this provider integration.' This callout was read from code; the cut proxy did not reach it because agent calls are non-streaming.
expected: One RecoveryCallout component: owner, problem, impact and next action per DESIGN.md. A single primary action, then secondaries in a left-aligned row. Plain-language unavailability reasons that tell the user what they can do.
why: Recovery moments are stressful, and a different layout each time slows recognition and raises error risk.
repro: Trigger 'Trace capture blocked' (Continue a reply, then send). Compare with ProviderContinuationRecoveryCallout.
recommendation: Extract a shared RecoveryCallout used by trace-call, trace-provenance, continuation and send-blocked recovery. Anchor it to the affected turn, not above the tab strip. Replace capability jargon with user-facing outcomes.

title: Footer hints don't match the focused context or current state: 'Y trace' types a letter, 'Enter send' shows in the transcript and collapsed composer, and hints don't refresh on resize
statement:
The footer does not track what keys actually do in the focused region or current state. Six problems were observed.

1. 'Y trace' is shown in every Console state. The hint tuple is ('Y','trace') (chat_screen.py:1197), but the binding is lowercase Binding('y', 'open_trajectory_view') (1940-1946).
   - With a message selected, Shift+Y does nothing and y opens Trace.
   - With the composer focused (the default), Y/y types into the draft ('Menu  y▌' on line 43 while line 45 shows 'Y trace').
   - Trace has no other visible entry point: no button, no palette entry, no F1 entry, and nothing on the selected-message action row ('Copy 🔊 Edit Fork ♻ ---> More…').
   - The only launch path is wiring.py:497-509 / review_selection.py:635.
   - semantic-trace-capture.md:1-40 explains capture internals and 'press c in a live Trace' but never says how to open Trace.

2. With the transcript focused, the footer still says 'Enter send / queue', although Enter toggles message selection there. j/k/c/e/f/r are not listed.

3. After collapsing the composer with the mouse, the footer still says 'Enter send / queue' (stable after 4 s). The COMPOSER_COLLAPSED variant 'Esc show composer' exists (1243-1246) but is not applied.

4. After resizing 120→80 (or 235→80), 'Alt+I inspect' is missing until focus moves. It is the only route into Inspect because the edge handle is hidden. A cold start at 80x24 does promote it.
   - Why: _set_console_composer_collapsed (11546-11573) never re-registers the footer, and the only screen call sites are 5250, 15657 and 23796. Re-registration runs only on focus-mode, setup-block, screen resume and rail focus.

5. With focus in a rail or the Inspect rail, the footer reads 'Esc composer · F6 panes | n/p Sections | Ctrl+Shift+F focus | F6 next pane | … | Enter send / queue'. F6 appears twice, 'Enter send' is advertised while Enter acts on rail rows, and the tail degrades to 'Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q' with no labels.
   - 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus' means focus mode (hide chrome) but reads as keyboard focus.

6. Related surfaces are also untruthful:
   - The session switcher's hint reads 'Enter:switch F2: rename · ↑↓:move' with mixed separators.
   - F2 in its search field replies 'Focus an open agent result to rename it.' (chats called 'agent results'), while F2 is Lab everywhere else.
   - F1 help lists 'More…: … diagnostics', which the menu does not have, and omits Y, Ctrl+Shift+H, Ctrl+Shift+P and slash commands (chat_screen.py:1193-1211,1286,1348; app.py:935-940; console_session_switcher_modal.py:2083,2535-2556).

The width-driven drops J6 also saw are covered in G1-18. PRODUCT.md says 'contextual help must reflect what is actually available'.
expected: Footer hints are registered per focused region: composer (Enter send, Ctrl+J newline, Alt+M model…), transcript (j/k, Enter select, c/e/r, Esc composer), rails (Esc composer, F6). Single-letter keys are printed exactly as typed ('y') and advertised only where they act. A chord such as Alt+Y, or a palette entry, opens Trace from anywhere, and Trace is also reachable from the Inspector Run group and the message action row or More… menu. The footer is recomputed on composer/status collapse, resize and pane focus, with no duplicate keys, and 'focus mode' is named explicitly. F1 is generated from the live bindings.
why: For keyboard-first users the footer is the main discoverability surface. In the default state it names a key that types text instead: a classic mode error on the product's inspectability feature ('inspect authority'). It also goes stale or misleads at exactly the moments hints matter: narrow widths, a hidden composer, a focused rail.
repro: Fresh ready launch at 160x45/235x52: press y and Y with the composer focused. Select a message and press Shift+Y, then y. F6 to the transcript and read the footer. Click 'Composer ▾' and read the footer. Launch at 120x40, run tmux resize-window -x 80 -y 24, and read the footer before and after F6. Press Alt+I and read the footer. Press Ctrl+K then F2. Press F1.
recommendation: Select footer variants by focused region (composer, transcript, rail, inspector) rather than stacking prepends. Call _register_console_footer_shortcuts() from the composer-collapse, status-collapse and on_resize paths and on transcript focus. Print single-letter keys as typed ('y'), and never advertise bare letters while a text field has focus. Add Alt+Y (or a palette 'Open trace') that works from the composer, add 'Trace…' to the Inspector Run group and the message More… menu, and open semantic-trace-capture.md with 'Open Trace: select a message and press y, or …'. Deduplicate keys, and label 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus mode'. Make F2 act on the highlighted switcher row from the search field, and generate F1 from the live bindings table.
evidence: uxrev/evidence/J6/09-transcript-focused.txt r52 ('Enter send / queue' while in transcript)
uxrev/evidence/J6/60-120x40-default.txt r40, 84-approval-pending.txt r45 (no Alt+A while approval pending)
uxrev/evidence/J6/70-80x24-default.txt r24 and 90-80x24-after-resize.txt r24 (no Alt+I) vs 92-80x24-esc-from-inspect.txt r24 (Alt+I present)

title: Footer truncation keeps a fixed prefix led by focus mode and pane keys, drops the state-critical hints (Alt+A, Alt+I/C, Ctrl+K/T, setup Enter) and strips labels, with no marker
statement:
AppFooterStatus keeps a prefix of the hint list as width falls, with no truncation marker (AppFooterStatus.py:540-580). The Console always prepends 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus', a chrome toggle, into slot 1 (chat_screen.py:5184-5206, 5197), and the F6/Shift+F6 pane keys follow it.

What survives at each width:
- 235 cols: 13 hints, 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus | F6 next pane | Shift+F6 previous pane | F1 help | Enter send / queue | Y trace | …'.
- 211 cols: ends 'Alt+A approval | Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q'. The context-rail label is gone and the palette and quit labels are stripped.
- 160 cols: 'Ctrl+T new tab', 'Alt+I inspect', 'Alt+A approval', 'Alt+C context rail' and the 'palette' label are dropped. Focus mode and both F6 hints survive.
- 120 cols: only 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus | F6 next pane | Shift+F6 previous pane | F1 help | Enter send / queue | Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q'. Ctrl+K, Ctrl+T, Alt+I, Alt+A and Y drop.
- 80 cols: 'F1 · Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q' with no labels.

State-specific hints lose out to the prepend:
- Ready 80x24 single-pane: 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus | Alt+I inspect | F1 · F6 · Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q'. Alt+C, the only route to the Context rail at this width, is dropped even though TASK-24703 promotes it to the front, because focus mode sits in front of the promotion (SINGLE_PANE and SETUP_BLOCKED tuples at 1211-1236).
- First-run Get-started card at 100x30: 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus | F6 next pane | Shift+F6 previous pane | F1 help | Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q'. The one state-specific hint, 'Enter continue setup', is cut.
- Alt+A, added so the approval card is keyboard-reachable, is not visible at any common width, including at 160 cols while an approval is pending.

Other problems:
- With rail focus the footer lists F6 twice ('Esc composer · F6 panes | … | F6 next pane').
- Global keys render as bare 'Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q' / 'F1 · F6' with no verbs.
- 'focus' (focus mode) is easy to confuse with keyboard focus and the F6 pane-focus hints next to it.
- The word count and DB sizes that console.md:115-116 promises never appear at any captured width.
expected: Hints are ranked by importance in the current state and rendered by priority, not list order: the focused region's Enter/Esc first, setup's 'Enter continue setup', Alt+A whenever approvals are pending, and Alt+I/Alt+C when a rail is hidden; then Ctrl+K and Ctrl+T; then merged 'F6/⇧F6 panes'; focus mode last except in focus mode (where it is the only exit). 'F1 all keys' is the always-kept anchor, and truncation appends '… F1 more keys'. A key's label is never dropped while the bare key is kept, and keys are de-duplicated before rendering.
why: The footer is where terminal users learn keys. At first run, 80 cols and mid widths it teaches pane cycling and hides approvals, session switching, Inspect and the setup action. Bare 'Ctrl+P' asks the user to recall what it does, which breaks PRODUCT's 'essential actions discoverable without memorised shortcuts'.
repro: Resize 235 → 211 → 160 → 120 → 80 and read the last row. Fresh profile at 100x30, skip the wizard, open Console and read the footer. Ready 80x24: read the footer. F6 into a rail at 235. Trigger an approval at 160.
recommendation: Give each footer hint a priority, a condition (e.g. 'Alt+A approval' only when approvals are pending, but then always first) and a short label ('^P palette', '^Q quit'). Let the state variant set priorities: setup puts Enter first, single-pane puts Alt+I/Alt+C first, and Ctrl+Shift+F goes low except in focus mode. Reorder CONSOLE_WORKBENCH_SHORTCUTS by task frequency (Enter send, Ctrl+K chats, Ctrl+T new, Alt+I inspect, F1 help). Merge F6/Shift+F6 into 'F6/⇧F6 panes' (saves about 20 cells). Rename the hint 'Focus mode' (or 'Zen'). Degrade by dropping the lowest priority first, never drop a label while keeping its key, append '… F1 all keys' when anything is dropped, and dedupe by key. Update console.md.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/UI/Screens/chat_screen.py:5184-5206 (focus hint prepended ahead of the single-pane/setup variants); 1211-1236 (SINGLE_PANE and SETUP_BLOCKED tuples)
Docs/User_Guide/console.md:115-116 ('a word count, and database sizes')

title: Footer key hints are illegible in paper_light (1.93:1) and solarized_light (1.17:1)
statement: AppFooterStatus paints its bar with $primary-background-darken-1, which is dark in these light themes, but colours the hint text with $text-muted, which is computed for the light page background. The result: 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus | F6 next pane | … | F1 help | Enter send / queue | …' is #636363 on #483525 = 1.93:1 in paper_light and #5c6a6a on #0077bd = 1.17:1 in solarized_light. textual-light happens to pass (5.42:1).
expected: The footer's foreground is computed against the footer's own surface. Key hints read at 4.5:1 or better in every shipped theme.
why: The footer is the Console's always-on list of shortcuts. PRODUCT.md requires essential actions to be discoverable without memorised shortcuts. In two popular light themes this aid is effectively blank.
repro: Ctrl+P → 'Theme: Switch to Solarized Light' (or Paper Light). Look at the bottom row. Run sgr.py runs <shot>.ansi 45.
recommendation: Put the footer on $panel with $text-muted, or keep the tinted bar and give its text a colour derived from that surface, for example $foreground at 70% over the bar, then verify the result. Add the footer row to the theme-matrix contrast test proposed in GAP3-01.

title: The Console header subtitle is a static feature list with a stray em-dash, breaks the destination-header contract, and leaves the active workspace invisible
statement:
The Console header subtitle is '— Chat, source handoffs, live runs, and control actions.' (console_workbench_state.py:137-138, 145-150).

How it differs from other destinations:
- It carries its own leading em-dash, unlike every other destination's subtitle ('Application logs and diagnostics.', 'Run and review evaluation jobs.', 'Draft and edit books, chapters, and scenes.').
- It lists features rather than stating a purpose.
- It truncates to 'Console — Chat, source handoffs…' at 80 columns.

The active workspace is not visible:
- On the default screen at 235x52 and 120x40, the only text mentioning workspaces is the collapsed section label 'Workspaces ▸'.
- The workspace name ('Default') appears only after the user expands that section ('Workspace  Default') or opens Inspect ('Where: Default › Chat 1').

F1's 'Actions' block repeats the header labels, including 'Help' itself, without keys.
expected: Per DESIGN.md, the destination header carries title, purpose, readiness, authority and primary action. The header renderer owns the separator. The second segment is a live breadcrumb, 'Default workspace › Chat 1 · Local · Ready', or at minimum a one-line purpose in the shared format.
why: It is the first line users read, and it looks different from every other destination. The workspace determines the Default Persona, project folder and retrieval scope, yet users cannot tell which context they are working in without opening a rail.
repro: Launch fresh and search the capture for the workspace name. Compare the Console header with the Logs or Evals header, and check it at 80 columns.
recommendation:
Make the header's second segment a live breadcrumb, '<Workspace> › <Chat title> · Local|Server · Ready', with no leading dash (the renderer owns the separator). Clicking the workspace opens Alt+W, and clicking the chat opens Ctrl+K. If a static purpose line remains, use 'Live work: chat, sources, and agent runs.'

Then drop the transcript title row 'Conversation | …' and the Inspect 'Where:' row. In F1, show each action with its key ('New tab — Ctrl+T').

title: The header action row has 5 unrelated buttons and no primary action, and its 'Settings' is not the F4 Settings one row above it
statement:
The header action row renders New tab, Settings, Context rail, Search Library and Help. Send and Stop are filtered out by TOP_ACTION_IDS (console_control_bar.py:20-26).
- 'New tab' duplicates the tab strip.
- 'Context rail' does nothing when the rail is already open, since it only reveals it.
- 'Search Library' duplicates the Inspect button.
- 'Settings' opens a modal titled 'Conversation settings'. The global nav directly above has 'F4 Settings' (app settings), and '/settings' is described as 'Open the full session settings modal' (console_command_suggestions.py:55).

The same surface is therefore called Settings, Conversation settings, session settings and Configure.
expected: A header with at most 3 actions, each unique and named for its object: 'Chat settings…', 'Search Library…', 'Help'.
why: The header is where users look first for actions. Duplicates, and a 'Settings' whose name collides with the global nav, leave users unsure which settings they are changing. The model-config review recorded the same scope confusion.
repro: Click the header 'Settings' and read the modal title. Compare with F4.
recommendation: Reduce the header row to 'Chat settings…', 'Search Library…' and 'Help (F1)'. Use 'Chat settings' consistently for the header, /settings, the Model › Configure button and the Inspect row. The model-config report's 'three named surfaces' proposal covers the editors themselves; this finding covers only the entry-point labels.

title: Footer, F1 and BINDINGS are hand-kept separate lists: F1 omits keys the footer advertises (Y, Ctrl+Shift+F), the slash layer and many real bindings, and repeats others
statement: The footer (CONSOLE_WORKBENCH_SHORTCUTS plus a prepended focus hint) and F1 (CONSOLE_WORKBENCH_SHORTCUT_GROUPS) are maintained separately. F1 and the header Help button open the same modal. The footer shows 'Y trace' and 'Ctrl+Shift+F focus', its FIRST hint, and neither appears in F1. Also absent from F1: Ctrl+Shift+H hands-free, Ctrl+Shift+P view context / Conversation Inspector; the transcript's s (select text), o (full output), v (review changes), n (review notes) and </> variants; the workspace tree's s (star) and m (row menu); the composer's Up/Down history, Right ghost-accept, Ctrl+U/Ctrl+W/Ctrl+C and Ctrl+A; the rail's Ctrl+Shift+←/→. The whole slash layer is missing: 23 commands, /help, $skill and the ! raw-CLI prefix. F1 never says '/' exists, and /help never mentions F1. Ctrl+K appears 3× and Ctrl+T 2×. 'F2: rename a session (in the Ctrl+K switcher)' conflicts with the nav's 'F2 Lab'. There is no link to the user guide. 'Y trace' is a bare-letter binding, so at the default composer focus y types into the draft while the footer keeps offering it. J1 also found F1 to be a reference dump that is not state-aware (see G3-21).
expected: One key registry feeds the footer, F1 and the palette. Every shown or footer key appears once in F1, with context-dependent keys labelled and advertised only where they work, plus a Commands row and a guide pointer.
why: F1 is the 'never-truncating' reference the code relies on (chat_screen.py:1240-1249), and PRODUCT.md requires contextual help to reflect what is available. Keys the footer teaches can't be looked up there.
repro: Press F1 and page to the end (PageDown ×3-5); compare with the footer; press Esc and type y (it lands in the draft).
recommendation: Build one ConsoleKeyRegistry of (key, action, label, scope, focus precondition, priority), generate the footer, F1 groups and palette from it, and de-duplicate. Add a 'Commands' group ('/ command list', '/help', '$name skill', '! raw CLI when armed'), cross-link /help and F1, mark scoped keys ('in the switcher'), and add a 'Full guide' pointer. Advertise 'y trace' only when focus is outside a text input, or move it to a chord. Add a test that every Binding(show=True), surface-local key and footer hint appears in F1.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/UI/Screens/chat_screen.py:1192-1210 (footer), :1233-1352 (F1 groups), :1909-2016 (BINDINGS: y 1946, ctrl+shift+h 1976, ctrl+shift+p 1981), :5197 (focus hint), :4910-4923 (workspace F1 group)

title: F1/Help silently does nothing while a decision card is shown or inside any Console modal (Trace, Ctrl+K switcher, composer Menu)
statement: Two mechanisms produce the same silent F1. (1) With a decision card ('Trace capture blocked') visible, F1 twice and the header 'Help' button produce no panel, toast or message, because action_show_workbench_help returns early when _console_decision_blocking() is true (chat_screen.py:4856-4861). (2) F1 is a non-priority App binding (app.py:926), and Textual's Screen._modal_binding_chain cuts the chain at the top modal, so F1 never reaches a ModalScreen. F1 did nothing in Trace, a ModalScreen with 23 single-letter bindings whose hint lines never say 'Esc close'; in the Ctrl+K switcher, whose own action_show_workbench_help is therefore unreachable; and in the composer Menu. Under the switcher, the page footer still advertises 'Enter send / queue | Y trace | Ctrl+K switch session', none of which work there. The guide index promises 'Press F1 anywhere'.
expected: F1 opens help for whatever owns input, including modals and decision cards (scoped to the decision's options), or at minimum explains why help is unavailable. Every modal hint names Esc and F1. The page footer reflects the modal or is visibly inactive.
why: Users most need help when they're unsure how to answer a blocking decision or when they're in the densest keyboard surface (Trace).
repro: Reach the Trace capture card and press F1 / click Help. ready 160x45: send, click the reply, y (Trace), F1 ×2; Esc; Ctrl+K, F1; Esc; Menu, F1.
recommendation: Make F1 a priority binding that dispatches to the top screen's action_show_workbench_help, falling back to the BINDINGS-derived panel (app_lifecycle.py:1689-1702). Replace the decision-blocking early return with help scoped to the decision's options, or at least a notify() such as 'Answer the card above first, or press Esc to cancel it'. Add 'Esc close · F1 keys' to every modal hint. Dim or replace the page footer while a modal owns input. Add a test that presses F1 over each Console modal and decision card.

title: The F1 panel is a system-organised text wall that relies on glyph and abbreviation legends: context comes last, Actions has no keys or descriptions, and it isn't state-aware
statement: F1 renders one plain-text Static (markup=False). It opens with 'Actions:', a bare label list (New tab, Settings, Context rail, Search Library, Help) that includes Help itself and has no keys or descriptions. Six prose 'Agents' fleet bullets follow, then the shortcut groups. Contextual sections ('Inspector n/p', 'What happens if I send now?', Workspace tree) are appended at the END, about 65 lines down and below the fold at 160x45. Wrapped lines lose their hanging indent ('Handle badges… artifact' wraps to column 2). The key column holds non-keys ('Queue shelf', 'Attach file', 'More…', 'Handle badges'). The panel teaches recall-only legends: "'N appr' = N approvals pending; 'art' = artifact ready", '● running · ◆ needs approval · ✓ finished · ✗ failed · ◈ …', 'Qn is the unsent prompt count'. Rail rows use yet another set (✋ ⛔ ✗ ⟳ ⏸ ⏹ ✉ ✓ 🔔), although ADR-017 committed the rail to text-only. On the first-run Get-started card, F1 shows the same blocked actions and fleet notes and nothing about setup (also noted in G3-36). L2 additionally flagged console.md layout-tour drift (see G3-24).
expected: A task-first panel ('Send & edit', 'Find chats', 'Branch & rewind', 'Approve & steer', 'Inspect & trace', 'Voice') with context-specific help at the top. Actions show key and purpose ('New tab — Ctrl+T'). Badges use words ('2 approvals', 'Artifact'). Help is state-aware (setup card: explain providers, 'Enter continues setup'). Bold headings and hanging indents.
why: The first F1 screen answers 'what is this tool made of' instead of 'how do I do X now'. Glyph legends shift the load from recognition to recall.
repro: ready 160x45: F1. Focus the Inspector (Alt+I), F1, End. fresh 100x30: Console card, F1.
recommendation: Restructure WorkbenchHelpState in this order: context, then tasks, then the full key reference (collapsible), then concepts (Agents prose last or behind 'Learn more'). Pass setup and blocked state in. Generate 'Actions' from WorkbenchAction tooltips with keys. Replace 'appr'/'art' badges with words, and consolidate status glyphs into the one shared vocabulary (G3-12). Render with Rich Text: bold headings and a two-column key table with hanging indent.

title: The slash-command help is shallow: /help <cmd> repeats the listing line, the list is in registration order, and unknown commands dump all 23 names
statement: '/help prefill' printed the same two facts as the listing ('/prefill [pin|clear] [text]' + 'Prepare the start of the assistant's reply'). It had no explanation of pin/clear, no example, no key and no doc link, although the listing promises 'Type /help <command> for details.'. The popup and listing follow registration order (/prompt, /system, /skills, /fewer-permission-prompts…), which puts /help 14th of 23, below the 8-row popup fold. An unknown command appends a System row, 'Unknown command /x — available: /prompt, /system, … (all 23). Press Enter again to send as text.', with no 'did you mean'.
expected: /help <cmd> gives usage, one example, the related key or palette entry, and a doc anchor. The list is grouped (Conversation / Generation / Run control / Navigation / Diagnostics) with /help first, or sorted by frequency. An unknown command suggests the nearest match or two.
why: With 23 commands, slash commands are Console's richest learnable surface. Users can learn a command's name but not how to use it.
repro: Type '/help prefill' + Enter; type '/' and scroll the popup; type '/x' + Enter.
recommendation: Extend ConsoleCommand with long_help, example, related_key and doc_anchor, and render them in the detail view. Group or sort the popup. Replace the full-list dump with a fuzzy 'Did you mean /help?' plus 'Type /help for all commands', shown as an ephemeral notice.

title: User Guide describes behaviour the app doesn't have: streaming, Stop placement, failure actions, 'nothing is auto-approved', approval vocabulary and recovery states
statement: chat-basics.md:320-335 says the reply row appears immediately with a dim 'Generating…' placeholder and streams with a '[streaming]' suffix; observed is a 2.5–3.3 s delay and no streaming. chat-basics.md:325 says 'a Stop button appears between Send and Mic'; observed, Stop is after Dictate and Redirect and clipped (G3-03). It says an errored reply is tagged '[failed]' with a single Try button; observed is 'Failed' with 'Copy Edit Fork Retry More…'. chat-basics.md:73-80 says 'delivery status is unknown' appears after reopening a conversation; it also appears in-session after Send without capture or Retry capture. agent-runs-and-tools.md:305 says 'Nothing is ever auto-approved, and built-in tools always ask first', yet calculator and get_current_datetime ran with no card. Lines :344 and :349 give two contradictory 'Bulk controls' bullets: the first is cut mid-sentence, the second uses retired labels 'Approve once (the default), Approve for session, Always allow'. F1 says 'Escape: return to the composer', which does not work from the transcript. No page mentions the 'Trace capture blocked' callout or its actions.

title: User Guide labels, layout tour and key claims describe a Console that no longer exists (Sessions section, ASCII handles, Mic/Attach/Save, chip names, F3, F9, stars, dialogs)
statement: console.md layout tour: :43-47/:341 describe a 'Sessions' section that 'starts open', but it was retired (left_rail.py:153-163) and the live rail starts with 'Terminal'. :46/:347 say the Character section appears only with avatars, but live it always shows ('Character · No chats'). Handles are written 'Context->' / '<-Inspect' / 'Inspect|--------->' (console.md:50,68,71,338-340; chat-basics.md:87; sessions-tabs-workspaces.md:21), while live shows 'Context ▸' / '◂ Inspect' / '▸ Inspect'. The composer is described as 'Send, Mic, Attach, and Save' (console.md:102-103, chat-basics.md:42-43, attachments-images-voice.md:16), while live has Menu + Send + Dictate. Chip names 'Library search', 'Auto: Never / Automatic', 'Assistant: Blocked / Allowed' (console.md:86,95,354; context-and-rag.md:747-749) differ from live 'Library · Auto off · Agent blocked'; context-and-rag.md:63 already uses the new form, and the 'System Prompt: off' chip is undocumented. console.md:115-116 lists the footer as F6, Shift+F6, F1, Enter, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+P, word count and DB sizes; live shows the Ctrl+Shift+F/Y set and no counts. Row menu: console.md:769 says '*** action menu', sessions-tabs-workspaces.md:55 says 'right-hand icon … press m', and live shows 💬. The guide describes a 'Search conversations' box (sessions-tabs-workspaces.md:49,191); live is 'Filter visible titles', truncated to 'Filter'. The guide describes '☆/★' star controls; the UI has a 💬 menu with 'Favourite'. Ctrl+K is called 'Switch Session' (console.md:15,669); the live title is 'Switch or resume'. The guide's 'Close Tab' dialog ('This tab has messages that will be lost… Close/Keep') differs from the code ('Close Console session?… Close/Stay'). 'Restore and resume' (Library button) vs 'Restore & resume' (toast/confirm). Key claims: F3 cycles switcher modes (sessions-tabs-workspaces.md:143,390,453), but the binding is Shift+F3 and F3 is global Logs. F9 is given as Settings (console.md:444, agent-runs-and-tools.md:585, context-and-rag.md:394), but Settings is F4 and F9 is not a navigation key. The Mic state table 'Mic / Mic… / Rec ● / Text…' (attachments-images-voice.md:110-119) differs from the code's 'Dictate / Dictate… / Dictating / Dictate…'. 'Mic' appears on 5 pages, yet that page claims 'Verified against dev @ ff435772c'. agent-runs-and-tools.md:2434 says approvals are 'mouse-driven' though Alt+A exists. The console.md keyboard table (658-680) omits Y and Alt+A and lists 9 of 23 slash commands. text-selection-and-feedback.md:24 points to 'Settings ▸ Console', but the category is 'Console Behavior'.
expected: The layout tour, control tables and key tables match dev. Key and label tables are generated from, or tested against, BINDINGS, the command registry and the shell shortcut map, and CI fails when a doc-quoted label or key no longer exists.
why: console.md is the first page a learner reads. Instructions like 'click Context->', 'use Mic', 'press F3' or 'press F9' point at nothing or send users to another destination, which erodes trust in all the docs.
repro: Read Docs/User_Guide/console.md 31-117 and 334-356 and sessions-tabs-workspaces.md next to 01-launch-160x45.txt; grep the cited lines against the cited code.
recommendation: Re-verify and rewrite the console.md layout tour and the sessions/tabs, attachments and agents key tables from a current capture. Generate each page's 'Keyboard & commands' table from the same registry as F1. Add docs tests: every **bold** UI label in Docs/User_Guide/console*.md must exist as a string in tldw_chatbook/ (with a prose allowlist), and every 'F<n>' or 'Ctrl+…' must resolve to a binding.

title: No Console glossary: 'Sources' means three things, 'Scope' two, readiness is stated in four vocabularies that disagree, and retrieval is called RAG / retrieval / evidence / Library search
statement:
Sources:
- On a fresh chat with Inspect open, 'nothing staged' is rendered five times at once: chip 'Sources: 0', card 'Sources: None staged', tray 'Sources — next send   none' with 'No sources attached. Stage sources from Library.', Run group 'Run recipe: … / sources not staged / …', and 'Source Readiness / Retrieval: not staged'.
- 'Sources: Notes, Media, Conversations (Prompts off)' uses the same word for the Library source-type filter.
- 'Live work sources' lists integration availability (Watchlists, Workflows, ACP, MCP), a third meaning.
- TASK-24610 found this ('all four were visible at once in a 33-column rail') but renamed only one row.

Scope:
- 'Scope: Everything available' (authority card) and 'Scope: everything   Narrow…' (row) both mean the retrieval item scope.
- On the Library screen 'Scope:' prefixes the source-type list instead, and the code knowingly swaps the prefix for Console (library_rag_state.py:1051-1058).

Readiness:
- Four vocabularies: header 'Ready' / 'Running'; Inspect 'Provider: ready' (green); 'Run: Failed — Agent run failed: provider …' in the same rail; Settings 'Configuration check has not run.' with 'Readiness: Anthropic / claude-haiku-4-5'.
- None of these reconcile after a 401: the header still read 'Ready'.

Success-green is used for neutral facts: 'Retrieval: not staged', the 'Run recipe' line and the 'Terminal' button.

Retrieval jargon:
- 'RAG' (workspace button), 'RAG scope…', 'RAG Scope: narrow retrieval to this workspace', 'Narrow RAG scope — X', 'Library Search/RAG retrieval', 'Create or select a workspace before setting a RAG scope.'
- 'Open retrieval scope picker', 'Automatic retrieval', 'Staged evidence cleared', 'Search Library evidence before sending'.
- The placeholders 'Ask Library sources' and 'What should the Library search look for?', plus 'Library · Auto', 'Library Search/RAG', 'evidence'.

Source-type lists differ: Library search offers Notes/Media/Conversations/Prompts, while the workspace scope picker offers All/Media/Notes.

Searches that ground a send and searches that merely navigate are not distinguished:
- The header 'Search Library' stages evidence in-Console.
- The rail 'Search all chats…' leaves for Library.
- There are also the rail filter, 'Search workspaces', Library's 'Search Library…' and 'Search / RAG — find all', Ctrl+K, and the scope picker's 'Filter by title…'.

With an empty Library, no search surface suggests importing sources; the scope picker only says 'No matching items.'
expected:
One Console glossary, a short table in DESIGN.md, applied in one sweep:
- Sources: anything that grounds a send. Staged items appear once, as 'Staged' or 'Next-send sources', with a count and list.
- Source types: 'Search in: Notes, Media, Conversations', drawn from one shared constant.
- Scope: the item scope, rendered identically on Library and Console by one formatter.
- Integrations: the live-work availability card.
- Library: where sources live. 'RAG' does not appear in Console UI copy.
- Readiness: one model ('Ready · not tested' / 'verified HH:MM' / 'Not ready · reason'), rendered identically in header, strip, Inspect and Settings.
- Green is used only for success.
- Actions that navigate away are marked '→ Library'.
- Empty-Library states offer 'Import sources'.
why: When statuses disagree, users stop trusting all of them, and the Console's contract is status visible without reading logs. Holding four meanings of one word in working memory makes the source-authority summary ambiguous, which PRODUCT.md explicitly rejects. Users also cannot predict which search grounds an answer and which merely navigates, which undermines the grounding workflow.
repro: Press Alt+I on a fresh chat at 235x52 or 160x45 and read top to bottom, then scroll to 'Live work sources'. Make a bad-key send, press Alt+I, and compare with the strip and header. Try the header Search Library, the rail Search all chats…, rail Workspaces ▸ RAG, and Inspect ▸ Narrow… with an empty Library.
recommendation:
1. Write the Console glossary (staged = 'Staged' / 'Next-send sources'; source types = 'Search in' / 'Search covers'; item scope = 'Scope', identical on Library and Console; integrations = 'Integrations'; Library = where sources live) and apply it in one sweep.
2. Remove 'RAG' from all Console UI copy; keep it in Settings or advanced docs only.
3. Make the authority box and the scope row read from the same formatter, and align source-type lists in one shared constant.
4. Collapse the duplicate 'nothing staged' rows (see G2-17).
5. Build one shared readiness projection consumed by header, strip, Inspect and Settings ('one evidence owner').
6. Audit $success usage so green means success only.
7. Mark navigating actions '→ Library', and add an empty-Library call to action in the search and scope modals.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/Library/library_rag_state.py:1051-1058 (Console passes prefix 'Sources' because its 'Scope:' means something else)

title: The Inspect rail is one ~90-row scroll of 14–15 unordered sections with four header styles, repeated readiness facts, glyph-only toggles and built-in tools mislabelled 'MCP'
statement:
At 235x52 the 44-column rail stacks about 14–15 sections, top to bottom:
1. 'Choose folder · Project' (the value comes before the label)
2. The 'What happens if I send now?' card
3. Environment ▾ with Refresh
4. Tasks
5. Agents, with 'Run history ▸' and 'View all runs'
6. 'Sources — next send'
7. Library search (type line, input, button)
8. 'Scope: everything  Narrow…'
9. Run (recipe, live work, provider)
10. Source Readiness
11. 'More' (a disclosure with no glyph; console_run_inspector.py:111-130)
12. Selected Conversation
13. Changes
14. Chat Dictionaries and World Books
15. Conversation settings (11 rows)
16. The bordered 'Live work sources' card of integration availability

Headers come in four styles: banded with ▾, banded with a ▸ summary, plain bold, and indented with a trailing action (also described as round-bordered and heavy-bordered cards). Separators vary: ':', '—', '·', '/' and ' - '.

Repeated readiness facts: 'Run: Ready', 'Live work: No active work', 'Provider: ready', 'Ready to send — credential not verified', and 'Endpoint · Not tested' / 'Generation · Not tested'. The last two still read 'Not tested' after five successful generations.

Built-in tools appear three ways: 'Tools: 6 ready', 'MCP: 6 tools ready' and 'MCP: Connected - 6 tools ready.' The built-in count is rendered as 'MCP' (console_display_state.py:237). Sources appear four ways (see G2-16).

Disclosure:
- Only two sections are collapsible, and only through the one-cell glyph. Clicking the 'Environment' label does nothing.
- Collapsing Environment leaves its 'Refresh' button stranded under the closed header.

Other problems:
- Recovery copy is truncated: 'Changes aren't tracked for this workspa…', 'Bind a folder and enable Change Review …'.
- A raw id is shown: 'Resume state: restored from dc487f1d-bc50-…'.
- Lore items (dictionaries, world books) sit among authority facts.
expected:
The rail has three fixed groups in a fixed order, using one header grammar ('Title   summary  ▾', ▸/▾ throughout, whole row as the toggle target):
- Next send: everything the model will see.
- Run: state, approvals, agents, environment/tasks/changes.
- Selected turn: citations, Library activity.

Within those groups:
- One fact per line, with no repetition.
- The pinned summary is the single readiness rollup, and it uses evidence from successful sends ('verified HH:MM').
- 'Built-in tools' and 'MCP servers' are kept distinct.
- Recovery copy wraps rather than being clipped, and controls are hidden when their section is collapsed.
- 'Label: value' is used everywhere.
- Integration availability and the settings block move out of the rail.
why: The rail answers 'what will happen / what is happening', but the answers are scattered. The reader has to scroll, re-parse several header styles and reconcile five near-duplicate readiness statements, one of which ('Not tested') contradicts what just happened. Density only helps when it is scannable.
repro: Open Inspect (Alt+I) after a few runs at 235x52 and scroll the whole rail with the mouse wheel. Click the 'Environment' label, then its ▾.
recommendation:
1. Restructure ConsoleInspectorRail into three ConsoleInspectorSection groups (Next send, Run, Selected turn), each with a full-row toggle and one header grammar.
2. Keep the pinned summary as the single readiness rollup and drop the Run section's duplicates. Mark a readiness row 'verified HH:MM' after a successful generation.
3. Merge the Sources blocks into one (see G2-16).
4. Label built-ins 'Built-in tools'.
5. Wrap recovery copy to two lines, hide section controls when collapsed, and remove the raw resume id.
6. Move 'Live work sources' to Home or Settings ▸ Diagnostics, or behind 'Integrations ▸' at the bottom.
7. Replace the 11-row Conversation settings block with one row: 'Chat settings: claude-haiku-4-5 · T 0.60 · Configure…'.
8. Use 'Label: value' everywhere, including 'Project instructions: choose folder'.

title: 'What happens if I send now?' covers only part of the next send, drifts from the chips and misstates sampling; the complete preview is buried in a second 'Inspector' behind the cost chip or an undocumented key
statement:
The pinned Inspect card lists Where / Scope / Run / Sources / Approvals, plus Credential / Model / Sampling / 'Assistant: General' (console_send_authority_summary.py:70-90 builds five core facts).

What the card leaves out: the system prompt, inline files, auto-retrieval on/off, persona, project instructions, lore (dictionaries/world books), history size and tools.

Where it is wrong:
- It kept saying 'Assistant: General' while the chip said 'Character: Samira'.
- It shows 'Sampling: T 0.60, P 0.95…', but the log says 'Anthropic: both temperature and top_p were provided; sending temperature and dropping top_p.'

To know what will actually be sent, the user has to combine the status strip (System Prompt, Assistant, Library auto-search), the Model section (temperature, max tokens), and Chat Dictionaries, World Books and project instructions further down Inspect.

The genuinely complete view is the 'Conversation Inspector' modal's Next Send tab (Messages 8, System 1, Staged sources, Tools, Raw JSON, Copy payload). It opens only from:
- the 'Context 0% · Current $0.00' chip, whose tooltip mentions it
- Ctrl+Shift+P or /context (chat_screen.py:1981, :6269-6280)

Ctrl+Shift+P is in neither the footer nor the F1 shortcut groups (chat_screen.py:1256-1330). The modal shares the name 'Inspector' with the rail. Its 'Staged sources' pane shows the wrong empty copy: 'No messages yet. Write a prompt to prepare the next send.'
expected: One pre-send summary built from the same prepared-request object as the full preview. It lists every context ingredient with counts as compact 'k: v' rows: System (custom | character), History (7 msgs), Files (2), Library (auto on / 1 staged), Tools (6), model, persona, project instructions, lore, and the model params that will actually be sent. It stays in sync with the chips and ends with 'Open full preview (Ctrl+Shift+P)'. F1 lists the key.
why: 'Exactly what goes to the model' is the main authority question in PRODUCT.md and journey step 7 for this persona. The answer exists, but finding it means reading four or more regions and recalling a hidden shortcut, and the visible summary misleads.
repro: Press Alt+I and read the card, comparing it with the chips. Then click the 'Context 0% · Current …' chip ▸ Context tab. Press F1 and look for Ctrl+Shift+P.
recommendation:
1. Rebuild the card from the prepared-request object the Conversation Inspector uses. Extend ConsoleSendAuthorityProjection with model, system prompt source, persona, auto-search, project instructions, files, history, tools and lore, using the existing '+N more' compact heading.
2. Show only params that will actually be sent.
3. Add a visible 'Preview next send (Ctrl+Shift+P)' action on the card and in the composer Menu, and add the key to the F1 Panes group.
4. Rename the modal 'Chat details' (tabs: Next send, Usage, Exchanges) so that 'Inspect' means the rail only.
5. Fix the Staged-sources empty copy.

title: Inspect 'Live work sources' dumps raw internal fields and Python reprs in a nested scroll region
statement:
The Inspect rail shows raw fields for staged sources:
- 'chunk_id:'
- "citations: ['--- Contents of photosynthe...', '--- Contents of photosynthe...', …]"
- 'requested_top_k: 15'
- 'result_id: 0b0a4bad-…'
- 'runtime_backend: rag-hybrid'
- 'score: None'
- 'score_kind: hybrid_fusion'
- 'search_mode: rag'
- 'source_selector_state: local'
- 'target_id: local:library-rag:…'

This sits in a nested scroll region inside the scrolling rail ('▼ more — scroll').

why: It puts developer debug output on a user surface, and the useful authority signal ('local') is lost among it.
