title: Inspect 'Agents' covers only sub-agents: 'View all runs' is empty after four runs, the ▸ discloses nothing, and a row click opens drill-in in the other rail
statement:
After four primary agent runs, the Inspect rail shows 'Agents  Run history ▸' and a 'View all runs' button.
- The ▸ does not expand, because there are no rows (agent.py:2016-2024).
- 'View all runs' opens 'Sub-agent run history — No saved sub-agent runs.' (right_rail.py:1650-1667: title 'Agents', view_all_label 'View all runs').
- Primary runs are listed nowhere except Trace.

Naming conflicts across rails: the left rail calls its section 'Agent' (singular, the primary run), while the Inspect 'Agents' (plural) means sub-agents only.

Clicking a sub-agent row in the right rail removes the Agents section from the right rail and opens the drill-in ('Sub-agent · error (Back)') in the left rail.
expected: Either the labels say 'Sub-agents' / 'View all sub-agent runs', or there is a true run history that includes primary runs. A disclosure glyph appears only when there is something to disclose. Drill-in opens in place, in the rail that was clicked.
why: A user looking for 'what agents ran in this conversation' follows the scent of 'View all runs', gets 'No saved … runs', and concludes history is broken. The cross-rail jump breaks the spatial model of where agent detail lives.
repro: After several tool runs, open Inspect and click 'Run history ▸', then 'View all runs'. Trigger a failed sub-agent and click its row.
recommendation: Rename the section 'Sub-agents' and the button 'All sub-agent runs', and hide the ▸ when there are no rows. Consider one 'Runs' section listing primary runs (status, duration, tools used, end reason) with sub-agents nested, each opening its Trace. Render drill-down inside the Inspect section with a Back affordance.

title: For 3–10 s after a workspace switch, Environment shows the previous repo's changes, branch, tasks and a clickable 'Review & commit… · 2 files'
statement: After a workspace switch, the Inspect rail's Environment and Tasks sections keep showing the previous workspace's data until the next 10 s poll tick. Depending on where the switch lands in the poll cycle, that is anywhere from 0 to about 10 s. It happens in both directions, and no "Checking workspace…" state is shown in between. W1→W2 (live): from +0.94 s the header, Workspace field and "Where: W2 Beta › W2 Beta Chat" all name W2, but Environment still lists W1's "Changes ▸ +2 −0", "main ▸", "Review & commit… · 2 files" and "Tasks · Backlog ▸ 1 task" until +9.75 s, when it flips to "Changes aren't tracked…". W2→W1 (live): W1 is active but Environment says "Changes aren't tracked for… / Bind a folder and enable C…" (untrue for W1) and W1's Tasks section is hidden until the next tick. The claim that a commit action "points at the wrong repository" is wrong. Clicking the stale "Review & commit… · 2 files" row while in W2 opens Change Review for the current conversation, W2, which reads "Changes aren't tracked for this workspace". So only the label and count are stale, and the click leads to a destination that contradicts them. No action runs against W1's repository. From the code only (not seen live, because the test repo has no PR): the PR rows (open PR URL, add PR summary, fix checks) read the stale snapshot, so during the window they could open or insert the previous repo's PR data.
expected: On a workspace change, Environment immediately shows 'Checking workspace…' with its actions disabled until the new root lands, and never shows another repository's state or actions.
why: The prior critique's P0 (stale root) is now transient rather than permanent, which is real progress. But for several seconds a commit action points at the wrong repository while the rest of the UI says you are in the other one.
repro: W1 with Change Review on and W2 with it off. Click the W2 tab and capture at 1, 3 and 7 s. Then click the W1 tab.
recommendation: On any change of workspace_id, land ENV_PENDING synchronously, keyed by the new workspace id, and disable 'Review & commit…' and 'Review in Change Review…' until a landing for that id arrives. Add a test that a workspace switch never renders the previous root's rows.
fix_direction: Add to TASK-31626 rather than filing a new task. (1) On any change of active workspace or conversation with the rail open, call into the controller right away (e.g. a notify_scope_changed() that runs poll_tick's root-change branch now). (2) Land an ENV_PENDING snapshot synchronously, keyed by the new scope, before dispatching, so the rows read 'Checking workspace…' and the PR/Tasks rows disappear instead of showing the old repo. (3) Row actions that read snapshot data (PR open/add, checks fix, task add) should check that the snapshot's landed root matches the current accessor, and do nothing or re-refresh otherwise. (4) Regression test for both directions (bound→unbound, unbound→bound, and bound→bound): after a switch, and before any tick, the section never shows the previous root's rows.
prior_art: KNOWN_OPEN — TASK-31626; TASK-31660; backlog/tasks/task-31626 - Workspace switch refreshes the Environment panel immediately.md; backlog/tasks/task-31660 - Environment-panel-state-honesty-UNBOUND-and-PENDING-states.md:31
verdicts: live: PARTIAL · code: PARTIAL · skeptic: PARTIAL

title: Many Tab stops are invisible or below 3:1: New tab/Temporary, scroll containers, header and composer buttons, menu rows, post-approval stops
statement: sgr diffs show stops with little or no perceivable change. (a) Tab-strip 'New tab' and 'Temporary' only shift the background from #1e1e1e to #272727 (1.12:1), with no underline or bold; #console-new-chat-tab and #console-new-temporary-tab have no :focus rule (_console.tcss:1325-1343). (b) Inside the collapsed 'Details' section there is a stop where nothing visibly gains focus. (c) The status-chip scroller is a stop shown only by blue 1-cell '─' separators, and the tab-strip scroller only by a blue '───' filler line. (d) The collapsed Inspect handle takes two stops, and the second shows only a blue scrollbar. (e) In the approval card, 'Deny all' is followed by a stop with no indicator, then a transcript scroll container shown only by its scrollbar turning blue. (f) Composer ▾ and Menu focus: background #1e1e1e→#155486 (2.1:1). Header actions (New tab/Settings/…): #242f38→#1c4666 (1.38:1), with no outline. Composer-menu rows: focused background #03253f vs #1e1e1e (1.06:1) plus underline. Switch focus ring: 2.19:1. The composer placeholder at 2.56:1 is covered in G4-41, and tab order in G4-42.
expected: Every Tab stop shows a clearly perceivable indicator (≥3:1 change plus a shape cue, e.g. outline: heavy $accent or reverse video). Containers that only hold focusable children are not stops themselves.
why: When focus 'disappears' on the next Tab, the user doesn't know what Enter will do. The keyboard-first user loses track of focus in the controls that start every workflow.
repro: 235x52: from the composer (Esc) Tab repeatedly; from the transcript Tab through the chips and tab strip; from the left rail Tab past 'Details'; with an approval pending, Alt+A then Tab ×7; diff captures.
recommendation: Apply one focus token set to all Console buttons, chips and menu rows (reverse video or a heavy accent outline), including :focus rules for #console-new-chat-tab and #console-new-temporary-tab. Set can_focus=False on scroll containers with focusable children (status chip scroller, tab strip scroller, handle wrapper, collapsed-section viewports, transcript scroll wrapper), or give them a visible focus frame. Add an sgr regression test asserting every Tab stop changes at least one cell by at least 3:1, like the existing Legible Disabled measurements.

title: Enter on a selected transcript message clears the selection, contradicting F1 and the docs; the text-selection toast teaches a sequence that always fails
statement: F1 ('Enter: show the selected message's actions'; chat_screen.py:1281) and Docs chat-basics.md:424 both say Enter reveals a selected message's actions. The code binds Enter to 'Toggle message selection' (action_confirm_selection; console_transcript.py:2994, 5445-5452), so Enter on a selected message clears it and hides its action row. Pressing s with nothing selected toasts 'Select a message first (j/k, then Enter) to select its text.' (5510-5513). Following it literally fails every time: j selects, Enter deselects, and s shows the same toast again. Reproduced live.
expected: Enter on a selected message moves focus into its action row, as documented. Only Esc clears the selection. The toast gives a sequence that works.
why: Both the help and the error message steer keyboard users into the failing path, which undermines trust in F1.
repro: Send a message; press j (action row and Guide line appear), then Enter (they disappear), then s (toast again).
recommendation: Make Enter on a selected message focus its first action button, and never deselect on Enter. Change the toast to 'Select a message first (j/k), then press s.' Add a test that walks F1's transcript group against the actual key effects.

title: The Get started card's no-provider escape ('Write a note in Library') can't be reached from the keyboard
statement: With the blocking Get started card up, Tab, Shift+Tab, Down and F6 all leave focus on 'Set up provider': the heavy border stays on it, and 'Write a note in Library' never receives focus. Esc does nothing. The secondary action, which exists for local-first users without a provider, is mouse-only. focus_primary_action (console_setup_modal.py:493-500) re-pins focus on every sync (:502-525).
expected: Tab and the arrow keys cycle between the card's actions, and the focus ring moves.
why: PRODUCT.md is keyboard-first, yet the only way forward that needs no provider requires the mouse.
repro: launch.sh j19 120 40 nokey → press Tab, BTab, Down, F6 and compare captures.
recommendation: Let Tab/Shift+Tab and Up/Down move between the card's visible buttons, including the detected-server and notes actions, and stop re-pinning focus to the primary action on every sync.

title: Several Console modals open without focus in their main input, so the first keystrokes are lost
statement: The Library search modal opened with focus on the scroll body; no focus is set on the query Input (console_rag_settings_modal.py:288-345). Typed 'RuBisCO enzyme' went nowhere, and Tab was needed before the query field showed a focus border (sgr diff 49→50). The Conversation settings modal, opened from the Provider chip, also swallowed typed text. The System-prompt editor and the New Workspace modal, by contrast, auto-focus their text field. The Library search hint 'Enter runs the search. Esc or a click outside closes…' sits below the fold of the fixed 20-row modal (height: 20 in BUNDLED_CSS; console_library_search_modal.py:51-61) and can only be seen by scrolling.
expected: Every modal whose purpose is text entry focuses that field on open, and hints and primary actions fit without scrolling at 235x52.
why: Keyboard-first users type immediately, and inconsistent focus rules across modals stop them building a habit.
repro: Header ▸ Search Library, then type at once: nothing appears in the field. Compare with Status ▸ System Prompt.
recommendation: Adopt a Console modal contract: AUTO_FOCUS on the primary input, primary action reachable without scrolling, hint line always visible. Add a test that types immediately after push_screen.

title: Multiline submit keys differ by surface: Enter sends in the composer, inserts a newline in Side chat, and edit modals have no submit key
statement: Composer: Enter sends and Ctrl+J / Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Side chat (a chat about a selection) is a plain TextArea: Enter inserts a newline and there is no send key (its only BINDING is escape; console_side_chat_modal.py:133,167). Settings modal: Ctrl+Enter = Apply, not advertised anywhere else (console_settings_modal.py:1136). Edit message, Edit system prompt and Review notes have no keyboard submit at all, so the user must Tab to the button (console_edit_message_modal.py:105-143; console_system_prompt_modal.py:61-113). Single-line modals (rename, fork title, feedback): Enter submits.
expected: Chat-like inputs (Side chat, Buddy quick reply) behave like the composer. Every multiline form modal submits with Ctrl+Enter, and its hint row says so.
why: The composer trains Enter = send. In Side chat that habit produces stray newlines, and edit modals have no fast path at all.
repro: Select transcript text ▸ Ask in Side Chat ▸ type ▸ Enter (a newline is inserted). Open Edit on a message ▸ Ctrl+Enter (nothing happens).
recommendation: Give Side chat the composer's key map (Enter sends, Ctrl+J inserts a newline). Add Binding('ctrl+enter', 'activate_primary') to every multiline modal through a shared action-row component, and print it in the modal's hint row.

title: The same single letters mean different things in adjacent Console surfaces (transcript vs Trace vs Inspector vs modals)
statement: Transcript: j/k = message, s = select text, e = edit, f = fork, r = regenerate, o = full output, v = review, n = notes, c = copy (console_transcript.py:2991-3003). In the Trace screen, reached from the transcript with y (trajectory_screen.py:204-256), the same letters mean: j/k = next/previous error, s = previous child agent, e = earlier, f = follow, r = retry, o = import trace, v = next feedback, n/p = match, c = capture, y = previous tool, u = next tool, a = next child, b = previous feedback. The pairs 'u/y tool' and 'a/s child' are not mnemonic. Elsewhere: Inspector n/p = sections (chat_screen.py:4874; console_inspector_section.py:921-926); prompt queue modal j/k select, e edit, u/d move, x remove (console_prompt_queue_modal.py:37-43); workspace files modal f filter, x exclude, Backspace back (console_workspace_files_modal.py:259-264); workspace tree s star, m row menu (console_workspace_tree.py:287-290). Removing a row is Delete in inspector sections, x in the queue, and a button only in the transcript. Trace footer hints use lowercase 'enter' while Console uses 'Enter'. The docs confirm c = capture in Inspector/Trace (chat-basics.md:550-551).
expected: A Console key grammar applied everywhere: j/k always move the item cursor, n/p (or n/N) the match, Enter inspects or acts, / filters, one key removes, m or Enter-on-row opens the row menu, and category jumps use a prefix (']e' / '[e', or Shift) as in vim or less. Key casing is the same in every footer.
why: Trace is one key away from the transcript. A user who presses c to copy changes the capture policy instead, and f (fork) becomes follow, often without noticing.
repro: In the transcript press j/k (messages move); press y, then j/k and c in Trace.
recommendation: Publish a Console key grammar in DESIGN.md (movement, filter, open, menu, remove, next/previous of a kind) and apply it to Trace first: keep j/k for row movement, and remap c/f/v/s/o/e/r to non-colliding or modified keys, with category jumps as ]e/[e, ]t/[t or n/N with a kind selector. Make 'remove' one key everywhere.

title: Essential information is available only on hover: the next-send cost ('Send | $'), badge and row-icon meanings, full tab titles
statement: The Send label gains ' | $' when an estimate exists. The '$' means 'hover to read the estimate', which exists only in Send's tooltip (console_composer_bar.py:377-385 label variants; 2016-2030 and 2240 price only as a tooltip; chat-basics.md:55-66 says 'hover Send'). Textual tooltips show on mouse hover, not on focus. The header switches' meaning is also tooltip-only (G4-50). The docs send users to hover for handle-badge meanings, full tab titles, conversation-row state icons and the dictation phase (chat-basics.md:92). The 'What happens if I send now?' card, which is focusable and listed in F1, has no cost row (console_send_authority_summary.py:368-378).
expected: Anything needed for a decision (cost, on/off state) is visible as text or reachable from the keyboard: a Cost row in 'What happens if I send now?', a real figure instead of a bare '$', and tooltip text shown on focus.
why: A keyboard-first user can't see the cost before sending, and a bare '$' with no explanation looks like a glitch.
repro: ready 160x45: type text and note 'Send | $'; Tab to Send: no estimate is visible without a mouse hover.
recommendation: Add 'Cost: ~$0.002 in / ≤$0.01 out' to the send-authority facts and to F1's 'What happens if I send now?'. Replace '| $' with '| ~$0.002' or '| est.'. Show tooltip text on focus for Send and the badges. Add On/Off words to the header switches (G4-50).

title: Rail controls silently leave Console: the green 'Terminal' jumps to Settings ▸ Privacy & Security with no explanation, and 'Search all chats…' / 'Archived chats' jump to Library
statement:
Every observable symptom reproduces on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c (ready mode, 235x52). Three supporting claims are overstated, and severity is P2, not P1.

What reproduces:
- **Rail item.** 'Terminal' is the first item in the Console left rail (col 5, row 9), bold #4ebf71 (7.16:1). It has no Locked label, no tooltip on hover, and no status text. It is the only green text in the rail. The colour is `$ds-authority-local`, which `core/_variables.tcss:86` aliases to `$success`.
- **Click and palette.** Clicking it, or running the palette command 'Console: Open Terminal', switches to F4 Settings with Mode set to Privacy & Security, scrolled to the top.
  - No toast or banner appears. A capture 2 s later is byte-identical, and the app log has no entry.
  - The landing viewport contains the word 'Terminal' 0 times.
  - The unlock block ('DANGER!!! RAW CLI + TERMINAL HOST ACCESS' and 'Allow raw CLI and Terminal access on this device') comes into view after 20 wheel-downs, not about 22.
  - Neither the block nor the checkbox is focused. `apply_navigation_context` in `settings_screen.py` supports a `field` target only for Providers & Models; for Privacy it just calls `_select_category`.
- **Locked card bypassed.** The in-Console locked card ('Terminal is locked. Unlock host access in Settings > Privacy & Security.' plus an 'Open Privacy & Security' button) exists but is never shown in the normal locked state. `action_open_console_terminal` opens the workspace only when the Terminal is permitted or a cleanup receipt is visible.
- **Chat browsing.** 'Search all chats…' and 'Archived chats' in the rail, and the same two buttons in the Ctrl+K switcher, all leave Console for Library ▸ Conversations with the All or Archived scope. The switcher is dismissed first. Neither label names the destination.

Corrections:
1. **"Loses their place" is overstated.** A typed composer draft survived the Terminal detour and the return to Console via the nav bar. Console state is kept; the problem is disorientation and the missing explanation, not lost work.
2. **This is not an accidental plan deviation.** The direct route is pinned by `Tests/UI/test_console_terminal_integration.py::test_locked_terminal_entry_routes_to_privacy_without_open_or_launch`. That test asserts navigation to Settings Privacy and asserts the workspace is not opened. The plan wording ("shows the explicit route to canonical Privacy & Security Settings") is ambiguous. So this is a deliberate but unexplained design choice.
3. **The green is not a false "ready" signal by design.** It is the documented local-authority role colour, which happens to share `$success`'s hue. The real defect is that nothing shows the locked state (DESIGN.md:126 and :344 require explaining why an action is unavailable, at the surface).
4. **The Search/Archived half is weaker.** The Library destination is by design (ADR-147; TASK-32276). The ellipsis on 'Search all chats…' is conventional ("opens a surface needing more input"). What remains is only a missing destination signifier, which is P3 polish.
expected: Controls that leave Console say so ('Open in Library ↗', 'All chats in Library ↗'). Locked features show their state and reason where they sit ('Terminal · Locked' in a muted colour). Activating Terminal opens the in-Console locked card or recovery callout (owner/problem/impact/next action) with 'Open setting'. That action deep-links to Settings and focuses the exact unlock checkbox.
why: The user clicks the most prominent rail item and lands on a dense, unrelated settings page with no explanation. An unexpected context switch loses their place and breaks their mental model of what Console contains. A green 'Terminal' that is actually locked states the wrong thing through colour alone. The design contract requires explicit blocked states and recovery at the point of need.
repro: Launch fresh in ready mode at 235x52 and click 'Terminal' (col 5, row 9) in the Console left rail: you land on Settings ▸ Privacy & Security. Also click 'Search all chats…' in the rail or in Ctrl+K.
recommendation:
1. Always open the in-Console Terminal card or recovery callout, which explains the lock and offers 'Open Privacy & Security'.
2. Deep-link with a field target so Settings focuses the unlock checkbox; Settings '/' search already supports landing on a field.
3. Give the rail item a state word ('Terminal · locked') and a neutral colour, and move it out of the top slot (see G2-36).
4. Suffix every cross-destination control with '↗' and the destination name ('All chats in Library ↗').
5. Tone down 'DANGER!!!' to calm, explicit copy per PRODUCT.md.
fix_direction:
Terminal:
- When the Terminal is locked, open the existing in-Console ConsoleTerminalWorkspace locked card instead of navigating away. It already says 'Terminal is locked…' and offers 'Open Privacy & Security'. At minimum, notify before navigating: 'Terminal is locked — opening Privacy & Security.'
- Update test_locked_terminal_entry_routes_to_privacy_without_open_or_launch to match.
- Extend Settings apply_navigation_context with a Privacy 'field' target for console.raw_cli_permitted. It should scroll to and focus the 'Allow raw CLI and Terminal access' checkbox, mirroring the Providers & Models field route (TASK-33008.2 pattern).
- Give the rail item a state word and tooltip, such as 'Terminal · locked' in muted colour. Keep $ds-authority-local for the unlocked or armed state only.

Search/Archived chats:
- Add a destination cue, for example 'Search all chats in Library ↗' or a tooltip 'Opens Library ▸ Conversations'.

Separately, consider softening 'DANGER!!!' to calm, explicit copy per PRODUCT.md:21.

title: The rail's 'New conversation' button appears, disappears and moves because it is a worker-mounted legacy alias; each change shifts the rows below and causes misclicks
statement:
'New conversation' is a 'transitional legacy alias'. An async worker mounts it out of band after the tray composes (_sync_console_legacy_workspace_context_aliases, chat_screen.py:14225-14290). It is inserted before #console-workspace-conversations when that exists, and otherwise at the end. It is dropped whenever the tray recomposes or relabels (console_workspace_context.py:655-661, where Relabeled drops out-of-band controls).

Observed positions within single sessions:
- J3: below the filter at first launch. Gone after the first send (captures 03–05). Back on a new empty tab (08). Above 'Archive this chat' (09). Missing at 13, 22 and 30; present at 43, 92 and 106.
- J7: below the filter (01, 09, 11). At the top of Conversations (05, 14, 30, and j72 after one resize). Absent (08, 12, 13, 31). It vanished during a send between 30 and 31.
- J8: below the filter (01). Gone (06). Back inside the Conversations action block (08, 130). Between captures 127 and 131, the Model section's 'System: none ▸' moved from row 34 to row 35, and a click on it landed on 'Max tokens' and did nothing.
- L2: below the filter at first paint (row 22). Absent after clicking 'Workspaces' (row 11) or the 'Context rail' header button. First row above 'Archive this chat' after a modal closed or a send.

The rail's width is also unstable: opening Inspect shrinks the left rail, rewrapping titles and truncating the Filter placeholder to 'Filter visible' (J6).
expected: One stable, composed-in 'New chat' control in a fixed slot that survives recompose, or none at all, since the header and tab strip already offer New tab. The left rail keeps a fixed width when the opposite rail toggles.
why: A primary action that moves or vanishes costs a search on each visit. Every appearance shifts the rows below by one, so mouse users misclick: 'Archive this chat' can land where 'New conversation' was, and the Model row click hit 'Max tokens'. Moving targets also change the Tab sequence without warning for keyboard and magnifier users.
repro: Launch and note 'New conversation' below the filter. Send a message: it disappears. Press Ctrl+T and send again: it reappears in a different slot. Or click 'Workspaces' or the 'Context rail' header button, then open and close a modal. Compare captures after Alt+I for rail rewrap.
recommendation:
1. Retire the worker-mounted alias.
2. Either compose 'New chat (Ctrl+T)' inside ConsoleWorkspaceContextTray.compose() at a fixed slot directly under the Conversations header, above the browse actions, or remove it and rely on the tab-strip New (see G2-14).
3. Give the left rail a fixed width that the Inspect rail cannot take from.
4. Add a test asserting the button's index among its siblings is unchanged after a Relabeled event and after a recompose.

title: First view repeats itself: the Conversations section duplicates the current chat, marks the active row only by colour, and stacks centred action buttons above the list
statement:
Layout of the Conversations section, top to bottom:
1. Three centred, full-width buttons: 'Archive this chat', 'Archived chats', 'Search all chats…'.
2. An unlabeled, non-interactive line naming the current chat, in the same blue as the active list row. The chat therefore appears twice ('Chat 1' / 'Chat 1 💬').
3. The filter.
4. Sometimes 'New conversation'.
5. The 'Chats' group.

The active row differs from the others only by colour: #57a5e2 vs #e2e3e5, both bold. The Workspaces tree uses '›' for the same meaning. At 100x30 the section shows only the buttons and the duplicate line, and the list itself is scrolled out of view.

On first arrival, 'Chat 1' appears four times: in the breadcrumb ('Conversation | Chat 1'), on the tab, as the current-chat line under Conversations, and under Conversations ▸ Chats ('Chat 1 💬').

Other repetition:
- 'New tab' is in both the header action row and the tab strip.
- A failed send renders an Assistant 'Failed / Response failed.' block and a separate 'System · Agent run failed…' row.
- Help lists Ctrl+K three times.

This is the 'duplicated Chat 1 rows' the owner noticed.
expected: Each object appears once per region. There is no duplicate current-chat line; it is shown, labelled 'Current:', only when the active chat is filtered out of the list. The active row carries a glyph or text marker ('›' plus bold), as in the tree. Actions sit in a left-aligned compact toolbar or in the section header's menu. There is one New-tab affordance and one failed-turn block.
why: Duplication pads a dense screen, makes a newcomer wonder whether there are two different chats, and uses up the scarce rows at small sizes. A colour-only active marker fails colour-blind users and low-colour themes.
repro: First arrival at 235x52: look at the rail. Relaunch at 100x30. Make any failed send.
recommendation:
1. Remove the selected-summary Static, or show it only when the active chat is filtered out. Alternatively drop the flat Chats group when there is only one chat.
2. Mark the active row with '›' plus bold, to match the tree.
3. Move Archive, Archived and Search into a left-aligned compact action row or the section header's menu, so the list gets the rows.
4. Keep New tab in the tab strip only (see G2-14).
5. Fold the System failure row into the failed assistant turn, and list Ctrl+K once in Help.

title: Finding a chat means choosing among five or six differently scoped, named and styled search fields spread across three owners
statement:
By rule (ADR-083:27-35), saved chats are split across three owners: the Workspaces Tree (named-workspace chats), the flat Conversations list (Default and unassigned) and the Character section (character chats). Only the Conversations list is visible in the collapsed-default state.

Each owner has its own search, and there are more on top:
- Rail 'Search workspaces': full-width, no Clear.
- Rail 'Filter visible titles': with Clear, and lowercases input (G2-07).
- Character 'Search chats'.
- Rail 'Search all chats…': navigates away to Library, although the ellipsis suggests a dialog.
- Header 'Search Library'.
- Ctrl+K 'Search sessions, workspaces, waiting, running, or finished…', with Active / History / Character chats tabs and its own 'Search all chats…' and 'Archived chats' buttons duplicating the rail's.

Scopes, verbs, field styles and clear behaviour all differ.
expected: One 'Find chat' path: a single, consistently styled rail search field (with Clear) that searches all three owners in place and groups results by owner (Workspace ▸ X, Character ▸ Y, Default). Ctrl+K is the same component in a modal. There is one explicit exit, 'Open in Library ↗', for archived or all-time full-text search, offered as an in-switcher escalation.
why: Users have to pick among five similar options, each behaving differently, before they can search at all. ADR-083's one-owner rule is sound for data, but it is pushed onto users as navigation, so they must recall 'which workspace or character was that in?' before they can find a chat.
repro: Look at the header, the rail's Workspaces and Conversations sections, then expand Character, then press Ctrl+K. Count the search inputs.
recommendation:
1. Merge the rail's search fields into one styled field with Clear and one placeholder verb ('Find chats…'). It searches all owners in place and shows results grouped by owner.
2. Keep ADR-083's one-owner rule for placement, not for search.
3. Make Ctrl+K the same component in a modal.
4. Make rail 'Search all chats…' open Ctrl+K in History with the query, keeping the Library hand-off as a second, explicitly labelled step ('Open in Library ↗').

title: The Chats list re-sorts when a chat is opened or renamed, so rows jump after the user acts on them; blank tabs are listed as chats
statement:
After relaunch, the order was Chat 1, Beta, Alpha, Say OK 5, Say OK 1.
- Clicking Say OK 5 moved it to the top.
- Clicking Beta then moved Beta to the top.
- Renaming 'Say OK 5' to 'Gamma…' moved it from last to fifth.

Never-sent blank tabs ('Chat 1', 'Chat 5') are listed with the same 💬 icon as saved chats.
expected: A stable order while the user works (for example by last-message time, which opening a chat doesn't change), or an explicit sort control. Unsaved blank tabs are shown differently or left out.
why: A power user working down the list to reopen several chats clicks the wrong row after each reorder.
repro: Relaunch, then click two rows in the Chats list one after the other. Rename a chat that is not open.
recommendation: Sort by last-message time, which doesn't change when a chat is opened or renamed. Freeze row order while the pointer is over the rail or a menu is open. Mark unsaved blank tabs '(new)', or keep them out of Chats until the first send.

title: The left-rail Agent section dumps raw step output (JSON split mid-token, unrendered markdown) in a different visual language from the transcript
statement:
After a run, the Agent section lists:
- '· model'
- '· calculator'
- '· {"expression": "1234*5678", "result": 7006652, …}', wrapped across lines
- '· 1234 × 5678 = **7,006,652**', with literal asterisks

After the todo run it shows '{"id":"2","version":1,"conten' / 't":"Finish project', split mid-key, and '… (+44 chars)' (agent.py:1240-1260).

Other problems:
- The 'Agent: done' status line scrolls out of the section's inner viewport.
- 'View full log' appears for some runs but not others: absent after the first run, present after the second.

The transcript renders the same content as tidy tool rows with markdown. DESIGN.md says tool, approval and recovery turns 'follow the same flow instead of becoming separate visual languages'.
expected: A compact step list in the same grammar as the transcript tool rows ('✓ calculator · 0.5s'), with results behind expand, markdown rendered or stripped, and the status line pinned.
why: Two regions show the same run in two visual languages, and the rail's version is the harder one to read.
repro: Expand the left-rail Agent section, then run the calculator and todo prompts.
recommendation: Reuse the transcript's tool-row presenter for the rail step list: one line per tool call with a status word and duration. Strip or render markdown, and never wrap JSON inside the rail. Pin the status line above the scrolled list. Always show 'View full log' when a stored log exists.

title: Exporting a conversation to Markdown is buried three levels deep behind an unlabelled 💬 icon, with Save filed under 'Copy as'
statement:
The only route found to save or copy a conversation as Markdown:
1. The 💬 glyph at the right of a chat row (no visible label or tooltip text).
2. 'Conversation actions'.
3. 'Copy as ▸'.
4. 'Clean markdown / Full transcript / Save .md…'.

So a save action sits under 'Copy as'. 'More ▸' is a whole page holding only 'Delete…'. None of this is in the palette, the composer Menu, the header or F1 help.

The reviewer's report notes that this only route also crashes the app (J8-01, which is not part of this batch).
expected: 'Export…' in the palette and the Menu. The conversation-row menu opens from a labelled affordance ('⋯ Actions'). Save and Copy are separate, and there are no single-item submenu pages.
why: Export is a core artifact-preservation task in PRODUCT.md, yet it is effectively undiscoverable.
repro: Look for an export action in the palette, Menu and header; then click 💬 on a chat row.
recommendation: Add a Console 'Export conversation…' action (Markdown clean/full, Chatbook, exchange export) reachable from the palette, the Menu and the conversation menu. Flatten 'More ▸' into the first page, with Delete separated. Use the unified row-menu signifier from G2-40.

title: The left rail mixes five jobs in an order that ignores frequency, and its 'Model' section does not show the model
statement:
Rail order, and what each section actually does:
- Terminal: a launcher that only works when armed, pinned first (left_rail.py:2061-2066).
- Workspaces: navigation.
- Conversations: navigation, but it leads with 'Archive this chat'. That is a state change on the current chat; it is always enabled, and on a new chat it only toasts 'Send and save this conversation before archiving it.' (archive.py:334-343).
- Character: navigation plus reactions.
- Model: configuration. It shows Temperature, Max tokens, 'System: none ▸' and Configure, but not the model name, which TASK-23196 moved to the status strip (left_rail.py:2271-2290).
- Agent: run monitoring ('Agent: idle', 'Progress: 0 queued'), duplicating Inspect 'Agents' and the Run chip (left_rail.py:2420-2500).
- Details: system status (storage, server).

The status chip says 'System Prompt: off' while the Model section says 'System: none'.

ADR-017:27 explicitly left 'merge, rename or reorganize the sections' out of scope, so the section structure has never been designed as a whole.
expected: Per DESIGN's screen grammar (primary list or queue, then workspace, then optional inspector), the left rail is the primary list: chats, grouped by workspace and character. Configuration, monitoring and system status belong in Inspect or Settings.
why: The rail is the first thing scanned in an F-pattern. Leading with a locked launcher and a state-changing action, and naming a section 'Model' without showing a model, costs attention on every visit.
repro: Expand each rail section at 235x52.
recommendation:
Adopt a clear region ownership:
- The left rail becomes 'Chats': one browser with New chat and search (see G2-19).
- Model and Agent move to Inspect's 'Next send' and 'Run' groups (see G2-17).
- Details moves to Settings ▸ Storage/Diagnostics, or to a 'Details' line in the header authority segment.
- Terminal becomes a tab-strip entry ('+ ▾ › Terminal'), /terminal and a palette item, shown with its lock state (see G2-12).
- 'Archive this chat' moves into the row action menu and the tab context menu, disabled with a reason until the chat is saved.

title: The cross-tab fleet line is 2.04:1, coloured 'running' even for approvals, says '1 other agents', can't be clicked, and vanishes when the rail collapses
statement: The only cross-tab summary, pinned in the left rail, renders fg #0c5f9e on #242f38 at 2.04:1, dimmed and in the 'running' token even when the text is '0 other agents running, 1 waiting for approval.' The copy reads '1 other agents running, 0 waiting for approval.': the ungrammatical plural is kept on purpose, and zero clauses are printed. It is a plain Static, so the user can't click through to the waiting tab. At 100x30 the Context rail collapses and the line disappears entirely. The parallel-cap refusal copy in the same product does fix 'agent/agents' grammar.
expected: A legible (≥4.5:1) summary using the warning token when a human is needed, grammatical, omitting zero clauses, clickable per clause, and still present when the rail is collapsed.
why: It is the one place that tells the viewer another tab needs them, and it is the lowest-contrast text on screen.
repro: Run in tab A needing approval, view tab B, and measure with sgr.py runs on rows 9–10. Then resize to 100x30.
recommendation: Remove the dim and use $ds-text-primary, or the warning token when pending > 0. Pluralize and drop zero clauses ('1 tab needs approval · 1 running'). Make each clause a button that activates that tab (reuse the ◆ route). Mirror the same summary as a status-strip chip so it survives rail collapse.

title: Three independent 'unseen result' stores: the tab ✓ clears on visit, the rail row keeps ✓ on the chat being viewed for minutes, and the nav '!' follows a third
statement: After A finished in the background and I visited it, the tab's ✓ cleared at once. The left-rail Chats row for A kept its green ✓ (fg #4ebf71) 8 s later, after an approval, and about 20 minutes later while A was the viewed chat. At one point both rail rows showed ✓ while the tab strip showed only B's. The nav '!' cleared and re-lit on its own schedule.
expected: Viewing a chat acknowledges its outcome everywhere at once: tab, rail row, Ctrl+K 'UNSEEN' group and nav badge.
why: Stale ✓ marks on the chat you are reading make the markers meaningless and hide real new results in other chats.
repro: Let a run finish in a background tab, click that tab, and compare the tab label with its rail row over the next minutes.
recommendation: Introduce one ConversationAttention projection per conversation, feeding tabs, rail rows, the Ctrl+K groups, the fleet line and the nav badge. Make one 'rendered/visited' event acknowledge the controller outcome, the activity receipts and the durable marks together.

title: 'N more conversations — search with Ctrl+K' reports the wrong number, and open blank tabs push every saved chat out of the rail
statement: With 303 saved chats the rail showed 11 rows and '64 more conversations — search with Ctrl+K'. Over the session the number changed to 74 (12 tabs), 13 (25 tabs), 83/84 (26 tabs), 70 (8 tabs) and back to 64 after relaunch, while about 292 saved chats were actually hidden. The count is the loaded page (at most 75 rows) minus displayed rows. With 25 tabs open, blank 'Chat 25'…'Chat 18' tabs filled every visible Chats row. The notice also sits above 'New conversation' and the list rather than at the list's end.
expected: The count should be the true number of chats not shown, or wording that doesn't imply a count (e.g. 'Showing 11 most recent of 303 · Ctrl+K searches all'). Saved chats shouldn't be displaced by untouched blank tabs.
why: A count that jumps between 13 and 84 misreports the size of the user's history and undermines trust in the rail as an index.
repro: Seed 300 chats, launch at 235x52, note the notice; open 10–25 tabs with Ctrl+T and watch it change.
recommendation: Get the total from a COUNT over the flat-lane scope (already available as the service 'total') and render 'Showing 11 of 303 — Ctrl+K searches all' at the bottom of the list. Exclude never-sent blank tabs from Chats, or group them under a single 'Open tabs' line (cf. G2-21).

title: The rail filter reports phantom matches ('2 matches. Showing 1 of 2' for one chat), and Clear once left the list showing only the current tab
statement: Filtering for '#099' showed '2 matches. Showing 1 of 2' with a single row. The DB has exactly one conversation title containing 099, and this reproduced twice. The rail sums the totals from the separate 'global' and Default-workspace scope queries but deduplicates the rows, so one chat returned by both is counted twice. In one run, clicking Clear left the Chats list with only 'Chat 1' under '64 more conversations' for at least 15 s (4 captures), until opening Ctrl+K forced a refresh. A later attempt did not reproduce this.
expected: The count should equal the number of distinct matching chats, and Clear should restore the unfiltered list immediately.
why: 'Showing 1 of 2' sends users looking for a second match that doesn't exist. An emptied list after Clear looks like data loss.
repro: Seed 300 chats; type a unique title fragment in 'Filter visible titles'; read the status; click Clear and capture over 15 s.
recommendation: Compute the total over distinct conversation ids (one query with scope IN (...) or a set union), and never let 'Showing X of Y' exceed the deduplicated set. On Clear, synchronously restore the settled unfiltered rows before any async refresh.

title: A saved conversation icon and colour disappear whenever the chat has a state marker; the 'leftmost icon control' is dead code, and the toast only mentions the icon
statement: I set 🚀 + Amber on a chat that was waiting for approval. The toast said 'Updated the icon for "Reply with exactly this mar..."'. Nothing changed on screen: the rail Chats row kept '✋', and there was no icon on the tab or in Ctrl+K Active or History. Reopening the picker showed '🚀 … #fbbf24', so the choice had persisted. The rail shows the custom icon only in the trailing row-menu slot, and only when the conversation has no attention state (approval, running, failed, ready, unread…). The picker's tooltip and the builder _conversation_appearance_button describe a separate 'leftmost icon control', but that method has no callers. After relaunch in ASCII mode, the custom icon shows only as the literal '[icon]'.
expected: The chosen icon and colour stay visible in a stable slot, separate from the run-state marker. The toast names what changed ('icon and colour updated').
why: Users set icons so they can find the chats that matter, and those chats are most often in an attention state. A choice that is saved but not shown reads as a failed save, so users repeat it.
repro: Trigger an approval card in a chat. Rail row menu → 'Icon and colour…', pick an icon and a colour, Apply. Look at the rail row, tab and Ctrl+K. Reopen the picker.
recommendation: Wire the existing leading appearance control into rail rows, or give the icon a fixed leading cell and keep state markers trailing. Mirror the same slot in tabs and Ctrl+K. Change the toast to 'Updated icon and colour for …' or 'Updated colour for …'. In ASCII mode, show the tint on a fixed glyph instead of the word '[icon]'.

title: Modal action rows vary in order, alignment, size, primary styling and dismiss verb across Console modals
statement: Most Console modals put Cancel left and primary right: auto-speak consent, capture policy, Edit message, endpoint template, exchange export, feedback, fork, rename ('Rename Chat Tab: Cancel Save'), summarize, System prompt ('Clear  Cancel  Apply', right-aligned, 3-row, Apply primary), prompt variables, trace export and Save .md. Reversed or odd: Library search 'Search Library | Cancel'; Library access 'Save | Cancel | Reload | Compare / Retry | Discard changes' (left, 1-row, Save first); Review notes 'Save | Cancel | Edit | Delete'; Scope picker 'Save | Clear scope | Cancel' / 'Confirm | Cancel'; Generate image 'Paste command | Cancel'; Appearance/Customize conversation 'Apply | Clear | Cancel' (Apply first, left); Reaction 'Use reaction | Clear | Cancel'; Project instructions 'Proceed | Cancel | Disable'. Conversation settings has Cancel first and then 3-4 commit buttons. Side chat has 'Send  Close'; Save as… and Help have 'Close'. The composer Menu has only a hint ('Esc closes…'), and the Style picker has no buttons or hint. The primary is unstyled in Save .md 'Save', Scope picker, Appearance 'Apply' and Reaction 'Use reaction', while 'Close' is styled primary in the run log and Conversation Inspector. The dismiss label varies: Cancel, Close, Back, Done, Stay, 'Keep current policy'. List pickers vary too: OptionList (character), sectioned rows (switcher), 3-row centred buttons (Menu, Save as, Style).
expected: One modal footer component: right-aligned [Cancel] [Primary verb] with the primary styled and on the right, destructive actions set apart, 1-row buttons in dense modals, and Esc/Enter hints. One list-picker component.
why: Spatial habit decides which button gets hit. Flipped orders cause wrong clicks and Enter-on-focus mistakes, for example Clear next to Apply.
repro: Open the header 'Search Library' (primary on the left), then any rename or Menu ▸ Save as Chatbook (primary on the right), then each modal listed.
recommendation: Build ConsoleModalFooter/ConsoleModalActions(primary, secondary=(), cancel='Cancel', destructive=()) to enforce order and variants and render the key hint ('Esc cancel · Ctrl+Enter primary'), plus a ConsoleListPicker. Migrate all ~40 Console modals. Use 'Close' only for read-only modals and never style it primary. Add a snapshot or AST test on button order.

title: Esc silently discards typed input in most text-entry modals but is guarded in Prompts and Library access
statement: The Prompts modal and Library access intercept Esc on unsaved edits and show 'Keep editing / Discard changes'; Library access even relabels Cancel as 'Keep editing'. Edit message, Edit thinking, Edit system prompt, Rename, Feedback comment, Fork title and Side chat use the default request_safe_cancel, so Esc drops what was typed with no warning. The Settings modal guards only memory-reset and compaction side effects and discards field drafts (noted in the 2026-09-26 report). Elsewhere in Console, Esc means 'return to composer' or 'clear selection', so users press it by reflex.
expected: One dirty-input rule for every Console modal: Esc on a modified field asks once (Keep editing / Discard) or preserves the draft for reopening.
why: One reflexive key loses a long message edit or system-prompt rewrite, and users can't learn which modals are safe.
repro: Press e on a message, type a paragraph, press Esc: the text is gone. Compare Menu ▸ Browse Prompt Library, edit, Esc: a guard appears.
recommendation: Add a dirty() hook to SafeModalDismissMixin. When it returns true, _perform_safe_cancel shows the same inline Keep editing / Discard row used by Prompts and Library access. Opt in all text-entry modals.

title: Ctrl+K switcher and nested-modal keyboard flow: F2 ignores the highlighted row, the modal re-centres while typing, mode buttons keep focus, Esc on Rename also closes the switcher, and Settings needs two Esc presses
statement: Baseline is good: cost consent, Ctrl+K, F1, Ctrl+P, More… and Settings all trap Tab and return focus to the invoker on Esc. The exceptions: (1) With one result marked '▸' and 'Enter switches to: Say OK 2', F2 says 'Focus an open agent result to rename it.' (jargon); it takes ↓ or Tab into the list first. (2) As results narrow from 4 to 1, the dialog re-centres, moving its title and search row from line 14 to line 19. (3) After clicking the 'History' mode button, typed text ('OK 3') goes nowhere because focus stays on the button. (4) Esc on 'Rename Chat Tab' (opened with F2 from the switcher) closes both the rename dialog and the switcher, so the list context is lost. (5) Conversation settings opens with the Provider list auto-expanded (10 rows): the first Esc only collapses it and shifts the layout, and a second Esc closes. (6) The switcher hint mixes formats and misses a separator ('Enter:switch F2: rename · ↑↓:move … Esc:close').
expected: F2 acts on the highlighted row. The modal keeps a fixed top anchor. Focus returns to the query after a mode change. One Esc closes only the topmost surface, and nested dialogs return to their parent. Pickers don't auto-expand on open. One hint format.
why: The keyboard-first switcher is the power user's main tool, and predictable dismissal is what makes modal-heavy keyboard work safe. These hitches cost keystrokes and lose context.
repro: Ctrl+K, type 'OK 2', F2. Click History and type. Ctrl+K → Tab → ↓ → F2 → Esc. Header Settings → Esc → Esc.
recommendation: Make F2 target the committed or highlighted row, and when nothing is selected say 'Select a chat in the list, then press F2 to rename'. Pin the switcher to a fixed top offset with a fixed-height results area. Focus the query after a mode button press. Push Rename on top of the switcher and pop back to it. Open the provider picker collapsed. Use one hint format: 'Enter switch · F2 rename · ↑↓ move · Shift+F3 mode · Esc close'.

title: The Edit Message modal opens with the caret at the start, and Ctrl+End doesn't move it
statement: Pressing e on a user message opens 'Edit Message' with the caret before the first character. Ctrl+End followed by typing ' Keep the whole reply under 12 lines.' inserted the text at the beginning ('Keep the whole reply under 12 lines.Reply in markdown …'), and the malformed prompt went out via Edit & resend.
expected: The caret starts at the end of the text, and Ctrl+End/End work as in any editor.
why: Appending a clarification is the most common edit, and here it silently produces a malformed prompt.
repro: Select a user message, e, Ctrl+End, type.
recommendation: Move the TextArea cursor to the document end on mount, and confirm Ctrl+End reaches the TextArea rather than a screen binding.

title: Clicking outside the message 'More…' menu to close it also activates the control underneath
statement: With More… open, I clicked outside the menu on the message's 'Copy' button. The menu closed and 'Copied message to clipboard.' fired. Earlier, a click beside the menu to dismiss it re-triggered Speak (log: console-message-action-speak pressed at 15:12:15). The outside-click handler dismisses menus after Textual has already delivered the press to the widget under the pointer. The code comment says focus has already moved there. The same row holds Edit, Fork, ♻ Regenerate and ---> Continue, which spend tokens or rewrite the chat.
expected: The first click outside an open popup only dismisses it, as on the web and in most TUIs.
why: A dismiss gesture can trigger a paid regenerate or a fork without intent.
repro: Select a reply → More… → click on 'Copy' (or ♻) outside the menu box.
recommendation: Render the menu over a transparent capture layer, or consume the first outside press (event.prevent_default/stop) when a menu is open. Apply the same rule to the selection, conversation-row and workspace menus.
evidence: gap5 log lines 599 and 604 (speak and copy pressed via outside clicks)

title: Rewind modal: a false 'Finish the current exchange' dead end, and keyboard and layout gaps
statement: /rewind opens 'Rewind' with no explanation of what Restore or Summarize will do. Prompt rows are centred and truncated at about 60 of 72 available columns ('#2  What energy density … does the Qu...'). Down does not move between rows (Tab does), and after Enter the actions mount below while focus stays on the row. With the tab idle ('Ready'), after a Continue turn, both Summarize buttons are disabled with 'Finish the current exchange before summarizing.'. Nothing is running and there is no way to 'finish'. The rule trips on a durable-unit boundary mismatch. 'Uses the active model once' is repeated under each disabled button. Esc closes the whole modal rather than going back from the action level.
expected: One line of purpose ('Restore removes later turns from the active path; you can switch back with Variants'). Arrow-key row navigation. Focus moves to 'Restore to here' after a row is chosen. Disabled reasons that are true and actionable. Esc goes back one level.
why: A power-user recovery tool that is hard to use from the keyboard and gives false reasons for disabled actions.
repro: Chat with 2+ turns → Continue on a reply → /rewind → Enter → pick a row.
recommendation: Add purpose copy and a consequence line per action ('Hides N later turns'). Left-align rows with full-width previews. Add up/down navigation and move focus to the primary action on reveal. Replace the durable-boundary refusal with a precise, fixable reason, or fix the boundary after Continue. Make Esc step back from the action level to the list.

title: Finishing setup with 'Start chatting' lands on a false warning: 'Provider settings changed before Console opened. Review setup and try again.'
statement: On a fresh profile, finishing Quick setup with 'Start chatting' reliably lands in Console with a warning toast: 'Provider settings changed before Console opened. Review setup and try again.' At the same moment the transcript says 'Ready — type a message to begin.', the status strip shows Provider: Anthropic / Model: claude-haiku-4-5, and the header shows Ready (the toast covers it). So setup worked, and the user is still told to redo it. Two details in the finding are wrong. (1) Duration: this is Textual's default 5 s warning toast, not ~12 s. It was visible 3.5-6 s after Enter and gone by 7.5-9 s. (2) Mechanism: the wizard's finishing writes are not the cause. The wizard stages the first-chat intent after its last write (setup_completed). What breaks the generation fence is Console's own first-mount rail-scope seed. During compose, _ensure_console_rail_scope_seed calls _save_console_rail_preferences, which writes [console.rail_state]."console_rail_state:global:shared-layout-v1". That write lands between 'Navigating to screen: chat' and 'Screen chat mounted', before on_mount consumes the handoff. So the first fix the finding recommends ('take the config revision after the wizard's last write') is what the code already does and would not help. Also, the toast only tells the user to review setup; nothing actually sends them back to the wizard.
expected: Setup ends with a success confirmation such as 'You're set up — Anthropic · claude-haiku-4-5', never with an alarm the user cannot act on.
why: Setup ends on an error that contradicts the Ready state beside it and sends the user back into the wizard for nothing.
repro: launch.sh j20 160 45 fresh → Enter → Down (Anthropic) → Tab Tab → paste key → Ctrl+N → Enter → Enter → Ctrl+N → Enter (Start chatting).
recommendation: Take the config revision after the wizard's last write, or compare provider and model values instead of the generation counter. If the intent really is stale, fall back silently to current defaults and show a success line naming the provider and model. Keep the warning only for a real mismatch, and name what changed.
fix_direction: Do not take the config revision later; the wizard already does that, so the fix has to be on the Console side. Options, matching TASK-33001.10's ACs: (a) fence on the saved provider and model rather than the global config generation counter. _current_first_chat_defaults already compares them after the generation check, so dropping or narrowing the generation gate to provider/model-relevant keys is enough to pass here. (b) Order the first-mount rail-scope seed write after the handoff consume. (c) When the fence fails but the current saved defaults still equal intent.provider and intent.model, apply or acknowledge the intent silently instead of warning. Keep the warning only for a real provider/model change, and name what changed. Separately, confirm success, e.g. 'You're set up — Anthropic · claude-haiku-4-5' (the extra AC this finding would add to TASK-33001.10). Important caveat: when the fence passes (my counterfactual run), Console lands with TWO tabs both titled 'Chat 1' (18-cf-landed.png): the first-mount default session plus the reserved first-chat session. Fixing only the fence would trade the false warning for a duplicate-tab defect. The fix should have the first mount adopt the reserved session rather than create another one.

title: Wizard: Enter means Next only sometimes; in the key field it runs a probe that asks for a nonexistent endpoint, and on Protect it opens the password dialog
statement: Every observable fact in the finding reproduces exactly on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c (fresh profile, 235x52), but the impact is overstated. On the Anthropic Provider step the footer says 'Enter / Ctrl+N next'. Enter in the API-key field with a key present never advances (a second Enter gives the same result, and the screen is unchanged 9 s later). Instead it shows 'Enter a valid endpoint before testing.', although Anthropic has no endpoint field and no visible Test button. From the first typed key character the panel shows 'Provider settings changed since test; test again.' (no test ever ran) directly above 'Key staged - it will be checked when you continue. Connection testing is unavailable for this provider.' On Protect with a key staged, focus lands on 'Set a password', so Enter opens the master-password dialog. After Esc, focus returns to that button, so Enter reopens the dialog. Ctrl+N advances from both steps, while Enter does advance on Welcome, Model and Voice, so the inconsistency is real. Overstated: the user is not stuck, because the working alternative (Ctrl+N) is on the same hint line and Next is visible. The user is not pushed into encryption either: the dialog is a cancelable modal, Esc leaves the config unchanged, and Summary reports keys stored as plain text. Net: misleading, contradictory copy plus an inconsistent Enter model on the onboarding path, with a workaround shown on screen, so P2 rather than P1. Two extras: (a) the prior-art point that TASK-1506 added a visible Test button does not apply to Anthropic, because that button lives in the connection section, which is hidden for cloud providers; for Anthropic, Enter-in-key-field starts a probe that can never run. (b) The Protect copy says 'Skip to leave keys as plain text' but there is no Skip control; the skip is Next, which is not focused.
expected: Enter consistently does what the footer says, or the hint follows focus. No request for an invisible endpoint, and no 'test again' where testing is unavailable.
why: A keyboard-first newcomer following the on-screen hint gets stuck on step 2 and is pushed into an encryption flow on step 5.
repro: launch.sh j13 235 52 fresh → Enter → Down → Tab Tab → paste key → Enter (stuck) → Ctrl+N … Protect → Enter (password dialog).
recommendation: In the key field, make Enter stage the key and advance. Put probing behind a visible Test button shown only where testing exists. For cloud providers, drop the endpoint copy or say 'This provider is checked when you continue'. Focus Skip/Next on Protect. Generate the footer hint from the focused control.
fix_direction: 1) In _advance_on_input_submit, drop the key-field exception, or at least apply it only when a probe is actually available (_probe_target() is non-empty and identity is not None). Otherwise Enter stages the key and advances. 2) In _launch_probe, never show endpoint copy for providers without an endpoint field; return early silently or say 'This provider is checked when you continue'. 3) In _invalidate_provider_test, show 'changed since test; test again' only when cancelled or invalidated evidence existed (not merely changed=True), and never when testing is unavailable for the provider. 4) Protect: give ProtectStep a preferred_focus() returning the Next button (or add an explicit 'Skip' button and focus it), and align the subtitle's 'Skip' wording with a real control. 5) Optionally derive the footer hint from the focused control (for example 'Enter sets a password' on the Protect button), or keep Enter consistently mapped to Next.

title: Wizard Provider step shows a config-jargon error before the user types and clips the list to 4 rows
statement: Highlighting Anthropic immediately shows 'Couldn't discover models for Anthropic. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or add api_key under [api_settings.anthropic]. Or go Back.' above an empty key field. Below it the helper says 'No key yet? Enter skips this step', so the screen says both 'go Back' and 'Enter skips'. The provider OptionList is 5 rows tall (Popular + 4 providers) with a scrollbar, while about 25 empty rows sit below. The other ~35 providers are hidden, and scrolling to them triggers G3-01. On first entry OpenAI is highlighted, but no key field shows until the highlight moves.
expected: No failure message before the user acts. Plain-language guidance with no TOML paths. The list uses the available height with Cloud/Local/Other headers visible, and the credential panel renders for the initially highlighted provider.
why: The first key screen greets the user with a config-syntax error and hides most of the choices.
repro: launch.sh … fresh → Enter → observe the list; press Down once.
recommendation: Hold discovery errors until a key is entered or Next is pressed. Use copy like 'Paste an Anthropic API key (get one at console.anthropic.com), or press Next to skip.' Size the list to its content, up to the free height. Render the credential panel for the initial highlight.

title: Wizard stepper and summary overclaim completion, use config ids, and render finish actions flat
statement: After skipping Protect, the stepper shows a green ✓ on Protect (all five step boxes #4ebf71), while the Summary says '✗ Key encryption — API keys are stored as plain text'. Voice shows '✓ Voice — PocketTTS (default voice)', although the step said 'Not tested yet' and the user did nothing. Values are raw ids ('Provider — anthropic', 'Theme — textual-dark'). The five finish actions (Start chatting, Add your first document, …) and 'Restore a backup' share the canvas background #1e1e1e, so only the focused one reads as a button. The Welcome step renders an empty red-tinted error strip (bg #352227) under 'Restore a backup' because Static('', classes='setup-step-error') lacks 'hidden'.
expected: The stepper distinguishes done, skipped and needs-attention. The summary uses display names and marks untested items. Finish actions look like buttons, with one primary. No error chrome appears without an error.
why: The last onboarding screen certifies things that aren't true and makes the next step hard to spot.
repro: Run Quick setup, skip Voice and Protect with Enter/Ctrl+N, and read the Summary.
recommendation: Give the stepper three states (✓ done, – skipped, ! needs attention). Mark Voice 'set, not tested'. Use provider_display_name and theme display names. Style the finish actions as buttons with Start chatting primary. Add 'hidden' to the empty welcome error Static.

title: The not-ready Console card is generic (doesn't name the provider or the missing piece), discards typed text, and F1 has no setup help
statement: In nokey mode (Anthropic + claude-haiku-4-5 configured, no key), the card reads '1. ● Connect a provider (API key or local server) 2. ○ Pick a model 3. ○ Send your first message'. Nothing says Anthropic is selected and only the key is missing, and step 2 shows ○ although a model is saved. Typing a draft ('Summarize the plot of Hamlet…') shows a one-time toast and the keystrokes are discarded (console_setup_modal.py:502-525), so after the key is saved in Settings the composer is empty. F1 while blocked shows the generic Console reference.
expected: 'Anthropic is selected but has no API key. [Add Anthropic key]', with the model step ✓ (claude-haiku-4-5). Keystrokes typed while locked become a draft that appears when the composer unlocks. F1 opens a 'Getting set up' section.
why: Users must work out what's missing, their typing is lost silently, and help ignores the one thing they need.
repro: launch.sh j14 235 52 nokey → read the card → type a sentence → Enter → paste key → Esc s → click the Console tab.
recommendation: Pass the provider display name and the blocker into step one ('Add an API key for Anthropic'), and mark step 2 done when a model is set. Buffer printable keys into the session draft. Swap F1 content to 'Getting set up' while the card blocks (see G3-21).

title: 'Skip setup' stacks three interruptions, lands somewhere different from 'Exit setup', and the consent modal names providers the user never configured
statement: Skipping from Welcome at 80x24 shows the Skip-setup confirm, then Home (not Console) with a 'Check model lists online?' modal, then a toast. The modal says 'tldw can fetch … from your configured cloud providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, MistralAI, Moonshot, OpenRouter, QwenCloud, ZAI) … using your configured API keys'. The list is hard-coded, and no provider or key is configured. The Home card says 'Set up Console model'. Exiting the wizard at step 2 instead lands on Console with the setup card.
expected: One consistent landing after leaving setup (Console with the card). Consent is asked only once keys exist, and it lists the providers actually configured.
why: A first-timer is asked to allow network calls 'using your configured API keys' when they have none, which undermines the honest-authority promise.
repro: launch.sh j16 80 24 fresh → Esc → Skip setup; compare with exit at step 2.
recommendation: Defer catalog consent until at least one catalog-capable provider has a key, and build the list from configured providers. Route skip and exit to the same Console setup card.

title: The command palette covers only 18 Console actions, while F1 claims it 'lists every Alt action'
statement: The Console palette provider exposes 18 entries (console_command_provider.py:31-126). Searches for approval, hands, dictate, trace, export, summar, fork, canvas, side chat, video and stop return only nav entries or 'No matches'. Missing: Stop, Review pending approval (Alt+A), Hands-free (Ctrl+Shift+H), Dictate, Trace (Y), Save/Copy as Markdown, Summarize, Fork, Side chat, Generate image/video, Attach file, Library access, Speak replies. F1 help says 'Ctrl+P: palette lists every Alt action — the reliable path' (chat_screen.py:1348). The first palette entry a new user sees is 'Recover agent work…'.
expected: Every visible or keyed Console action has a palette entry with the same name as its button, plus its shortcut.
why: The palette is the user's catalogue for 'what can this do?'. Claiming completeness when it isn't complete breaks trust, especially for macOS users whose Alt chords don't work.
repro: Ctrl+P, then type each query.
recommendation: Generate palette entries from one Console action registry shared with the header, Menu, slash commands and key bindings. Add a test asserting every Binding and every WorkbenchAction has a palette hit. Put 'New chat tab' and 'Change model…' ahead of the recovery tools. Include close/rename/archive (G4-45).

title: Conversation colour palette works only on dark themes: 21 of 22 swatches are below 3:1 on a light theme, and the preview prints the hex code in the chosen colour
statement: In the 'Icon and colour…' picker under solarized_light, the swatch squares measure 1.23:1 (Lime), 1.36 (Amber), 1.42 (Green), 1.47 (Cyan), up to 2.43 (Indigo); only Ruby reaches 3.83. After choosing Amber, the preview line reads '🚀 Reply with exactly this mar...  #fbbf24', with the hex code drawn in #fbbf24 at 1.36:1. It is not a preview of how the rail row will look. Swatch names exist only as hover tooltips. The palette source says 'All still truecolor-readable on dark rail panels', and the colour is applied as a fixed Rich-markup hex, so a light-theme user can pick a colour that later renders unreadably.
expected: Swatches and applied tints clear 3:1 against the rail surface in the active theme, or are adjusted to the theme's light or dark mode. Names are visible for keyboard users. The preview shows the actual row.
why: The feature exists to make chats findable at a glance. In a light theme most choices produce a marker that is nearly invisible. A keyboard or low-vision user cannot tell 'Cyan' from 'Sky' without hovering.
repro: Theme solarized_light. In the rail Chats row, open the row menu (the trailing glyph) → 'Icon and colour…'. Measure the swatch row. Type 'rocket', Enter, click the third swatch.
recommendation: Store the hue, and render it through a helper that lightens or darkens it until it reaches ≥3:1 against $ds-surface-panel in the current theme. Better still, render conversation colour as a background chip behind the icon. Show the highlighted swatch's name next to the strip (for example 'Amber · #fbbf24'). Replace the preview with a mock rail row in the current theme.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/Chat/console_appearance.py:29-54 (fixed hex palette; comment 'readable on dark rail panels'); tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_appearance_picker_modal.py:275-286 (tooltip-only names), :504-518 (preview prints hex); console_session_switcher_modal.py:107-110 ([{color}] markup)

title: Manual Library search shows no progress for about 25 s (silent first-use model download), then stages evidence unannounced
statement: On a fresh profile, the first manual Search Library run downloads the 87 MB sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model from the Hugging Face Hub and never says so. From Enter to completion took 21 s, 24 s and 23 s across three live runs. The Console is not silent during the wait, which contradicts the finding. Within about 2 s the always-visible strip above the composer shows "Staged for next send · 1 source [Un-stage]" with the row "Library Search/RAG retrieval — Library Search/RAG". The status bar also changes from "Sources: 0" to "Sources: 1", and the Inspect rail edge shows "1 staged". The real problem is that this in-progress state reads as evidence already staged. The only in-progress cue on the main surface is the row's accent-blue colour (#0178d4 on #242f38, 3.01:1). There is no "Searching…" text, elapsed time or progress, and the word "Retrieving" appears only inside the Inspector. On completion the row text changes in place and no notice appears. Pressing Send during the search is refused rather than sent without evidence, which also contradicts the finding. The refusal uses wrong-cause copy: "Console send blocked: Library search has no available evidence. Review source authority before sending." Un-stage during the search clears the strip but does not cancel the search. About 18 s later the result stages itself again ("Sources: 1", strip back), with no notice, and would be attached to the next send.
expected: A visible 'Searching Library… 12s · Cancel' state near the composer or strip. First use discloses the local embedding model download (size, source). On completion: 'n sources staged for your next message'.
why: With no feedback, users re-run the search or send without evidence, and the evidence then attaches silently to whatever they send next. An unannounced network download also undercuts local-first trust.
repro: Fresh profile: Search Library ▸ type a query ▸ Enter, then watch the main surface for 30 s.
recommendation: Show the pending 'searching' state in the always-visible staged-evidence strip above the composer ('Searching Library… 12s · Cancel'). Block or warn on send while a search is pending. Gate the first embedding download behind a one-time disclosure with its size.
fix_direction: Give the in-progress state its own display in ConsoleStagedEvidenceStripState when launch.status is 'searching'. The heading should read "Searching Library… Ns", with a Cancel control and no "N source(s)" count, and the search should not count toward "Sources: N" or "1 staged". Make Cancel and Un-stage cancel the 'console-library-rag-search' worker group. Also give each launch a staging token so a late outcome is dropped if the user has un-staged or replaced it. Replace the blocked-send copy for a pending search with "Library search still running — wait or cancel it". When the search finishes, show a notice such as "1 source staged for your next message". Before the first embedding download, tell the user the model name, size (~87 MB) and source (Hugging Face Hub) and ask for consent, or pre-fetch the model during setup.
