verdicts: live: PARTIAL · code: PARTIAL · skeptic: PARTIAL
evidence: tldw_chatbook/UI/Console_Modules/retrieval.py:451-452 (a 'searching' status exists but is surfaced only in the Inspector)

title: Opening a 400-message chat shows 'No messages yet.' under the previous chat's title for about 2 s
statement: After pressing Enter on 'Long build log review' in Ctrl+K, captures at about 1.5–2.5 s show the new tab 'Long build log rev…' already in the strip. The header still said 'Conversation | Chat 1', the transcript showed the empty state 'No messages yet.', and the cost chip already showed the new chat's '$0.3961'. The transcript painted at about 3–4 s.
expected: The header should switch immediately, and a loading state such as 'Loading 400 messages…' should appear instead of the empty-state copy.
why: For about 2 seconds the chat looks empty, as if its history were lost, and the header, tab and chip disagree about which chat is open.
repro: Seed a 400-message chat; Ctrl+K → type its title → Enter; capture every 0.5 s.
recommendation: Update the transcript header and tab selection synchronously on activation. Render a 'Loading conversation…' placeholder (with the message count if known) until the first hydrated window paints, and reserve 'No messages yet.' for chats with a confirmed zero count.

title: Extends G1-03: /generate-image gives no progress at all; the prompt vanishes and the header says 'Ready' until the image arrives
statement: Enter on '/generate-image a sunny meadow…' cleared the composer. At +2 s and +6 s the transcript still read 'No messages yet.' and the header 'Ready'. Nothing indicated generation, and no user turn recorded the request. The card appeared only when the backend returned (the mock delay was 6 s; real backends take 10–60 s). There is no Cancel. On failure the handler restores the draft as a collapsed paste token.
expected: An immediate in-transcript 'Generating image · backend · elapsed · Cancel' row, anchored to a user turn showing the command, and replaced by the card when done.
why: Long silent waits past the 10 s limit lead users to resend, which the in-flight guard then refuses with a system message.
repro: Configure any image backend → Composer Menu → Generate Image → enter a prompt → Paste command → Enter → capture at 2 s and 6 s.
recommendation: Append a pending generation card at dispatch, with backend, elapsed time and a Cancel that sets a cancellation flag the batch checks. Echo the command as a user turn. On failure, restore the draft as plain text.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/UI/Console_Modules/image.py:1336-1380 (draft cleared, batch awaited with no progress row)

title: Below 100 columns both rails can render at once, crushing the transcript to 14–16 columns at 80x24 (26 at 90x30); stored preferences make this survive a restart
statement:
The defect is real and wider than reported, but P2 fits better than P1. Below 100 columns, if both rails are explicitly open, both render beside the transcript. Measured transcript width between the rail borders: 16 columns at 80x24, 26 at 90x30, 36 at 99x30, and 10 at 74x30.

Three routes produce it, each reproduced live:
1. Open Context and Inspector at 235x52, then relaunch with REUSE=1 at 80x24. The stored left_open_explicit and right_open_explicit markers survive the restart, and the screen shows 'No / messages / yet.', 'Chat ▸' and 'Conversation |'. A live resize from 235 to 80 gives the same result.
2. At 80x24 with Context open and Inspect's edge handle hidden, press Alt+I. The transcript drops from 50 to 16 columns and the reply wraps one word per line.
3. At 80x24 with Inspector open, press Alt+C twice to hide and reopen Context. Both rails end up open, because console_context_reveal_preferences closes Inspector only in the 100-149 band.

The layout is also inconsistent across widths. At 100 columns the app collapses Context and shows a notice saying the terminal is "too narrow for it", yet at 99 and below, where there is less room, both rails render.

The cause is in console_rail_state.py: each rail is checked alone against its own budget (left 70, right 74; lines 931-945), and nothing adds the two rails together. The only both-rails rule (_inspector_priority_width, lines 712-717) covers 100-149.

Two corrections to the finding. Route 2 measures 16 columns, not 14, which leaves about 10 characters of text. And resolve_console_rail_priority always favours Inspector, not the last-opened rail, so "keep the last-opened rail" would need new code.

On severity, the transcript is never hidden. Both rails keep their labelled collapse controls on screen ('Context ◂' and '▸ Inspect'), and Alt+I appears in the footer. Clicking '▸ Inspect' at 80x24 restored the full-width transcript in one step. The catch is that this close is saved to the global shared-layout-v1 scope, so it also closes Inspector at wide widths. A user who moves between a full-screen and a split terminal will hit the crushed layout again each time.
expected: Below 100 columns at most one rail renders beside the transcript, which keeps at least its 40-column usable floor (CONSOLE_RAIL_MAIN_USABLE_COLUMNS). Opening the second rail collapses the first, or opens Inspect as an overlay or sheet, with a brief note.
why: The transcript is where the user reads replies. Two stored preferences, or one keypress, can make it unreadable at the smallest supported size, and a restart doesn't fix it. Low-vision users with large fonts are effectively at 80x24.
repro: At 235x52 open Context (handle) and Inspector (Alt+I) → quit → REUSE=1 launch.sh j7 80 24. Or at 80x24 with Context open, press Alt+I.
recommendation: Add a combined budget: when left_min + right_min + main_usable exceeds the available columns, apply resolve_console_rail_priority (keep the last-opened rail) at every width below 150, not only from 100 up. Alternatively render Inspect as an overlay closed with Esc below the single-pane threshold. Pin the 40-column transcript floor in a geometry test at 80x24 and 90x30 with both explicit preferences stored.
fix_direction:
Extend the Inspector-priority conflict rule below 100 columns:
- Simplest change: drop the lower bound in _inspector_priority_width (columns < 150), or add a combined-budget check (left open, right open, and columns < 30 + 34 + 40). resolve_console_rail_priority, console_context_reveal_preferences and console_auto_open_would_evict_context all read that predicate, so Alt+I, Alt+C and the handles all switch rails consistently. The 74/70 per-rail budgets still apply to a single rail.
- Show the existing task-32327 collapse notice when this happens.
- If last-gesture-wins is preferred over Inspector-wins, that needs new state; the current resolver cannot express it.
- Stop a narrow-width close from rewriting the wide-width shared layout. Either keep narrow resolution render-only (it already is for the forced collapse), or make the switch a render override rather than a stored right_open=false.
- Add geometry pins with both explicit markers stored at 74x24, 80x24, 90x30 and 99x30, asserting the transcript is at least 40 columns and only one rail renders. Replace the width > 0 assertion in test_tools_chip_opens_inspector_at_80x24_single_pane.
- Amend ADR-043 to state the combined budget.
prior_art: NEW — backlog/decisions/043-console-rail-compact-collapse-yields-to-explicit-toggle.md:14-19; backlog/decisions/043-console-rail-compact-collapse-yields-to-explicit-toggle.md:64-86; TASK-18911; TASK-19639; TASK-23197; TASK-2154.2; TASK-32327
verdicts: live: PARTIAL · code: CONFIRMED · skeptic: PARTIAL

title: The Inspector appears at 118–128 columns, then disappears when the terminal is widened, with a false 'too narrow' warning
statement: With Context collapsed, growing the terminal live from 101 to 120 auto-opened the Inspector rail (the 118–128 'standard-width contract' band; console_rail_state.py:78-79; _should_open_standard_width_inspector at chat_screen.py:13648-13690). Growing on to 149 collapsed it again and raised the warning toast 'Inspector rail collapsed — the terminal is too narrow for it. Reopen it with Alt+I (or widen the terminal).', even though the user had just widened the terminal; the collapse notice fires on any open→closed transition (chat_screen.py:22566-22625). At 150 and above it stays closed because the default preference is closed. At 120 the Inspector shows or hides depending on whether Context is open.
expected: Rail visibility never decreases as width increases: either auto-open at every width of 118 and up, or never. 'Too narrow' copy fires only when the width actually shrank below the rail's budget.
why: Split-pane users drag widths constantly. A panel that appears in an 11-column band and then vanishes with a false explanation erodes trust in the layout.
repro: Context collapsed → tmux resize-window 101 → 120 (Inspector opens) → 149 (Inspector closes, warning toast).
recommendation: Replace the band with a monotonic rule, e.g. auto-reveal at 118 columns and above when readiness rows qualify, and only auto-hide on shrink. Pass the resize direction into _notify_console_responsive_rail_collapse and suppress 'too narrow' copy when the width grew.

title: Fixed chrome takes 12 of 24 rows at 80x24, and several of those rows repeat information shown elsewhere
statement: Transcript viewport as a share of height: 235x52 = 38 rows (73%); 211x44 = 30 (68%); 120x40 = 26 (65%); 100x30 = 18 (60%); 80x24 = 12 (50%). At 100x30 and 80x24 another row goes to the 'Each tab runs its own agent…' banner, truncated without an ellipsis. Fixed rows at every size: the nav's decorative ╭──╮ active-tab arc row, label row and rule; the header purpose line ('Console — Chat, source handoffs, live runs, and control actions.'); an action row (New tab / Settings / Context rail / Search Library / Help) duplicating the tab-strip New tab, the rail handle, Alt+C and the Inspector's Search Library; a rule; the 'Conversation | <title>' row, which duplicates the active tab label; then a rule, status strip, composer and footer. Two blank padding rows remain at 40 rows of height because compact mode starts only below 35 rows (CONSOLE_COMPACT_HEIGHT_ROWS = 35, chat_screen.py:758).
expected: Below about 30 rows: a one-row header (title plus readiness), the action row folded into the palette or tab-strip row, no nav arc row, no redundant title row, and one-time tips as toasts rather than transcript rows. Consider compact mode at 40 rows or fewer.
why: A tmux or split-pane user at 80x24 gets 11 lines of conversation. Reclaiming 4 redundant rows gives about 35% more reading area without losing any capability.
repro: Capture the same conversation at each size and count the rows between rule 6 and the bottom rule.
recommendation: Define a compact-height chrome contract for 30 rows or fewer: one header row, no nav arc, the title row merged into the tab strip, the action row collapsed to '⋯' or the palette, and tips as transient toasts. Measure transcript share in a geometry test, targeting at least 60% at 80x24. Related: G4-55 (duplicate title).

title: At 80x24 the setup wizard opens mid-sentence and truncates its recommendation and its small-terminal warning
statement: At the smallest supported size, the first visible body text is 'Next — Esc exits setup.', because the title and product explanation are scrolled off. The step labels (Welcome/Provider/…) are hidden, leaving bare numbers. The recommended option is cut to '(reco…'. The bottom banner reads 'Small terminal (80×24) — setup works best at 100×30 or larger. Everything still', cut mid-sentence.
expected: The step title and one-line purpose stay visible, the stepper shows the current step's name ('Step 1 of 6 · Welcome'), and the warning wraps or is shortened.
why: A newcomer on a small terminal first sees a sentence fragment.
repro: launch.sh j16 80 24 fresh; capture after load.
recommendation: Scroll the welcome step to the top on mount (focus the radio without scrolling past the intro). Show the current step name in the compact stepper. Shorten the banner to fit 80 columns.

title: Tabs that overflow the strip hide their run/approval markers; the overflow '▸' carries no state, and at 100 columns the only other cross-tab signal (the fleet line) is gone
statement: At 120x40 with four tabs, the fourth tab (✓ finished) was scrolled off behind a plain '▸' (fg #a7abaf) with no marker summary. At 100x30 the third tab was squeezed to '✓▸', and the Context rail, which holds the fleet line, was collapsed. A background tab's ◆ in that position would leave only the ambiguous nav '!'.
expected: The overflow affordance summarises hidden attention (for example '▸ 1◆ 1✓'), or attention-bearing tabs are kept in view.
why: The laptop widths the persona uses (e.g. 120 columns) are exactly where parallel runs lose their only signals.
repro: Open four tabs with a finished background run, resize to 120x40 and then 100x30, and inspect the tab strip row.
recommendation: Render the overflow chevron with the highest-precedence hidden marker and a count (◆ first). Alternatively, auto-scroll or pin tabs that turn NEEDS_APPROVAL into view, and add the fleet chip to the status strip (see GAP1-06).

title: Conversation settings: five entry points, two different surfaces titled 'Conversation settings', and drifting state names
statement: The header 'Settings', palette 'Console: Session settings…', '/settings — Open the full session settings modal' and left rail Model ▸ 'Configure' all open a modal titled 'Conversation settings'. The Provider and Model chips open a different quick popover that is also titled 'Conversation settings'. For the same state, the rail shows 'System: none' and the chip 'System Prompt: off'. The rail Model section never names the model. The header tooltip says 'Configure provider, model, tools, and generation'. This extends the 2026-09-26 report's '4 editors' finding with the entry-point naming.
expected: One name per surface ('Chat settings' for the full modal, 'Switch model' for the quick popover), used identically by the button, palette, slash command and modal title. The rail Model section leads with the model name.
why: Users can't predict which surface a control opens, or whether two labels describe the same state.
repro: Trigger each entry point and read the modal titles.
recommendation: Create a Console action registry with canonical label, verb, shortcut and slash alias, and render the header, palette, help and modal titles from it (the same registry as G3-18/G3-19).

title: Four ways to change the theme behave differently: one is a dead end and one silently doesn't persist
statement: Typing 'theme' in Ctrl+P lists two nearly identical commands first: 'Theme — Change the current theme' and 'Theme: Change Theme — Open theme selection menu'. (1) 'Theme: Change Theme' opens nothing. It closes the palette and shows a toast: "Type 'theme' in the command palette to see all available themes". (2) 'Theme' is Textual's built-in picker. It live-previews themes listed by raw id (textual-light, 80s_anime_ova_sunset, ansi-dark…), with no light/dark tag and no current-theme marker. It does not persist: after switching to nord this way, config.toml still said default_theme = "textual-dark", and a relaunch came back in textual-dark with no warning. It shows no toast either. (3) 'Theme: Switch to Paper Light' applies, persists, and toasts 'Paper Light is now your theme (was: Textual Light)'. (4) Settings > Theme has swatches, 'active · launch', light/dark tags, a preview, and separate Use and Try. The same theme is named 'textual-light', 'Textual Light' and 'Theme: Switch to Textual Light' depending on the route.
expected: One theme command, with one persistence contract (preview, then keep or revert), consistent names, and a visible light/dark tag. That is the Settings > Theme model.
why: A user who picks a theme through the first, most obvious palette entry loses it at the next launch without being told. A second user runs a command that only explains how to run a different command. Both teach users that palette results can't be trusted.
repro: Ctrl+P, type 'theme', Enter on 'Theme', type 'nord', Enter. grep default_theme in the profile's config.toml, then relaunch with REUSE=1. Separately: Ctrl+P, type 'change theme', Enter.
recommendation: Make 'Theme: Change Theme' open the Settings > Theme picker, or a palette sub-list with live preview whose Enter persists and Esc reverts. Replace or override Textual's built-in 'Theme' system command (App.get_system_commands) so it goes through use_theme and queue_launch_default. Everywhere, show display names with a '(light)' or '(dark)' tag and mark the current theme.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/app_command_providers.py:84-91 and :166-171 (show_theme_submenu only notifies); :173-196 (switch_theme persists); tldw_chatbook/app.py:953-966 (COMMANDS = App.COMMANDS | {...} keeps Textual's own Theme system command)

title: The ASCII glyphs setting applies live while Settings calls it an unsaved draft, and 'Discard changes' leaves the Console in ASCII mode
statement: Toggling Settings > Appearance > ASCII glyphs immediately switched the Console to ASCII markers ('[!]', '[approve]', 'v', '>'), while the State bar said 'Draft — save with s · 1 unsaved · revert with r'. Glyphs already painted stayed mixed until re-rendered: '[!] Reply with exactl ✕', 'Status ▾', '◂ Inspect'. I then reverted ('Revert Settings changes → Discard changes'). Settings showed 'ASCII glyphs Disabled' and 'No unsaved changes'-style state, but the Console kept rendering '[!]', '[approve]', 'v' and '>' for the rest of the session. set_ascii_glyph_mode is called only on toggle, never on revert or discard. The revert confirmation also appeared only after a noticeable delay: several r / click / Enter attempts showed nothing before the dialog appeared.
expected: Either the setting is a true draft (preview with t, apply on s), or it is labelled 'Applies immediately'. Revert restores the live mode, and all Console glyphs repaint at once.
why: The persistence badge exists to make save models legible (DESIGN.md, dense-form convention). Here it misstates what happened. Revert, the documented way back, leaves the UI in the mode the user just rejected, and only a restart fixes it.
repro: F4, '/' ascii, Enter, Enter (toggle). Go to Console and note the ASCII markers. F4, r, then 'Discard changes'. Go back to Console: markers are still ASCII.
recommendation: Mark ASCII glyphs as 'Applies immediately' and exclude it from the category draft, or apply it only on save. In either case, call set_ascii_glyph_mode from revert, discard and save-failure paths, and post an app-wide 'glyph mode changed' message so Console regions re-render their glyph-bearing labels immediately.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macbook-dev-Documents-GitHub-tldw-chatbook/c28a6a75-4221-4434-989d-fbf24a73c96b/scratchpad/uxrev/evidence/GAP3/52-settings-ascii-toggled.txt (Draft · 1 unsaved) and 53-console-ascii-live.txt (Console already ASCII, mixed glyphs)

tldw_chatbook/UI/Screens/settings_screen.py:25638-25652 (only call to set_ascii_glyph_mode); :33327-33332 (revert resets the label only); tldw_chatbook/Widgets/glyph_fallback.py:62-65 (documents that painted widgets keep old glyphs)

title: Run state is projected separately per region, so header, strip, Inspect, rail, handle and pill contradict each other ('Ready' while blocked; 'Blocked'/'Not ready' during a healthy run)
statement:
Confirmed live on origin/dev 64579cce2c. Run state is computed separately for each region, and the regions contradict each other at the same moment.

(1) Healthy run, at 235x52 and at 120x40:
- Header: 'Running'. Chip: 'Run: Agent running.'
- Inspect card: 'Run: Blocked'.
- Inspector Run group, in red: 'Provider: blocked - Provider setup needed: current run is active'.
- Model rail, in red: 'Not ready - current run is active'.
- Collapsed handle badge: 'setup'.

(2) 504 leading to the Trace capture blocked card ('Choose one action.'):
- The chat row shows the no-entry glyph plus 'Blocked', and the handle says 'blocked'.
- The header says 'Ready'. The authority card says 'Run: Ready', 'Live work: No active work' and 'Provider: ready'.
- The composer says 'Send disabled: type a message', and there is no run chip.

(3) After a 401:
- The header says 'Ready' and there is no chip.
- Only the transcript 'Failed' row, the handle 'failed' and a truncated 'Run: Failed - Agent run failed: provider ...' remain.
- When scrolled up, the jump pill reads 'stopped - jump to latest' next to the 'failed' handle badge.

(4) Pending approval:
- The header stays 'Running'.
- Each surface uses its own words and glyphs: nav '!', tab diamond, row hand plus 'Approval required', chip 'Run: Waiting for your approva...', Inspect 'Run: Waiting for approval', transcript 'Waiting for your approval' and 'Awaiting approval'.
- The red 'Provider: blocked - Provider setup needed' row persists.

Extra contradiction found: for 1-2 s after Enter, the chat row shows the running glyph while the header and authority say 'Ready' and the transcript says 'No messages yet.'.

Corrections to the finding:
- The 'setup' badge does not come from agent.py:515, which is the fleet line. It comes from build_console_inspector_rail_badge and _has_setup_blocker_row (console_rail_state.py:606-617, 675-676) matching the Inspector 'Provider: blocked' row.
- The main root cause is _build_console_inspector_state (chat_screen.py:14413-14431). It sets provider_ready from settings_readiness.operability == 'ready_to_send'. That is False during every active run, because the blocker is active_run (console_session_settings.py:1714-1715). The Provider row therefore becomes 'blocked'. The authority projection checks provider blocked before run_active (console_send_authority_summary.py:145-149), so it shows 'Run: Blocked'. TASK-32345 narrowed only _console_provider_blocker_copy, not this derivation.
- Not reproduced live in 3 attempts: 'Send blocked - finish provide...' during validating at 120 cols. The Preparing window never rendered. The code path is real: the queue tooltip rides setup_blocked_reason (chat_screen.py:22368-22376) and hits the fallback at console_display_state.py:302. The earlier evidence file L2/40 shows it.
- The missing check mark on the viewed tab after success matches the legend ('clears once you visit that tab'), so it is weak as a defect.
expected: One ConsoleRunPresentation (state, label, reason, next action), computed once per session and consumed by the header pill, run chip, tab marker, chat-list row, Inspect handle/edge, authority line, composer reason and jump pill. It uses one closed vocabulary: Ready · Preparing/Sending · Running · 7s · Waiting for you/approval · Paused (needs decision) · Failed · Stopped · Emergency-stopped. A healthy in-flight run is shown as busy ('Running — next send will queue'), never as 'blocked', 'Not ready', 'setup needed' or error colour. The header carries the viewed tab's terminal outcome ('Failed — see reply', 'Paused — decision needed') until the next send.
why: The most prominent status, the header, is the one most often wrong, because it cannot express failed, paused, approval or emergency-stop. Meanwhile a normal run reads as a configuration failure and may send users into Settings to 'fix' a working provider. When regions disagree, users stop trusting every status word, which breaks the 'status visible without reading logs' promise.
repro: (a) Reach the Trace capture card or the 401/429 path and compare header, chat list, Inspect handle and authority box. (b) At 235x52 open Inspect (Alt+I), send 'Reply with exactly three short bullet points about tea.', and in the first 8 s read the Inspect card, Run group, Conversation settings, Model rail and handle. At 120x40 read the composer reason during 'Run: Validating provider.' (c) After a failed run, scroll up and read the jump pill.
recommendation: Build a single ConsoleRunPresentation projection that includes a first-class 'busy' state and a 'decision required' state, and derive every region's label from it. Map recovery_action == 'wait_for_active_run' to one string ('Running — next send will queue') in build_console_readiness_presentation, the Inspector Provider row and the send-authority 'Run' fact. Give the composer reason its own 'Preparing…' branch for validating. Use a neutral 'Busy — run in progress' in the Model rail, not red. Drop the raw 'setup' handle badge unless a real setup blocker exists. Keep the run chip visible, with a dismiss, for terminal failed/paused states. title: The status strip overflows silently and by fixed order: values are cut mid-word, and Approvals, Context/cost and Sources disappear first
statement:
The Console status strip is a HorizontalScroll with a hidden scrollbar (console_status_chips.py:460) and a fixed chip order (462-528). It cuts off at the right edge with no cue, and the cut lands mid-token at every standard width. Live captures on origin/dev 64579cce2c:
- 235x52 after typing 'hi': ends 'On next send ~+$'.
- 235x52 during a run: ends 'Approvals: 0 pending     Co'.
- 235x52 with a pending approval: ends 'Approvals: 1 pen'.
- 211x44: ends 'Co'.
- 160x45: ends at 'Sources: 0'.
- 120x40: ends 'System Prompt: o'.
- 80x24: ends 'Provider: Anthropic     Mode'.

Because the order is fixed, the Approvals count, Context/cost and Sources chips drop off first. 'System Prompt: off' and 'Assistant: General' stay visible. Zero-state handling is inconsistent: Tools, Scope and Cost hide when empty, but 'Sources: 0' and 'Approvals: 0 pending' still render.

The finding misses something worse: a cut can leave a value that looks complete but is wrong. At 235x52 the strip read 'Current $0.01', but Shift+wheel showed the real value was '$0.0173 · On next send —'. Another run showed '$0.02' when the real value was '$0.0207'.

Three corrections to the finding:
1. compact_label is used below 120 columns (line 855). At 100x30 it renders 'Ctx 0% · Now $0.0207 · Next'. By then the cost chip has already scrolled out of view, so it never helps at rest.
2. A pending approval is not invisible at 160 or 80 columns; only the Approvals count chip is. The run chip leads the strip as 'Run: Waiting for your approva…', and that chip does use an ellipsis. The inline 'Approval required' card, the nav '^2 Console !' badge, the chat-list 'Approval required' row and 'Waiting for your approval' also all show.
3. Hidden chips can be reached. Tab moves focus through the chips and scrolls each one into view, Shift+wheel scrolls the strip, and the Inspector shows cost, context and model.
expected: Chips are ordered and dropped by importance. Run state, Approvals when non-zero, Context/cost and Model come first; library policy and static configuration drop first; zero-value chips hide consistently. Chips switch to compact forms before clipping ('Appr 2', 'Ctx 34%', '$0.12', 'Model: haiku-4-5', or one 'Anthropic · claude-haiku-4-5' chip). Whole chips truncate with an ellipsis, or a trailing focusable '+N ▸/▾' chip opens the full status. Nothing is cut mid-token. Context/cost and Sources stay visible at 120 columns.
why: Cost, approvals, grounding (Sources) and the active model are what an operator checks before sending, and they are the first things lost. From 160 columns down a pending approval or filling context is invisible, and its absence reads as 'nothing pending / fine'. Clipped fragments ('~+$', 'Mode', 'Co') are meaningless or misleading, which undermines PRODUCT's 'status visible without reading logs'.
repro: Launch ready mode and read the 'Status ▾ …' row at 235x52 (after typing 'hi' or attaching a file), 211x44, 160x45, 120x40 (row 36) and 80x24 (row 22/24). Start a run at 235x52 and read row 48.
recommendation: Give each chip a priority and a compact form, and fill the width by priority: temporary/run, approvals (only when > 0), Context/cost ('Ctx 0% · $0.00'), one merged model chip ('Anthropic · claude-haiku-4-5'; drop 'Provider:' when Model implies it), next send ('2 staged · auto-search off'), library policy/permissions, then Sources, Tools, System Prompt and Assistant. Apply one zero-state rule: hide 'nothing to report' chips. Use the existing compact_label below about 200 cols. When anything is dropped, render a trailing focusable '+N ▸' overflow chip that measures hidden children and opens a popover or the Status panel. Never clip mid-token. Keep the 'Status ▾' collapse. Add layout tests at 80, 120, 160 and 235 columns.
fix_direction:
Keep the Status ▾ collapse and the scroll-reachability contract, but stop cutting mid-token. At minimum:
(a) Add a trailing focusable overflow marker ('+N ▸') whenever the strip overflows. TASK-25828 already names the missing end-of-strip cue as the residual valid issue.
(b) Never cut inside a chip. Drop or ellipsize whole chips so a partial number like '$0.01' can never show.
(c) Choose the compact cost label by the strip's actual available width, not by screen width < 120.
(d) Apply one zero-state rule to Sources and Approvals: hide them at 0, like Tools, Scope and Cost.
(e) Optionally move cost/context and the approvals count ahead of provider and system-prompt metadata.
Point (e) reverses the Library-first ordering recorded in TASK-25828, so it needs an owner decision. Add layout tests at 80, 120, 160 and 235 columns asserting that no visible chip ends mid-token.

title: The status strip permanently says 'Agent blocked' on a ready profile, but it only means the Library tool is off
statement:
Reproduced live on a ready profile at 235x52 on origin/dev 64579cce2c. The first status chip always reads 'Library . Auto off . Agent blocked'. It shows at launch next to the header 'Ready' and the transcript line 'Ready - type a message to begin.'. During a run it sits right beside 'Run: Agent running.'. After a successful get_current_datetime tool call it sits beside 'Tools: 6 ready', while the left rail shows 'Agent: done' in green. Hovering shows a tooltip that only repeats the label. Clicking opens 'Library access'. Its status lines run straight into an unstyled 'Automatic retrieval' heading with no gap. It explains 'Agent Library access' as 'whether the assistant may use the built-in Library capability', while the same strip uses 'Assistant: General' for the persona. So 'Agent' names both the runtime and a Library permission, and only the 'Library .' prefix scopes 'blocked'.

Corrections to the finding:
(a) The chip is NOT styled as a fault. It uses the same neutral colours as the Provider and Model chips (fg #e1e1e1 on #1e1e1e), so 'looks like a fault' rests on wording alone.
(b) 'Blocked' is literally accurate: the Library permission defaults to Blocked.
(c) The G3-17 'setup' badge is real, but it is not a keyword heuristic misfiring on a healthy row. During every active run the Inspector readiness row itself says 'Provider: blocked - Provider setup needed: current run is active'. This is because the blocker code 'active_run' is fed through the 'Provider setup needed: {blocker}' template at console_settings_summary.py:167. The 'What happens if I send now?' card says 'Run: Blocked' mid-generation, and the rail badge correctly reads that wrong row and shows 'setup'. Everything clears to 'Run: Ready' / 'Provider: ready' when the run ends.

The wording is confusing and inconsistent (H2/H4), but it blocks no task: the agent works, and one click on the chip explains it. That makes it P2, not P1.
expected: The chip names the scope of the restriction, e.g. 'Library: auto off · agent search off' or 'Library tool: off'. The tooltip explains the consequence ('The agent cannot search your Library; click to change'). 'Blocked' is reserved for real run blockers.
why: It sits in the most-scanned strip, always on, and is misleading in the general sense. It contradicts the header and run chip, and the surrounding UI never explains it.
repro: Launch the ready profile. Read, hover and click the strip's first chip. Compare with the left-rail Agent section after a successful tool run.
recommendation: Rename the chip to name the capability, not the actor: 'Library · auto off · agent search off', using 'Off'/'On' instead of 'blocked'. Give it an explanatory tooltip. Pick one noun ('agent') in the modal copy, and keep 'Assistant:' for the persona only, or rename that chip 'Persona:'.
fix_direction: This needs an owner decision to reverse TASK-25834's kept chip wording and re-pin its five test files. (1) Name the capability, not the actor: 'Library: auto off . agent search off' or 'Library tool: off', using on/off rather than allowed/blocked. (2) Give the chip a real tooltip that states the consequence and the action, e.g. 'The agent cannot search your Library during a run. Click to change.'. (3) Use one noun in the modal body ('agent' to match its heading), and add spacing and heading styling between the status lines and the 'Automatic retrieval' axis. (4) Separately and independently, stop routing blocker 'active_run' through the 'Provider setup needed:' template. Give it its own 'Provider: in use - a run is active' wording, and make the 'What happens if I send now?' card say 'Run: queued after current run' instead of 'Blocked'. The 'setup' rail badge then disappears without touching the heuristic.

title: The Context/cost chip turns amber when the prompt cache goes cold with no text change (colour-only state; the ○/⚠/● glyph is stripped), and token usage is unexplained
statement: At boot the chip reads 'Context 0% · Current $0.00 · On next send —' in white (#e1e1e1 per J6; #a5a5a5 per J7). A few minutes after a reply it reads 'Context 0% · Current $0.00' (or '$0.002') in amber #fea62b, with no text change. The class .console-chip-cold applies color $ds-status-info (_console.tcss:281-283), which equals $accent (_variables.tcss:46); the class is toggled at console_status_chips.py:846-848. It recolours the context-fullness text too, although that is not what went cold. The cost tracker marks cold, alert and normal states with ○ / ⚠ / ● (console_cost_tracker.py:767-775), but build_console_context_cost_state strips those suffixes (console_context_controls.py:451-457). The only explanation, 'Cache: expired', is in a hover tooltip that keyboard users cannot reach. The same amber is used for info states elsewhere, so 'info' reads as 'warning', although the code comment calls cold 'not an alert'. J8 read the amber as a cache-break alert. J4 also found 'Context 0%' next to 'Tokens: 13.9k' after one short question: Conversation Inspector shows every assistant turn using about 14k input tokens (tool schemas) with no explanation. The hover-only 'Send | $' price is covered in G1-20.
expected: Any state shown by colour also changes the text ('○ cache cold' / 'cache expired'), with colour scoped to the cost segment. Cold maps to $text-muted plus the word, and accent/warning colours are reserved for alert (⚠). Info and warning use distinguishable tokens. The tooltip content is reachable on keyboard focus (e.g. a one-line expansion like the existing width-uncapping :focus rule). The Context breakdown explains where tokens go ('~14k tokens/turn are tool definitions (6 tools)').
why: Colour-blind and low-vision users can't tell anything changed. Sighted users read a routine cache expiry as a context or cost warning with nothing to act on, and cannot interpret spend or context use.
repro: 235x52: send one message, wait about 5 minutes for the cache TTL to lapse, and compare row 48 with the capture right after the reply. Hover the chip. Open Conversation Inspector.
recommendation: Keep the cold/alert glyph and a word in the merged label. Split it into 'Ctx 12%' and '$0.04 ○ cache cold', colouring only the cost part. Map cold to $text-muted and give info its own neutral token distinct from warning amber. Add a 'Tools ~14k' row to the Context breakdown. Make the tooltip's content available on keyboard focus.

title: Approvals count shows 1 for three pending calls, and the Approvals chip and Alt+A hint are truncated or hidden when an approval is pending
statement: With three todo_create calls awaiting decisions, the Inspect summary said 'Approvals: 1 pending · action required' and the strip 'Approvals: 1 pen…'. The count function returns 1 for any pending card (chat_screen.py:14331-14353), while the user guide says the chip 'counts tool calls waiting on you' (agent-runs-and-tools.md:164). During a run, a 'Run: Waiting for your approva…' chip is inserted at the front of the strip, and a 'Tools: 6 ready' chip appears after the first send. Together they push Approvals to a truncated 'Approvals: 1 pen' at 235 cols and remove Context entirely ('Co'). At 120x40 the Approvals chip is never visible, and the footer drops 'Alt+A approval' (it ends 'Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q').
expected: The count equals the number of calls needing a decision ('3 calls'). Approval state has a fixed, never-truncated leading slot. Alt+A survives footer truncation whenever something is pending. 'Tools: N ready' is counted at compose so the strip doesn't reflow on first use.
why: At the one moment approvals matter, the chip meant to announce them is cut off and under-counts, and on a ThinkPad or split-pane width it is gone.
repro: Ready 235x52: send a prompt producing three todo_create calls, then read the strip and Inspect summary. Repeat at 120x40.
recommendation: Count undecided calls. Give Run and Approvals fixed leading slots that never truncate, and let lower-priority chips (System Prompt, Assistant, Sources, Tools) collapse first (see G1-05). Make footer truncation keep Alt+A while an approval is pending (see G1-18). Show 'Tools: N ready' before the first send.

title: The status strip stays horizontally scrolled after keyboard focus leaves it, garbling the first chip for the rest of the session
statement: Tabbing through the status chips to the last (cost/context) chip scrolls the strip left, and it never scrolls back after focus leaves. The strip keeps reading 'Status ▾  · Agent blocked …' at 235, 120, 160 and 80 cols. While an approval was pending, the first chip read 'Status ▾ our approva…' (the start of 'Waiting for your approval' cut off). J8 saw the same after horizontal scrolling ('Status ▾ ry · Auto off' until reload). Trailing chips are clipped at the right edge ('Assistant: Ge') with no overflow marker (see G1-05).

title: The Context chip never warns: it stays the same dim grey at 0%, 45%, 80% and 100%+, and it measures against the model window rather than the budget that triggers compaction
statement:
The Console 'Context N%' status chip never escalates. In live captures it was the same dim #a5a5a5 on #1e1e1e (6.77:1) at 0%, 30%, 57%, 82% and 100%+, and also while sends were blocked at the compaction threshold. The neutral chips beside it are brighter (#e1e1e1, 12.75:1). Its classes come only from the prompt-cache alert/cold state (console_status_chips.py:846-848). Its percentage is request_tokens / safe_input_ceiling (191,904 for claude-haiku-4-5), and it ignores both the compaction trigger and any custom conversation budget (console_context_controls.py:420-431).

With the default automatic budget, the budget is derived from that same ceiling (effective budget = safe ceiling minus mandatory input). So the chip roughly tracks the trigger basis: it shows about 80% when the 80% trigger is reached, but gives no emphasis or wording at that point.

With a custom budget the chip is badly misleading. With a 6,000-token budget it read 'Context 2%' while Settings > Context and memory showed 'Effective 6,000 / Next request 3,899'. It read 'Context 3%' when the next send was blocked by the Ask compaction gate.

Nothing warns before the send. Send stays primary-enabled at 100%+ and at the threshold, and the Inspect card 'What happens if I send now?' says 'Run: Ready' in both states. The trigger in tokens appears only in the chip tooltip; Settings shows 'Compact at (%) 80'.

Visibility is worse than stated. The chip is off-screen not only at 80x24 but already at 160x45. It is visible only at about 211 columns or wider, and truncated even there. This comes from the horizontal-scroll strip design (TASK-2154.5 / G1-05).
expected: Fullness should escalate in words and colour as the chat nears the point where something happens (the compaction trigger or the overflow). It should be measured against the limit that actually governs behaviour, stay visible at 80 columns, and warn before the send rather than after.
why: The chip is the one always-visible context signal, and it stayed calm right up to the chat being blocked. Users cannot anticipate compaction or overflow.
repro: Compare chip at Context 45% (long chat), 100%+ (1.2 MB paste draft), 80% (blocked near-full chat); in a custom-budget profile compare chip % with Settings ▸ Context and memory 'Next request / Effective'.
recommendation: Derive a fullness state from the effective trigger/budget: normal <70% of trigger, 'near limit' (amber + word) ≥70%, 'compacts next send' / 'over limit' (red + word) at the trigger or ≥100%. Label the denominator when a custom budget applies ('Ctx 85% of 6k budget'). Keep a minimum 'Ctx 80%!' form that survives strip overflow at 80 columns. Show a composer-level warning before Send when the draft pushes past the trigger or the window.
fix_direction: Derive a fullness state from the governing limit: conversation_tokens against compaction_trigger_tokens, with the safe ceiling as the hard stop. Map it to classes and words: normal; 'near limit' (warning colour) at 70% or more of the trigger; 'compacts next send' or 'over limit' (error colour) at or past the trigger or the ceiling. Apply it to the chip independently of the cache alert/cold classes. When a custom budget is active, label the denominator (e.g. 'Ctx 85% of 6k'). Feed the same preflight decision into the composer's Send hint and the Inspect 'What happens if I send now?' card ('Next send will ask to compact'). Give the context segment its own short chip or a priority slot so a compact 'Ctx 80%!' survives strip overflow at 80 to 160 columns (coordinate with G1-05).

title: Creating a chat has three visible buttons and four names; the tab-strip 'New tab' / 'Temporary' buttons scroll with the tabs, get clipped mid-word, look like tabs, and 'Temporary' reads as a status
statement:
Three visible creation buttons, one function:
- At rest the 235x52 screen shows 'New tab' in the header action row (row 5), 'New tab' in the tab strip (row 8) and 'New conversation' in the rail (row 22).
- The header new-tab action and the rail button both call _create_native_console_session_from_active_context() (chat_screen.py:4816-4817 and :24766-4768).
- Ctrl+T, /new ('Open a new Console chat tab') and the palette do the same.

Four names for one action:
- 'New tab' (header and strip, both visible at once), 'New conversation' (rail), 'New chat' (workspace row menu) and '/new'.
- F1 adds 'new tab (new agent)'.
- Workspaces 'New' creates a workspace, not a chat.

The 'Temporary' button:
- The strip reads 'Chat 1 ✕  New tab  Temporary'. 'Temporary' is a button that creates a temporary tab (tooltip 'New temporary Console tab — not saved locally').
- It is an adjective sitting beside a saved chat, and the same word is the temporary-state label ('Temporary — not saved', decoded from ◌).

The strip's create buttons scroll with the tabs:
- Both sit inside the scrolling tab HorizontalScroll.
- Clipped forms: 'New ▸' at 100 and 84 columns, 'Temporar▸' at 99, 'Tempor▸' at 120 with the Inspector open. At 80 columns with rails open they are gone.
- They share the inactive tab's styling (fg #e1e1e1 bold on #1e1e1e, the same as 'Chat 2').
- The '▸' overflow hint is the same glyph used for collapsed sections and 'Context ▸'.
expected: One visible creation control, in the place users look for it: the tab-strip end, with Ctrl+T. It uses one verb and noun across header, strip, rail, menus, commands and F1. The create actions sit in a fixed cluster outside the tab scroll viewport, styled as actions rather than tabs ('+ New chat', '+ Temporary chat', or a split 'New ▾' offering regular or temporary). Overflow has its own counted affordance ('‹ 2 more ›').
why: Three buttons with two names suggest different behaviours, and users hesitate over which one keeps workspace context. 'Temporary' can be read as saying the current chat is unsaved, or the option can be missed entirely. On narrow panes the primary create action scrolls out of reach or reads as a truncated tab name.
repro: Look at the default 235x52 screen (rows 5, 8 and 22). With two tabs, resize 120 → 100 → 84 columns and read the tab-strip row.
recommendation:
1. Keep one creation control, New / Ctrl+T, at the tab-strip end, and remove it from the header. Replace the rail's 'New conversation' with a '+' on the active workspace row ('New chat in <Workspace>') only if its behaviour differs; otherwise remove it (see G2-13).
2. Pick one creation noun and verb ('New chat', or 'New tab' if tab becomes the canonical noun) and use it in the header, strip, rail, menus, /new and F1.
3. Move New and Temporary to a fixed right-hand cluster outside the tab HorizontalScroll, with a distinct flat-action style and a leading '+'.
4. Relabel Temporary with a verb ('New temp', which fits the 13-cell slot, or '+ Temporary chat'), or fold both into a split 'New ▾'.
5. Use a counted overflow hint instead of a bare ▸.
6. Rename Workspaces 'New' to 'New workspace…'.

title: Open tabs and the active chat are not restored on relaunch; the user lands on a new blank 'Chat 1'
statement:
Five tabs were open at quit, with 'Say OK 1' active and 'Alpha' scrolled to the middle. After relaunching with REUSE=1, the only tab was a new 'Chat 1' with 'No messages yet.'

Each saved chat opened from the rail becomes a new tab, and the blank Chat 1 stays open beside the reopened chats. The User Guide says nothing about what reopens.
expected: The saved tabs from the last session reopen in order, with the active tab and drafts. Alternatively, the empty state offers 'Reopen last session (4 chats)'. The behaviour is documented, and the blank default tab is replaced when the first action is opening a saved chat.
why: Resuming yesterday's work is the researcher persona's core loop. Rebuilding context by hand from the rail or Ctrl+K costs a click per chat and leaves a stray blank tab.
repro: Open several saved chats in tabs, press Ctrl+Q, and relaunch with REUSE=1.
recommendation: Persist the ordered list of saved conversation ids for open tabs, the active id and the drafts. Restore them on launch, or show a one-click 'Reopen last session' in the empty-state line. Replace the blank default tab when the user opens a saved chat as the first action. Document the behaviour in the User Guide.

title: Ctrl+K History sorts each day alphabetically instead of most-recent first
statement: History → TODAY listed Say OK 1 (9m), Say OK 2 (7m), Say OK 3 (6m), Say OK 5 (2m). Within each calendar bucket the sort key is the lower-cased title (sorted by (section order, title.casefold(), row_key); console_switcher_state.py:1261-1290). The Active tab and the rail sort by recency.

title: Temporary chats look like saved chats everywhere except the tab glyph and one status chip
statement:
Before the first send, a Temporary tab shows '◌ Chat 4'. The ◌ is explained only in the tooltip, which can't be read without hovering (console_session_surface.py:118-126). The status strip shows an orange italic 'Temporary — not saved' at the far bottom-left.

Everywhere else the chat looks saved:
- The rail Chats list shows it with the same 💬 icon as saved chats.
- Ctrl+K lists it as 'OPEN AGENT … Chats · Console tab'.
- The transcript header ('Conversation | Chat 4'), the empty state ('No messages yet.') and the composer give no hint.
- Temporary chats share the saved chats' 'Chat N' numbering.

The list and switcher code have no ephemeral handling (grep of console_workspace_context.py and console_session_switcher_modal.py).
expected: 'Temporary' appears in words everywhere the chat does: tab, rail row, Ctrl+K row, transcript header, and the empty state ('Temporary chat — not saved; closes with the tab'). ◌ remains as a secondary cue only.
why: The ephemerality is only obvious to someone who already knows the glyph. After switching away and back through the rail or Ctrl+K, users can't tell that the content will vanish.
repro: Click 'Temporary' in the strip, then compare the tab, rail row, Ctrl+K row and header.
recommendation: Add a text 'Temp' badge on the tab and in rail and Ctrl+K rows, 'Temporary' in the transcript header, and a one-line explanation in the empty state. Keep ◌ as a secondary cue, and source the marker from the unified glyph table (G2-24).

title: For 1.5–3 s after a tab switch during live runs, the screen shows two different chats at once
statement:
When a run is live in either tab, a session-tab switch is not atomic. For roughly 0.5 s to 2 s, the screen shows two chats at once. The regions always split into the same two groups:
- Group 1 moves to the target chat first: Inspect's "What happens if I send now?" block (Where / Run / Live work / Provider), the Conversations "current" row, the Chats-list highlight, the pinned Tasks panel, the composer's Send/Queue label, the top-right Running/Ready chip and the left-rail Agent line.
- Group 2 still shows the source chat: the tab-strip active highlight, the "Conversation |" header, the transcript and the status-strip "Run:".

Timings: in 9 live switches, the whole switch took 1.6 to about 4.5 s after the click. For the first 0.5–2.3 s nothing changed except a mouse-hover tint on the clicked tab. The mixed state then lasted 0.25 s to more than 1.2 s. In one case it was still mixed at 3.0 s.

The Tasks-panel leak is real. The target chat's plan ("Tasks · 0 of 2 done / alpha task / beta task") appears above the source chat's transcript, and in the other direction it vanishes from above its own transcript.

The mix has a concrete effect on sending. The composer sends to the session its mounted draft belongs to (chat_screen.py:19096 `_console_visible_send_session_id`), not the store's active session, so in the mixed window the "What happens if I send now? Where:" preview and the composer's Send label describe the target chat while Enter acts on the source chat. I reproduced this: text entered while Inspect said "Where: Default › Call the todo_create too…" (chat A) and the button read "Send" was queued on chat B and ran there.

Idle switches (no live run) are atomic at 100 ms resolution, though they take 1.5–2.4 s with no feedback.

Corrections to the finding:
- "1.5–3 s" is the length of the whole switch, not of the mixed window.
- The tab highlight does not lead. It flips in the same 100 ms frame as the header and transcript, so the fix needs immediate feedback on the tab itself.
- The GAP1 54/55 captures come from rapid alternating clicks about every 2.5 s, which inflates the timing.
- I could not reproduce the variant where tab B is highlighted while the header still shows A over a blank transcript.
expected: A switch is atomic from the user's point of view: every region names the same chat, or a single 'Opening <title>…' placeholder is shown until it does.
why: Users act on what they see. Combined with GAP1-01, a half-switched screen invites typing, approving or reading into the wrong chat. The Tasks panel leak shows one agent's plan under another chat's transcript.
repro: Start slow runs in two tabs, open Inspect (Alt+I), click the other tab and capture at 1–2 s. Compare the tab highlight, the 'Conversation |' header, the transcript, Inspect 'Where:', the rail current row and the Tasks panel.
recommendation: Derive all region projections from one session snapshot and apply them in one batch update. Until the new session's projection is ready, dim the work area and show a single 'Opening <title>…' line. Give the tab highlight immediate (<0.1 s) feedback, and make every region header carry the same session identity, so a mismatch can be caught by a test that asserts all regions name one session.
fix_direction:
Treat the switch as one transaction from the user's point of view:
1. On click, apply the tab-strip active state right away (under 100 ms), then dim or cover the work area with a single 'Opening <title>…' placeholder until the new session's projection is ready.
2. Defer the store-bound projections (Inspect send-authority block, rail current row, Chats highlight, Tasks panel, composer Send/Queue label, top-right chip, left-rail Agent line) until the transcript and draft remount commits. They should read one session snapshot and repaint in one batch; in `switch_session`, the synchronous `_remount_task_panel` should be deferred to that commit point too.
3. Make the "What happens if I send now?" preview and the composer label derive from `_console_visible_send_session_id`, not the store's active id, so preview and action cannot disagree. Alternatively, block send while the painted session and the active session differ; that overlaps GAP1-01.
4. Add a regression test with a live background run that samples every region's session identity after the switch and asserts they are always equal, the Tasks panel included.

TASK-26834's latency work shortens the window but does not close it.

title: Extends G2-03: cross-tab attention toasts fire while the user is on Console, say 'Return to Console', and use five templates for two events
statement: While viewing tab B in Console, a background approval raised 'A Console session needs approval to use a tool. Return to Console to respond.', naming neither the tab nor the fact that the user is already in Console. Background completions raised 'Agent in Call the todo_create tool o... (Default) finished.' For the D4 completion, that named toast was followed by the generic 'A Console turn completed while hidden. Return to Console to review.', so one event produced two toasts. The nav badge '⌃2 Console !' lights and stays lit on the destination the user is currently viewing whenever any background tab has an unseen outcome or a parked decision; it also lit when a modal covered Console.
expected: One notification per event that names the chat and the action, for example '<title> needs approval — Alt+A' or '<title> finished — Ctrl+K', with no 'Return to Console' when Console is displayed, and a nav badge that doesn't point at the current destination.
why: The notices are unhelpful: they don't say which tab, and 'Return to Console' contradicts where the user is. The duplicates add noise, and a permanently lit '!' on the current destination trains users to ignore it.
repro: Two tabs, slow proxy. Start a todo_create run in A, switch to B, and capture every 1.3 s until A parks. Repeat with a plain run in A and let it finish while B is viewed.
recommendation: Route all five through one notifier with one template per event type, deduplicated per receipt id across the runtime and screen channels. Name the chat, offer the key (Alt+A / Ctrl+K), use severity=error for failures, and branch the copy on whether Console is displayed. Keep the nav badge off the current destination, or turn it into a per-tab count shown in the tab strip.

title: Extends G2-22: Ctrl+K History over 300 chats pages by recency but sorts each bucket alphabetically, and page 2 opens with the selection off-screen
statement: History shows '1–50 of 303'. The TODAY, PREVIOUS 7 DAYS and OLDER buckets are each sorted A→Z, so page 1's OLDER rows read 3w, 1w, 3w, 2w, 1w… and page 2 (51–100, all OLDER) reads 12w, 11w, 13w, 6w, 10w…. That is neither recency nor a usable alphabetical index, because each page restarts at A. After clicking Next, the list stayed scrolled to the bottom and focus stayed on Next, while the header said 'Enter opens: Clean up grant proposal #084 · 1 of 50' and that row was off-screen. PageDown and End stop at row 50 and never advance a page. The hints ('Enter:open · ↑↓:move · Shift+F3:mode · Esc:close') don't mention paging, and the 'Previous' button is clipped to 'Previo'.
expected: Rows should be sorted by recency within buckets. PageDown past the last row should load the next page. A page change should reset scroll and selection to the top, and paging keys should appear in the hints.
why: At realistic volume, History is the main way back to older work, and its order and paging defeat both scanning and keyboard use.
repro: Seed 300 chats with varied dates; Ctrl+K ▸ History; PageDown ×6; click Next.
recommendation: Sort by last_modified desc inside each bucket. Make PageDown on the last row (or Ctrl+→) load the next page and select its first row. Reset scroll_y and the highlight on page change and move focus back to the list. Add 'PgDn:more' to the hints. Use ‹ › or 'Prev'/'Next' so labels fit.

title: Ctrl+K spends two lines per row on repeated 'SAVED CHAT · Chats · Saved chat' and hard-clips long titles in a fixed 76-column modal
statement: Every History row is 'SAVED CHAT   <title>' plus a second line 'Chats · Saved chat · 5h', so only 10 of 303 chats are visible at once. The modal is fixed at 76 columns even on a 235-column terminal. 80-character titles are cut with no ellipsis ('Explain the difference between prompt caching an', 'Plan migration of the notes vault from Obsidian'), and the 'Enter opens: Explain the difference' line is clipped as well. The truncation budget is min(70, width−4), wider than the visible title column, so the ellipsis falls off-screen. In Active mode all 21 open tabs, including blank ones, are labelled 'OPEN AGENT'.
expected: Rows should be one line each, showing the title, age and a badge only where it differs from the default. The modal should use more of a wide terminal, and truncation should end with an ellipsis at the visible edge, with the full title shown in the selection line.
why: At 300 chats the switcher shows few rows, and similar long titles become indistinguishable, so users open the wrong chat.
repro: Ctrl+K ▸ History at 235x52; type 'compaction' to find an 80-char title.
recommendation: Collapse each row to one line ('Title…   5h') with the kind badge only for non-default kinds (Character, Temporary, Workspace). Let the modal grow to ~min(120, 60% of width). Truncate at the measured title-column width with '…', and wrap the full title in the 'Enter opens:' line. Replace 'OPEN AGENT' with 'Open tab' and mark blank tabs 'empty'.

title: At 25 tabs the strip hides the active tab, its overflow arrows do nothing when clicked, and tabs 10–25 have no keyboard route
statement:
With many open tabs, switching to a tab that is already open does not scroll the strip. This happens after a Ctrl+K switch and after a terminal resize, and the strip then shows no highlighted tab. Reproduced twice with 25 tabs at 235x52: after Ctrl+K to Chat 3, and later to Chat 1, the header read 'Conversation | Chat 3' / 'Conversation | Chat 1'. The strip still showed Chat 18-25, or Chat 20 through Temporary, and no visible tab had the active style, even 8 s later. At 80x24 after a resize, the active Chat 24 was also off-strip; only Chat 20-22 were visible (about 3 tabs). Ctrl+T does scroll the new tab into view, but its close button stays hidden behind the right overflow glyph.

The overflow glyphs are inert Statics. Three clicks on the left glyph changed nothing. Their tooltip says to use the mouse wheel, and neither glyph shows how many tabs are hidden; the only count is 'Active (25)' in Ctrl+K. Wheeling from the far-right end back to Chat 1 took 112 notches, not ~140. Tabs use a fixed 24-cell pitch, so 7-8 fit at 235 columns. New tab and Temporary scroll off with the strip, but New tab is still reachable from the header toolbar and Ctrl+T.

Keyboard: there is no next/previous-tab key. Alt+1..9 are dead in a real terminal as well: ESC+1 and ESC+9 typed composed characters into the composer (TASK-1802). So the finding is wrong that tabs 1-9 have a key route. It is also wrong that tabs 10-25 can only be reached through Ctrl+K. Tab/Shift+Tab visits every tab button and close button, scrolls the focused one into view, and Enter activates it. Eight Shift+Tabs from the transcript plus Enter switched to Chat 24, so this route costs about 2 presses per tab.

The claim that the strip 'stops telling users which chat they are in' is overstated. The title row directly above the strip and the rail's current row both still name the active chat.
expected: The active tab should always be scrolled into view. Overflow controls should be clickable, with a hidden count. Next/previous-tab keys should exist, and tab width should adapt to the title.
why: With many parallel chats, the strip stops telling users which chat they are in, which is the one job of a tab strip, and keyboard users lose tab navigation.
repro: Open 25 tabs (Ctrl+T plus Ctrl+K opens); Ctrl+K to an early tab; click '◂'; count wheel notches to reach the first tab.
recommendation: Call scroll_to_widget on the active tab after every activation, whatever the route. Make ‹ › buttons that page the strip and read '‹ 17' / '4 ›'. Add Ctrl+PgUp/PgDn (or Alt+←/→) for previous/next tab, and list them in F1 and the footer. Size tabs to content (min ~12 columns, max ~24) with a left-aligned title. Pin New tab/Temporary and the active tab's ✕ outside the scrolling region.
fix_direction: Make the active tab visible whenever it changes, not only when the strip is rebuilt. Schedule _scroll_active_tab_into_view from the in-place update path whenever active_session_id differs from the last scrolled id, and again from the strip's _on_resize. Scroll to include the tab's ✕, for example by scrolling to the close button or to a region spanning both. Make the overflow glyphs clickable page-left/page-right controls that show the hidden count (e.g. '‹ 17' / '4 ›'). Add previous/next-tab bindings that actually arrive in a terminal, such as ctrl+pageup/ctrl+pagedown, and list them in F1 and the footer. Also resolve TASK-1802, because Alt+1..9 are dead. Content-sized tabs and pinning New tab/Temporary outside the scrolling region are design changes: TASK-2154.4 and TASK-375 chose fixed widths on purpose, so they belong in a separate task.

title: Mid-switch, Inspect says W2 while the tab, header and transcript still show W1; tabs from every workspace share one strip, and clicking one silently switches workspace
statement: 1 s after picking W2 in 'Change Workspace', the pin read 'Where: W2 Beta › W2 Beta Chat' and the rail read 'Workspace W2 Beta', while the header, tab and transcript still showed W1 Alpha Chat and its messages. The composer draft 'draft typed in W1' had already vanished. It settled by about 5 s. Afterwards the tab strip holds 'W1 Alpha Chat ✕ W2 Beta Chat ✕' with no workspace marker, and clicking the W1 tab silently switched the active workspace back to W1 (the draft was preserved there). A workspace can therefore be switched in three ways: Alt+W, the tree, or a tab click.
expected: The switch is atomic, with every region updated together or a brief 'Switching to W2…' overlay. Tabs show their workspace (prefix or grouping), and switching via a tab is announced.
why: The user can't tell which workspace, and therefore which folder authority, the next send will use, and a routine tab click changes global context.
repro: Type a draft in W1, press Alt+W, choose W2 and capture at 1 s. Then click the W1 tab.
recommendation: Gate every region's projection on one switch generation. Label or group tabs by workspace, and toast 'Switched to W1 Alpha' when a tab click changes workspace.

title: The Ctrl+K switcher labels chats with internal workspace ids ('workspace-local-1 · Console tab'), and the workspace switcher shows no folder or repo
statement: In Ctrl+K's Active list, rows read 'Write a new file notes.txt... / workspace-local-1 · Console tab · 5m', 'W1 Alpha Chat / workspace-local-1…' and 'W2 Beta Chat / workspace-local-2…', where the display names are 'W1 Alpha' and 'W2 Beta'. Rows are also labelled 'OPEN AGENT'. The Alt+W 'Change Workspace' list shows only names, with no bound folder, repo or chat count.
expected: Workspace display names in every switcher, plus a short scent line such as 'proj-alpha · 2 chats'.
why: Users can't map an id to a workspace, which undermines the multi-workspace workflow this feature exists for.
repro: Create two named workspaces with chats and press Ctrl+K.
recommendation: Resolve workspace_label to the registry display name, falling back to 'Default'. Add the bound-folder basename to the Alt+W rows.

title: Ctrl+K 'Character chats' mode cannot browse characters or start a chat, and it drops the footer hints the other modes show
statement: The mode shows only 'Search local Character chats by Keyword…' and 'Type a Keyword to search local Character chats'. It lists nothing until a keyword is typed, even with 4 characters available, and it cannot start a chat with a character. Text typed after selecting the mode did not reach the field (focus stayed on the mode control), and Shift+F3 (the footer's 'Shift+F3:mode') did not change mode. The 'Enter:… · ↑↓:move · Shift+F3:mode · Esc:close  Cancel' footer shown in Active and History disappears in this mode. The only in-Console way to start a character chat is the status-strip chip 'Assistant: General' → 'Choose character' → 'Swap in this chat / Start new chat', which is a different surface with different grammar.
expected: 'Character chats' lists characters with their recent chats (most-recent first), offers 'New chat with <character>', and keeps the same footer, Cancel and focus behaviour as the other modes.
why: The mode's name promises character navigation, but it requires recalling a keyword, and it duplicates, without replacing, the character picker.
repro: Ctrl+K → click 'Character chats' → type a name.
recommendation: Merge the character picker into this mode: an empty query lists characters, and Enter offers Resume latest, New chat or Swap into this chat. Reuse the switcher footer, and focus the query field on mode change.

title: 'Discard' leaves the discarded prompt in the model context, so the next reply answers it too
statement:
Confirmed three times in the live app, including after a relaunch. Choosing Discard on the "Response delivery status is unknown" panel settles only the assistant row, which becomes "Response discarded." with generation state `discarded`. The user prompt stays in the saved history as an ordinary row with no marker. Every later provider request resends that prompt, not just the next one, and the model answers it along with the new prompt.

The prompt may never have reached the provider before the Discard:
- In J2's case, the proxy log has no j2 POST between 12:58:53 and 13:04:04, and the app log shows the trace reservation failing (`unsupported_surface_change`) before the request was entered.
- In my run, the codeword request got an injected 500 from the review proxy without being forwarded to Anthropic.

So in both cases Discard leads the app to send, for the first time, a prompt the user chose not to have answered.

The user guide also misleads. `Docs/User_Guide/console/chat-basics.md:78-80` says Discard "settles the interrupted response without replaying the request", but the request text is replayed as history in every later send.

Reviewer confidence can go from medium to high.
expected: Discard removes the prompt from the next request's context, or offers 'discard reply and prompt'. If the prompt stays visible, the transcript marks it as excluded.
why: Users believe they cancelled a request. It silently skews the next answer and costs tokens, and the merged answer is hard to diagnose.
repro: Trigger the unknown-delivery panel, choose Discard, send a different prompt, and inspect the reply.
recommendation: When a turn is discarded, exclude its user row from the provider history projection, or ask 'Also remove your prompt from context?'. Render excluded rows with a visible 'not sent to model' tag. Apply the same rule to failed turns the user abandons.
fix_direction:
This needs an owner decision recorded as an ADR-079 amendment, plus a matching update to the ADR-097 discard-chain witness. Options:

(a) Make Discard remove the turn's user prompt from the provider-history projection. Persist an explicit per-message exclusion flag rather than relying on status='failed', so it survives a reload. Show a visible "Not sent to model" tag on the user row, and offer a way to "Include in context again".

(b) Split the action in two: "Discard reply (keep prompt in context)" and "Discard reply and prompt". Default to removing both when the provider was never contacted or delivery is unknown.

(c) At minimum, change the post-discard copy to say "Response discarded — your message stays in the conversation and will be sent with your next message", and fix `chat-basics.md:78-80`, which currently says "without replaying the request".

Whichever option is chosen should also apply to the trace-recovery "Cancel send" discard path (`console_chat_controller.py:8786`) and to other failed turns the user abandons.

Add a regression test on `provider_messages_for_next_send_estimate` and `_provider_messages_for_session`: after Discard, the discarded user row is absent, or explicitly tagged, both before and after reload.

title: Answers show no source authority; 'Citation repair unavailable' is jargon, and the only Library hit was the current chat citing itself
statement: Grounded Console answers show no per-answer source control on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c. This happens even when the model cites correctly, so the problem is wider than the finding says, but its cause is different. Live repro: the current chat was staged through Inspect ▸ Search Library "RuBisCO enzyme" with the default Sources. The prompt "Which enzyme fixes CO2? Cite your source." then got the answer "RuBisCO fixes CO2. Source: [S1] Study note from chat history." That is a valid [S1] marker. No "Cited sources (1)" button appeared and no notice appeared. The bare "[S1]" points at nothing the user can open. After the send, all six citation-provenance tables in the profile's ChaChaNotes DB held 0 rows (rag_citation_traces, rag_message_trace_owners, rag_evidence_runs, rag_evidence_snapshots, rag_trace_evidence_refs, rag_answer_attempt_payloads). The log shows the turn took the durable_commit path. That matches the open regression TASK-22302: durable turns drop the citation finalizer. The footer is gated on those persisted counts (console_transcript.py:6749-6758 "Cited sources (n)"; chat_screen.py:18361-18367), so it cannot appear for any turn right now. The finding reads the absence as the uncited/"repair unavailable" design choice (TASK-553.16 AC#2); that choice only covers answers without markers. The copy "Citation repair unavailable · Original response kept" is real (console_transcript.py:613-614). It shows only when the model omits or garbles markers and the repair request fails. The lead's J4 capture shows it. I did not reproduce it: my model cited correctly, and my second send reported "capture_provider_failure", so no evidence was sent. The self-match is real. The only Library hit was the active conversation, shown only as "Remember this study note: i... — conversation", with no "this chat" label. retrieval.py:646-721 has no exclusion for the active conversation. But in both runs it was the only hit because the Library was empty, so the severity of that sub-point is lower than the finding implies. The underline sub-point is also misread. "photosynthesis.md" is not a fake link: Textual 8.2.8's MarkdownIt("gfm-like") linkify turns it into a real link to http://photosynthesis.md (the .md suffix is Moldova's ccTLD). The same happens to other names that end in a country-code extension, such as readme.py. Clicking one calls webbrowser.open on an unrelated external domain (console_transcript.py:1954-1963).
expected: Every grounded answer shows a 'Sources (n)' affordance listing each source with its type and authority (local file, note, media, this conversation). Self-matches of the active conversation are excluded or labelled. Notices use plain language ('No inline citations — see Sources'). Underline is used only for real links.
why: Source authority is a stated product principle and the core need of the researcher persona. Users cannot verify grounding, and retrieval quietly feeds the chat back into itself.
repro: Search Library for 'RuBisCO enzyme' with the default Sources; the staged hit is the current chat. Send 'Cite your source'.
recommendation: Render a per-turn Sources row whenever any evidence (staged, auto-retrieved or inline file) went with the request, whether or not the model emitted citation markers. Exclude the active conversation from Conversations retrieval by default. Rewrite the notice as 'No inline citations — see Sources'.
fix_direction: 1) Fix TASK-22302 first, so durable turns write citation provenance; that alone brings back 'Cited sources (n)' for correctly cited answers. Add a live-app or integration assertion that a send with staged evidence and an [S1] reply produces a footer. 2) Then revisit the TASK-553.16 AC#2 decision: show a per-turn 'Sources sent (n)' row whenever evidence accompanied the request, cited or not, and make [S#] tokens in the body resolve to it. 3) Replace 'Citation repair unavailable · Original response kept' with plain language, e.g. 'No inline citations — see Sources'. 4) Exclude the active conversation from Conversations retrieval by default, or label it 'This chat'. 5) Disable fuzzy linkify in Console Markdown (use a parser_factory with linkify off, or schema-only linkify) so bare filenames are not turned into http:// links.

title: Swapping in a character relabels all earlier assistant replies with the character's name
statement:
The visible symptom is real and reproduces. After "Swap in this chat", every earlier assistant turn in the session takes the new identity's name. Nothing in the transcript marks where the identity changed. The confirmation copy only asks "swap into this chat, or start a new one?" and does not warn that earlier replies will be relabeled. The only cue is the transient toast "This chat now uses X."

Each later swap relabels the same replies again. In my run, two replies generated as General went "Assistant" -> "Samira 'Sammy' Vadem" -> "Default Assistant". "Default Assistant" is itself a character card, so swapping back never restores the original "Assistant" label.

The same label feeds per-message Save-to-Library titles and the Save-as/Chatbook message_role. A pre-swap reply saved after a swap is therefore attributed to the new character.

Stored data is not rewritten. The persisted sender is only the role ("assistant"), and the label is computed at render time from the session's current identity. That is the documented model in ADR-046 (which rejected "store a resolved display name on every message") and ADR-149. So this is a design gap that needs an ADR amendment (a per-message identity snapshot and/or a swap divider), not a regression. It is P2, not P1: the harm is presentational, it only follows a deliberate user action, and "Start new chat" is offered right beside the swap button.
expected: Past turns keep the identity that produced them, and the swap appears as a transcript divider ('Character changed to Samira …').
why: It rewrites history and misattributes answers, a provenance and trust problem for anyone reviewing or exporting research chats.
repro: Send 2–3 messages as General, then Assistant chip ▸ choose a character ▸ Swap in this chat, and scroll up.
recommendation: Store the speaker identity per message at generation time and render from it. Insert a system divider row on swap.
fix_direction:
Amend ADR-046/ADR-149, then implement the change.
1. At generation time, snapshot the producing identity (kind, id, display name) into each assistant message's local metadata. The metadata envelope can already hold template provenance. Have the resolver prefer that snapshot for assistant rows and fall back to the session identity for legacy messages. That keeps ADR-046's retroactive relabel for user rows and for rows with no snapshot.
2. When an identity swap is applied to a non-empty chat, insert a non-provider "identity changed" transcript divider (e.g. "Character changed: Assistant -> Samira"). Exclude it from model context.
3. Until then, cheapest mitigation: add one line to the placement dialog, e.g. "Earlier replies will be relabeled as <name>; use Start new chat to keep them as-is."
