title: Turn status labels mislabel the phase ('Generating…' for about 18 s before the provider is contacted), show elapsed time only sometimes, and 'Failed' uses the same amber as progress
statement: The turn status labels 'Failed', 'Generating…' and 'Connecting tools… · 7s' all render #b4915e bold on #242f38 (4.65:1), with the same amber role stripe as a successful reply. The first send showed an elapsed counter ('Connecting tools… · 7s'). The 12 s slow wait and the stall showed a static 'Generating…' with no elapsed time, although nothing was being generated because the provider had not responded. On J5's first send, the assistant row showed 'Generating…' with no elapsed figure from about 7 s until the reply. The log shows 'console agent reply start' at 12:04:59, trace_reservation at 12:05:16 and provider_entry only at 12:05:17. The user guide (agent-runs-and-tools.md:54-56) says this pre-provider phase is marked 'Connecting tools… · 4s'.
expected: Turn status maps to semantic tokens: running = $accent, waiting = $text-muted with elapsed time, failed = $error with 'Failed ✕', stopped = $warning. Elapsed time is always appended after about 1 s. The phase is named accurately: 'Connecting tools…/Preparing run…' for the whole pre-provider window, including trace reservation, then 'Waiting for Anthropic…/Waiting for provider', 'Running tools', and 'Generating…/Writing reply' only once the provider request is in flight.
why: Past 10 s, users need progress and an accurate phase to decide whether to wait or stop, especially while Stop is hidden (G1-01). Failure doesn't stand out when scanning, and long waits look identical to hangs. Speed itself belongs to the PERF series; the mislabelled phase does not.
repro: Compare status-label runs in the 504, drip and first-send captures. On a fresh ready launch, send a tool prompt, capture every 3 s, and compare with log phase timestamps.
recommendation: Emit 'Connecting tools…' for the whole pre-provider window with a ticking elapsed timer, and switch to 'Generating…' at provider_entry. Map each status to a semantic token (failed = $error plus word/icon), and always append elapsed time after 1 s. Drive these from the shared run presenter (G1-04).
evidence: app log 12:04:59 'console agent reply start' → 12:05:16 trace_reservation → 12:05:17 provider_entry

title: Message actions mix words with glyphs (🔊, ♻, --->) that need a truncating legend; Retry vs ♻ differ; the More menu truncates labels until their meaning changes
statement:
A selected assistant row reads 'Copy  🔊  Edit  Fork  ♻   --->  More…'. Regenerate is '♻' (U+267B, ambiguous width; it renders at one cell and looks like a small 'o' speck). Continue is '--->', the kind of hard-coded ASCII arrow TASK-23195 removed from the rail headers. Speak is '🔊'.

The meanings are given only in a 'Guide:' line ('🔊 Speak · r ♻ Regenerate · ---> Continue'). At 120x40 that line truncates to '… f Fork · r ♻', dropping Regenerate, Continue and 'Esc clear'. It gives no key for 🔊, ---> or More…, so reaching them takes up to 7 Tabs.

The same action changes name and key between row types:
- On a failed turn Regenerate is the word 'Retry', no key is listed, and pressing r does nothing.
- User rows also offer ♻ and --->.
- System error rows offer no actions, not even Copy for the error text.

The Fork refusal reads 'Fork unavailable — Saved active leaf lineage is unavailable.' (jargon; see G1-09).

The More popover is fixed at 24 cells (console_message_more_menu.py:63), and a code comment acknowledges the truncation (console_message_actions.py:370-392):
- 'Summarize up to here as note' renders as 'Summarize up to'.
- 'Save transcript up to here as note' renders as 'Save transcript', which misstates the scope.
- Message-scoped items (Save as…, Helpful, Not helpful, Delete, Capture as note) and span-scoped items share one list.
- Delete is not separated.
- Labels mix 'Save as...' (three dots) and 'Save as…'.

J8 also found that Summarize spends tokens without a preview (G1-40).
expected: Text labels at normal widths, with key hints inline ('Copy c · Edit e · Regenerate r · Continue · Speak · Fork f · More… m'). Glyphs are allowed only as an optional prefix beside the word or as a narrow-width fallback (the row has about 150 free cols at 235). The same action has the same label and key on every row type (Retry = Regenerate = r), in a fixed order, disabled with a reason rather than removed. Copy is available on System and error rows. The More menu is wide enough for full labels, grouped by scope (This message / Up to here), with Delete last and separated. Disabled reasons are plain language with a next step ('Fork needs a saved conversation').
why: Users cannot recognise icon-only actions without a legend that disappears at common widths. Low-vision users can't read one-cell symbols. The same action changing name and key between states breaks learning, and a truncated 'Save transcript' misstates what the action does.
repro: Select an assistant message at 235x52 and at 120x40 (or F6 to the transcript and press j). Select a failed turn. Select a System error row. Click More….
recommendation: Render 'Copy  Speak  Edit  Fork  Regenerate  Continue  More…' in words, collapsing to icons only below a width threshold (keep ascii_glyphs fallbacks), so the guide line only needs key letters. Bind m = More… and a speak key. Bind r to retry on failed turns and use one label for Retry/Regenerate. Add Copy to System rows. Size the More popover to its longest label (or use a modal list), add two headed scope groups and a separator before Delete, and normalise the ellipsis. Rewrite the Fork disabled reason with a next step.
evidence: uxrev/evidence/J6/tab_tr235/*.diff (7 Tab stops to reach More…)

title: Markdown headings and table headers render as low-contrast, underlined blue 'links' (2.62:1; 2.25:1 when selected), and H1 is centred
statement: H1 ('Sorting Algorithms'), H2s ('## Demo', 'Common Sorting Algorithms', 'Insertion Sort Implementation', 'Complexity Comparison') and table header cells render #0178d4 on the #353836 markdown surface at 2.62:1. That makes them the lowest-contrast text in the reply, failing AA. Table borders are 1.68:1. H2s are non-bold and underlined, and a function name in a code block is also underlined, so they read as hyperlinks (DESIGN task-185: underline reads as a link). H1 is centred across 180 columns while H2s are flush left. When the message is selected, every line becomes bold and underlined and the headers drop to 2.25:1. The single-newline collapse ('1 2 3 4 5') also reproduced twice for J2 (see G1-27).
expected: Headings are the strongest scan anchors: bold $text/$ds-text-primary (h1/h2 may use an $accent that clears 4.5:1), not underlined, left-aligned to the body edge, optionally with a muted rule or blank line above. Table headers are bold $text. Code identifiers are not underlined. Selection is shown by a background tint and the edge, without underlining content.
why: Reading the reply is the core task, and long answers are scanned by heading. The anchors are the hardest text to see and look clickable, which slows re-finding sections and invites dead clicks.
repro: Ask for markdown with #/## headings and a table, capture, and run sgr pairs on heading rows (J7: r19 H1, r26 H2). Select the message and re-measure.
recommendation: Override the Markdown H1–H3 and table-header styles in the Console transcript CSS: left-aligned, bold $ds-text-primary, no underline. Remove underline from code identifiers. Make the selection style a background tint plus the edge only. Add an SGR contrast assertion for the heading run in a test.

title: Assistant markdown collapses single newlines: 'one number per line' renders as one line
statement: The prompt 'Count from 1 to 40, one number per line.' rendered as '1 2 3 4 … 40' on a single line at 160x45. J2 independently noted the same single-newline collapse reproducing twice ('1 2 3 4 5'), recorded under G1-26. Lead confidence: medium.
expected: As in most chat UIs, soft line breaks in model output render as line breaks.
why: Line-oriented output (lists without markers, poems, addresses, logs, CLI output) becomes unreadable.
repro: Ready mode: send 'Count from 1 to 40, one number per line.'
recommendation: Render soft line breaks as hard breaks (breaks=True equivalent) in assistant and user message markdown, outside code blocks.

title: The main transcript scrollbar thumb is invisible (1.01:1); an earlier fix was applied to other scrollers but not this one
statement: The transcript thumb renders '▆' at #2d2d2d on #242f38, which is 1.01:1. #console-native-transcript, #console-workspace-tree and the session chat-log still use scrollbar-color $ds-grid-line (_console.tcss:1267-1270, 908-911). TASK-31665 AC#15 measured exactly this pairing at 1.01:1 and moved the settings modal and 'five more scrollers' to $ds-text-muted (_console_panels.tcss:24-40). The left rail body's thumb is visible (text-muted), so two scrollbars seen side by side disagree.
expected: Every Console scroller, above all the transcript, uses the visible thumb token.
why: In long conversations the thumb is the only indicator of position and remaining length.
repro: Any long reply; run sgr.py on the cell in the transcript's last column.
recommendation: Switch the three remaining selectors to $ds-text-muted. Add a stylesheet lint rejecting scrollbar-color: $ds-grid-line on $ds-surface-panel.

title: A stale 'Agent run failed' System row stays below the good answer after a successful Retry
statement: After a 504, Retry on the failed turn produced 'ok', but the row 'System — Agent run failed: provider returned HTTP 504 …' stays directly below the successful reply. The transcript therefore reads as if the answer failed afterwards. The row persisted after relaunch and accumulates across retries (also seen on the 429 path).
expected: A resolved failure collapses into a quiet annotation on the successful turn ('Retried after 504 · 1 attempt') or is removed.
why: It creates a misleading history and clutter that accumulates across retries.
repro: Proxy 504, send, choose 'Send without capture'. Set the proxy to normal, select the failed turn, and choose Retry.
recommendation: Tie the System failure row to the attempt id and mark it superseded (collapsed to one muted line) when a retry of that turn succeeds.

title: Keyboard j/k selection moves off-screen without scrolling, so the selection and its action bar are invisible
statement: With the latest (tall) assistant message selected, pressing k selected the user message above. That message and its action bar stayed out of view, so the screen showed no selection, and further typing appeared to do nothing. Only scrolling up revealed 'User … Copy Edit Fork ♻ ---> More…' with the selection. The only cue was the highlighted, bold, underlined 'Conversation | …' pane header.
expected: Selecting a message scrolls at least its role line and action bar into view. For messages taller than the viewport, the role line is aligned to the top.
why: Keyboard users lose track of what e, r or f will act on, so they could act on an unseen message.
repro: Ready 235x52 with a long last reply. Click an Assistant role label, then press k twice.
recommendation: In _select_relative, call scroll_to_widget or scroll_visible on the selected row, top-aligned with its action bar.

title: /rewind shows no consequences before or after 'Restore to here' and offers no way back
statement: The Rewind modal lists '#1 Say OK 2'. Selecting it adds 'Restore to here', two summarise buttons and 'Never mind', with no text about later turns (console_rewind_modal.py:236-265). After Restore, the transcript shows only 'No messages yet.' with the prompt back in the composer. There is no banner, branch indicator or undo. The reassurance ('Nothing is deleted: the rewound turns remain reachable as a branch') appears only in the guide, which also admits that restoring on the first prompt does not survive a restart and that /rewind can only be reached by typing it (branching-and-rewind.md:130-133,214-220).
expected: One line in the modal ('Later turns are kept as a branch; you can switch back with < >'), a post-rewind banner with 'Undo rewind', and a palette entry.
why: An empty transcript after rewind looks like data loss, so users will avoid a useful feature.
repro: In a one-turn chat: /rewind, Enter, choose #1, then 'Restore to here'.
recommendation: Add consequence copy under 'Restore to here', an inline 'Rewound to #1 · 2 turns kept on a branch · Undo' banner, and palette and message-action entries. Fix the first-prompt persistence case, or state it in the UI.

title: 'Summarize up to' silently spends tokens and saves a note with no preview, location or link; More-menu Delete is not separated
statement: Message More… lists 'Summarize up to' and 'Save transcript'. The real labels are 'Summarize up to here as note' and 'Save transcript up to here as note', truncated by the fixed 24-cell menu (console_message_more_menu.py:63; labels at console_message_actions.py:380-391), so 'Save transcript' reads as saving the whole transcript (see also G1-25). Clicking Summarize immediately made a provider call (proxy log 13:21:22 j82 POST) and toasted 'Saved summary as Note.' There was no preview, cost, destination or open link. A ConsoleSummarizePreviewModal exists but was not used. Delete sits between feedback items with no separation.
expected: Full labels (widen the menu or shorten the wording, e.g. 'Summarize → note'). Paid LLM actions show a preview with Save/Discard and a cost estimate. The toast includes the location and 'Open note'. Delete is in its own group with a confirm.
why: Surprise spend and an output the user can't locate break the local-first 'durable artifacts' promise, and the truncated labels mislead.
repro: Select an assistant message ▸ More… ▸ Summarize up to.
recommendation: Size the More menu to its longest label, or use two-line rows. Route summarize through the existing preview modal with a cost estimate. Put the note location and an 'Open note' action in the toast. Separate Delete with a divider and a confirm (see G1-02 for delete scope).

title: In long chats Home loads only ~17 earlier turns per press, shows nothing about how much history remains, and the scrollbar describes only the loaded window
statement: When you open a long chat (200 exchanges, 400 messages), it starts at the latest turn. From there, each Home press with the transcript focused loads one scroll-back chunk. At 235x52 a chunk is about 17 turns. Starting from turn 200 the first visible turn went 174, 157, 140, 121, 103, 86, 69, 61 (the 3,000-line reply), 43, 27, 9, 1, so turn 1 took 12 presses. Each chunk settles in under a second. Pressing Home rapidly helps only partly: 5 quick presses advanced 3 chunks. Nothing tells the user how much history is left. There is no 'loading earlier' row, no 'N earlier turns', no 'start of conversation' marker, and no position readout or jump-to-turn. The scrollbar thumb only describes the loaded window. It does not stay mid-track as the finding says. It drifts upward (rows 26-27, then 22, 19-20, 18, 16-17, 16 on a track of about rows 11-46). It then jumps DOWN to row 35 once the 3,000-line reply is loaded, while the reader is at turn 69 of 200. So the thumb position has no stable relation to where the reader is in the conversation. End returns to turn 200 in one press. The asymmetry is per open, not permanent. Once history is loaded in the current open, Home reaches turn 1 in one press. Switching to another tab and back rebuilds the window, and Home is back to one chunk per press (175, 158, 141).
expected: Home (and g) should go to the start of the conversation, hydrating as needed, or at least show 'Turns 175–200 of 200 · earlier turns load as you scroll'. The scrollbar should reflect the whole conversation, or a textual position should be shown.
why: Reviewing or citing early context in long work sessions is a core Console task. Users can't tell whether they've reached the beginning or how far away it is, and a keyboard user has to press Home 14 times.
repro: Open a 400-message chat, click a message, press Home repeatedly, note the first visible Turn number and the thumb position each time; press End.
recommendation: Add a one-line position/hydration row at the top of the loaded window: '▲ 174 earlier turns — Home loads all · PgUp loads more', and 'Start of conversation' when complete. Make Home/g hydrate to turn 1 (the tail-window perf goal still holds on open). Add jump-to-turn (Ctrl+K 'Go to turn…' or /goto 61). Consider a textual 'turn 141/200' indicator in the transcript header while scrolled away from the tail.
fix_direction: Keep the TASK-15455/15777 open-time performance bounds and add the feedback on top. (1) Show a thin row above the mounted slice when the hidden prefix is non-empty, for example '(up arrow) 174 earlier turns, PgUp loads more, Home loads all'. When the prefix is empty, show 'Start of conversation'. The count is already known from _set_hidden_prefix. (2) Override Home on ConsoleTranscript to go to the first message through the existing bounded far-jump (reveal_message or re-centred window), so it does not walk chunk by chunk. This mirrors scroll_end's tailward handling. (3) Optionally add a 'turn N / M' readout in the transcript header while detached from the tail, and a Go to turn entry (Ctrl+K or /goto) that reuses reveal_message. (4) Update Docs/User_Guide/console.md 'Long conversations' to describe Home's behaviour and the new indicator.

title: A 3,000-line reply renders fully inline, with no fold, size label or way to jump past it
statement: Turn 61's 3,000-line fenced code reply renders all 3,000 lines inline. It has no language label, no line count, no per-block copy and no collapse, so getting past it takes about 70 PageDowns, and Home paging stalled on it. Tool rows already have a 'Full output' (o) pattern, but assistant replies have nothing similar.
expected: Very long blocks should fold by default beyond a threshold, with a header giving language, line count and actions (expand, copy block, open in viewer) and a one-key skip to the next turn.
why: One oversized reply makes the rest of the history hard to reach and scan.
repro: Open the seeded 'Long build log review' chat and navigate to Turn 061.
recommendation: Fold code blocks or replies longer than N lines (e.g. 60) into 'python · 3,000 lines · showing first 20 · [Expand] [Copy block] [Open]', reusing the tool 'Full output' viewer. Let ]/[ (or j/k with selection) jump turn to turn past folded content.

title: Tool rows show model-directed prompt text and raw JSON as the user's record, and the same tool has two names
statement: A deny renders as 'tool call denied by the user: mcp__uxstamp__stamp_text. Do not retry this call, do not rephrase it, and do not pursue the same outcome by another route. Ask… (+29 chars)'. A timeout renders as 'ERROR: … do not retry'. The user's own ask_user answer renders as '{"answered":true,"answers":[{"question":"Which colour do you prefer?","selected":["Blue"],"other_text":null,"unanswered":false}]}' plus a separate '▸ Question answered · done' row. MCP results render as '{"result": [{"type": "text", …}]}'. The approval card calls the tool 'uxstamp · stamp_text', but the transcript row calls it 'mcp__uxstamp__stamp_text'.
expected: A user-facing summary per outcome ('You denied stamp_text', 'You answered: Blue', 'Result: [STAMP] hello'), with the model-facing text available under a disclosure, and one display name for each tool everywhere.
why: Instructions written for the model ('do not rephrase it') read as scolding or nonsense to people. The record of the user's own decisions should be the clearest thing on screen.
repro: Deny an MCP call, answer an ask_user question, and let one approval time out. Read the transcript rows.
recommendation: Add a presentation layer for tool rows: an outcome verb, a one-line human summary, and 'Show raw' for the payload. Map llm_name to 'server · tool' in every row, and bring Trace into line.

title: After a selection 'Comment' is submitted, the resulting reply never renders: the tab stays on 'Generating…' and 'Agent running' until the user switches tabs
statement: Sometimes, but not reliably, the Console transcript-sync poll stops partway through a run. The transcript then stays on 'Assistant  Generating…' / 'Run: Agent running.' after the reply has finished, until a tab switch forces a repaint. The earlier GAP5 artifacts show this happened twice, both times on a selection-Comment turn. It is not deterministic and its trigger is unknown: the stated repro (select text, Comment, Enter, wait 60 s) rendered the reply live 7 times out of 7 in a fresh isolated profile under varied conditions. The stated root cause is also wrong. The Comment/feedback dispatch does start the transcript sync timer. It runs through the same ConsolePromptQueueUIController.dispatch -> _stage_normal_chain -> _commit_captured_console_draft -> screen._start_console_transcript_sync_timer() path as a composer send, and the original logs show the timer running at the moment of the comment dispatch. Something stopped it 2-3 s later while the run was still in progress.
expected: The reply renders as soon as the run completes, as it does for a normal composer send.
why: The user believes the agent is still working and waits indefinitely, or sends duplicate prompts. The completed answer is effectively lost from view.
repro: Drag-select text inside any assistant reply → selection menu → Comment → type a comment → Enter. Wait 60 s without changing tabs.
recommendation: Route feedback dispatches through the same path as composer sends, so the transcript sync timer starts and final UI sync runs on completion. Add a regression test in which a feedback-comment turn reaches 'complete' without a tab switch.
fix_direction: Do not 'route feedback through the composer path': it already goes through that path. Make the end-of-run repaint independent of the poll timer staying alive. Options: have the runtime or controller terminal edge (_finish_custodied_turn / the terminal run-state transition) schedule one _sync_native_console_chat_ui on the attached view; or make the poll's self-stop re-check after a final sync and re-arm while any accepted turn remains in runtime custody. Also consider re-arming the timer at the end of _reconcile_console_after_attach when poll is needed, not only through the on_screen_resume in_flight_run_count() > 0 branch. To pin the trigger first, launch through launch.sh with a PYTHONPATH sitecustomize that logs a stack trace and (run_state, in_flight_run_count, app.screen) on every _stop_console_transcript_sync_timer call, then repeat Comment flows under CPU load or with modal open/close near dispatch. Regression test: a feedback-comment turn whose run spans a modal push/pop reaches 'complete' on screen without a tab switch, including when a suspend or resume lands mid-run.

title: 'Comment on selection → Submit' silently sends a new model turn, and quotes the wrong text
statement:
Reproduced live on origin/dev 64579cce2c.

1. Submit sends a new model turn with no warning. I asked for a code-block reply, drag-selected rendered code lines and chose Comment. The modal shows "Comment on selection", an "Optional comment" field and Cancel / Submit, and says nothing about sending. Pressing Enter posts a "[Comment]" user turn and starts a real provider call: the log shows "Routing to endpoint: anthropic" with draft_length=64, which is exactly the length of the composed message. A new assistant reply follows. The same submit also adds a "Review note" annotation to the reviewed message, which makes it look as if Comment only saved a note. The viewport stayed where it was; the only on-screen change was a "reply ready — jump to latest" pill. The user guide does document the send (text-selection-and-feedback.md:111-115), so "silently" means nothing tells the user at the moment they act.

2. The quote does not match the selection, and the cause is broader than a fence line. On markdown rows the pointer-to-source mapping is wrong in two ways:
   - Rows are spread evenly across the source lines, fence lines included.
   - The column ignores the code block's indent.
   Also, set_selection_range no longer snaps to whole lines, so ADR-068's claim that snapping bounds the error is stale.
   Live results:
   - Dragging over "def add(a, b):" and "return a + b" quoted "f add(a, b):", "    return a + b" and a stray "```".
   - Dragging over the single line "return a + b" quoted "turn a + b".

3. Every selection action uses the same wrong text. Copy selection put "turn a + b" on the clipboard, which contradicts TASK-32033 AC#2 (Done).

4. Two highlights disagree. Textual's native blue highlight covers exactly the rendered line. The reverse-video strip under the block, and the modal's quote preview, show the wrong text that is actually sent.

5. One recommendation is already met. The modal already previews exactly the quote the model receives; the problem is that this quote is wrong, not that it is hidden.

6. The hint "No active run — start a run to send review feedback" sits right under the enabled Comment button. That wording suggests Comment also needs a run, when in fact Comment starts one.
expected: The modal says what Submit does ('Sends your comment to the assistant as a new message'), and its button names the action ('Send comment'). Otherwise the comment is saved as an annotation only. The quote is exactly the text the user highlighted.
why: The user thinks they are leaving a note, but they spend tokens and change the conversation. A wrong quote means the model is asked to act on text the user did not select.
repro: Ask for a reply with a code block → drag-select two rendered code lines → Comment → type text → Enter.
recommendation: Rename the action 'Send comment to assistant' and add one line of consequence copy in the modal: 'Starts a new reply · uses the active model'. Also offer a 'Save as note only' option. Map the selection back to source using rendered-to-source offsets that account for fence lines, and show the exact quote the model will receive.
fix_direction:
Disclosure (H1/H5):
- Rename Submit to 'Send to assistant', or 'Send comment'.
- Add one line of consequence copy in the modal, e.g. 'Sends as your next message and starts a reply with <model>' (or 'queues behind the current run').
- Offer 'Save note only', which writes the transcript_annotations row without calling _dispatch_prompt.
- After a send, scroll to the new turn or show a toast.
- Reword the menu hint so it clearly applies only to Request changes/LGTM.

Quote accuracy:
- Stop mapping rendered cells to markdown source by even distribution. Either build the quote from the rendered text Textual's native selection already exposes (for example the screen/widget selected-text API), or build a real rendered-row-to-source map per block, with code-block rows mapping to their fence body and the indent/padding columns subtracted.
- Until that exists, snap markdown and code-block selections to whole source lines inside the fence. Never include fence lines, and never start mid-line.
- Make the reverse strip and the native highlight agree, or drop one of them.
- Add a regression test: drag over rendered code-block lines, then assert that get_selection_text(), Copy and the Comment quote equal exactly those lines.
- Update the stale ADR-068 text, and reopen or extend TASK-32033 AC#2, since Copy of Markdown code is not exact.

title: Continue ('--->') sends the literal UI instruction 'Continue and extend the selected message.', which the model cannot resolve
statement:
Continue ('--->') never extends the selected reply in place. It always adds a new, separate assistant row (controller:19897-19902). The provider receives the ephemeral user turn "Continue and extend the selected message." (CONSOLE_CONTINUE_INSTRUCTION, controller:2645, appended by _ensure_user_continuation_instruction at 22926-22938). The model cannot see that "selection". With claude-haiku-4-5 this produced a clarification non-answer in 2 of 3 live trials: "I don't have a 'selected message' to extend…" and "I don't have context about a previously selected message to continue from…". In the third trial the model rewrote the whole answer in a new bubble: the original 3 planets repeated, plus 5 more. That duplicates content instead of continuing it. The User Guide promises "Continue — extend the selected message with more generated text" (chat-basics.md:451).

The trace-capture tail is real, but only when Library automatic retrieval is on, which it was in the GAP5 session. In that case, every later send in the chat stops at "Trace capture blocked" (trace_reservation error_category=unsupported_surface_change). I saw it on 2 of 2 sends after Continue. A control chat with the same two Library questions and no Continue sent fine. Each blocked send can be pushed through with Retry capture, which leads to a "Response delivery status is unknown… Retry anyway" card, and then Retry anyway. In a plain chat without Library retrieval, the next sends after Continue worked (2 of 2), so the finding's general repro ("select any reply → Continue → send") does not reproduce as written.
expected: Continue extends the chosen reply in place, or appends 'continued' text visibly linked to it. The instruction sent is model-meaningful ('Continue your previous answer from where it stopped'), and the chat stays usable afterwards.
why: The action spends tokens to produce a confused non-answer, and it silently breaks later sends in the chat.
repro: Select any assistant reply → click '--->' in its action row → wait for the reply → then send a new prompt in the same chat.
recommendation: Replace the instruction with provider-meaningful text, or use assistant-prefill continuation where the provider supports it. Render the continuation attached to the source reply. Make CONTINUE-route turns valid trace surfaces, so later sends are not blocked.
fix_direction: (1) Replace CONSOLE_CONTINUE_INSTRUCTION with provider-meaningful text, e.g. "Continue your previous response exactly where it stopped; do not repeat earlier text." Better, use assistant-prefill continuation (send the selected assistant text as a trailing assistant turn) for providers that support it. (2) Render the continuation attached to the source reply: merge it into the source reply, or visibly label it "continued from ↑", and make the ephemeral instruction inspectable in the trace/Inspector. (3) Only offer Continue on the latest assistant reply, or give mid-transcript Continue branch semantics, so the new row is not appended far from its source. (4) Make a CONTINUE turn a valid predecessor trace surface under RETRY_OMISSION, so the next RAG turn does not raise unsupported_surface_change. Add a regression test for the sequence RAG turn → continue → RAG turn. Route this tail to G4-10 / PR #2882 and confirm #2882 covers it, since this reproduction shows the continue message action is the trigger. (5) Update chat-basics.md:451 to describe the actual behaviour.

title: No per-code-block copy; selecting code underlines the whole message and shows a raw-markdown fragment
statement: Code blocks render with no language label and no copy affordance. The only options are whole-message Copy, which includes the heading and markdown fences, or a drag-select followed by 'Copy selection'. Even a selected reply shows only 'Copy 🔊 Edit Fork ♻ ---> More…'. During a drag-selection the entire message body turns underlined (bold underline, #e1e6eb on #194466), and a raw fragment ('`python / def add(a, b):') is painted beneath the rendered block. The 🔊 emoji shifts the overlay border by one column on its row.
expected: Each fenced block has a compact header ('python · Copy'), plus a keyboard path (for example 'c' on a focused block). Selection highlight does not underline unrelated text or show raw source.
why: Copying code is a primary task for the builder/operator persona. Making it depend on precise mouse selection is slow and error-prone.
repro: Ask for two code blocks → try to copy only the bash one-liner.
recommendation: Add a per-fence header row with the language and a Copy button (and 'Save as file…'), reachable by Tab inside the selected message. Drop the underline from the selection style, and never render raw-source excerpts in the transcript.

title: Keyboard focus, the active tab, the selected message and 'region has focus' share one style, so real focus is ambiguous
statement:
Confirmed live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c at 235x52, with the exact colours given in the finding. The real keyboard focus, the active session tab, the region-focused rail collapse button, the focused-pane title row and the selected transcript message all use one style: $ds-focus-bg + $ds-focus-fg + bold underline. The only thing that sets real focus apart is Textual's built-in Button:focus `background-tint: $foreground 5%`, which shifts #194466 to #1c4666, a 1.028:1 change.

(1) Left rail. After F6, Terminal (real focus, #1c4666), 'Context ◂' (#194466, from the region-focused rule) and the active tab (#194466) all render bold, underlined and blue. Shift+Tab onto 'Context ◂' changes only #194466 to #1c4666, so the stop is invisible. Pressing Enter then collapsed the rail, which proves focus was on it.

(2) Tab strip with 2 tabs. Focusing the inactive 'Chat 1' tab (#1c4666, bold underline) makes it look the same as the active 'Chat 2' tab (#194466, bold underline). The pane title 'Conversation | Chat 2' is also painted with the same style, so three look-alikes sit within two rows. Focusing the active tab itself is also a 1.03:1 change.

(3) Alt+I. When the Inspect rail opens, '▸ Inspect' gets the region style while real focus is on the body card.

(4) Selecting a message. With j, the selected message body renders fully bold, underlined and blue. For the user message the speaker label does too; the assistant label keeps its amber role colour. This persists after focus leaves the transcript: with Shift+F6 to the rail, four groups looked focused at once (Context ◂, Terminal, the active tab and the selected assistant paragraph).

Additions to the finding:
- The transcript's pane-title cue from TASK-20937.3 uses the same trio, and it stays lit while focus is in the tab strip.
- The left rail already has a separate region cue: its pane divider turns #0178d4. The collapse-button paint is therefore redundant as well as ambiguous.
- In the same strip, 'New tab' and 'Temporary' show focus only as #1e1e1e to #272727 (1.12:1), with no weight or underline change. This is a sibling invisible-focus stop.
expected: One distinct, high-contrast treatment reserved for keyboard focus. Active and selected states use a different, non-focus cue (marker glyph, left bar, bold without underline). Region focus shows only on the pane border or title.
why: 'Where am I?' is the most basic question for a keyboard or low-vision user. With 2–3 elements looking focused and the real focus move at 1.03:1, users lose their place and press Enter on the wrong control. Underlining whole paragraphs also hurts readability.
repro: 235x52: F6 to the left rail (Terminal focused), then Tab repeatedly and compare 'Context ◂', 'Terminal' and the active tab. F6 to the transcript, Tab to the tab strip, and compare the focused tab with the active tab.
recommendation: Define focus as its own token set used only by :focus, with a shape change (outline, heavy border or ▶ marker) and a background at least 3:1 against the unfocused state. Restyle active tabs as bold plus a '▎' marker without underline, and selected messages with a tinted left bar and a highlighted speaker label, never a body underline. Remove the region-focused rule on the collapse buttons and signal region focus on the pane title or border (see G4-39).
fix_direction:
1. Reserve one focus-only treatment that is never reused for state. Give it a shape change, such as a thick left or right outline edge, a heavy border or a ▶ marker (the codebase already uses `outline-left: thick $ds-action-focus` for the Inspect body), and at least 3:1 against the unfocused look. Stop relying on Textual's 5% tint.
2. Restyle `.console-session-tab-active` as bold plus a marker glyph or bottom edge, with no focus background and no underline, following the TASK-32071 nav-bar precedent ("distinct by shape, not colour alone").
3. Restyle `.console-transcript-message-selected` as a tinted left bar plus a highlighted speaker label, with no body underline. Dim it, or drop it to a quieter variant, when the transcript does not have focus.
4. Delete the `.console-edge-region-focused #console-*-rail-collapse/open` rule. Keep the pane divider recolour (it already exists) or a title-row cue that is not the focus trio.
5. Give 'New tab'/'Temporary' a real :focus cue.
6. Add a regression test that asserts, via a Pilot snapshot of computed styles, that exactly one widget renders the focus treatment at each Tab stop.

title: Contrast failures on the default screen at every size: focused composer placeholder 2.56:1, primary button labels 3.78:1, input boundaries about 1.05:1
statement: sgr.py pairs at 235x52, 120x40 and 80x24. The composer placeholder 'Ask, command, or paste task...' is #625e4c on #1e1e1e (2.56:1) in its default focused state and 6.77:1 unfocused, so focus makes it darker (console_composer_bar.py:3040-3042, style='bright_black'). The left-rail filter placeholder is 3.52:1 (#737373), and so is the switcher search placeholder. The active nav key hint '⌃2' is 2.91:1 (#91bce2 on #0065be). Primary button labels are #ddedf9 on #0178d4, 3.78:1: 'Enable' (cost consent), 'Save' (rename), 'Submit' (approval), 'Use for this conversation' (settings). 'Deny' and 'Deny all' are 4.47:1. The filter field's boundary glyphs are 1.05–1.29:1, the switch knob is 1.42:1, and the composer focus edge █ is 2.25:1 against its own cell. J8 independently measured the placeholder at 2.56:1.
expected: Text at least 4.5:1, including placeholders that carry the only instructions. Non-text state and focus indicators at least 3:1. Primary action labels at least 4.5:1.
why: Low-vision users can't read the composer's own instruction or the labels on the most consequential buttons (Enable, Submit, Save) in the default theme.
repro: Launch at each size and run sgr.py pairs on the boot capture. Open the cost-consent, rename and approval dialogs and run sgr.py on their button rows.
recommendation: Render the placeholder with $ds-text-muted in both states (6.77:1 as measured unfocused). Darken the $primary button backgrounds or use dark text so primary labels reach 4.5:1. Raise input-boundary and knob colours to at least 3:1. Add these pairs to the contrast ratchet already used for disabled labels (DESIGN.md 'Legible Disabled Rule').

title: Run and attention states use three glyph vocabularies across tabs, rail rows and rail sections, and the row status glyph doubles as the row-menu button
statement: Tabs and the fleet use ● running, ◆ needs approval, ✓ finished, ✗ failed, ◈ sub-agent (console_chat_models.py:186-192; the F1 legend at chat_screen.py:1366-1370 decodes only this set). Conversation rows in the left rail use the conversation_attention set: ⟳ running, ✋ approval, ⛔ blocked, ✗ failed, ⏸ paused, ⏹ stopped, ✉ unread, ✓ ready, 🔔 new, and 💬 by default (conversation_attention.py:21-32, 85-91). Rail sections use console_glyphs.STATUS_GLYPHS: ● running, ⚠ blocked/stuck, ✗ error/cancelled, ✓ done (console_glyphs.py:13-17, 68-83), although that module calls it 'the ONE vocabulary every Console rail section shares'. Ctrl+K uses uppercase words instead. Observed: during a run the tab showed '● Say OK 1' / '● In under 250 words…' while the rail row showed '⟳'. For a blocked Temporary send the rail showed '⛔' plus the sub-line 'Blocked', while the tab showed only '◌', with no blocked marker. Unread is a lone '✉'. The status glyph replaces the default '💬' on the row's actions-menu button (console_workspace_context.py:2131-2148), so a status indicator doubles as the menu affordance. Every idle row carries a double-width colour 💬 emoji, which conflicts with the 'no decorative terminal skin' contract. The user guide lists two separate vocabularies (sessions-tabs-workspaces.md:33-35, 70-76).
expected: One state → (glyph, short label, token) table, with text-presentation glyphs and ASCII fallbacks, rendered the same on tabs (including blocked and approval), rail rows, sections, the switcher, the fleet, the Inspector and the F1 legend. A separate, stable row-actions affordance (⋯ / [...]) shown on hover or focus, with neutral rows carrying no icon.
why: A returning user scanning for 'what needs me' has to learn two or three icon sets, and blocked is invisible on the tab, the most visible surface.
repro: Send in a tab and compare the tab glyph with the rail glyph mid-run; trigger a Temporary capture block and compare the tab with the rail; compare with F1's 'Status markers'.
recommendation: Merge the three tables into console_glyphs.STATUS_GLYPHS (running, needs-approval, blocked, failed, paused, stopped, unread, done, new), e.g. ● running, ⚠ blocked, ? approval, ✓ ready, • unread, and have ATTENTION_PRESENTATIONS, tabs, sections and the F1 legend read from it. Show status as a separate prefix glyph, and replace the default 💬 with an empty cell plus a hover/focus '⋯'. Use text in ASCII mode.
evidence: uxrev/evidence/J3/15-sent4.txt (rail '⛔ Blocked' vs tab '◌ Say OK 4')

title: Controls grammar varies by region: disclosure glyphs carry three or four meanings, toggle/checkbox glyphs differ, footer separators mix, and 'Settings' points to two surfaces
statement: ▸ means a collapsed section ('Workspaces ▸'), a submenu ('Copy as ▸', 'Change status ▸', 'More ▸'), 'collapse this rail rightward' ('▸ Inspect'), the current-row cursor ('▸ CURRENT' in Ctrl+K) and the collapsed Context handle ('Context ▸'); GLYPH_ACTIVE and GLYPH_COLLAPSE_RIGHT are both '▸' (console_glyphs.py:12-17). ▾ means an expanded section ('Conversations ▾'), a dropdown ('More ▾'), and a collapse action ('Status ▾', 'Composer ▾'). ▴ means expand ('Expand ▴', 'Status ▴'). ▼ means 'scroll for more' ('▼ more sections — scroll') and also renders as '▼ Details', which looks like an expanded header. ◂ / ‹ mean collapse-left ('Context ◂'), open Inspect ('◂ Inspect') and menu back ('‹ Back'). The wizard and Settings collapsibles use ▶/▼. The two neighbouring collapsers disagree: 'Status ▴ Status hidden' names the region, while 'Expand ▴ Composer hidden' names the action. Toggles: header '▌' switch, radio '▐●▌', checkbox '▐X▌' (the X glyph appears whether checked or not), wizard checkbox '▐ ▌'. Buttons: boxed round (card), heavy-edge focus, flat text on canvas (wizard finish, 'Restore a backup', rail 'Archive this chat'). The footer mixes '|' and '·' in one line ('F1 · F6 · Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q'), and the Inspect-focused footer lists F6 twice ('F6 panes' and 'F6 next pane'). The Console header 'Settings' opens 'Conversation settings' while nav 'F4 Settings' is app Settings. The failed-turn button says 'Retry' while help says 'r: regenerate'.
expected: A small controls contract: one disclosure pair (▸/▾) for state only, a distinct submenu glyph (›), ◂/▸ for rail edges only, a distinct row cursor, ▼ only in the fold hint and always with 'more'; one toggle pattern with a state word; one button style per priority tier; one footer separator; unique labels for different destinations; both collapsers reading '<Region> ▾' / '<Region> ▸ (hidden)'.
why: In a terminal UI the glyphs are the signifiers. When each region teaches its own grammar, users must recall meaning by location, which raises the learning cost and works against the unification the owner is aiming for.
repro: Compare captures J1/29, 36, 50, 51, 57 and L1/01, 04, 21, 27, 38 side by side.
recommendation: Write a Console controls/glyph grammar table in DESIGN.md (disclosure, submenu, rail edge, row cursor, fold hint, toggle, button tiers, footer separator, label uniqueness) and lint shipped labels against it. Rename the header button to 'Chat settings'. Align 'Retry' and 'regenerate'.
evidence: uxrev/evidence/J1/50-badkey-inspect.png (footer 'Esc composer · F6 panes | n/p Sections | … F6 next pane')

title: In the default theme the accent colour equals the warning colour, so focus, emphasis and warnings all look the same
statement: textual-dark (default_theme at config.py:3738) defines accent=#ffa62b and warning=#ffa62b. #fea62b was measured on: the appearance-picker modal border ($accent, no warning intended; console_appearance_picker_modal.py:113 'border: tall $accent'), composer-menu disabled reasons ($warning), the cost-chip cache alert, assistant role stripes, and the temperature/max-token values in the Model rail. The recovery-card primaries are the same orange (G4-27).
expected: Distinct tokens for focus/accent and warning (e.g. a steel-blue accent in a Chatbook product theme), per DESIGN.md's 'Earned Accent' and 'Semantic First' rules.
why: When everything emphasised is warning-orange, real warnings such as budget alerts and blocked reasons lose salience.
repro: Conversation actions ▸ Icon and colour…; open Menu; compare with the amber cost chip.
recommendation: Ship a Chatbook default theme, or override the ds-* aliases, so that $ds-action-focus differs from $warning. Audit decorative Console uses of $accent (modal borders, numeric values).

title: The active chat's title appears up to six times on screen, truncated in different ways; provider and model repeat 3–4 times
statement: After one send, with Inspect open at 235x52, the title appears in: the tab 'Reply with exactly…' / 'In under 250 words…'; the transcript title row 'Conversation | Reply with exactly three sh...' / 'In under 250 words: give a...'; the Conversations selected-summary row, over two lines ('Reply with exactly three / sh...'; console_workspace_context.py:1788-1795, above the filter); the Chats list row 'Reply with exactly thr…'; Inspect 'Where: Default › Reply with exactly three…'; and Ctrl+K '▸ CURRENT  Reply with exactly three sh...'. At 160 and 120 columns the rail's selected line wraps to two rows while the list row ellipsizes ('In under 250 word…'). Both '…' and '...' are used. Before any send, 'Chat 1' appears twice in the Conversations section alone. Provider and model appear in the status chips, the Inspect Run recipe and the Inspect Conversation settings block ('Provider: Anthropic', 'Model: claude-haiku-4-5'), even though TASK-23196 removed one copy for this very reason (left_rail.py:2279-2290).
expected: Show each identity fact once per region class: the tab strip owns chat identity (highlighted in the rail list), with no separate title row, selected-summary line or Inspect 'Where:' row. Truncate everywhere with one rule (single line, '…', middle-ellipsis for long titles) and keep the full title in a tooltip.
why: Each repeat costs a row in the most space-constrained regions, and different truncations make one chat look like several.
repro: Two tabs, Inspect open at 235x52; send one message; Ctrl+K; resize to 160/120.
recommendation: Remove the 'Conversation |' row, the rail's selected-summary line and the Inspect 'Where:' row. Keep provider/model in the status chip (and the Next-send group if needed), not in the Conversation settings summary. Add one shared truncate_title() helper that uses '…'. The header breadcrumb can own workspace identity.

title: The empty area above short transcripts renders in the terminal's default background instead of the transcript surface
statement: When the transcript is shorter than the viewport, the unused area above the first message is emitted as ESC[2m ESC[49m spaces (dim, terminal-default background) instead of the transcript surface #242f38. It renders as a large block in the terminal's default colour: white in the PNG renderer and in light terminals, black or a mismatched colour in dark ones.
expected: The spacer uses the transcript surface token.
why: A large visual defect on every new or short chat, especially in light-background terminals.
repro: /help in an empty chat, or send one message, then look above the first block.
recommendation: Give the transcript spacer or top-fill widget an explicit $ds-surface-… background, and add an SGR assertion that no Console region emits 49 (default background).

title: Extends G4-52: approval state gets a different colour and a different word in every region
statement: For one pending approval, each region renders it differently. Tab: '◆' in the neutral label colour (#e1e1e1, no warning colour). Rail row: '✋' in amber #fea62b plus the text 'Approval required'. Fleet line: running-blue at 2.04:1, 'waiting for approval'. Ctrl+K: 'WAITING FOR YOU ▸ APPROVAL'. Status chip: 'Approvals: 1 pen…'. Header: 'Running'. Inspect: 'Run: Waiting for your approva…'. Toasts: 'needs approval to use a tool' / 'needs approval.'. The glyph map for tabs and the one for rail rows are separate tables.
expected: One approval token (glyph + warning colour + one noun such as 'Needs approval') used identically everywhere.
why: It is the most time-critical state in a multi-agent session, and its signal changes shape from region to region, which forces users to learn eight mappings.
repro: Park an approval in tab A, view B, then capture the tab strip, rail, fleet line, Ctrl+K, strip and header.
recommendation: Define one attention table (kind → glyph, ASCII fallback, colour token, short label, long label) and have the tabs, rail, switcher, fleet line, status chip and notifier consume it. Approval uses $warning, with the label 'Needs approval'.

title: Status, warning and 'send blocked' text becomes unreadable in light themes because status colours are raw theme colours, not the text-safe variants
statement:
The core claim holds. I reproduced it live on origin/dev 64579cce2c. Console text that must be read, such as reasons and consequence lines, is coloured with raw theme hues. The warning, ready, running, info, paused and approval-required status tokens resolve to warning, success, primary and accent. The authority-local token resolves to success. None of these is bound to Textual's text-* variables, which adjust to light or dark themes. In the same recovery state, switching theme live:
- Composer 'Send blocked - resolve response recovery first': 8.50:1 in textual-dark, 1.38 in textual-light, 1.19 in paper_light, 2.63 in solarized_light.
- Recovery-card line 'Retry anyway may send a duplicate request...': 6.96, 1.27, 1.47 and 2.63.
- Rail 'Terminal' button: 7.16, 1.63, 1.21 and 2.62.

Corrections:
(a) The placeholder turns warning-coloured only when setup blocks Send (for example 'choose a model'). In that state the typed draft is also warning-coloured, which is worse. In the recovery state the placeholder is muted text at 3.14 light and 6.77 dark.
(b) The transcript 'Failed' label (2.96 in light) does not use a status token. It is a dim status line in the assistant accent, which already adapts to the theme. The dim style is the cause.
(c) The 2.62:1 headings in dark come from Textual's default markdown heading colours (primary), not from the ds status tokens.
(d) 'Terminal' uses the authority-local token, so the fix must also cover the authority and source-role token families.
(e) Raw status-error and status-blocked still colour some text, at 3.06:1 even in textual-dark, so error is only partly migrated.
(f) The contrast gate already checks text-success and text-warning in every theme (TASK-32947). What is missing is wiring the status tokens to them, plus a lint.
expected: Every foreground that must be read — status words, block reasons, consequences, markers — passes 4.5:1 in any shipped theme. The raw hues are used only for borders, background tints and non-essential decoration. DESIGN.md already requires semantic tokens and readable labels.
why: In a light theme the user cannot read why Send is blocked, or the warning that a retry may be sent twice. That is the recovery information PRODUCT.md says must be visible without reading logs. The same token set works in one colour scheme and fails in the other, so tuning for dark themes keeps breaking light themes and the reverse.
repro: Profile 'ready' at 160x45. Create a response-recovery state (proxy 500, then 'Send without capture'). Ctrl+P → 'Theme: Switch to Textual Light'. Read the composer's 'Send blocked…' reason and the recovery card's 'Retry anyway may send a duplicate…' line. Run sgr.py runs on those rows.
recommendation: Split each status role into a hue token and a text token. Add $ds-status-ready-fg, running-fg, warning-fg, info-fg, approval-fg and paused-fg, bound to Textual's $text-success, $text-primary, $text-warning and $text-accent, exactly as task-31264 did for error, placeholder and disabled. Then replace every `color: $ds-status-*` in _console*.tcss (about 40 rules) with the text token, and keep the raw tokens only for `border:` and `background: … N%`. Add a CI theme-matrix contrast test that renders the Console's status strip, composer reason, recovery card and rail markers in textual-dark, textual-light, paper_light, solarized_light and high_contrast_yellow_black, and asserts ≥4.5:1.
fix_direction: Add a text token for each role (ready, running, warning, info, paused, approval, authority-*), each bound to $text-success, $text-primary, $text-warning or $text-accent. These are already AA-pinned in every theme. Use them in every color: rule, and keep the raw hues for borders and tints. Add a lint test that no color: rule consumes a raw status or authority token. Handle the dim 'Failed' label and the markdown heading colours as separate fixes.

title: Extends G4-52: ASCII mode has two separate substitution tables, so one state gets different ASCII in the tab and the rail, and finished vs failed differ only by case
statement: With appearance.ascii_glyphs on, tabs resolve through glyph_fallback.ASCII_GLYPH_FALLBACKS, but rail rows resolve through a different table, conversation_attention.ATTENTION_PRESENTATIONS. The same approval state therefore shows as '[!]' on the tab and '[approve]' on the rail row. A background run that finished shows '[x]' on its tab and '[ready]' on its rail row. Failed is '[X]' on the tab and '[failed]' on the rail. The tab's finished marker '[x]' differs from failed '[X]' only by letter case. It also sits beside the tab's close button, which ASCII mode renders as a bare 'x': '[x] Say hi in two wor x'.
expected: One ASCII vocabulary, shared by tab, rail row, rail section and legend. Tokens are distinct by shape and word, not by case, and never collide with the close control.
why: ASCII mode is meant for users whose fonts can't show the Unicode markers. For them, the markers are the only run-state signal. A done/failed pair that differs only in case, next to a close 'x', invites misreading a failure as success, and closing tabs by mistake.
repro: Settings > Appearance > ASCII glyphs: Enabled, then s to save and relaunch. In one tab send 'Say hi in two words.' and immediately click another tab. Wait about 20 s and read the tab strip and the rail's Chats rows.
recommendation: Collapse both tables into one glyph registry. Each state gets its Unicode glyph, its ASCII token, its label and its legend text in one record, and tabs, rail rows, section headers and F1 all read from it. Pick case-insensitively distinct ASCII tokens (for example [ok] / [fail] / [appr] / [run]), and render the close control as '[close]' or a Unicode-safe fallback, never a bare 'x' next to a bracketed 'x'.

title: ASCII glyph mode is only partly applied: status and composer toggles, fold hints and transcript disclosures stay Unicode, F1's legend never changes, and rail labels truncate titles
statement: After saving ASCII mode and relaunching, 'Composer v' switched to ASCII, but the status strip toggle one row above still reads 'Status ▾'. The rail fold hint still reads '▼ Agent · Details' / '▼ more sections — scroll', transcript tool rows still read '▸ Error', and the approval card's dropdown shows '▼'. F1's legend still says 'Status markers: ● running · ◆ needs approval · ✓ finished · ✗ failed · ◈ …' and 'parks with a ◆ badge', although none of those glyphs appear on screen in ASCII mode. In Unicode mode the rail uses ✋, which isn't in the legend either. The rail's ASCII labels are 6–10 cells wide ('[approve]', '[running]', '[chat]', '[icon]'), which cuts titles to about 12 characters ('Reply with e…', 'Say hi in tw…'). '[chat]' and '[icon]' name the row-menu button but say nothing about what it does.
expected: Every glyph literal in the Console resolves through the ASCII mapping. The F1 legend is generated from the active mapping. ASCII labels fit a fixed narrow budget so titles survive.
why: A narrow-font user who enables ASCII mode still gets missing or tofu glyphs in the status strip and transcript. F1 then explains glyphs they cannot see, which breaks recognition over recall at the one place meant to decode the markers.
repro: Enable and save ASCII glyphs, relaunch, open a conversation that has a failed tool row, and press F1.
recommendation: Add a test that scans Console widget modules for non-ASCII glyph literals that don't go through resolve_glyph or resolve_glyph_text. Build CONSOLE_FLEET_MARKER_LEGEND from the same registry proposed in GAP3-05, in the active mode, and include ✋. Cap ASCII rail markers at 3–4 cells, for example [A] with a hover or F1 explanation, or move them before the title.
