title: Extends G4-60: the empty area above short transcripts is dim text on the terminal's own background, a dark slab inside light themes
statement: New fact: a per-row capture of a two-message chat in textual-light shows the spacer rows above the first message emitted as ESC[2m ESC[49m, meaning dim text on the terminal's default background. Every other transcript cell is #d0d0d0. On a dark terminal, a light theme therefore shows a 20-row dark block above the conversation. On a light terminal, a dark theme shows a light block. In the dark theme on a dark terminal the defect is almost invisible, which is why it was scored lower before.
expected: The transcript scroll region paints its whole height with the transcript surface token.
why: In a light theme, the largest region of a new or short chat looks broken. It also moves where the conversation seems to start.
repro: Theme textual-light. Open a chat with one exchange. Run: tmux capture-pane -e -p -S 19 -E 19 and look for \x1b[49m inside the transcript column.
recommendation: Give the transcript's spacer or top-padding widget an explicit `background: $ds-surface…` and drop the `dim` style. Add an SGR assertion that no cell inside the Console layout uses default background (49) in any theme.

title: Radio selection in the Trace export and Trace Privacy dialogs is carried by dot colour alone, and the highlighted row differs from the selected one
statement: Every option renders as '▐●▌'. Selected: dot #8ad4a1 on #242f38 (7.81:1). Unselected: #000f18 on #242f38 (1.42:1). The difference is colour and luminance only. In Trace export the highlighted, underlined row is 'Safe summary' (bg #153854), while the selected profile is 'Redacted diagnostic'. The Library access modal uses distinct glyphs (●/○), and within it the two groups use different frames: a boxed RadioSet versus a tall-input style.
expected: Selected and unselected differ by glyph (● vs ○, or [x] vs [ ]), not colour alone. The cursor highlight and the selection are visually distinct. There is one radio style across Console modals.
why: Users with colour-vision deficiency, or in low-contrast themes, cannot tell which export profile or capture scope is active. The cursor-versus-selection mismatch invites exporting the wrong profile.
repro: Trace (y) → w; Inspector → Capture settings…; measure with sgr runs.
recommendation: Add an app-stylesheet rule giving RadioButton distinct on and off glyphs, plus a ≥3:1 unselected indicator. Keep the cursor highlight as a subtle background, not underline plus fill. Use one radio frame style.

title: Speak replies: consent names an unconfigured provider, the failure points to a nonexistent 'STTS Settings', recovery grows the header, and Paused is tooltip-only
statement:
Reproduced live on origin/dev @ 64579cce2c (ready profile: Anthropic key only, OPENAI_API_KEY unset).

- **Consent without a readiness check.** Turning on Speak replies shows a consent modal: 'Provider: OpenAI / Destination: https://api.openai.com / Provider charges may apply.' No readiness check runs first. The modal comes back on a new tab even after the app has already logged OpenAI TTS as configuration_invalid.
- **Three stacked toasts.** After Enable, the next reply shows 'Failed 🔊'. About 3 s later three toasts stack:
  - 'A Console turn completed while hidden…' (false; that is G3-16).
  - 'Automatic speech paused. Use Retry speech for this reply or Resume auto-speak for future replies.'
  - 'TTS failed: TTS is not configured; open STTS Settings'.
- **'STTS Settings' does not exist.** Settings calls the category 'Speech & TTS' and Lab calls the mode 'Speech'. The User Guide itself says 'Settings ▸ Speech & TTS'. The toast copy is plain text, not an action.
- **Recovery row shifts the layout.** A third header row, 'Retry speech  Resume auto-speak', appears and pushes everything below it down one row.
- **Retry repeats the failure.** Pressing it immediately shows 'Retry speech failed. Automatic speech remains paused.' plus the same STTS toast.
- **Paused looks the same as on.** The paused switch has the same colours as enabled-and-not-paused (fg #000f18 on bg #4ebf71, reverse). The only sign of the pause is the hover tooltip 'Automatic speech is paused after a failure.'
- **The Failed badge disappears after navigation.** The recovery row stays after going to Library and back, but the reply's 'Failed 🔊' badge is gone. The header's 'Retry speech for this reply' then points at a reply the transcript no longer marks.

Refinements to the finding:
- The extra header row was a deliberate, documented choice (TASK-21201 notes; User Guide: 'two buttons appear'). It is a design problem, not a regression.
- The failed message already has an icon-only 🔊 speak/retry control next to 'Failed'. A per-message retry exists, just unlabelled.
- The row staying after navigation follows from the paused state being persisted. It is not a defect by itself. The defect is that the badge it refers to is lost.
expected: Consent checks readiness first ('OpenAI TTS isn't set up — Set up / Cancel'). The failure names the real destination with a direct action ('Open Settings ▸ Speech & TTS'). Paused is shown as text on the control, and Retry/Resume sit next to the failed message.
why: The user is shown charge-sounding consent for a provider they never configured, then hits a dead-end recovery path. This violates the honest-unavailable-state and specific-next-action contract.
repro: ready (Anthropic only): toggle Speak replies ▸ Enable ▸ send any message.
recommendation: Gate consent on TTS readiness and show 'Not set up' with a Set up action. Replace every 'STTS Settings' string with the real destination and make it actionable. Render Paused as a third, text-labelled switch state. Move Retry/Resume into the failed turn's badge row instead of growing the header.
fix_direction:
1. Gate consent on TTS readiness. Before opening AutoSpeakConsentModal, read the effective provider's catalog health. If it is not_configured or configuration_invalid, show a 'Not set up' state with an 'Open Settings ▸ Speech & TTS' action instead of charge-sounding consent.
2. Replace every user-facing 'STTS Settings' string (tts_events.py, stts_events.py, speech_catalog_mixin.py) with 'Settings ▸ Speech & TTS'. Make the error toast or recovery offer that as a direct action.
3. When the failure is configuration_invalid or not_configured, hide or disable Retry, or relabel it 'Set up speech'.
4. Show Paused as a visible third switch state or a text label next to Speak replies.
5. Consider moving Retry/Resume into the failed turn's speech badge row (the 🔊 is already there; give it a label). Keep the Failed badge across navigation while the session is paused.
6. The stacked false 'completed while hidden' toast belongs to G3-16.
verdicts: live: CONFIRMED · code: CONFIRMED · skeptic: PARTIAL

title: Per-message Speak shows a success toast alongside the failure, and stamps 'Failed 🔊' on a good reply
statement: With no TTS configured, clicking 🔊 on a complete reply raised two toasts at once: 'Speaking message.' (normal) and 'TTS failed: TTS is not configured; open STTS Settings' (error). The reply header then shows 'Failed 🔊' in the same slot and grey used for response status, so it reads as though the answer failed. Speak is offered, and not disabled, while TTS is unconfigured. This is separate from G3-08, which covers the header 'Speak replies' switch.
expected: Speak is disabled, or labelled 'Speak (set up voice…)', when no TTS backend is ready. Only the real outcome is toasted. A speech failure is shown as 'Speech unavailable' tied to the 🔊 control, not as a message status.
why: The feedback is contradictory, and it makes a correct answer look failed.
repro: Profile without TTS → select any assistant reply → click 🔊.
recommendation: Check TTS readiness before dispatch. Report only the terminal outcome. Move the speech state into the action row ('🔊 unavailable — set up voice') instead of the message status slot.
evidence: gap5 log lines 596-598 (TTS generation failed, then 'TTS complete for message …')

title: Image card: 'View' actually hides the image, the full-size viewer is not offered, and the metadata is misleading
statement: The generated-image card shows the image plus 'Style Custom · Source together · Seed random · Prompt …' and 'View  Save'. Clicking 'View' on the visible image blanked the image area, leaving only a green strip. A second press collapsed the card to '[image] … 🖼 image/png · 3 KB' under an 'Image Generation' box. The label stays 'View' in both states. ConsoleImageViewerModal exists, but Console only opens it for the character avatar, so generated images have no full-size or zoom view. 'Style Custom' appears when the modal's Style was 'None'. 'Source together' is a raw backend id, and 'Seed random' hides the seed actually used, so the image cannot be reproduced. The action legend names 'Save Image', but the card says 'Save'.
expected: 'Hide image' and 'Show image' toggle labels, plus an 'Open' action for the full-size viewer. Metadata shows 'Style: none', the backend's display name and the concrete seed.
why: The label and the action are inverted, and a generated image cannot be inspected at full size.
repro: Generate an image → click View twice → compare with the rail avatar click, which opens the viewer.
recommendation: Use state-dependent toggle labels and add an 'Open' action that pushes ConsoleImageViewerModal with the variant. Record and display the resolved seed. Show 'Style: none'. Map backend ids to display names.

title: The approval card preselects 'approve once' for risk-floored tools, and auto-denies after 120 s with no way to extend
statement: _DEFAULT_DECISION = 'approve_once' for every row except raw shell (chat_approval_card.py:99, 155-162). That includes rows flagged 'High risk: this tool changes local data and always asks first.' (197-206), so pressing Submit approves them. The card counts down 'Auto-denies in M:SS' from 120 s (270-286) with no extend control. Found by code inspection; not exercised live because tools are gated off in the review profile.
expected: Risk-tagged rows have no preselected decision, or Deny preselected (as raw shell already does). The countdown offers 'Extend'.
why: Submit is the obvious button, and approving a data-mutating tool should never be the default. Auto-deny penalises users who read the arguments carefully.
repro: Code inspection; enable a risk-tagged tool and trigger a call to see it live.
recommendation: Extend the raw-shell default-deny rule to every risk_floored/definition-changed row, and add 'Need more time (+2 min)'.

title: Identity and agent nouns drift: Assistant/Character/Persona, actor, Buddy, agent/sub-agent/delegated agent, run/turn
statement: The identity chip changes its key word with state ('Character: X', 'Persona: X', 'Assistant: General'), and its Enter action is 'Choose character'. A toast says 'This actor has no reaction pack.'. The composer menu has 'Buddy…', which its tooltip doesn't mention. Library access titles an axis 'Agent Library access' but explains it as 'whether the assistant may use…', while the chip says 'Agent blocked'. The Close-tab dialog lists 'Live agent turns' and Leave/Quit lists 'Live agent runs' for the same count. 'Cancel all agents' has the tooltip 'Stop every running sub-agent'. 'Delegated agents' and 'sub-agent' are used interchangeably.
expected: A glossary: 'assistant' is the generic speaker, with Character/Persona as its source value ('Assistant: Persona · X'); 'agent run' is one execution; 'sub-agent' is a delegated child. Each term is used identically everywhere.
why: PRODUCT.md warns against collapsing Personas, agents and other concepts, and the copy blurs them in both directions.
repro: Compare the Close-tab and Quit dialogs; compare the Library chip with the Library access modal.
recommendation: Add a Console glossary to DESIGN.md (assistant, character, persona, Buddy, agent run, sub-agent, turn). Keep the chip key stable as 'Assistant:', use 'runs' in both dialogs, and rename the button 'Cancel all sub-agents'.

title: The full run log for a stopped run is one empty 'record 000001 [model]' page titled with a raw UUID
statement: 'View full log' after the stopped todo run opened 'Full run log — c4e95f21-7635-42fe-b3ab-542519b0ae87'. It had a single row 'record 000001 [model]', an empty body filling the modal, and 'Page 1 · End of log'. There was no mention of the three proposed calls, the pending approval or the stop.
expected: The log names the conversation and time and lists proposed calls, decisions and the stop reason. If the stored log is empty, it says so and points to Trace.
why: The guide calls this the 'complete, stored record', yet it answers none of 'what did the agent do and why did it stop'.
repro: Stop a run while awaiting approval ▸ left-rail Agent section ▸ 'View full log'.
recommendation: Title the log with the conversation name and start time, with the id in the subtitle. Include decision and stop records, and add an 'Open in Trace' action.

title: At the parallel-run cap, a send from another tab is refused with no option to wait in line, and 'interrupt it' has no cross-tab control
statement: Code-cited; I did not capture it live because Alt+digit through tmux typed characters instead of switching tabs. With max_parallel_runs (default 3) busy sessions, a send from any other tab returns the toast 'N agents already running (<titles>). Wait for one to finish or interrupt it.' The dispatch is refused: there is no 'queue until a slot frees', and interrupting means visiting each tab and using its collapsed-composer Stop (G1-01). The tip 'Each tab runs its own agent — up to 3 in parallel' is shown in every tab.
expected: A refused fourth run offers 'Start when a slot frees' (auto-queue) and a direct 'Stop <title>' choice.
why: The cap is advertised by the tip, so users will hit it. A toast that tells them to go and do something elsewhere is the weakest recovery available.
repro: Start three slow runs in three tabs, then send in a fourth tab.
recommendation: Admit the send into that tab's queue in a 'waiting for a free slot' state (with the same shelf UI), and show inline actions 'Stop <oldest run>' and 'Raise limit…' (linking Settings ▸ Console Behavior).

title: Collapsing 'Status ▾' or 'Composer ▾' frees no rows, hides state and Send, and the two use different disclosure grammar
statement: Collapsing 'Status ▾' leaves a full row reading 'Status ▴ Status hidden' (console_status_chips.py:437-447,530-546). Collapsing 'Composer ▾' leaves a full row reading 'Expand ▴  Composer hidden' (console_composer_bar.py:3152,6237-6245,6529). Neither returns any vertical space, and both hide state (the composer collapse also hides Send and Dictate). Status keeps its noun while Composer switches to the verb 'Expand', and the glyph grammar differs from the rails (▸ collapsed / ▾ open) and rail handles (◂/▸). After collapsing the composer by mouse, the footer still advertised 'Enter send / queue', because the COMPOSER_COLLAPSED variant ('Esc show composer', chat_screen.py:1243-1246) was not applied (see G1-17).
expected: Collapsing reclaims space, e.g. merging both collapsed controls into one shared row, folding the strip into the header, or moving the indicator into the footer. Collapsers are dropped where they cannot save space (keep them only for a multi-line composer). One disclosure convention ('<Name> ▸' collapsed, '<Name> ▾' expanded) is used everywhere, and the footer re-registers on toggle.
why: Users collapse chrome to gain density. When nothing is gained, the controls are noise and a way to accidentally hide the input and status, and the stale hint is inaccurate.
repro: At 120x40, click 'Status ▾', then 'Status ▴', then 'Composer ▾'. Compare row counts and read the footer.
recommendation: When collapsed, render Status as a 1-cell handle inside the composer row, or render both collapsed controls on one shared row. Otherwise drop the collapsers at one-row heights. Standardise on ▸/▾ with the region noun. Call _register_console_footer_shortcuts from the composer collapse and expand handlers.

title: Queue shelf jargon and truncation ('Draining', 'Mana'), plus a 'Queue 1' rail entry that looks like a chat
statement: Queuing during a run works and shows 'Queue 1/10 · Draining · Next: "Name one star."' with the buttons 'Mana' (truncated 'Manage') and 'Pause' at 120 cols. The tab label gains a 'Q1 ●' prefix, and the Chats rail shows 'Queue 1' as if it were a conversation.
expected: '1 queued · sends after this reply · Next: …' with [Manage] [Pause] fully visible, and the queue count as a badge on the conversation rather than a separate rail row.
why: The queue is a good feature, but jargon and truncation make its state and controls harder to read.
repro: Ready 120x40, proxy slow. Send, type another prompt, and press Enter.
recommendation: Rename 'Draining' to 'sending in order', reserve width for the shelf buttons (the same fixed-width clipping as 'Rest' in G1-13), and render the queue count as a badge on the existing conversation row.

title: The newline key (Ctrl+J) is undiscoverable at the point of need
statement: The footer says 'Enter send / queue' and the placeholder 'Ask, command, or paste task...'; neither mentions newline. Ctrl+J works (verified), and Shift+Enter works only where the terminal delivers it, but both are listed only in the F1 help groups (chat_screen.py:1295).
expected: A contextual hint ('Ctrl+J newline') in the placeholder, or in the footer while the composer is focused.
why: Users write multi-line prompts by pasting from elsewhere, or send prematurely.
repro: Ready 235x52: look at the composer and footer, then press Ctrl+J.
recommendation: While the composer is focused, change the footer hint to 'Enter send · Ctrl+J newline', replacing 'Y trace', which does not apply there (see G1-17).

title: The idle composer permanently says 'Send disabled: type a message', still says 'Send' while the button reads 'Queue', and there are two different empty states
statement: At rest, about 30 cells of the composer row show 'Send disabled: type a message' (console_display_state.py:307-308), a disabled-state message for the normal empty state. During a run the same text shows while the button reads 'Queue' (J7 noted the same contradiction beside an enabled-looking Queue; see G1-01). The empty transcript says 'Ready — type a message to begin.' on first launch but 'No messages yet.' in new tabs.
expected: No reason text when the only 'reason' is an empty draft, since the placeholder already says what to do. During a run: 'Enter queues after this run'. One empty-state sentence.
why: Permanent 'disabled' copy dilutes the reason strip, so a real blocker in the same slot is easier to overlook.
repro: Launch; open a new tab; start a run.
recommendation: Return '' for the empty-draft case, add a run-aware queue hint, and unify the empty-state copy.

title: No slash commands for grounding actions (attach, Library search, scope, context), and a non-matching '/lib' makes the popup vanish silently
statement: The '/' popup lists /prompt, /system, /skills, /fewer-permission-prompts, /prefill, /generate-image, /generate-video and /stream-video, but nothing for attach, Library search, retrieval scope or the next-send preview. Typing '/lib' makes the popup vanish with no 'no matching command' message.
expected: /attach, /library <query> (stage evidence), /scope and /context (open the next-send preview), plus an empty-match row ('No command matches /lib — try /library').
why: The persona's most frequent grounding actions need mouse trips to chips and menus, contrary to 'keyboard-first' and 'essential actions discoverable'.
repro: In the composer, type '/' then 'lib'.
recommendation: Add the grounding commands to console_command_suggestions and show an explicit no-match row (with close-match suggestions; see G1-36).

title: Extends G4-41: the composer placeholder uses a fixed ANSI 'bright_black', so it misses the theme-aware placeholder token (1.94:1 in the high-contrast theme)
statement: The focused composer placeholder renders as fixed #625e4c on every dark theme: 2.56:1 on textual-dark (G4-41) and 1.94:1 on high_contrast_yellow_black, the theme a low-vision user is most likely to pick. On light themes it is #777777 (3.14–3.65:1). Every other Input uses $ds-text-placeholder, which task-31264 made $text-muted for this reason. The composer is the one field left behind.
expected: The composer placeholder uses $ds-text-placeholder, like other fields, and so follows the theme.
why: The main input of the main surface is the least readable field in the high-contrast theme.
repro: Ctrl+P → 'Theme: Switch to High Contrast Yellow Black'. Focus the empty composer and measure row 43.
recommendation: Resolve the placeholder style from the component's CSS (for example a `.composer--placeholder` component class that uses $ds-text-placeholder) instead of a Rich colour name. Do the same for GHOST_TEXT_STYLE and PASTE_TOKEN_STYLE.

title: First-arrival chrome and the Console purpose line use internal jargon, and the purpose line differs across three surfaces
statement: Five-second test on first arrival: the header reads 'Console — Chat, source handoffs, live runs, and control actions.' (console_workbench_state.py:138). The action row offers 'Context rail'. The status strip leads with 'Library · Auto off · Agent blocked' (G4-18). The left rail's first item is 'Terminal', a button in success green (#4ebf71; left_rail.py:2061-2066) that looks like a status. The tab strip shows a bare 'Temporary'. The composer menu offers 'Impersonate' and 'Buddy…' with no description. The purpose line also differs by surface: header '— Chat, source handoffs, live runs, and control actions.'; chat_screen.py:16308 'Agent workbench for chat, source handoffs, live runs, and control actions.'; palette 'Open Console for live agent work, approvals, tools, and RAG' (app_command_providers.py:279). Separately, DESIGN.md says the composer grows 'to four with the draft', while the code has MAX_DRAFT_ROWS = 8 (console_composer_bar.py:469) and the docs say eight.
expected: One plain-language purpose line reused everywhere that tells a first-timer what to do (e.g. 'Chat with your model; attach Library sources; watch runs and approvals'). Actions styled as actions, with green reserved for ready or success. One-line descriptions on unfamiliar menu items. DESIGN.md matches the code.
why: The first screen should make the first action obvious. Instead it front-loads unexplained product vocabulary and a scary 'blocked', and reviewers don't know whether DESIGN.md or the code is the contract.
repro: Any ready or post-setup arrival at 235x52 or 160x45; open the composer Menu; read the cited lines.
recommendation: Define one CONSOLE_PURPOSE constant in plain words and reuse it in the header, screen and palette. Move 'Terminal' into the rail body as an ordinary action row (see G4-56 for colour). Add one-line descriptions to composer-menu items. Rename 'Context rail' per G4-16. Update DESIGN.md to 8 rows.
evidence: DESIGN.md (Dense-form control convention: 'growing to four with the draft') vs tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_composer_bar.py:469

title: Mixed casing, ellipsis and spelling conventions
statement: Title Case outliers among mostly sentence-case labels: 'Edit Message' / 'Edit Thinking' modal titles next to 'Edit system prompt'; 'Generate Image' and 'Generate Caption' next to 'Attach file' in the same menu; 'Save Image' next to 'Save copy'; 'Show Files' (tray) next to 'Show files' (menu); 'Undo All', 'Ask in Side Chat', 'More Details', 'Improve My Prompt'; the 'System Prompt: off' chip next to 'System prompt'. The message action 'keep' is lowercase. Ellipsis: '...' in 'Save as...' (action and modal title), 'Preparing...', 'Starting...' and 'Cancelling...' versus '…' in 'Stopping…', 'Forking…' and 'Undoing…'. The 'opens a dialog' ellipsis is uneven: 'Rename…', 'Buddy…' and 'Reaction…' have it, while 'Settings', 'Configure', 'Search Library', 'Generate Image', 'Attach file' and 'Terminal' open surfaces without it. Spelling mixes British and US: 'Favourite' and 'Icon and colour…' open a picker whose placeholder says 'custom color'.
expected: Sentence case, '…' (U+2026) everywhere, '…' reserved for 'opens a surface that needs more input', and one spelling locale.
why: Each is small, but together they are the most visible sign of the 'still WIP' feeling the owner described.
repro: Open Menu, a message's actions, and the row menu.
recommendation: Add a copy lint in Tests/Architecture over Console Button/Static/label literals that flags Title Case after the first word (allow-list proper nouns such as Library, Console, Chatbook, MCP), three-dot '...', and spellings outside the chosen locale.

title: 'Favourite' in the menu confirms as 'Starred', and the ASCII star collides with the row-menu affordance
statement: The conversation menu offers 'Favourite' / 'Remove favourite'. Choosing it runs _toggle_console_conversation_star, which toasts 'Starred "x".' / 'Unstarred "x".', shows ★, and is bound as 's Star/Unstar' in the workspace tree. In ASCII-glyph mode a starred row is prefixed '* ', and the conversation row-menu affordance in the tree is also ' *'.
expected: One verb and noun pair (star/starred, or favourite) and a distinct ASCII fallback.
why: The confirmation doesn't echo the action the user took, and in ASCII mode one asterisk means both 'starred' and 'row menu'.
repro: Open a row's 💬 menu → Favourite → read the toast.
recommendation: Use 'Star' / 'Unstar' in the menu to match the ★ glyph, the key and the toast. Change the ASCII star to '+' or '[*]', or the row-menu affordance to '[...]'.

title: Archive and restore friction is inverted: the archive receipt defaults to Undo, restore needs a red confirmation, and Archive looks enabled on unsaved chats
statement: Archiving happens instantly (good), with a receipt whose default focus is 'Undo' (bg #183a54, underline), so a reflexive Enter reverses the archive. Restoring from Library needs a 'Restore conversation?' confirmation, and its confirm button 'Restore & resume' uses error red (#b93c5b, 4.47:1). 'Archive this chat' looks enabled on an unsaved blank chat but then only toasts 'Send and save this conversation before archiving it.'
expected: The receipt's default focus is 'Done'. Restore needs no confirmation, or uses a neutral/primary style. When archive is unavailable, it is disabled with the reason shown inline.
why: Red trains users to fear a safe action. The Undo default risks reversing the action just taken, and an enabled button that refuses breaks the 'inert actions carry why' rule.
repro: Archive a chat and note the focused button; Archived chats → Restore and resume; on a new blank tab click Archive this chat.
recommendation: Focus 'Done' in the archive receipt. Drop the restore confirmation or style it as primary. Disable 'Archive this chat' with a '— send first' annotation when the chat is unsaved.

title: Toasts cover the header's status and switches, far from the action that raised them
statement: 'Copied message to clipboard.' (after c or Copy in the transcript) and 'No approval is pending.' (Alt+A) appear top-right over 'Speak replies / Hands-free / Ready' for several seconds, about 40 rows from the transcript or composer where the action happened. The ToastRack is docked top/right (chat_screen.py:1900-1907).
expected: Feedback appears next to its source (an inline 'Copied' on the action row, or near the composer) or in a consistent bottom status line, without covering state chips.
why: Low-vision users zoomed in on the transcript or composer miss top-right toasts, and the toasts hide the readiness status while they show.
repro: Select a message, press c, watch the top-right; press Alt+A with nothing pending.
recommendation: Dock the Console ToastRack bottom-right above the composer, or echo short confirmations inline on the triggering row. Persistence is covered in G4-33.

title: Disabled and unavailable reasons use about seven grammars, and message-action reasons appear only in tooltips
statement: Forms seen: 'Send disabled: type a message' (console_display_state.py:308); 'Discard — none selected' (console_agent_progress_modal.py:79); 'X unavailable — reason' (Prompts, Environment, Inspector; console_prompts_modal.py:680,715,744); 'Unavailable: choose a model first.' (Settings; console_settings_modal.py:3467-3469); 'Undo All is unavailable: …' (chat_screen.py:1052); '[unavailable: reason]' (/help; console_help.py:34); 'Label (unavailable) reason' (Save as; console_save_as_modal.py:102). Disabled message actions put their reason only in button.tooltip, which appears on mouse hover and never for keyboard users (console_transcript.py:8363-8366, 8309-8319). The one exception is Fork, whose reason is appended to the Guide line.
expected: DESIGN.md's rule applied in one form ('Action — reason' in the label or an adjacent line), visible without hover.
why: PRODUCT.md is keyboard-first, and a tooltip-only reason on a disabled transcript action is invisible to that user.
repro: Select a message whose Regenerate or Edit is disabled and Tab to it: no reason is shown.
recommendation: Add a disabled_label(action, reason) helper that returns 'Action — reason' and use it everywhere. For glyph-only transcript actions, extend Fork's Guide-line pattern to every disabled primary action.

title: Key notation and hint grammar differ on every surface (case, separators, colons, Esc vs Escape), and F1 lists the switcher-local F2 as a global key
statement:
At least eight hint grammars were seen.
- The nav bar uses '⌃1'…'⌃0' (NAV_HOTKEY_GLYPH, main_navigation.py:44-48), while the footer, F1 and docs use 'Ctrl+K'.
- The footer writes 'Y trace' in uppercase, which reads as Shift+Y, for the lowercase 'y' binding. F1 and the other hints use lowercase ('j / k', 'c').
- 'Esc' and 'Escape' both appear. The Trace footer uses lowercase 'enter'.
- App footer: 'F1 help | Enter send / queue', with a global cluster ' · ' and bare keys 'Ctrl+P · Ctrl+Q'.
- Rail-focus prefix: 'Esc composer · F6 panes', next to a duplicate 'F6 next pane'.
- Inspector: 'n/p Sections', capitalised with no spaces, while F1 uses 'n / p' (chat_screen.py:1197,1319,5199,5205).
- Transcript guide: 'Guide: j/k select · c Copy · 🔊 Speak'.
- Trace: 'n/p match · j/k err · u/y tool' (trajectory_screen.py:232-256).
- Switcher: 'Enter:switch F2: rename · ↑↓:move · Shift+F3:mode · Esc:close', with mixed spacing and missing separators inside one line (console_session_switcher_modal.py:252-254,418,2090-2100).
- Modals: 'Waiting for results · Esc:close', 'Opening… · Esc: cancel', 'Esc / click to close' (console_image_viewer_modal.py:93), 'Enter runs the search. Esc or a click outside closes without changes.' (console_rag_settings_modal.py:336-338), 'Profile: X · ↑/↓ · Enter apply', 'Esc closes without changing your draft.' (trace_export_dialog.py:236).
- Setup wizard: 'Enter / Ctrl+N next · Ctrl+B back · Esc skip setup'.
- F1 uses 'F6: next pane' and 'Escape: …'. Its 'Global & modals' group lists 'F2: rename a session (in the Ctrl+K switcher)', while the nav shows 'F2 Lab', and pressing F2 at the Console navigates away.
- Palette and slash descriptions put keys in parentheses ('(Ctrl+K)', '(Alt+M)').
expected: One KeyHint renderer and one notation: 'Ctrl+K', 'Esc', 'Enter', lowercase single-letter keys (in backticks or a key-cap style), '<key> <verb>', ' · ' within a group and ' | ' between groups, no duplicates. Modal-local keys are listed under that modal, not under Global.
why: Notation is how keys are recognised. Mixed forms make users re-parse every surface, duplicated or mis-cased hints ('F6' twice, 'Y') look like errors, and a local key listed as global creates avoidable mode errors.
repro: Compare nav row 2 with the footer. Press Ctrl+K and read the hint line. Open the Inspector and Trace footers. Press F1 and read 'Global & modals'. Launch a fresh profile at 100x30 and read the wizard footer.
recommendation: Extract shared format_key() and format_hints() helpers (e.g. Widgets/key_hints.py), and route AppFooterStatus, the transcript guide, Trace, the switchers, modal hint rows, the wizard and F1 through them. Add a lint test for key casing and the separator set. Move F2 and Shift+F3 into a 'Ctrl+K switcher' F1 group. Use 'Ctrl+1' in the nav when width allows, or teach ⌃ once in F1.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-macbook-dev-Documents-GitHub-tldw-chatbook/c28a6a75-4221-4434-989d-fbf24a73c96b/scratchpad/uxrev/evidence/L4/21-inspector-open.txt line 45 ('Esc composer · F6 panes | n/p Sections | … | F6 next pane')

title: After exiting setup, the nav shows two highlighted tabs (Home with stale focus styling, Console active)
statement: On landing on Console after exiting the wizard at step 2, '⌃1 Home' carries a bold underline on a tinted background (#10314b). At the same time '⌃2 Console' has the active background (#0065be; label 4.76:1, its '⌃2' hint 2.91:1). Two tabs look selected. The reviewer rated confidence as medium.
expected: Only the active tab is highlighted. Keyboard focus on the nav is shown with the focus accent only while the nav actually has focus.
why: 'Where am I?' becomes ambiguous at the moment of first arrival.
repro: Exit setup at step 2 and look at row 2.
recommendation: Clear stale nav focus styling when focus moves into the destination, or move focus into the Console card on arrival (it already focuses the card button).
evidence: evidence/J1/11-after-exit-setup.ansi: sgr runs row 2 (Home bg #10314b bold underline; Console bg #0065be)

title: Nav overflow leaves an invisible, inert gap where a partially fitting item is painted in the background colour
statement: A nav item that only partly fits is still laid out, but painted fg=bg (#121212 on #121212, 1.00:1). Examples: 'F5 Researc' at 160 columns, '⌃8 Workflo' at 100, '⌃7 S' at 80. It leaves a blank gap of 5–10 cells before 'More ▾'. The gap is inert (clicking it did nothing), and the clipped text shows up in copied or plain-text output (main_navigation.py:498).
expected: Items that do not fit entirely are removed, and 'More ▾' sits directly after the last whole item.
why: The dead gap looks like a rendering bug and wastes nav width at exactly the sizes where width is scarce.
repro: Resize to 160, 100 and 80 columns; check sgr.py runs for row 2.
recommendation: Set display:none on nav items that do not fit completely, rather than recolouring them.

title: 'Verified against' stamps have become a 135-line changelog that doesn't certify the page: branch names, contradictory claims, task ids in user prose
statement: console.md carries 12+ stamp paragraphs (lines 757-892, about 15% of the page). They name 'working tree', 'fix/library-notes-…' and 'feat/model-config-…' branches, several are marked 'not re-checked live', and the 2026-08-30 stamp says the rail's default open set is 'Sessions + Conversations' while citing TASK-23199, which retired Sessions. attachments-images-voice.md:266 claims verification although its Mic table is wrong. voice-and-hands-free.md, canvas.md, semantic-trace-capture.md, video.md and buddy-conversation.md have no stamp. The Console pages contain 88 task-id mentions, e.g. the heading '### Routing a created chat onto a specific provider (TASK-32874)' (agent-runs-and-tools.md:2008).
expected: One line per page ('Verified against dev @ <sha>, <date>, live|headless'), updated whenever the page's UI changes. History lives in backlog/docs.
why: A stamp should tell readers whether they can trust the page. These are noise, and some vouch for wrong text.
repro: grep -n 'Verified against' Docs/User_Guide/console.md Docs/User_Guide/console/*.md
recommendation: Collapse the stamps to one per page, move the history to backlog/docs, strip TASK ids from headings and prose, and add a preflight check that each page's stamp commit postdates the last change to the modules it cites.

title: Console guide pages aren't task-oriented: the 2,881-line agents page opens with a Watchlists recipe, 'Common tasks' sits at 84% depth, and the Trace page opens with storage internals
statement: agent-runs-and-tools.md has 2,881 lines and 61 headings. It opens with '## Running the Watchlists workflow from Console', ahead of '## What this page covers', and '## Common tasks' is at line 2405. context-and-rag.md is 1,205 lines and console.md 892. semantic-trace-capture.md opens with 'Provider-only material…', 'durable owner', 'pre-send trace reservation' and 'final semantic values handed to Chatbook's provider adapter', and never says how to open Trace.
expected: Each page opens with its 3-6 most common tasks as numbered steps, then reference material. Long pages are split, and jargon is glossed.
why: People read docs to finish a task. On these pages reference comes first and the steps are buried.
repro: wc -l and grep -n '^## ' on the cited pages.
recommendation: Adopt a page template: purpose → 'Do it' tasks → layout tour → reference table → troubleshooting. Split agent-runs-and-tools.md into 4-5 pages (approvals, fleet, raw CLI/Terminal, tool catalogue). Open the trace page with 'What Trace shows / how to open it / reading one call'.

title: Keyboard accelerators are shown in the palette and slash popup but not in F1 Actions, the control bar, the composer Menu or the action row
statement: The slash popup ('/model … (Alt+M)', '/new … (Ctrl+T)') and the palette ('(Ctrl+K)', '(Alt+W)') teach keys. These do not: the F1 'Actions' list; the control bar (New tab = Ctrl+T); the composer Menu ('Browse Prompt Library…' = /prompt; 'Attach file' = paste/drop, and Alt+V for images); the transcript action-row buttons. The action guide shows keys for Copy/Edit/Fork/Regenerate but not for 'Full output' (o), 'Review' (v) or '</> Variants'.
expected: Every list of actions shows its accelerator in the same position and format as the palette.
why: The most discoverable menus are the ones that don't teach the faster route.
repro: Open Menu and F1, and compare with the palette and the slash popup.
recommendation: Add an optional accelerator field to WorkbenchAction and the composer-menu entries, and render it right-aligned and muted as in the palette, sourced from the same key registry as G3-19.

title: Prior Inspect-rail critique issues are still present on dev: silent Refresh, Tab never reaches the rail, inverted open/close glyphs, and a footer that ignores focus
statement:
Items from .impeccable/critique/2026-09-05 (right_rail) that are still open:

(a) Refresh still gives no feedback. Clicking it changes only the button's press tint for a moment (focus edge 2.19:1 → 1.73:1), with no 'Refreshing…' or 'Updated HH:MM' text.

(b) Tab from the composer never reaches the rail. The order is Composer ▾ → Menu → Dictate → Redirect → (off-screen) → header 'Speak replies'.

(c) The glyph pair is still '◂ Inspect' when closed and '▸ Inspect' when open.

(d) When the rail is focused, the footer shows 'n/p Sections' and also 'Enter send / queue', although Enter on the rail summary does not send.

Fixed since the critique: the false 'No git workspace' on cold start now reads 'Changes aren't tracked for this workspace…', though that copy is truncated (see G2-17).
expected: Refresh acknowledges within 0.1 s and states freshness. Tab order reaches the rail, or F6 is taught at the composer. Open/close signifiers are consistent. Footer hints follow the focused region.
why: These issues were already raised, and they still cost keyboard users orientation and trust in how fresh the data is.
repro: Open Inspect and click Refresh, capturing at 0.3 s and 2 s. Tab six times from the composer. Compare the handle and header glyphs. Focus the rail summary and read the footer.
recommendation:
Apply the critique's own fixes:
1. Refresh shows a transient 'Refreshing…' state, then 'Updated 12:31'.
2. Include the rail in the composer's Tab ring, or have Tab from the last composer control move to the rail.
3. Use one glyph convention, aligned with the rail-grammar work in G2-39.
4. Filter footer hints by the focused region.

title: Environment and Change Review list untracked files as 'A' (added) with '+0 −0'
statement: '?? untracked.txt' (as git and the Terminal report it) appears as 'A untracked.txt +0 −0' in Environment ▸ Changes and under 'Added (1)' in Change Review, although the file has 1 line and nothing is staged.
expected: 'U' or '?' untracked, with the real line count, matching git's vocabulary.
why: Before a commit, users need to know what is staged. 'A' tells them the file is already added.
repro: Create an untracked file in a bound repo and expand Environment ▸ Changes.
recommendation: Keep the collapsed letter for grouping, but render untracked files as 'U' (untracked) in both surfaces and count their lines from the untracked-preview diff.

title: In Environment, '…' means both 'opens another screen' and 'text cut off', and expanding a row shifts the rows below it
statement: In the same section, 'Review in Change Review…' and 'Review & commit… · 2 files' use '…' as the documented 'opens another surface' marker, while 'Changes aren't tracked for…' and 'Remote tldw_server — not…' use it as truncation. Expanding 'Local ▸' pushed 'main ▸' down, so a follow-up click at the old position missed.
expected: Separate glyphs for navigation (for example '→' or '↗') and truncation. Expanding one row doesn't move other click targets without warning, or does so with a focus-preserving scroll.
why: The row-marker convention only works if its glyphs aren't shared with truncation.
repro: Look at Environment in W1, then click 'Local ▸' and then 'main ▸' at their original positions.
recommendation: Change ENV_MARKER_OPENS_SURFACE to a glyph that is never used for ellipsis, and make truncated rows show their full text on focus.

title: F6 pane focus is shown only by a hue change in the border (1.00:1 luminance), and the composer's focus is a single blue cell
statement: F6 recolours the pane frame from #6f7782 to #0178d4. Both are 3.01:1 against the background and 1.00:1 against each other, and the border shape doesn't change. The transcript also highlights its 'Conversation | …' title bar, which works as a cue, but it keeps a sticky bold-underline highlight after mouse clicks, so two panes can look focused at once. The rails have no such title cue. The left rail shows focus only with an underline on 'Context ◂', and the header toggle's focus is a thin box at 2.19:1. The composer's whole focus signal is a 1-column '█' at x=1 plus a blinking caret, with no background change and no bold, although DESIGN.md's dense-form convention promises three concurrent signals: edge weight, background and bold.
expected: One pane-focus treatment that doesn't rely on hue and changes by at least 3:1 (heavier or double border, or a highlighted title row) on every pane, matching the composer. The composer implements DESIGN.md's triple signal. Title highlights clear on blur.
why: Colour-blind and low-vision keyboard users can't tell which pane will receive keys, which makes F6 navigation guesswork and compounds G4-12.
repro: 235x52; press F6 repeatedly; diff consecutive captures with sgr.py.
recommendation: Add a focused-pane class that switches the border style (e.g. round→heavy) and highlights the pane's title row. Give the left rail and Inspect rail a title row they can highlight, as the transcript has. Implement the composer's documented thick $ds-action-focus edge, $ds-focus-bg and bold. Clear title highlights on blur. Verify with a ≥3:1 sgr diff test.
evidence: uxrev/evidence/J6/tab235/004.diff (composer focus vs unfocus: edge + caret only)

title: Tab order doesn't follow visual reading order, and most regions are outside the default Tab cycle
statement: From boot, with focus in the composer, Tab cycles 11 stops: composer input → Composer ▾ → Menu → Dictate → (jump to top-right) Speak replies → Hands-free → (jump to top-left) New tab → Settings → Context rail → Search Library → Help → back to the input. Shift+Tab is the exact reverse. The left rail, tab strip, transcript, status chips and Inspect handle are reachable only with F6 or Alt keys (CONSOLE_TAB_REGIONS pairs the header and control bar with the composer, and the chips with the transcript; chat_screen.py:939-946). Inside the transcript region Tab goes transcript → status chips (below) → tab strip (above). In the Ctrl+K switcher the mode tabs (Active/History/Character chats, visually on top) come last, after Cancel: search → list → Search all chats → Archived → Cancel → Active → History → Character chats. J8 also saw Tab go from the composer's bottom row straight to the header switches, with Send and Dictate not clearly in sequence.
expected: Within each region Tab follows top-to-bottom, left-to-right order: header actions before the composer, the tab strip before transcript content, and switcher modes before the search field (or modes on ←/→).
why: Keyboard users build a mental map from the screen. Jumping bottom → top-right → top-left breaks it, and 40 Tab presses never reach the conversation list or tabs, which hurts discoverability for anyone who hasn't learned F6.
repro: 235x52 boot: Tab ×45, Shift+Tab ×13 with an sgr diff after each; Ctrl+K and Tab ×9.
recommendation: Order each Tab region by layout position (header → composer; tab strip → transcript → status). Put the speech switches last in the header group or move them into the composer's voice cluster. In the switcher put the mode tabs first, or bind ←/→ (and show Shift+F3) for modes. Mention F6 on the empty-transcript line ('F6 moves between panes').

title: No keyboard or palette way to close, rename or archive the current chat
statement: Console binds Ctrl+T (new tab), Ctrl+K (switcher) and hidden Alt+1..9 (chat_screen.py:1925-2020), but nothing to close, rename or archive the current tab. Palette searches for 'close', 'rename' and 'archive' return no such command. Renaming the current tab needs a second mouse click on it, a gesture described only in its tooltip. F2 works only inside Ctrl+K on a focused row.
expected: Ctrl+W (close tab, with the loss dialog), F2 (rename the current chat), and palette entries 'Close tab', 'Rename chat…' and 'Archive chat', each showing its key.
why: PRODUCT.md promises keyboard-first control and essential actions without memorised shortcuts, yet these actions need the mouse.
repro: Ctrl+P → type 'close', 'rename', 'archive'.
recommendation: Add screen bindings and palette commands for close, rename and archive. List Ctrl+W and F2 in the footer and F1 help, and show Alt+1..9 in the tab tooltips.

title: Appearance picker keyboard path: Tab walks the whole emoji catalogue; the default grid is raw catalogue order with duplicate-looking pairs
statement: The picker opens with focus in 'Search icons by name…', which is good. Tab from there moves into the emoji grid one emoji at a time; each Tab highlighted the next emoji (🥇, then 🥈…). Apply is reachable only with Shift+Tab ×3 (Cancel, Clear, Apply). The modal shows no key hint. Enter in the filter only selects the first match. The default grid starts '🥇 🥈 🥉 🅰️ 🅰 🆎 🧮 🪗 🩹 🎟️ 🎟 🚡', then flags and '👽 👾'. That is raw alphabetical catalogue order, with text and emoji variants (🅰️/🅰, ✈️/✈, 🎟️/🎟, ⚗️/⚗) shown as separate, near-identical choices.
expected: The grid is one Tab stop with arrow-key movement. A visible hint reads 'Enter select · Ctrl+S apply · Esc cancel'. The default set is curated: recents plus about 24 work-relevant icons, with variant pairs de-duplicated.
why: PRODUCT.md is keyboard-first. Here Apply is buried behind a reverse-Tab trick, and the first screen of choices is noise.
repro: Open 'Icon and colour…' and press Tab three times. Then press Shift+Tab from the filter.
recommendation: Make the EmojiButtons non-focusable, move the highlight with arrow keys from the filter (as ConsoleStylePickerModal does), bind Ctrl+S or Enter-on-highlight to Apply, and add the hint line. Seed the grid with recents and a small curated set, and fold VS16 variants into one entry.
evidence: tldw_chatbook/Widgets/Console/console_appearance_picker_modal.py:85-95 (default order), :267 (grid can_focus=False but its EmojiButtons are focusable), :334-349 (Enter selects, doesn't apply)

title: The left rail's fold hint misses a section whose label is just under the fold ('▼ Details' while Agent is also hidden)
statement:
At 120x40 the rail showed 'Model ▸', a divider, then '▼ Details'. The Agent section label was also hidden: scrolling the rail revealed 'Agent ▸' above Details.

Cause: _hidden_section_titles tests header.region.y >= bottom (left_rail.py:1767), but the section header has a border-top row (_console.tcss:806-814). When only the divider is visible, the label row is below the fold, yet the header is not counted as hidden.

At other heights the hint worked ('▼ Agent · Details').
expected: The hint lists every section whose label row is not visible.
why: The hint exists to tell users exactly what is below the fold (TASK-23195). An off-by-one that hides one section while naming the next sends them to the wrong place.
repro: Ready mode, one conversation, 120x40. The left-rail bottom reads '▼ Details' while Agent is not visible; wheel-scroll the rail to see Agent.
recommendation: Compare the header's content-region top (region.y + border-top), or its bottom, against the fold: a header is hidden if its label row is at or below the fold. Add a geometry test at the exact height where only the divider fits.

title: The two rails use different header, handle, alignment, chevron and fold-hint patterns
statement:
Headers and handles:
- The open Context rail header is 'Context ◂': label first, right-aligned, plain.
- The open Inspector header is '▸ Inspect': arrow first, underlined, on a tinted band (right_rail.py:120).
- Collapsed handles are 10–12-column, full-height columns with one vertically centred word. The Inspector handle's badge sits at the very bottom, far from its label.

Alignment inside Conversations (console_workspace_context.py:1777-1788):
- 'Archive this chat / Archived chats / Search all chats…' are centred labels in a dark block narrower than the rail.
- 'New conversation' and the chat rows are left-aligned.
- The 'Chats ▾' subgroup is plain weight, but its chevron sits in the same column as the section chevrons, so it reads as a peer section.

Chevrons: ▸/▾ for sections, ▴ for collapsed Status and Composer, ▼ for fold hints and the jump pill, and ◂/▸ for handles and tab overflow.

Fold hints: the Inspector's hint is generic ('▼ more sections — scroll'), while the left rail's names sections.
expected: One rail-header grammar (same arrow side, same band), handles no wider than 3 columns with the badge beside the label, left-aligned action rows, and one disclosure glyph set.
why: When sibling regions use different patterns, users have to relearn each one, and the owner is working towards a unified Console.
repro: At 235x52 with both rails open, then collapse both.
recommendation:
1. Put the arrow on the outer edge for both rails ('◂ Context' / 'Inspect ▸'), with the same band style.
2. Use the existing 3-column vertical handle variant (ConsoleRailHandle vertical=True), with the badge stacked under the label.
3. Left-align all rail action rows.
4. Use ▸/▾ for every disclosure.
5. Port the named-section fold hint to the Inspector.

title: The 'open this row's actions' affordance has five different signifiers and an unadvertised key
statement:
The same affordance is signified five ways:
- '💬' on conversation rows. It reads as 'chat', not 'menu', and status glyphs replace it (conversation_attention.py:87-91).
- ' @' on workspace rows in the tree.
- ' *' or '[chat]' on conversation rows in the ASCII tree (console_workspace_tree.py:29-32, 744-758).
- 'More…' on transcript messages.
- 'More ▸' in the conversation menu and bare 'More' in the workspace menu (console_workspace_actions.py:130).

The key is `m` on tree and conversation rows (chat_screen.py:22716-22733), and Enter then Tab to 'More…' in the transcript. The key is not advertised anywhere except the tree's BINDINGS.
expected: One row-menu signifier (for example '⋯', or '[...]' in ASCII) and one key (m, listed in F1) on every row type.
why: Users must learn four symbols for one affordance, and '💬'/'@' don't read as 'menu', so recognition gives way to recall.
repro: Look at the Chats group (💬), the workspace tree and a selected message (More…).
recommendation: Standardise on '⋯' (ASCII '[...]') for row menus and show status as a separate prefix. Bind `m` on transcript messages too, and list 'm row menu' in F1 and in the rail footer variant.

title: 'Progress: 0 queued' and its modal are supervisor jargon shown to every user
statement:
The left-rail Agent section always shows a 'Progress: 0 queued' button, even on a profile that has never spawned a sub-agent.

It opens 'Queued progress (this session)' with this text above an empty list: 'Inspection does not collect reports or wake an idle supervisor. Restart loses this queue. Discard does not stop children or erase history copies. Queue full? Check progress counts in conversation navigation; other conversations may hold capacity.' (console_agent_progress_modal.py:58).
expected: The button is hidden until there is queued sub-agent progress, and its copy is in task terms ('2 sub-agent reports waiting for the main agent').
why: It adds noise to the section users scan for run status and teaches nothing they can act on.
repro: Expand the left-rail Agent section and click 'Progress: 0 queued'.
recommendation: Show the button only when count > 0, or when a fleet exists. Rewrite the modal intro as one plain sentence with a 'Learn more' link.

title: A blocked chat's rail row puts 'Blocked' on its own line in title style, so it reads as a separate chat
statement: When a chat is blocked, its rail row renders as 'Chat 25 ⛔' followed by a line 'Blocked' at the same indent and style as a chat title. When the chat is active, both lines are in the same blue, reading 'Near-full context test' / 'Blocked', like two chats.
expected: Status should sit on the same line (e.g. a trailing 'blocked' tag), or on an indented, muted second line that is clearly subordinate.
why: It adds a phantom list entry and misleads scanning in an already crowded rail.
repro: Block a send in any chat (e.g. the over-limit paste) and look at the rail Chats list.
recommendation: Render status as a right-aligned muted tag on the title line ('Near-full context…  blocked'), sharing the glyph+word vocabulary with tabs and Inspect (cf. G4-52).

title: Character presence in the left rail: a 14-row avatar squeezes the other sections, the title is cut mid-word, and 'Reaction…' is enabled with no character
statement: At 160x45 the imported card's avatar takes rows 20-33 of the left rail. Model, Agent and Details collapse into one '▼ Model · Agent · Details' row. The section header reads 'Character · Captain Mi ▾' (cut mid-word), and the status chip 'Character: Captain Mirela Voss' pushes 'Sources' off the strip. With no character active, 'Reaction…' is a live button, and pressing it only toasts 'Choose a local Character or Persona before selecting a reaction.'.
expected: A compact avatar (for example 6–8 rows, expandable on click) that keeps the other rail sections reachable. Truncation at word boundaries or with a tooltip. 'Reaction…' disabled with an inline reason until a character or persona is active.
why: The decorative portrait outweighs operational controls in a dense workbench.
repro: Start a new chat with an imported card that has an embedded image; view the left rail at 160x45.
recommendation: Cap the avatar height relative to the rail height, click to enlarge (the viewer modal already exists), and disable 'Reaction…' with an inline reason.

title: The attach file picker defaults to unsorted 'Discovery order', starts in the process CWD, wraps its type filter, and doesn't name hidden files
statement: 'Select File to Attach' opens with 'Sort Discovery order', interleaving folders and files non-alphabetically (Project_Guidelines.md, Packaging, PRODUCT.md, …). The 'All Supported Files' select wraps onto two lines. The picker starts in the process CWD rather than HOME or the last attach folder, although it remembers the last folder afterwards. '1 hidden by filter' doesn't name the hidden files.
expected: Folders first then alphabetical, the filter label on one line, and hidden files listed on demand.
why: It slows finding the right source file, a frequent action.
repro: Composer ▸ Menu ▸ Attach file.
recommendation: Default to 'Name, folders first'. Widen or abbreviate the filter select. Make '1 hidden by filter' clickable to show which files were hidden and why.

title: In light themes the switcher's modal frame blends into the dimmed page (1.02–1.13:1)
statement: The Ctrl+K switcher's tall frame (#ededed) and body (#d0d0d0) sit on the dimmed backdrop (#dcdcdc/#e0e0e0) at 1.10–1.13:1 in textual-light, and at 1.02–1.08:1 in paper_light. The dimmed approval card's text ('{"direct', 'Once', 'This cal') runs right up to the modal's edge with no visible boundary. In dark the same frame is 1.36:1.
expected: A modal boundary at 3:1 or better against the backdrop in both light and dark themes, with the same frame on every modal (see G3-28/G4-58).
why: Without a clear edge, the modal's rows and the dimmed rows behind it read as one region. That slows scanning and makes misclicks outside the modal more likely.
repro: Theme paper_light, with an approval card on screen. Press Ctrl+K.
recommendation: Give the shared modal frame a round border in a token that reaches ≥3:1 against the dimmed backdrop in both light and dark themes, for example $accent, or $foreground at 40%. Check it in the theme-matrix test.

title: Picker row grammar differs: the image-style picker uses 3-row centred buttons (5 of 13 visible), unlike Ctrl+K's one-line rows
statement: 'Console: Insert image style…' lists each style as a 3-row, centred, bordered button ('Realistic Portrait — Portrait (portrait_realistic)'), so only 5 of 13 styles fit at 160x45 before scrolling. Ctrl+K and the rail use left-aligned one-line rows with a highlight bar. The composer Menu uses the tall centred style (G1-35), and the appearance picker uses an emoji grid. The style picker shows no key hints, although it supports Up/Down, Enter and Esc.
expected: One picker-row pattern for all Console pickers: left-aligned, one or two lines, a visible highlight, and a hint row.
why: Centred tall buttons break the left-edge scan, and hide most options behind scrolling in a list of just 13.
repro: Ctrl+P → 'image style' → Enter.
recommendation: Render the rows as a one-line OptionList-style list, with the id shown muted at the right and the preview kept below. Share one picker base with the prompt and character pickers.

title: New Workspace dialog: 'Define project context' is checked by default but fails, persona-memory controls show with Persona 'None', the folder field has no label and Enter does nothing, and the rejection copy is wrong
statement: 'Define project context after creating' is pre-checked. On Create, the log shows 'ValueError: Personal Context is unavailable' and the only feedback is a short toast ('Workspace created, but project context setup is unavailable.'). With Default Persona 'None', 'Persona memory: Read only' and 'Confirm this Persona may write memory' remain visible. The folder input has only a placeholder ('~/path/to/project (optional)'), and Enter in it does not add the folder (you must click 'Add folder'). A folder inside a protected directory is rejected with '…cannot be bound: it is, or contains, the protected path…' when it is actually contained by it.
expected: Unavailable options are hidden or disabled with a reason. Dependent persona controls hide when Persona is None. The field is labelled 'Project folder', Enter adds it, and the rejection says 'is inside'.
why: A default that is guaranteed to fail teaches users to ignore the dialog, and wrong copy misleads the fix.
repro: Open Workspaces ▸ New in this profile, set Persona to None, type a folder path and press Enter, then Create.
recommendation: Disable 'Define project context' with a reason when Personal Context is unavailable. Collapse the persona-memory rows when Persona is None. Label the field, bind Enter to Add folder, and use rule-specific rejection copy.
evidence: evidence/GAP4/app-log-run2.log ('Workspace profile scope preparation failed' / 'Personal Context is unavailable')

title: No hysteresis at rail width thresholds: a one-column drag across 99/100 toggles the 30-column Context rail every time
statement: In the live sequence 101 → 100 → 99 → 100 → 99, the Context rail appeared and disappeared on every step, and the transcript reflowed by 30 columns each time. The resize handler de-duplicates by band only (console_rail_width_band) and has no enter/exit margin. The same applies at 84 (single-pane) and 150 (Inspector).
expected: A small dead band, e.g. collapse below 100 and re-expand only at 104 or more.
why: The target user resizes panes often. Flicker and a full reflow near a breakpoint lose the reading position and look unstable.
repro: tmux resize-window -x 101/100/99/100/99 -y 30 in sequence; read row 12.
recommendation: Store the last applied band and require crossing the threshold by ±3 columns before changing it. Unit-test the band function with enter and exit sequences.

title: At narrow widths the tab strip shows an orphaned ✕ and hides New tab, Temporary and the active tab's ✕
statement: At 100x30 with 4 tabs the strip reads '◂        ✕        Chat 3         ✕        Chat 4        ▸'. A ✕ appears with no label because its tab is scrolled out ('◂' at c32, lone '✕' at c40), and the active tab's ✕ and the New tab/Temporary buttons sit past the ▸.
expected: Whole tabs scroll, so a ✕ never shows without its label, and New tab and the active tab's close stay pinned outside the scroll area.
why: An unlabelled ✕ is ambiguous about which tab it closes, and New tab is an essential action.
repro: Relaunch at 100x30 and press Ctrl+T three times.
recommendation: Snap the scroll offset to tab boundaries. Pin 'New tab' and 'Temporary' outside the scrolling container, or collapse them into a '+' menu at narrow widths.

title: Settings > Appearance mixes a raw checkbox ('Animations ▐X…') with On/Off word toggles in the same motion group
statement: Among Reduce motion 'Disabled', ASCII glyphs 'Enabled/Disabled' and Smooth scrolling 'Enabled', the Animations control is a Checkbox rendered as '▐X…' (truncated) or a bare 'X', with no state word.
expected: DESIGN.md: 'Toggles and switches: always paired with a text-state word'. All four motion toggles use the same control.
why: It makes the one ambiguous control harder to read, in the group where ASCII mode lives, which users open when glyph rendering is already unreliable.
repro: F4 → '/' ascii → Enter. Look at the Motion and scrolling group.
recommendation: Switch Animations to the same Enabled/Disabled word toggle as its neighbours.

title: Tab label prefixes stack ('Q1 ● …') and push out the ellipsis; the queue is named four different ways
statement: Queued tabs render 'Q1 ● Call the todo_cr ✕' and 'Q2 Reply with the sin ✕': the title is cut mid-word with no '…', while unqueued tabs keep 'Call the todo_crea…'. The same queue appears as 'Q1' (tab), 'Queue 1' (a rail row that looks like a chat), 'Queue 1/10 · Draining' (shelf) and 'Queue 2/10 · paused · failed' (modal).
expected: A fixed marker slot and a consistent ellipsis, with one queue term and count format.
why: It is polish, but in a narrow strip the prefix eats the part of the title that identifies the chat.
repro: Queue a prompt behind a running turn, switch tabs, and read the tab label.
recommendation: Reserve a two-cell status slot before the title (the highest-precedence marker only) and move the queue count to a compact suffix. Truncate the title with '…' after adding prefixes, and adopt one queue vocabulary ('2 queued') across the tab, rail, shelf and modal.

title: Tables stretch to full transcript width on wide terminals and wrap mid-token on narrow ones; prose runs about 180 columns wide
statement: At 235 cols a 5-column comparison table spans about 170 cols. The Algorithm column is 44 cells wide, and each value sits 30 or more cells from its neighbour. At 100 cols cells wrap inside tokens ('O(n / log / n)', 'Merge / Sort'), making each row 3 lines. Prose paragraphs run the full 180-column width, beyond DESIGN's 65–75 character guidance for prose-heavy regions. Reviewer confidence: medium.
expected: Table columns are sized to content with a sensible maximum, short tokens are not broken, and prose width is capped on very wide terminals.
why: Comparison tables are harder to scan when values are far apart or split across lines.
repro: Ask for a markdown table and view it at 235 and 100 cols.
recommendation: Render transcript tables with content-fit widths (expand=False, maximum about 100 cols) and no_wrap on cells shorter than about 12 characters. Cap transcript prose at about 100–110 cols on wide terminals.

title: End/G don't jump to the latest message; the 'jump to latest' pill needs Tab plus Enter
statement: After PageUp, the pill '▼ reply ready — jump to latest' appeared. End and G changed nothing (empty capture diff); ConsoleTranscript has no home/end/G bindings (console_transcript.py:2991-3004). The pill is focusable, and Enter or Space activates it, which works but is slower than a standard key. Reviewer confidence: medium.
expected: End/G scroll to the newest content and re-attach follow; Home/g go to the top.
why: Terminal users expect pager keys, and keyboard-only users otherwise have to hunt for the pill.
repro: F6 to the transcript, press PageUp, then End.
recommendation: Bind end/G → jump_to_latest and home/g → scroll_home on ConsoleTranscript, and list them in F1.

title: Unification: media and artifact cards use three different action grammars, and Canvas actions don't say they open a browser
statement: Image card: 'View' (toggle) and 'Save'; the legend table says 'Save Image'. Video card: glyph-only '▶' and 'Save'; the legend table says '▶ Play' and 'Save copy'. Canvas card: 'Hello Canvas · revision 1 · updated' with 'Open revision' and 'Follow latest'. Both Canvas buttons open an external browser (open_canvas_with_textual → app.open_url), which the card never says. 'updated' on the first revision is ambiguous. Errors render as 'Revision unavailable · {error_code}'. The canvas_create tool row above the card dumps raw JSON ('{"canvas":{"canvas_id":"408a…","content_sha256":…').
expected: One card grammar: title, a one-line status, primary 'Open' (with '↗ browser' where external), 'Save…', and '⋯ More'. The same verbs in card and legend. Human status ('Created just now'). Tool rows summarised ('Created canvas "Hello Canvas"').
why: The user has to relearn each artifact type. An unexpected browser launch from a terminal app is surprising.
repro: Generate an image, create a canvas ('Use canvas_create…') and compare the card controls with the legend line.
recommendation: Create a shared MediaCard component with a common action vocabulary and external-open signifier. Derive the legend from the same labels, and summarise tool JSON for canvas_create.

title: The '▼ reply ready — jump to latest' pill persists after any completed run, implying an unread reply
statement: With the transcript scrolled up while no run was active and no new reply existed, the pill read '▼ reply ready — jump to latest'. The label is mapped from the last run status 'completed', so it stays indefinitely after any reply.
expected: Show 'reply ready' only when a reply has completed since the user scrolled away; otherwise show a neutral 'jump to latest'.
why: A false unread-reply cue sends users looking for new content that does not exist.
repro: After any reply completes, scroll up in the transcript and open a modal or menu.
recommendation: Track an 'unseen since scroll' flag and choose the label from it rather than from the last run status.

title: Buttons come in at least four styles, a secondary action outweighs the primary, and semantic green marks non-success states
statement: Header actions are flat bold text on the panel. Rail actions are dark #1e1e1e blocks with centred labels. Tab-strip actions look identical to inactive tabs. 'Clear' is a muted #9e9e9e block. In the composer, 'Send' is a dark block, disabled until you type, while 'Dictate' is bold white flat text, so the secondary action is the most prominent control in the idle composer. 'Terminal', pinned at the top of the rail, is an action coloured with the local-authority green ($ds-authority-local), so it reads as a status. The Inspector renders neutral or negative states in success green (#4ebf71), e.g. 'Retrieval: not staged' and 'sources not staged'. 'Tools: 6 ready' gets the bold alert emphasis, making a routine count the loudest chip (console_status_chips.py:896-905; _console.tcss:946-960).
expected: DESIGN button tiers (primary, secondary/ghost, tertiary) applied everywhere, and semantic colours used only for their named states.
why: The eye goes to the wrong controls, and a green 'not staged' teaches users that the colour means nothing.
repro: Idle 235x52 with Inspector open; sgr runs on rows 5, 8, 9, 14, 48 and 35-44.
recommendation: Define three Console button classes and move every Console button onto one of them. Style Dictate as a ghost button. Colour Terminal as an action, not an authority. Colour Inspector rows by their own readiness (neutral when not staged). Emphasise chips only when they need attention (approvals > 0, errors).

title: Side-stripe borders on transcript turns, list rows and callouts contradict DESIGN.md's rule against them; user and assistant turns use unrelated visual languages
statement: DESIGN §6 says 'Don't use side-stripe accent borders on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts', and its transcript rule asks for one 'role/body grammar'. Assistant turns carry a tall orange left stripe (border-left: tall $ds-chat-assistant-accent-*; the ▊ beside 'Assistant') with a nested grey markdown box, and code blocks form a third nested box. User turns are a blue-tinted band with no stripe. Transcript system events use a warning left stripe. Ctrl+K switcher rows carry colour-coded left stripes by state (waiting=warning, working=primary, new=success, current=accent, error=error; console_session_switcher_modal.py:237-247), so state is carried by colour alone. Error callouts in the Settings and endpoint modals use border-left: thick $error, and the voice preview a thick accent stripe. No ADR records an exception.
expected: Either full borders or tints plus a text state label as DESIGN.md prescribes, or an ADR sanctioning specific stripes (e.g. one assistant-turn speaker rule). One role grammar: the same body indent for both roles and at most one surface level.
why: The design contract and the shipping UI disagree, so contributors can't tell which to follow. Three nesting levels use up horizontal cells and add noise in the most-used region.
repro: Any exchange with markdown and code; Ctrl+K with tabs in several states.
recommendation: Decide with an ADR. Either keep the assistant-turn stripe as the single sanctioned speaker rule and convert the rest (switcher rows gain a state-word column; error callouts get a round $error border and tint), or amend DESIGN.md. Drop the inner markdown background so the body sits on the turn surface, keeping code blocks as the only inset.

title: About ten modal frame styles, and 18 Console modals hard-code 'border: tall gray; background: black'
statement: Frames seen: round $ds-grid-line (Settings, System prompt, Run log, Scope, Style, Workspace files); tall $ds-grid-line (Ctrl+K switcher, Prompts); solid $ds-grid-line (Conversation Inspector); round $primary (Save .md, Terminal session, Fork); tall $primary (Trace export, Exchange export, Archive receipt, Capture policy); tall $accent (Appearance, Reaction); solid $primary (Prompt queue); tall $border (Library access); round $panel (Endpoint template); thick $error (Global Full confirmation). In addition, 18 modals (composer menu, Edit message/thinking, rename, save-as, rewind, side chat, feedback, review notes, Library search, workspace switcher/rename, character picker, image viewer, video capacity, auto-speak, summarize, generate image) declare the literal colours 'border: tall gray; background: black' in widget CSS, with no token override. Measured on the composer menu, the border is #808080: 4.74:1 in textual-dark and 2.99:1 in textual-light, below 3:1. DESIGN.md says round borders for panels and inspectors, tall borders only for destination headers, and semantic tokens only.
expected: One Console modal frame (e.g. round $ds-grid-line on $ds-surface-panel), with a warning or error variant only when state requires it.
why: The frame is the common-region cue that says 'this is a modal'. Ten variants make it read as decoration, and the literal colours ignore the 27 light themes.
repro: Open Menu (tall gray on black), Ctrl+K (tall), header Settings (round); switch to Textual Light via Ctrl+P and reopen Menu.
recommendation: Define one .console-modal-frame rule in _console_panels.tcss using ds tokens and apply it to every Console modal. Delete the per-widget border and background declarations. Add a CSS lint that rejects named colours (gray/black/white) in Console CSS.

title: Text inputs mix a 3-row tall-border style (border 1.05:1) with the one-row composer convention; placeholders clip mid-word and fall below contrast minimums
statement: The rail 'Filter visible titles' input and the Inspector 'Ask Library sources before sending' input each take 3 rows with a tall border of #191919 on #1e1e1e (1.05:1), so the field edge is invisible (console_workspace_context.py:1796-1806). The composer is a one-row field with a left edge. The filter placeholder clips to 'Filter visible' (211) and 'Filter' (160 and below) with no ellipsis and measures 3.52:1. The composer placeholder measures 2.56:1 (G4-41) and clips to 'Ask, command, or paste' at 80 columns.
expected: Every Console field follows the one-row convention (left edge at rest, thick accent on focus), with placeholders at 4.5:1 or better and short enough to fit ('Filter…').
why: The filter alone costs 3 of the scarce rail rows at 30-row heights, and two input grammars sit in the same view.
repro: Resize 235 → 160 → 120; sgr.py pairs.
recommendation: Restyle ConsoleBrowserSearchInput and the Inspector Library input to the one-row field class. Shorten the placeholders ('Filter titles', 'Ask Library…') and raise their colour to $text-muted.
evidence: uxrev/evidence/J7/09-state-235x52.ansi (pairs: 1.05 border, 2.56 composer placeholder, 3.52 filter placeholder)

title: Voice controls are split between header and composer, and the header switches carry state by colour only
statement: 'Speak replies ▌' and 'Hands-free ▌' are one-row Switches in the destination header's status area (row 4), with state carried only by knob colour and position. 'Dictate' is in the composer. The auto-speak recovery buttons (Retry speech, Resume auto-speak) live in a hidden row of the control bar. DESIGN.md's dense-form convention says toggles are 'always paired with a text-state word'. The colour-only paused state in G3-08 is one consequence.
expected: One voice cluster next to Dictate ('Dictate · Speak replies: Off · Hands-free: Off') with state words, and recovery buttons in the same cluster.
why: An optional feature occupies the header's readiness area, with colour-only state that breaks the project's own rule.
repro: Look at row 4 of the default capture.
recommendation: Move ConsoleSpeechControls into the composer row after Dictate, or into a 'Voice ▾' popover. Render state as text ('Speak replies: Off'). Free the header status area for the workspace/authority breadcrumb.
